The "Drive & Kick" offense is a three-player weave used to run time off the clock. The ball handler drives to the basket; if denied, they pass outside and replace the receiver to continue the weave. Against baseline defenders, the dribbler can kick out to the corner or drop a pass to a back-cutting player.

UNC Chapel Hill placed Professor Dwayne Dixon on leave to investigate his alleged advocacy of politically motivated violence. Dixon, a former member of the now-disbanded antifascist group Silver Valley Redneck Revolt, previously faced dismissed charges for armed counterprotesting but remained employed. The current investigation follows fliers at Georgetown University promoting a Redneck Revolt affiliate, the John Brown Gun Club. Turning Point USA spokesperson Andrew Kolvet linked Dixon to the group online, demanding his firing. UNC stated the leave allows for an investigation that could lead to termination. The AAUP and a petition with over 900 signatures condemned UNC's actions, accusing the university of capitulating to right-wing attacks based on unsubstantiated rumors. Dixon is among several faculty recently disciplined after right-wing figures identified them on social media following Charlie Kirk's death.

Three Illinois gang members were fatally shot at point-blank range on Aug. 13, 2017, at Great Lakes Dragaway near Union Grove, Wis., during a racing event. Kenosha County Sheriff David Beth suspects the killings were gang-related. The suspect, an unidentified black man in his 20s or 30s, fled in a vehicle and remains at large. The murder weapon was not recovered. The event drew 15,000 attendees and lacked weapons screening, though the shooting occurred in the parking area. Authorities noted the victims' families were uncooperative.

Coach Joel Quenneville and Stan Bowman discuss their hockey team's strong performance, balance, and progression throughout the season and playoffs. Bowman praises goaltender Corey for his consistent play, which allows the team to focus on its strengths. Both note the maturity of the core group and the impact of young players. Bowman emphasizes that success stems from incremental improvements, internal growth, and a collective team effort involving scouting and coaching staff. They express a desire to sustain success and maintain roster continuity despite salary cap challenges. Quenneville highlights the challenge of facing the upcoming opponent, specifically mentioning defenseman Chara and the opposing goalie's abilities, stressing the need to screen the goalie and force the opponent to play defense. Bowman commends Bryan Bickell's development, while Quenneville praises Patrick Sharp's productive playoff performance and recalls his time playing in Windsor.

The Bearish Engulfing candlestick pattern is a technical analysis tool indicating a potential reversal from an uptrend to a downtrend. It consists of a bullish candlestick followed by a bearish one that completely engulfs the previous body, signaling a shift in market sentiment to bearish. Traders use it to adjust positions, enter short trades, and set stop-losses above the first candle's high. Backtested on the S&P 500 since 1993, it has a 55-65% win rate and 311 occurrences. Its accuracy can be improved by combining it with indicators like RSI or MACD. Traders must manage risks like false signals and volatility using stop-losses, position sizing, and diversification. It indicates stronger bearish sentiment than similar patterns like the dark cloud cover or bearish harami.

The 50 EMA strategy is a technical analysis method using the 50-day Exponential Moving Average to identify medium-term trends and generate buy and sell signals. Traders often combine it with indicators like RSI or MACD for confirmation. While a simple crossover strategy underperforms buy-and-hold on assets like gold and the S&P 500, adding a second indicator filter significantly improves results for stocks like QQQ and SPY, offering higher risk-adjusted returns and lower drawdowns despite being invested only about 27-29% of the time. The strategy also performs decently on bonds. Traders are advised to backtest, use appropriate timeframes, and manage risk.

The AMD Secure RNG Library provides an API to access hardware-generated random numbers using x86 instructions (RDRAND and RDSEED). It abstracts low-level programming, manages hardware failure checks, and allows retry attempts. The library exposes APIs to fetch single or array values of 16, 32, and 64 bits, plus byte arrays, and includes functions to verify hardware support. Although hardware access via memory-mapped I/O is slower than software PRNGs, a hybrid approach—seeding PRNGs with hardware values—can enhance both security and performance for applications like cryptography, HPC, and gaming.

A federal appeals court granted a stay, allowing the Education Department to fire half of its Office for Civil Rights (OCR) staff. The court concluded the OCR case did not differ enough from a prior Supreme Court ruling that permitted similar department-wide firings.

Following the murder of conservative activist Charlie Kirk, the Trump administration and right-wing figures blamed liberal nonprofits, with the Justice Department drafting plans to potentially investigate the Open Society Foundations. In response, liberal nonprofits and funders, who have been preparing for months, are exploring various strategies to protect themselves. Options include merging, relocating outside the US, surrendering 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status to register as businesses, and gearing up for legal battles. Foundations are also accelerating grant disbursements to support organizations facing a hostile operating environment and government funding cuts. Nonprofit leaders warn that the administration's actions aim to damage their reputations, drain resources through legal defenses, and induce self-censorship, which could ultimately dismantle civil society.

Carolina Herrera appointed Lisa Arnold as vice president of retail and Thea Terenik as vice president of global merchandising. Both report to Emilie Rubinfeld. Arnold will oversee global retail, while Terenik will lead brand positioning and product strategy. The brand also added Maria Borges to its fall modeling campaign.

British shares dropped on Thursday, with the FTSE 100 down 0.6 percent, after Federal Reserve minutes indicated a balance sheet shrinkage later this year. Financials, including Lloyds and RBS, weighed heavily on the market. Pearson declined 8.9 percent due to an ex-dividend trade and a broker downgrade. Conversely, real estate and mining stocks gained. Mid-cap Allied Minds fell 8.4 percent below its IPO price after cutting funding for seven portfolio companies, while Tullow Oil and BTG rose.

This pre-posttest study analyzed the impact of enforcing Kenya's 2014 national referral guidelines on orthopaedic and trauma facility referrals to Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH). Following the guidelines' enforcement in July 2021, data from 468 referrals showed a significant reduction in direct referrals from lower-tier facilities (Tiers II and III) and an increase from higher tiers (IV, V, and VI). Forty-three health facilities, predominantly private and lower-tier, ceased direct referrals to KNH. The primary factors associated with referrals were inadequate human resource capacity, infrastructure, equipment availability, patient preference, and financial considerations. The study concludes that enforcing referral guidelines successfully reduced inappropriate lower-tier direct referrals to KNH.

U.S. manufacturing faces a shortage of qualified workers for advanced, automated jobs requiring technical skills. As part of the AP's Future of Work series, the passage highlights how blue-collar workers struggle to adapt while skilled workers benefit.

The 1-2-2 Zone is a basketball defense effective against outside shooting, fast breaks, and late-game lead protection. It positions the point at the top, wings at the elbows, and baseline players above the blocks. Defenders shift based on ball location, with baseline players working in unison, wings working opposite, and the point guarding the ball out front or the high post. Variations include wing corner shifts (staying out for pass denial or dropping to help the post), a corner trap, and switching to a 2-1-2 zone on the first pass to match a two-guard front. The zone can also be extended into a half or full-court press.

Probiotics are known to improve gut health, but new Emory University research suggests they may also protect the liver from drug and alcohol-induced damage. In a mouse study, a diet rich in the probiotic Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) improved the liver's antioxidant response, protecting it from oxidative damage caused by high doses of acetaminophen. The protein Nrf2 plays a key role in this protection. Researchers note further studies are needed to see if these results apply to humans. Probiotics are not a substitute for medicine, and a doctor should be consulted before use.

This email compiles news articles from March 2001 regarding Enron Corp. and other energy market developments.

Enron CEO Jeff Skilling attributed the company's recent stock price drop to "multiple compression" from high price-to-earnings ratios. Analysts also cited Enron-specific factors, including declining broadband valuation, the terminated Blockbuster video deal, and unpaid bills from India's Dabhol plant. Skilling maintained Enron's profit targets and defended its "virtual integration" business model.

Enron's 2000 proxy statement showed Chairman Kenneth Lay received a $7 million bonus and Skilling $5.6 million, reflecting the company's strong performance.

The IntercontinentalExchange (ICE) planned to trade U.S. refined products off the Colonial Pipeline, while EnronOnline considered adding similar products. Enron also proposed a large LNG thermal power plant in Japan and was involved in a power project in Nigeria, which planned to break up its state power monopoly.

FERC sought input on coordinating wholesale power transactions among regional transmission organizations to address "seams" issues. California regulators approved a nearly 50% electricity rate hike to assist utilities, a move Skilling supported.

Additionally, Viacom canceled plans to spin off Blockbuster, whose video-on-demand venture with Enron had failed. An online investor tournament also highlighted Enron as an economic "plumbing" company.

Despite global education expansion, deficiencies persisted by 2020 and worsened with COVID-19. The paper examines the pandemic's implications for Comparative and International Education (CIE) in achieving Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 4, established by the UN and detailed in the Incheon Declaration. 

Prior to the pandemic, global education fell short in participation, quality, and equality. COVID-19 caused further deterioration through school closures affecting 91% of students, exacerbating inequalities, and reducing quality, though it also forced the conservative education sector to adopt technology. 

The paper argues that CIE, which studies education systems within societal contexts, should investigate the pandemic's educational ravages and the use of technology to recommend strategies for achieving 2030 education goals. Addressing these challenges can also help CIE overcome its own deficiencies, such as the "black box syndrome," Northern hegemony, lack of autochthonous theory, and limited academic and practical impact. Ultimately, CIE is pivotal for using pandemic experiences to build better education systems and reach 2030 objectives.

In Closson v. Billman et al. (1904), Closson sued to foreclose a material man's lien for lumber supplied to contractor Worley for constructing a house for Billman. Closson had co-signed a bond guaranteeing Worley would complete the work "according to the contract," which required Worley to furnish and pay for materials. After Worley failed to pay for the lumber, Closson filed the lien. The court affirmed the judgment for the defendants, holding that the guarantor on the bond is liable for the liens because completing the work according to the contract includes paying for materials. The court clarified that Closson was a guarantor, not a surety. His liability on the bond was a sufficient defense against the lien foreclosure to avoid circuity of action. Because the guaranty was executed contemporaneously with the contract, notice of acceptance was not required. The burden to plead and prove any omission of notice of default and resulting damages rested on the guarantor.

Mesh Shading moves object list processing to the GPU, enabling more scene objects and new geometry algorithms. Variable Rate Shading dynamically adjusts shading rates to improve frame rates by reducing unnecessary work. Texture-Space Shading caches shading results in a private coordinate space to eliminate duplicate work. Multi-View Rendering renders multiple views in a single pass, regardless of differing origins or directions.

Texas Tech University briefly posted an FAQ clarifying new policies prohibiting faculty from teaching about transgender identity before removing it three days later. The guidance advised against pronoun language and LGBTQ allyship statements on syllabi but permitted preferred name policies. It clarified the policies do not affect independent research. The FAQ only applied to the flagship campus; other system campuses lack written guidance but face verbal bans on terms like "transgender." Health-care instructors worry these bans conflict with certification exam requirements for transgender patient care. The Texas AAUP criticized the policies for violating academic freedom.

On January 28, 2019, NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K announcing it issued a press release and shareholder letter updating its financial guidance for the quarter ended January 27, 2019. The furnished documents are not considered "filed" under the Securities Exchange Act. The report was signed by CFO Colette M. Kress.

Motley Fool Money reviews three credit cards, stating its ratings are independent of partner compensation. The Wells Fargo Active Cash Card offers unlimited 2% cash rewards, a $200 bonus after spending $500, 0% intro APR for 12 months, no annual fee, and up to $600 in cell phone protection. The Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Card provides 1.5% cash back on all purchases (5% on Capital One Travel bookings), a $300 welcome bonus, 0% intro APR for 15 months, and no annual or foreign transaction fees. A Citi card earns 2% cash back on purchases (1% when buying, 1% when paying), 5% on Citi Travel, and a $200 bonus after spending $1,500, featuring a 0% intro APR on balance transfers for 18 months. All three cards recommend a good to excellent credit score (670-850).

This June 7, 2001 VentureWire newsletter covers venture capital and technology business news. Top stories include FreeMarkets and Adexa terminating their $340M acquisition agreement (FreeMarkets instead taking a 3% stake for $6M), inVentures merging with Redwood Partners to form Redwood Partners International (raising a $100M fund), ChipData closing $23M in Series B funding, and Bob Lisbonne joining Matrix Partners from Crosspoint. The newsletter also reports numerous funding rounds across companies including Corus Pharma, ThruPoint, DevelopOnline, TelOptica, and Genicon Sciences; company shutdowns and layoffs at Intransit Networks, Music.com, Notara, and Wapit; new deals involving i-drive and GlobalEnglish; Triton spinning off three companies; multiple M&A transactions including Salu, ClosingGuard, Platinum Equity, and Manugistics; new board appointments; executive changes at PhoneFree/Gemini Voice Solutions, Nationtax Online, and BlueKite.com; and venture capital fund news from nCoTec and Whitney & Co.

The present disclosure provides systems, methods, devices, and computer-readable storage media for route planning for vehicles, such as automated guided vehicles (AGVs), based on a map. The system obtains a map containing node information and acquires motion status information of other vehicles in the target region. By modifying the node information—such as weight values, passability, and turn capabilities—based on the motion status of static and moving vehicles, the system generates a modified map. It then determines a target route from a start node to a destination node by calculating total costs associated with the nodes using algorithms like A-star. The total cost incorporates the cost from the start node, the estimated cost to the destination, distance costs, and turn costs. This route planning approach accounts for the motion of other vehicles to prevent collisions and improve the accuracy and efficiency of the planned route.

W. T. Hay, a discharged bankrupt, appealed an order refusing to stay a writ of execution on real estate he had conveyed to his wife prior to bankruptcy. The court dismissed his appeal, holding that Hay lacked standing because he no longer owned or claimed the property. If the conveyance was fraudulent, the property passed to the bankruptcy trustee; if not, the wife held title. Questions regarding the bank's right to proceed post-discharge or the validity of a sheriff's sale must be raised by the wife, as the execution does not affect Hay's rights.

The passage outlines U.S. policy toward the Soviet Union for 1983. In arms control, the U.S. must maintain high standards for reductions and verifiability, blaming the USSR for impeding progress, while focusing on INF and START. On regional issues, the U.S. should test Soviet intentions on Afghanistan, counter the Soviet "Asian offensive" via US-PRC dialogue, and address conflicts in southern Africa and the Third World. For human rights, the U.S. will use private diplomacy to seek improvements like Jewish emigration and press a democracy offensive. Economic relations must avoid subsidizing the Soviet economy or military, potentially using the Joint Commercial Commission. Bilateral relations should involve mutual, reciprocal steps, such as a new cultural agreement. The U.S. should build toward a potential summit through four dialogue levels: summitry, ministerial contacts, ambassadors, and departmental specialists. Ultimately, the U.S. will maintain its established policy, placing responsibility for any continued tensions on Moscow if its criteria are unmet.

Delta Insurance is expanding its presence in the South Island's booming technology sector. Underwriter Karl Samson highlights Delta's broad liability, cyber, and environmental insurance offerings. Delta joined Canterbury Tech and is New Zealand's only risk management-led cyber insurance provider. Samson brings 12 years of experience to support local businesses and brokers.

MacKenzie Scott continues her philanthropy by providing large, unrestricted grants to diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives. Recent donations include $70 million to UNCF for historically Black colleges and universities, and tens of millions to Native Forward and 10,000 Degrees for underrepresented students. Over the past five years, Scott has donated over $19 billion to thousands of organizations focused on education, healthcare, and economic security. She is also expanding into mission-aligned investing to further amplify her social impact.
A traditional Eurasian method uses live ants and their bacteria to acidify and thicken warmed cow's milk into yogurt.

In March 2020, Lisa Baird became commissioner of the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL), the third attempt at a U.S. women's professional soccer league following the collapses of WUSA and WPS. Initially subsidized by U.S. Soccer, which paid national team player salaries, the NWSL operated as a single entity. Shortly after Baird's arrival, the COVID-19 pandemic suspended operations. Baird secured a government loan to pay player salaries and implemented a phased return-to-play protocol. The NWSL became the first U.S. professional league to return, staging the 2020 Challenge Cup in a Utah bubble, followed by a Fall Series. During this period, the league achieved a 493% increase in television viewership, secured new sponsors, and supported player social justice initiatives. As the league entered its ninth year, Baird and team owners focused on converting casual fans, integrating new teams and high-profile investors, rebranding, increasing media exposure, navigating the separation from U.S. Soccer, and negotiating a new collective bargaining agreement.

This study investigates Cu-doped NiO thin films synthesized via an ultra-fast spray pyrolysis technique (1.5 minutes at 450°C) for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) sensing. XRD analysis confirmed that Cu successfully substituted Ni in the cubic lattice, causing lattice expansion and a minor decrease in crystallite size. Optical characterizations showed that Cu doping enhanced visible light absorption, reduced the bandgap from 3.70 eV to 3.65 eV, and increased defect density, as evidenced by Raman and photoluminescence spectra. Electrical measurements indicated that both films exhibited decreased resistance upon LPG exposure. However, the Cu-doped NiO film demonstrated superior performance, achieving a sensitivity of 1.8 at a 5V bias compared to 1.3 for undoped NiO. The study concludes that Cu doping introduces beneficial structural and electronic modifications, significantly enhancing the gas sensing capabilities of NiO films.

On November 13, 2017, Apple Inc. issued and sold $7 billion in senior unsecured notes across six maturities (2019–2047) with interest rates ranging from 1.800% to 3.750%, pursuant to an underwriting agreement dated November 6, 2017 with Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, and Merrill Lynch. The notes were issued under an indenture dated April 29, 2013 with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company as trustee and rank equally with Apple's other unsecured and unsubordinated debt.

The passage details AMD AGESA software interfaces, data structures, and procedures for processor and system initialization across PEI, DXE, and S3 resume boot phases. It describes PPIs, HOBs, and PEIMs used for early core initialization, memory setup, and reset coordination. Key entry points—such as AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost, AmdInitEnv, AmdInitLate, and resume functions—are outlined with their parameters, dependencies, and status codes. The text also specifies required host environment call-outs for memory allocation, SPD reading, and AP execution, alongside platform configuration options for VRM, PCIe, memory, and graphics subsystems.

Best Buy is offering the Lenovo Legion 7i Gen 10 gaming laptop for $1,650. It features a 2,560 x 1,600 OLED screen with a 165-Hz refresh rate and 1,000-nit peak brightness. Powered by a 115-watt RTX 5060, it achieves high frame rates but has under five hours of battery life. It also includes an excellent trackpad, keyboard, and numpad.

On February 1, 2018, Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K announcing its fourth quarter and full-year 2017 financial results. The filing includes a press release and information on non-GAAP financial measures as exhibits, and was signed by Senior Vice President and CFO Brian T. Olsavsky.

Alek Minassian, 25, was charged with 10 counts of first-degree murder after driving a rental van into Toronto pedestrians, killing 10 and injuring 15. His motive remains unclear. Officials stated the attack was not a national security threat. Prime Minister Justin Trudeau urged unity, noting the threat level was unchanged. Canadians mourned with memorials and lowered flags, while the officer who peacefully arrested Minassian was praised.

In 2016, U.S. airlines achieved record-low rates for domestic flight cancellations, mishandled baggage, and involuntary passenger bumping. On-time arrivals improved to 81.4 percent, with Hawaiian Airlines ranking first. Consumer complaints also decreased by 11.3 percent from 2015.

The Jerusalem Post asks readers for $5 monthly to support its accessible journalism. Subscribers receive an almost ad-free experience, premium content, a Hebrew learning magazine, Jerusalem Repor content, and a daily ePaper.

OHSU scientists attempted to create human eggs in the lab using a cloning technique that previously produced healthy mouse pups. A new paper reveals the human cell attempt is mostly unsuccessful so far, though they developed "mitomeiosis" to reduce chromosome numbers. Researcher Mitalipov acknowledges the technology needs refinement but remains optimistic it can eventually work to treat infertility and enable same-sex reproduction.

Improving farmers' conditions requires broad education focused on practical life, good citizenship, the dignity of labor, and cooperative spirit. Farmers benefit from voluntary organizations like the grange movement, which provide economic and social advantages. While farmers must primarily help themselves, the Department of Agriculture provides effective assistance by working through farmer associations and coordinating with states. Government and farmers successfully cooperate on threats like the boll weevil and cattle fever tick, while national policies on irrigation and forest preservation yield significant benefits. Additionally, Congress is urged to fund a memorial amphitheater at Arlington. Finally, the passage advocates for a constitutional amendment granting Congress authority over marriage and divorce to prevent state law discrepancies and effectively eradicate polygamy.

A study of 19 mothers and their babies suggests the brain chemical dopamine plays a key role in mother-infant bonding by motivating maternal care. Researchers found that mothers secreted more dopamine when watching their own babies, and higher dopamine levels were linked to more sensitive, optimal caregiving. Conversely, less responsive mothers secreted less dopamine. This research helps explain both healthy maternal caregiving and potential struggles, highlighting the importance of responsive care for infant brain development. Experts note the study's small size limits broad applicability and leaves questions about whether strong bonding is innate or developed.

Trauma and adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) significantly impact post-secondary students' academic performance, behavior, and well-being, with healthcare students facing additional risks of secondary traumatic stress. To address this, the authors reviewed literature on trauma-informed care (TIC) frameworks for health profession education (HPE), specifically occupational therapy (OT). The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) outlines six core principles and ten implementation domains for TIC, emphasizing safety, trustworthiness, and empowerment. 

Implementing TIC in higher education requires leadership support, policy changes, faculty training, and student involvement. Effective models include the PATH simulation-based training and peer-led health coaching. However, OT curricula currently lack a strong focus on trauma. The authors suggest OT educators seek professional development, adopt trauma-informed pedagogical strategies (such as providing advance notice of triggering content and embedding self-care modules), and reflect on their practices. Adopting TIC in OT education can mitigate trauma's effects, fostering a supportive environment that improves student retention, graduation rates, and overall academic success.

This June 8, 2001 issue of National Journal's CongressDailyAM covers several congressional developments. House Appropriations released FY02 subcommittee allocations largely following President Bush's requests but with billions more for Labor-HHS, VA-HUD, and Energy-Water. House leaders planned to stick to Bush's FY01 supplemental spending request despite defense hawks calling it inadequate, with veto threats if Congress adds substantially. The Senate Democratic takeover was expected to have minimal impact on House partisanship, as Republicans felt liberated to pass their preferred legislation. Rep. Steve Largent announced his November resignation to run for Oklahoma governor. Rep. Asa Hutchinson's pending departure to head the DEA left business groups seeking a new champion for liability reform legislation. Labor Secretary Chao announced ergonomics forums, drawing GOP praise but Democratic skepticism. FDA officials warned about safety risks from mailed prescription drugs. The House Energy and Commerce Committee remained open to adding generic drug reform to a Medicare prescription drug bill. EU officials expressed concern about Bush's steel import investigation. Senate Republicans and Democrats neared agreement on an organizing resolution. Bush intended to nominate Jo Anne Barnhart as Social Security commissioner. GOP Census Board members released a report questioning statistical sampling. House lawmakers introduced legislation requiring public input and congressional approval for large national monuments.

AMC Entertainment proposes doubling authorized shares to 1.1 billion, risking shareholder dilution. The company holds over $3 billion in net debt and saw weak Q3 box office revenues. AMC trades at a discount to peers like CNK due to ongoing losses, negative equity, and cash burn. The company was severely impacted by the pandemic, facing plunging attendance and delayed releases.

Robert Stuart's research argues the BBC Panorama documentary "Saving Syria's Children" fabricated a 2013 Syrian school bombing. The passage details Stuart's highlighted discrepancies: medical professionals question the victims' visible injuries; victim counts vary widely between 25 and 50 among sources; and the event's timing differs by up to six hours among BBC crew members. Additionally, the text notes the backgrounds of two British doctors in the documentary: Dr. Saleyah Ahsan is a former British Army captain with ties to medical simulation training, and Dr. Rola Hallam's father may be connected to the Syrian National Council. The author concludes this alleged fakery raises broader concerns about narratives used to justify western intervention.

The widespread use of HRP2-based malaria rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) has driven the emergence of *pfhrp2/3* gene deletions, causing false-negative results and threatening malaria control. This study uses a mathematical model to assess the global risk of *pfhrp2* deletion spread, focusing on sub-Saharan Africa. Researchers estimated parameters like fitness costs, HRP3 cross-reactivity, and linkage between *pfhrp2* and *pfhrp3* deletions using WHO data. They developed two risk scores: the "Innate Risk Score" (potential for spread if established) and the "Prospective Risk Score" (continued spread based on current prevalence). Malaria prevalence was identified as the primary driver of deletion selection, with lower prevalence increasing selection pressure. The model predicts 73 of 106 countries have at least one region at risk of reaching a 5% misdiagnosis threshold within 20 years, with high-risk areas in the Horn of Africa, East Africa, and parts of West Africa. Despite data uncertainties, these risk maps and an interactive tool aim to guide surveillance and the deployment of alternative RDTs.

Researchers created early human embryos from skin cells by fusing a skin cell nucleus with an empty donor egg and using chemicals to coax the cell to halve its chromosomes. However, the resulting embryos had abnormal chromosome counts and were not viable. While this proof-of-concept may eventually help treat infertility or allow same-sex male couples to have genetically related children, the technique is currently too inefficient for clinical use. Researchers estimate it will take at least a decade before clinical trials, which are currently prohibited in the United States.

The lecture models protein folding using fixed-angle linkages, where edge lengths and angles are fixed, allowing only rotations around edges. This relates to the protein folding problem (predicting a protein's 3D shape) and the protein design problem. The discussion covers four main problems:

1. Span: Finding the maximum or minimum distance between chain endpoints. Finding flat min/max span is NP-hard, though 3D max span for orthogonal chains is solvable in linear time. The general 3D span problem remains open.
2. Flattening: Determining if a fixed-angle chain has a flat, non-self-intersecting state. This is NP-hard.
3. Flat state connectivity: Determining if all flat states are connected via continuous motions. This is open for general chains but proven for orthogonal and obtuse chains.
4. Locked chains: Fixed-angle chains can be locked. Equilateral and equiangular chains can be locked, but it is open whether chains that are simultaneously equilateral, equiangular, and obtuse can be locked.

The lecture also introduces "producible protein chains," modeling the ribosome as a cone from which a protein chain is produced. It is proven that all producible configurations of such chains belong to a single connected component and are flat state connected. This is achieved by defining a canonical configuration and algorithmically folding any producible state into this canonical state and back.

This email compiles July 2001 news articles on California's energy crisis. Key topics include:
- Criticism of Governor Gray Davis for signing expensive long-term power contracts that burden the state budget, and his efforts to bail out Southern California Edison despite conflict-of-interest concerns involving his advisors.
- The SEC launched a preliminary inquiry into whether Davis' energy consultants used inside information to trade power company stocks. Five consultants were fired for conflicts of interest, and Davis' press secretary, Steve Maviglio, disclosed purchasing Calpine stock.
- Consultants Mark Fabiani and Chris Lehane agreed to forgo state payments to settle a conflict-of-interest lawsuit over their concurrent work for Davis and Edison.
- Federal energy regulators limited California's potential power refunds to under $4 billion, significantly less than the $9 billion sought. Davis plans to appeal.
- San Francisco placed two measures on the November ballot to create public utility districts and remove PG&E from the city's electricity market.
- Texas initiated a pilot program for electricity deregulation, while Maryland regulators reviewed Baltimore Gas and Electric's planned corporate split to avoid California-like issues.

Gas colic in horses, while common, can lead to severe complications like colon displacement. It occurs when normal hindgut fermentation gas builds up instead of passing. Primary causes include inadequate forage, stall confinement, stress, and rapid feed changes. Restricting forage disrupts digestion, leading to gorging and ulcers, while confinement reduces intestinal motility. Preventing gas colic requires providing forage 24 hours a day, increasing pasture turnout to reduce stress, and transitioning feeds gradually over one to three weeks. Additional preventative measures include using slow feeders, avoiding inflammatory ingredients like sugar and soy, and supplementing with B vitamins, yeast, or colostrum to support digestive health.

The Newark Police Department is seeking the public's help to locate nine suspects in seven unsolved shootings and robberies dating back to June 2016. Public Safety Director Anthony Ambrose released the suspects' photos and crime details. Authorities request confidential tips via phone, website, or smartphone app, which may result in rewards.

Asus launched the Zenfone 5Z in India, exclusively on Flipkart starting July 15. Priced from Rs. 29,999 to Rs. 36,999 across three variants, the smartphone features a 6.2-inch notch display, Snapdragon 845 processor, Android Oreo, and dual rear cameras. Launch offers include ICICI card discounts and Jio benefits.

In People v. Helzer, the court held that sexual delinquency is an alternate sentencing provision, not a penalty enhancement. To avoid prejudice, a defendant must be tried by a separate jury for the sexual delinquency charge, empaneled immediately after conviction on the principal charge. The defendant is entitled to 20 peremptory challenges for this second jury due to the possible life sentence, but only the standard number for the initial jury. The sexual delinquency charge must be included in the original indictment before the principal trial begins, and no reference to it may be made to the first jury. The court affirmed the defendant's gross indecency conviction but remanded for a new hearing on the sexual delinquency charge before a separate jury. Chief Justice Kavanagh dissented, arguing the statute is unconstitutionally void for vagueness.

On March 27, 2017, Tesla, Inc. reported that underwriters exercised their option to purchase an additional $127.5 million of Tesla’s 2.375% Convertible Senior Notes due 2022. On March 30, 2017, Tesla issued these Option Notes under a Fourth Supplemental Indenture. Concurrently, Tesla entered into additional note hedge transactions, paying approximately $26.6 million to reduce potential dilution, and issued additional warrants allowing counterparties to acquire up to 0.8 million shares at a $655.00 strike price, receiving approximately $6.9 million in proceeds.

The American Cancer Society updated its guideline to recommend colorectal cancer screening for average-risk adults beginning at age 45, lowered from 50, due to rising cancer rates in younger adults and modeling showing a favorable benefit-to-burden balance. The age 45 recommendation is "qualified," while screening for those 50 and older remains a "strong recommendation." Adults should choose from various stool-based tests or structural exams, as no test is prioritized. Positive non-colonoscopy results require a follow-up colonoscopy. Screening should continue through age 75 for healthy adults, be individualized for those 76 to 85, and be discouraged for individuals over 85. The update addresses a 51% increase in colorectal cancer among adults under 50 since 1994, a trend expected to persist as these cohorts age.

The NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture introduces advancements over Pascal, utilizing GDDR6 memory for improved bandwidth and power efficiency. It features a new display engine supporting 8K resolution, HDR, and enhanced video encoding. Turing simplifies VR connectivity with USB-C and VirtualLink, and improves SLI bandwidth using NVLink. A major innovation is real-time ray tracing, enabled by dedicated RT Cores that accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) traversal and ray-triangle intersection, supporting a hybrid rendering model combining rasterization and ray tracing. Turing also integrates Tensor Cores for AI-based NGX features like Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS), InPainting, and AI Super Rez. Additional rendering technologies include Mesh Shading for efficient geometry processing, Variable Rate Shading (VRS) for dynamic shading rates, Texture Space Shading (TSS), and Multi-View Rendering (MVR). The architecture spans the TU102, TU104, and TU106 chips, which vary in core counts and features, and introduces the RTX-OPS metric to evaluate hybrid rendering performance.

Higher wind supply and easing demand lowered European prompt power prices, while forwards tracked lower coal prices. The outlook remains bearish due to improved French nuclear supply and falling demand. German, French, and Czech power contracts dropped, while gas and oil prices gained.

The University of Manchester’s Students’ Union launched Earth Week with a panel featuring Asad Rehman and Martin Empson. Rehman discussed climate change's impact on developing countries, noting it causes mass displacement and arguing climate refugees deserve legal protection due to wealthy nations' disproportionate emissions. Empson urged public involvement through protests and petitions, stressing the need to unite environmental and migration movements to create hope.

Canada's Privacy Commissioner is investigating the 2016 Uber breach affecting over 57 million users, which Uber concealed for a year via a $100,000 payment to thieves. Global investigations and an Alberta lawsuit are underway. Uber is cooperating but hasn't disclosed Canadian impact. The Commissioner seeks proactive enforcement, though laws limit actions to Federal Court rather than direct fines.

American Girl is releasing its first male doll, Logan Everett, a drummer for a contemporary character, due to fan requests. The company is also re-releasing the classic Felicity Merriman doll and introducing two new dolls later in 2017: Z Yang and Nanea. The 18-inch dolls cost $115.

Quantum spin relaxation in radical pair systems is essential for applications in quantum computing, spintronics, and quantum biophysics. Modeling these systems presents three main computational challenges: ensemble averaging of randomly oriented initial nuclear states, exponential growth of Hilbert and Liouville space dimensionality, and numerically stable long-time propagation. To address these issues, this work introduces tensor network methods to spin chemistry. The authors detail the radical pair Hamiltonian—comprising Zeeman, hyperfine, exchange, dipolar, and Haberkorn relaxation terms—and present stochastic matrix product states (MPS) and vectorised matrix product density operators (vMPDO). These tensor network approaches reduce the exponential scaling of computational elements, enabling more efficient simulations of radical pair dynamics and avian magnetoreception.

An experienced cave rescuer describes the Thai cave rescue of 12 boys and their coach as exceptionally difficult. While the standard protocol for flooded caves is to wait for water to subside to protect rescuers, monsoon rains may keep this cave flooded for months. The team survived nine days without food, leaving them weak and requiring gradual refeeding to avoid fatal complications. The three primary rescue options are: teaching the team to dive out, which is highly dangerous for novices; drilling a new entrance, which requires heavy equipment and precise mapping; or waiting for the water to recede. If their location remains safe from further flooding, they can stay and receive supplies; otherwise, the risky dive is the only remaining option. Rescuers face significant pressure to act despite the dangers.

Terry Rozier scored a career-high 31 points in his second career start, leading the short-handed Boston Celtics to a 119-110 victory over the Atlanta Hawks. Jayson Tatum added a career-high 27 points for Boston, which suited up only 10 players due to injuries, including Kyrie Irving's quad contusion. Despite solid economic growth, the Bank of Japan (BOJ) is hesitant to exit its ultra-loose monetary policy due to the risk of sharp yen appreciation and low inflation. A weak yen is a key policy accomplishment, and officials fear signaling normalization could trigger a damaging yen spike. While staying the course risks leaving the BOJ behind other central banks and depleting recession-fighting tools, any rate adjustments next year would likely be modest, one-off moves. Political pressures, including Prime Minister Abe's focus on stock prices and wages, alongside an impending leadership change, further complicate the outlook. The BOJ may slightly raise yield targets and slow asset purchases to prepare for potential economic shocks without resorting to unpopular negative rates.

The Arizona Supreme Court held that A.R.S. § 13-4033(B) bars a defendant from directly appealing a contested post-judgment restitution order entered pursuant to a plea agreement that contemplated payment of restitution up to a capped amount. Frank Hoffman pleaded no contest to DUI and agreed to pay restitution up to $53,653.45. After a contested hearing, the court ordered him to pay $40,933.45. Hoffman attempted to directly appeal, but the superior court dismissed the appeal. The Supreme Court affirmed, reasoning that treating such restitution orders as part of a "sentence" furthers the legislature's goal of eliminating direct appeals from plea agreements, avoids a hybrid review system, and aligns with the mandatory nature of restitution at sentencing. The court disapproved prior cases that had assumed jurisdiction over similar appeals without considering § 13-4033(B). Defendants must seek appellate review of such orders through Rule 32 post-conviction relief proceedings.

This study presents a non-invasive blood-based test to detect primary glial malignancy (GLI-M) in patients with intracranial space-occupying lesions (ICSOL). Standard diagnosis relies on invasive tissue biopsies, which carry procedural risks. The test enriches circulating glial cells (CGCs) from peripheral blood and identifies them via multiplexed immunocytochemistry profiling for GFAP and OLIG2. Analytical validation confirmed the test's accuracy, precision, and stability. Across multiple case-control and prospective clinical studies, the test differentiated GLI-M from benign brain tumors (BBT), epithelial malignancies with brain metastases (EPI-M), and non-glial CNS malignancies (NGCM), demonstrating high sensitivity (92.9% to 100%) and 100% specificity. Orthogonal verification via FISH showed 100% concordance in EGFR gene amplification detection between CGCs and matched tumor tissue. This minimally invasive test provides direct evidence of GLI-M to aid clinical decision-making, though it does not detect rarer subtypes like CNS lymphoma or differentiate tumor grade.

Dr. Howard W. Ellzey, a Memphis physician, was convicted of conspiracy and eleven counts of illegally distributing controlled substances. The author shares their experience with panic disorder and outlines expert-recommended strategies to manage panic attacks. Unlike "anxiety attacks," a non-clinical term for persistent worry, panic attacks are sudden, intense bursts of fear lasting under 30 minutes, often without a trigger. Symptoms include a pounding heart, shortness of breath, and fear of dying; a physical exam is advised to rule out other conditions. To cope, professionals recommend writing down reassuring facts and mantras, visualizing panic as a passing wave, using smartphone games or relaxing music for distraction, and practicing slow, deep breathing daily to calm the body during an attack.

Using the 2019 NSECE Household Survey, this study applied Latent Class Analysis to identify five distinct Child Care and Early Education (CCEE) search types based on up to two information sources families used: (1) CCR&R or Friends/Family, (2) Internet Search or Social Media, (3) Known Providers or Friends/Family, (4) Social Media or Friends/Family, and (5) Friends/Family or Internet Search. The analysis found that search types varied significantly based on whether families sought information on the type of care, whether the child had a condition affecting care provision, and geographic region. However, search types were largely similar across other family and child characteristics. Limitations include the restriction of recording only the first two sources mentioned and an analytic sample that was higher-income, more likely to be two-parent working households, and English-speaking compared to the overall survey population.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU features 40GB of HBM2 memory with SECDED ECC and a 40MB L2 cache enhanced by residency controls and compute data compression. It utilizes 108 SMs with third-generation Tensor Cores, improving data sharing and fetching through asynchronous copy instructions and barriers. The architecture introduces Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology, partitioning a single GPU into up to seven isolated instances with dedicated compute and memory resources for quality of service and fault isolation. It also includes third-generation NVLink (600 GB/sec total bandwidth), PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, and robust error containment. Additional hardware accelerators include NVJPG for JPEG decoding, an Optical Flow Accelerator, and five NVDEC units. CUDA 11 advances support task graphs, asynchronous barriers, and cooperative groups. The A100 powers the DGX A100 system, delivering 5 PFLOPS of performance. The architecture also supports fine-grained structured sparsity to optimize compute throughput with minimal accuracy loss.

This lecture covers various web security vulnerabilities and their defenses. It begins with the Shellshock bug, where attackers exploit CGI servers by injecting malicious Bash environment variables via HTTP headers. It then discusses Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), where attackers inject malicious scripts, and defenses like browser filters, HTTP-only cookies, privilege separation, content sanitization (using frameworks like Django or Markdown), and Content Security Policy (CSP). The lecture also covers SQL injection and path traversal via unsanitized inputs. Regarding session management, it explains the risks of cookies and explores alternatives like stateless cookies using Message Authentication Codes (MACs), DOM storage, and client-side certificates. Finally, it details protocol vulnerabilities like URL parsing discrepancies and the GIFAR attack, as well as covert channel attacks that use timing and rendering differences to deduce a user's browsing history.

Eagles WR A.J. Brown expressed frustration over his lack of targets, stating he wants the ball to help the struggling offense and in high-pressure situations, not for personal stats. UK scientists found that bumblebee queens exposed to neonicotinoid pesticides, widely used on crops like corn and canola, were 26 percent less likely to lay eggs. Swarthmore students often stress over perfection in academics and internships, but it is acceptable to make mistakes and laugh at oneself. The lecture reviews problem set 8 before discussing Hadamard transform realizations of Reed-Muller codes over the binary field F2. The professor explains the universal matrix Um, its self-inverse property, and how to build graphical realizations using simple constraint nodes. A comparison is made between cyclic and cycle-free (trellis) graphical realizations for the 8,4,4 code, illustrating the trade-off between complexity and decoding optimality. The lecture also briefly contrasts this approach with other graphical models like factor graphs, Markov graphs, and Bayesian networks. Finally, the professor introduces the sum-product algorithm for A Posteriori Probability (APP) decoding. APP decoding calculates the probability of variables given a received sequence by separating intrinsic and extrinsic information. The session concludes by explaining the past-future decomposition of cycle-free graphs to efficiently compute these probabilities using the Cartesian product lemma, with the remainder of the algorithm deferred to the next class.

This study investigates the interplay between brain ageing and multiple sclerosis (MS)-related neurodegeneration using deep learning on structural brain MRI scans. While the brain-age gap (BAG) captures deviations from healthy brain ageing, it may miss disease-specific effects. The authors propose the brain-predicted disease duration (DD) gap, which models disease duration to measure a patient's deviation from typical MS disease trajectories. Results from a multicentric cohort show that the DD gap is largely independent of BAG and significantly explains additional variance in physical disability (EDSS) both cross-sectionally and longitudinally. An alternative MS-specific ageing model (MS-age gap) was also tested but did not significantly improve disability prediction over BAG. The DD gap is sensitive to MS-specific imaging patterns, such as lesions, and is validated as a clinically meaningful biomarker of MS-specific brain damage and disease progression, complementing the classical brain-age paradigm.

The Situation Calculus is a logical language for specifying dynamical systems in AI. Reiter's successor state axioms solved the frame problem using the Markov property, while Gabaldon later extended this to non-Markovian theories where action effects depend on past situations. Scherl and Levesque extended Reiter's work to knowledge-producing actions but remained Markovian. This paper models a taxonomy of obligations, necessary for domains like smart contracts, using non-Markovian Situation Calculus theories. It introduces the sequential temporal Situation Calculus, non-Markovian control, and a door-opening example. Finally, it summarizes the formalization of the obligation modality using a deontic fluent to represent deontic accessibility.

The TPS7H500x-SP series are radiation-hardness-assured current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. This study examines blockchain education across 533 AACSB-accredited US universities to address the enterprise knowledge gap regarding blockchain implementation. Blockchain integration is a cross-functional endeavor spanning management, supply chain, IT, and law, requiring a mix of technical, social, methodological, and personal competences. 

Researchers identified 151 universities (28%) offering at least one blockchain course. Private universities and those with larger undergraduate populations are more likely to offer these courses, the majority of which are at the undergraduate level. While Computer Science and Information Systems departments host the most courses, offerings also appear in Business, Law, and other diverse fields. 

Course content primarily covers fundamentals, digital assets, and technical development. Furthermore, blockchain education frequently intersects with emerging technologies such as AI and IoT. The study concludes that academic institutions are adopting an interdisciplinary approach to blockchain education. Future research should evaluate how well these curricula align with industry competency demands and track the evolution of these programs over time.

The disclosure describes noninvasive physiological monitors and methods that combine data from multiple optical sensors at different patient measurement sites to generate a single, robust measurement of physiological parameters like oxygen saturation and pulse rate. Unlike conventional monitors that process data from single sites independently, this system feeds raw or minimally processed data from multiple sites into a single signal processor algorithm. Additionally, the sensors can feature multiple photodetectors arranged in a three-dimensional spatial configuration conforming to the patient's anatomy. This configuration provides diverse light path lengths, improves measurement robustness, and offers topology information to confirm correct sensor placement. The system can process data from multiple light emitters and photodetectors across different tissue types, such as the nose and fingertip, to provide a comprehensive assessment of the patient's physiological status.

The device supports three read protocol categories: legacy SPI with single SDO-x, legacy SPI with dual SDO-x, and source-synchronous (SRC). It defaults to SPI-00-S on power-up. Changing protocols requires programming SDI_MODE[1:0] in SDI_CTL_REG and setting SDO_MODE[1:0] = 00b in SDO_CTL_REG. The selected protocol governs both read and write operations. Dual SDO-x mode, enabled by setting SDO1_CONFIG[1:0] to 11b, launches two bits per SCLK edge. Valid write operations require a minimum of 32 SCLKs.

The patent describes a surgical robot arm and wrist design featuring torque sensing. The wrist comprises an articulated terminal portion with multiple revolute joints, including a universal joint, and up to four torque sensors. These sensors measure forces applied to the surgical instrument, enabling force feedback to the surgeon. The arm utilizes a specific sequence of roll and pitch joints to provide high mobility, eliminate kinematic singularities, and mimic human wrist motion while remaining compact. This configuration allows multiple arms to operate closely in confined surgical spaces and enables end effector maneuvering without enlarging the patient's incision.

This book identifies patterns for distributed systems, beginning with single-node container groups. Professor William Green concludes the course with a wrap-up of stochastic methods: Metropolis Monte Carlo, Kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC), and Molecular Dynamics (MD). Multidimensional integrals often use weighting factors like the Boltzmann distribution or Bayesian probability densities. In Metropolis Monte Carlo, selecting an appropriate step size is critical; too large leads to repeated states, and too small results in inadequate sampling. Adaptive step sizing and knowing the expected answer beforehand are recommended to verify results. However, achieving high accuracy requires exponentially more samples due to 1/sqrt(N) scaling. 

KMC is used for non-stationary probability distributions governed by differential equations, such as chemical kinetics on catalytic surfaces. These systems can have an immense number of states (e.g., 4^100), making exact solutions impossible. The Gillespie algorithm uses random numbers to determine event timing and type. Computational tricks include ignoring or slowing fast processes like diffusion, removing very slow processes like coking, and using Poisson distributions for initial conditions. 

MD solves Newton's equations of motion using force fields, often employing the Velocity Verlet algorithm for energy conservation and thermostats for thermal bath interactions. MD is time-accurate but limited to nanosecond timescales due to tiny time steps, making it unsuitable for slow processes or systems with long relaxation times. Green emphasizes that Metropolis MC, KMC, and MD serve different purposes, and researchers must select the appropriate tool for their specific problem. Finally, marginal integrals can simplify problems by integrating out unneeded variables.

In Lewis v. Bayer AG, plaintiffs moved for class certification on behalf of individuals who ingested Baycol, a cholesterol drug withdrawn from the market in 2001 due to severe side effects. Plaintiffs proposed four classes: Class I (Pennsylvania medical monitoring), Class II (nationwide medical monitoring), Class III (nationwide personal injury), and Class IV (Pennsylvania personal injury).

The court evaluated the motion under Pennsylvania Rule of Civil Procedure 1702. It found the numerosity requirement satisfied for all classes but determined that commonality was lacking for Classes II, III, and IV. Nationwide classes (II and III) failed due to conflicts of law among states, and personal injury classes (III and IV) failed due to individualized questions of causation and medical history.

For Class I, the court found that commonality, typicality, adequacy of representation, and fair adjudication requirements were met solely for the medical monitoring claim. The court denied commonality for Class I's unjust enrichment and Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law (UTPCPL) claims due to individualized issues of reliance and injury.

The court granted the motion in part, certifying Class I exclusively for medical monitoring, and denied certification for all other classes and claims.

The lecture compares model-free policy gradient and value function methods in robotics. Policy gradient methods scale well and guarantee convergence but are local and suffer from high variance. Value function methods are data-efficient but struggle with convergence, as small value estimate changes can drastically alter policies. 

To combine their advantages, actor-critic algorithms represent both a policy (actor) and a value function (critic) simultaneously. By updating the policy slower than the value function, these methods achieve strong convergence and reduced variance. 

The professor presents a case study from their thesis involving "Toddler," a passive walking robot modified with ankle actuators. Using an actor-critic algorithm with a linear function approximator, the robot updated its policy once per footstep to achieve a deadbeat controller on its return map. Toddler learned to walk in minutes, adapted to terrain changes, and recovered from a broken ankle. The inclusion of a value function estimate significantly accelerated learning, demonstrating the effectiveness of model-free optimization on real underactuated robotic systems.

This prospective study of 157 patients hospitalized for acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) evaluated bioimpedance spectroscopy (BIS) for predicting clinical outcomes. Wireless communication is complicated by fading, unlike wireline communication which primarily deals with white Gaussian noise. In free space, electromagnetic field strength decreases as 1/r with a propagation delay of r/c. A moving receiver introduces a Doppler shift; a single shift can be tracked and corrected. However, multipath fading occurs when multiple paths with different Doppler shifts interfere, causing rapid signal cancellation that is difficult to track.

Using ray tracing, the received signal is modeled as a sum of attenuated and delayed paths. This makes the wireless channel a linear time-varying filter rather than a linear time-invariant one, meaning standard Fourier transform multiplication does not apply; instead, time-varying convolution is used. At baseband, the channel's time variance is driven by the Doppler spread—the difference between the maximum and minimum Doppler shifts across paths. This Doppler spread determines how long the channel appears time-invariant, dictating how frequently the system must measure and adapt to the channel to maintain communication.

The lecture continues the theme of folding polygons into convex polyhedra, representing them with gluing trees. It discusses combinatorial bounds and algorithms for general, edge-to-edge, and bounded sharpness gluings. General and edge-to-edge gluings have exponential upper and lower bounds (2 to the theta n) on the number of combinatorial types. Bounded sharpness polygons, where reflex angles are at most 360 minus a constant, have polynomial bounds. Finiteness is achieved by treating rolling belts as a single combinatorial type. An exponential upper bound is proven by bounding tree leaves and nodes, while a spiky star polygon demonstrates the lower bound. For bounded sharpness, a constant limit on leaves yields polynomial bounds. Algorithms include dynamic programming for edge-to-edge enumeration in exponential time, and a polynomial time decision algorithm that minimizes glued angles. General gluing enumeration also uses dynamic programming, running in exponential time generally, but polynomial time for bounded sharpness. The lecture concludes with examples of gluings for a Latin cross, yielding 85 gluings and 23 distinct polyhedra, and the rolling belts of triangles and squares.

The passage details interrupt handling and doorbell page configuration for guests and hosts. Guests must execute HLT with interrupts disabled and resume as if receiving a #HV. ASTROCO is a conformer-style encoder for astronomical time series that improves upon transformer models like Astromer by combining global self-attention with local depthwise convolutions and gating mechanisms. Inputs are fused via learned projections, and features are mixed across layers using trainable softmax weights. Using a BERT-style masked-reconstruction strategy, ASTROCO models outperform Astromer v1/v2 on the MACHO R-band dataset, achieving better reconstruction and classification with fewer resources.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU introduces significant architectural advancements for High-Performance Computing (HPC) and AI. A100 Tensor Cores accelerate IEEE-compliant FP64 computations, delivering 2.5x the FP64 performance of the V100. For mixed-precision HPC workloads, TF32 Tensor Cores provide the fastest and most robust results in iterative refinement solvers. A100 also introduces Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity with a 2:4 pattern, doubling compute throughput for deep neural networks by skipping zero values without compromising inferencing accuracy.

The GPU features a combined L1 data cache and shared memory (192 KB/SM), simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution, and a 40 GB HBM2 memory subsystem providing 1555 GB/sec bandwidth. Its 40 MB L2 cache is 6.7x larger than V100, supported by Compute Data Compression and L2 cache residency controls to optimize data fetch efficiency. 

A100 supports Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology, partitioning a single GPU into up to seven isolated instances with dedicated compute and memory resources for multi-tenant environments. It utilizes third-generation NVLink (600 GB/sec total bandwidth) and PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV. Additional hardware features include NVJPG decode, an Optical Flow Accelerator, improved atomics, and five NVDEC units.

CUDA 11 advances include Task Graphs for reduced launch overhead, asynchronous copy operations and barriers for efficient data movement, and Cooperative Groups. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs, delivering 5 PFLOPS of performance, and is supported by a fully optimized software stack via the NGC Private Registry. The passage also includes a primer on sparse neural networks, detailing how fine-grained structured sparsity maintains accuracy while optimizing compute throughput.

This study evaluates the global ranking trends of the top five higher education institutions (HEIs) in ten Asian countries (Bangladesh, China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Pakistan, Philippines, Russia, Thailand, and Vietnam) using the Times Higher Education World University Rankings (THE WUR) from 2015 to 2025. The lecture covers renormalization and logarithm summation in Soft-Collinear Effective Theory (SCET), focusing on the b to s gamma process. Counterterms cancel ultraviolet divergences, including 1/epsilon squared divergences. The anomalous dimension consists of a regular term and a cusp anomalous dimension, the latter arising from a kink in the Wilson line path. Solving the renormalization group equations produces a Sudakov exponential with double logarithms. The lecture details the perturbative information needed for leading, next-to-leading, and next-to-next-to-leading log calculations. Wilson coefficients are typically fixed by external kinematics when operators involve distinct collinear directions. Conversely, operators with fields in the same direction involve loop momenta, leading to integral renormalization group equations such as the DGLAP equation. The lecture then introduces deep inelastic scattering (DIS) in the Breit frame, separating hard and collinear modes. It identifies the effective theory operators that correspond to parton distribution functions (PDFs) and explains how their matrix elements lead to DIS factorization theorems.

The passage discusses the value of patterns in distributed systems development, emphasizing how open source communities highlighted software development as a collaborative endeavor. Patterns offer general blueprints for organizing distributed systems, enabling developers to learn from past mistakes, share a common vocabulary, and build reusable components.

Single-node patterns group tightly coupled containers on one machine to isolate resources, separate concerns, and facilitate team scaling. The sidecar pattern pairs an application container with a secondary container to add functionality like HTTPS, configuration synchronization, or monitoring. The ambassador pattern uses a proxy container to broker interactions between an application and external services, such as sharded databases or service brokers. The adapter pattern standardizes heterogeneous application interfaces for consistent monitoring, logging, and health checks.

Multi-node distributed patterns, such as microservices, rely on loosely coupled components communicating over networks. Replicated load-balanced services use identical, stateless replicas behind a load balancer for redundancy and horizontal scaling, often enhanced with caching and SSL termination layers. Sharded services partition data across multiple replicas to manage large states, improving memory utilization and capacity. These shards can be replicated for resilience and combined with caching to optimize performance and handle high request loads.

The passage describes a method, system, and hardware for configuring a Deep Neural Network (DNN) to efficiently implement activation functions using programmable lookup tables (LUTs). The method involves providing calibration data to a hardware representation, monitoring the input range to an activation module, generating LUT data specific to that determined range, and loading it into the LUT. This optimizes LUT usage by focusing on expected input values rather than the full possible range. The hardware uses interpolation, such as linear or quadratic, to estimate values between LUT entries. For input values outside the determined range, the system can clamp outputs to boundary values or extrapolate using a linear approximation. Additionally, the hardware may include a Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) that can bypass the LUT to reduce power consumption when a ReLU activation function is required. The passage also details a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) hardware architecture comprising convolution engines, accumulators, and shared buffers, as well as integrated circuit manufacturing systems for producing the described hardware.

This study introduces GeoSQL-Eval, an automated evaluation framework, and GeoSQL-Bench, a benchmark of 14,178 tasks, to assess Large Language Models (LLMs) in generating PostGIS queries. The cup and handle pattern is a bullish continuation chart formation introduced by William O'Neil. It consists of a cup—a rounded bottom forming after a price rally—and a handle, a slight downward drift on the cup's right side. A breakout above the handle's resistance signals trend continuation. Volume typically decreases during the cup and handle formations and spikes upon breakout. The pattern's duration varies, and traders often place stop-loss orders below the handle or cup's bottom. Backtests by Ali Akhtari and Thomas Bulkowski show mixed results, with Bulkowski noting a 26% failure rate. The pattern reflects market psychology shifting from pessimism to optimism and is best used alongside other indicators, particularly in low to moderate volatility. An inverted version signals a downtrend continuation. Common trading mistakes include entering prematurely, ignoring volume, and neglecting broader market context.

The lecture introduces the induced graph removal lemma, which allows modifying a graph by adding or removing edges to eliminate induced copies of a subgraph. Standard regularity methods fail here due to irregular pairs. To overcome this, the strong regularity lemma is introduced, producing a pair of partitions where a refinement is extremely regular. A corollary of this lemma yields a partition with no irregular pairs between selected subsets. This corollary is used to prove the induced removal lemma through partition, cleaning, and counting steps. The lecture also covers the infinite removal lemma for infinite pattern sets and connects these concepts to property testing, demonstrating that all hereditary graph properties are testable using oblivious testers.

Higher-order Feynman diagrams with self-energy loops produce infinite amplitudes due to logarithmic divergences, making calculations impossible. This is addressed by introducing a cutoff scale and renormalizing physical masses and couplings into bare values plus corrections. Because experiments occur at specific scales, these infinite corrections do not prevent comparisons with theory. The electromagnetic, weak, and strong couplings "run" or evolve depending on the energy scale. Introducing new particles alters this running behavior, potentially unifying these interactions at a high energy scale. Ultimately, observed masses and couplings are evaluated at specific scales and run as a function of that scale.

NeoWorld is a deep learning framework for interactive world generation from a single image. It uses a hybrid object-centric scene structure that represents backgrounds as lightweight 2.5D Gaussian layers and progressively unfolds foreground objects into full 3D models based on user interaction or prompts. The system employs panoptic segmentation and a compact codebook for efficient object-centric attribute binding, ensuring cross-scene alignment. It integrates Large Language Models to interpret user commands for object manipulation and animation. Experiments demonstrate that NeoWorld outperforms prior 2D and 2.5D methods in 3D consistency, text-to-scene alignment, and user engagement. Limitations include its cascaded module architecture, which can propagate upstream errors related to alignment, LLM interpretation, 3D reconstruction, and segmentation.
