The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system featuring an analog front-end with input clamp protection, programmable gain amplifiers (PGA), and wide-common-mode voltage rejection circuits. It supports configurable analog input ranges, bandwidths, and output data formats. The device uses a source-synchronous data interface supporting 2-lane or 4-lane modes with SDR or DDR, and includes a data output randomizer to minimize ground bounce. Additional features include simple and moving data averaging, test patterns for debugging, and a speed-boost mode for up to 8MSPS on a selected channel pair. Configuration is managed via SPI or daisy-chain SPI, with multiple register banks for settings like input range, common-mode control, and power-down. The ADC requires a free-running sampling clock and supports synchronization across multiple devices using the SMPL_SYNC signal. It features an internal precision voltage reference with the option for an external reference. Application examples include automated test equipment (ATE), with guidelines provided for power supply decoupling and PCB layout.

Senator Sherwin Gatchalian urged the Department of Education to resolve delays in public school teachers' bonuses, unpaid since 2016-2017. DepEd blamed failed biddings and clearance issues, while teachers noted funding was already allocated. Gatchalian urged streamlining clearance processing.

Tuberculosis (TB) is a major infectious disease, and extrapulmonary TB (EPTB) affects organs outside the lungs. EPTB is treated with the same four first-line drugs as pulmonary TB, but its treatment is less studied. Existing physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models do not simulate all four drugs or include major EPTB sites. The authors developed a whole-body PBPK model incorporating pleura and lymph node compartments to simulate the temporal distribution of rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol. Calibrated and validated with plasma and lung data, the model predicts drug concentrations at EPTB sites. Predictions show rifampicin and isoniazid generally exceed critical concentrations, whereas ethambutol and pyrazinamide often fall below them in certain tissues. Despite limitations, such as assuming no drug-drug interactions and a single lymph node compartment, this model serves as a starting point for evaluating and optimizing EPTB treatment regimens.

On February 2, 2015, Apple Inc. entered an underwriting agreement with Goldman, Sachs & Co. and Deutsche Bank Securities Inc. to issue and sell senior unsecured notes. These include $500 million of Floating Rate Notes due 2020, $1.25 billion of 1.55% Notes due 2020, $1.25 billion of 2.15% Notes due 2022, $1.5 billion of 2.50% Notes due 2025, and $2 billion of 3.45% Notes due 2045. Issued under a 2013 indenture with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A., the notes rank equally with Apple's other unsecured debt. Floating Rate Note interest is paid quarterly, and Fixed Rate Note interest is paid semi-annually.

Microsoft Corporation filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2017. The company reported total revenue of $24.5 billion, an increase from $21.9 billion in the prior year, and net income of $6.6 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $0.84. Microsoft operates through three segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing, which generated $8.2 billion, $6.9 billion, and $9.4 billion in revenue, respectively. Total commercial cloud revenue reached $5.0 billion. Total assets stood at $249.1 billion, with net cash from operations of $12.4 billion. The company early adopted new accounting standards for revenue recognition and leases, which materially impacted its balance sheet and required the restatement of prior periods. The LinkedIn acquisition, completed in December 2016 for $27.0 billion, is included in the financial results. A $40.0 billion share repurchase program was approved in September 2016, with $35.2 billion remaining as of September 30, 2017. A quarterly dividend of $0.42 per share was declared.

The K-T collaborative EVT registry integrates data from 9,941 endovascular thrombectomy (EVT)-treated acute ischemic stroke patients from South Korea (CRCS-K) and Taiwan (TREAT-AIS) to study real-world outcomes and the impact of age. Taiwanese patients were older, had more vascular risk factors, more severe strokes, and longer treatment times, correlating with lower functional recovery. Conversely, 90-day mortality was higher in the Korean cohort. Age strongly influenced EVT outcomes; patients aged 80 and older experienced worse functional recovery, higher mortality, and lower successful recanalization rates, with the most pronounced effects between 75 and 85 years. Symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage risk remained similar across age groups. Despite worse outcomes in the elderly, a subset achieved favorable results, indicating age alone should not exclude patients from EVT. The study highlights the value of multinational registries in identifying regional variations to refine stroke care, while noting limitations such as differing data collection methods and missing imaging data.
GBMC neonatologist Dr. Maria Pane includes parents in care rounds to support families. She values teamwork and supports the Father’s Day 5K NICU fundraiser.

The Federal Reserve raised the federal funds rate by 0.25 points to a 1 to 1.25 percent target. This second hike in half a year is the third since Chair Janet Yellen ended the flatline policy after the 2007 crisis.

Amazon's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2022, reports a 7% increase in net sales to $121.2 billion and a net loss of $2.0 billion, largely due to a $3.9 billion loss from its Rivian investment. Operating income decreased to $3.3 billion. AWS sales grew 33% to $19.7 billion, while the North America and International segments reported operating losses. During the first six months of 2022, Amazon acquired MGM Holdings for $6.1 billion, repurchased $6.0 billion of common stock, and extended the estimated useful lives of its servers and networking equipment, which reduced depreciation expense. Total cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities were $60.7 billion as of June 30, 2022.

The lecture introduces Probabilistically Checkable Proofs (PCPs), which allow a verifier to check a proof by querying only a few random locations. PCPs are defined as a complexity class with parameters for completeness, soundness, randomness, and queries. The instructor constructs a PCP with polylogarithmic query and randomness complexity for NP languages using the GKR protocol. This involves computing low-degree extensions for each layer of a verification circuit and placing all possible sumcheck prover messages into an oracle. The verifier simulates the GKR protocol by querying this oracle. Soundness relies on the sumcheck protocol's soundness, a union bound, and a low-degree test for the input layer. The lecture also mentions a transition to cryptography and computational soundness.

A Stephens County jury convicted Robert Pearl Bryson of aggravated sodomy, aggravated child molestation, child molestation, and failure to register as a sex offender. On appeal, Bryson challenged the sufficiency of the evidence, several trial court rulings, and claimed ineffective assistance of counsel. The appellate court affirmed the convictions, finding the evidence sufficient based on victim testimonies and Bryson's year-long absence from the state without notifying authorities. The court found no error in denying his motions to quash, withdraw counsel, and sever charges, noting the offenses were connected and withdrawal would delay trial. The court also ruled Bryson's no contest plea was properly admitted to establish a prior conviction for sex offender registration requirements. Finally, the court held Bryson waived his ineffective assistance claim by not raising it at his first post-conviction opportunity.

This study investigates the impact of mydriasis on image gradability and AI-based diabetic retinopathy (DR) screening using a portable fundus camera. Analyzing 327 patients, researchers found mydriatic images had a significantly higher gradability rate (82.1%) than non-mydriatic images (55.6%). In non-mydriatic images, systemic hypertension, older age, longer diabetes duration, male gender, and Indigenous race were associated with lower image quality. An AI model (ResNet-200d) achieved higher accuracy (82.91% vs. 79.23%) and fewer false positives with mydriatic images, though the difference was not statistically significant. The findings suggest mydriasis improves image quality and AI precision, potentially reducing unnecessary referrals in resource-limited settings. However, non-mydriatic imaging remains necessary where dilation is unfeasible. Limitations include operator experience, selection bias, and reliance on a single dataset and camera model.

The paper introduces Flash Fused Distributed Primitives (FFDP), a framework to scale image registration to ultra-high resolutions across multiple GPUs. It identifies key bottlenecks in image registration—grid sampling, cross-correlation, and mutual information—and proposes fused CUDA kernels to reduce memory usage on a single GPU. For multi-GPU scaling, FFDP introduces Grid Parallel for boundary-synchronized image sharding and a distributed ring sampler. Experiments show FFDP accelerates traditional registration pipelines by up to 7.48x with 59% less memory, and deep learning pipelines by up to 6.14x with 24% less memory. The framework successfully registered a 250µm in-vivo MRI to a 100µm ex-vivo human brain volume with over 11.8B parameters in one minute using 8 GPUs. On a simulated 250µm dataset, the method improved accuracy at higher resolutions and required up to 500x fewer GPU-hours than alternative methods.

This paper investigates the relationship between Artificial Intelligence (AI), Big Data (BD), and Advanced Analytics (AA) within digital business platforms. As digital transformation accelerates, enterprises must leverage BD and AA to enhance AI-driven decision-making and maintain competitive advantages. The author develops a multidimensional data-driven AI innovation taxonomy framework and an AI/BD/AA micro-level value chain, which includes data acquisition, curation, storage, and usage. 

Using a methodology based on literature reviews and expert interviews, the research identifies seven overlapping technological platform areas that support digital business. The study introduces a five-level AI maturity framework—ranging from human-led initial analytics to machine-controlled advanced analytics—to evaluate human-machine relationships and automation maturity. This framework assists organizations in identifying industry use cases, communicating AI value, and managing the innovation potential of data-driven AI business models. The research provides a strategic tool for managers and investors to evaluate AI innovation, while emphasizing the importance of ethical norms in AI development.

Ulysses S. Gandy appealed his second manslaughter conviction and ten-year sentence for a 1976 collision that killed three people. Gandy assigned four errors: the verdict was against the evidence's weight, the court refused Instruction D-13, the court admitted State's Exhibits 1, 5, and 7, and the jury received no food recess during deliberations. 

Witness testimony conflicted regarding the vehicles' post-collision positions and Gandy's intoxication. While a few witnesses detected no alcohol, nine testified Gandy was highly intoxicated. The Mississippi Supreme Court found sufficient evidence for the jury to determine Gandy was intoxicated and in the wrong lane, constituting culpable negligence. The Court found no reversible error in refusing Instruction D-13, as other instructions properly covered intoxication. It also upheld the admission of the exhibits, noting they illustrated the scene as personally observed by witnesses, not as a reconstruction of the impact. Lastly, the Court found no merit in the jury recess claim since jurors could have requested a break. The trial court's judgment was affirmed.

This document is a specification update for the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3, detailing multiple hardware errata, their implications, and resolutions. Documented issues include SSMI synchronization failures with simultaneous IRQs, UDMA failures when the bus master is enabled before PIO command packets, and wake event inputs not functioning from the ACPI S3 state. Other errata cover incorrect RTC CMOS RAM accesses, I/O failures to LPC devices during block and demand mode legacy DMA, and USB controller register read failures when clock gating is enabled. The document also notes ATAC hangs with WORD-aligned PRD addresses, LPC aborts on specific SYNC patterns, and incorrect NEGACK status bit behavior in the SMB controller. Additional issues involve a GLPCI retry counter that does not distinguish between accesses, GPIO High Bank register write failures after suspend, insufficient SMBus hold time, missing LOWBAT_FLAG after abnormal standby, and Sleep_X signal deassertion failures. Resolutions provided include using alternative transfer modes, applying specific programming workarounds, or utilizing external circuitry, though some issues currently have no resolution.

The speaker accepts the presidential nomination, contrasting their party's vision of hope, growth, and individualism with the opponents' record of pessimism, high taxes, inflation, and deficits. The speaker highlights their administration's achievements, including economic growth, job creation, tax cuts, and military restoration, while criticizing the opponents' past economic policies and current legislative obstructionism. They advocate for a balanced budget amendment, a line-item veto, tuition tax credits, enterprise zones, and nuclear arms reduction. The speech concludes by celebrating American values, diversity, and the enduring promise of freedom, symbolized by the Olympic torch and the Statue of Liberty.

The study proposes a meta-population model to quantify how Google Community Mobility Reports (GCMR) explain SARS-CoV-2 transmission dynamics. The model links GCMR data from four settings (retail and recreation, grocery and pharmacy, transit stations, and workplaces) to contact frequencies, while accounting for seasonality, virus variants (Alpha and Delta), and vaccination. Applied to regions in Norway, Sweden, and Germany, the model found that GCMR settings explained 39% of infections in Norway, 60% in Sweden, and around 65% in Germany. Transit stations and workplaces were the most important transmission settings in Norway and Sweden, whereas retail and recreation was most important in Germany. A 20°C temperature increase reduced transmissibility by approximately 40%, and the Delta variant doubled transmissibility compared to the wildtype. The model assumes a linear relationship between GCMR activity and transmission-relevant contacts, alongside constant multiplicative effects for seasonality and variants across all settings.

Texas Instruments cautions that integrated circuits can be damaged by electrostatic discharge (ESD) without proper handling. The revision history notes the ADS8685W and ADS8689W changed to Production Data status. Section 11 provides mechanical, packaging, and orderable information, including details on part status, RoHS, and markings. TI disclaims all warranties for its resources, limits its liability to the annual purchase price, and assigns users full responsibility for validating their applications.

California's energy crisis involved high prices from diverse suppliers, including public entities, not solely the Texas firms criticized by Gov. Davis. FERC-mediated talks between California and power generators failed; a judge will recommend a refund plan of up to $1 billion, below California's $8.9 billion demand. A Senate committee accused Duke Energy of withholding price-bidding data for a price-gouging probe, though Duke claims compliance. Separately, a judge ruled California's attorney general can share subpoenaed documents from Reliant, Mirant, and Dynegy with Oregon and Washington for a price-collusion investigation.

In India, Enron's Dabhol Power Co. CEO Neil McGregor resigned. Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay met with Indian officials to resolve a payment dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB), which defaulted and stopped buying power. Phase II construction is halted at 85% completion. Lay stated Enron has no immediate plans to quit India.

Additionally, Enron Broadband Services invested in Tropic Networks' $60-million financing. Despite a 43% stock drop and challenges in California and India, analysts rated Enron a "buy." Independent power producers were expected to meet Q2 earnings targets, bolstered by April and May electricity prices.

EUR/USD is rising for a fourth session amid a directionless dollar and US inflation data. Markets await ECB and FOMC minutes. Resistance is at 1.1846, 1.1894, and 1.1911; support at 1.1722, 1.1687, and 1.1611.

Grief is a unique, personal emotional reaction to loss, including the death of a loved one, life changes, declining health, or moving homes. Anticipatory grief can occur before an impending loss, such as a terminal illness. Relocating can trigger grief due to lost memories and support networks; delaying major moves post-bereavement is recommended. Grief does not follow sequential stages but fluctuates based on life experience, circumstances, and personality. Common reactions include numbness, denial, acceptance, yearning, repeating the event, restlessness, loss of confidence, guilt, anger, and profound sadness. While grief's duration varies and the deceased is always missed, the intense period eventually lessens. Individuals are encouraged to seek support from friends, family, GPs, or specialist organizations.

The Patriots had a historically poor offensive performance against the Dolphins but trailed by only seven points in the final minute. Stephen Gostkowski's unsuccessful onside kick attempt was described as bizarre, and the Dolphins recovered to win the game.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system featuring a built-in analog front-end. It supports simple and moving data averaging to improve SNR and provides test patterns (fixed, digital ramp, alternating) for debugging. The device can be reset or powered down via hardware pins or register writes, followed by an initialization sequence requiring a free-running sampling clock. A speed-boost mode allows up to 8MSPS for a selected channel pair. Configuration is managed through SPI or daisy-chain SPI across three register banks. Targeted at ATE applications, the device achieves low total-unadjusted-error post-calibration and offers selectable bandwidth modes for multiplexed signals. The document also outlines power supply decoupling, board layout guidelines, register maps, and packaging information.

Researchers led by Joshua Caldwell improved hyperlensing by using isotopically purified hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). By using 99 percent isotopically pure boron, they reduced optical losses and tripled polariton lifetime, enhancing imaging resolution by a factor of ten. This allows lenses to potentially resolve objects as small as 30 nanometers. Unlike existing nanoscale microscopes, hyperlenses use low-energy infrared light to safely image living cells in their natural environments and provide spectroscopic data. Researchers project further improvements using larger crystals.

To beat the soccer offside trap, attackers must recognize when defenders move up instead of retreating, avoid offside positions, and exploit the space behind. Effective tactics include dribbling through, executing timed through passes, making horizontal, checking, deep-lying, bending, or delayed runs, passing short or back, delaying for time, and using a designated "non-runner." Recognizing failed traps is also crucial. Successfully beating the trap leaves the striker one-on-one with the goalkeeper and often discourages opponents from using it again.

Researchers found that periwinkle sea snails adapt to predicted future ocean acidification by producing less-dense, less-soluble shells. This suggests periwinkles and potentially other calcifying organisms may adapt to acidifying oceans.
In People v. Roldán, the judgment was reversed and the defendant acquitted based on case No. 2037, which shared the same issue and evidence, differing only in loan amount.

China blacklisted Canadian firm TechInsights and nine subsidiaries, banning them from Chinese business for endangering national security. This followed TechInsights publishing an analysis of Huawei's AI chips and a report suggesting their processors contained international components. The restrictions prohibit Chinese entities from collaborating with TechInsights. Analysts state the ban highlights China's tightening control over tech information and the growing fragility of international technology research collaboration amid geopolitical competition.

Barron's argues Netflix's stock could lose over half its value due to competition from Disney and Facebook, cash-burning practices, and unconventional accounting. The passage counters this bearish outlook by asserting that competition fears are overblown given Netflix's past growth despite Amazon and YouTube, the company has demonstrated pricing flexibility without losing subscribers, and its 104 million subscriber base provides a strong competitive moat. It concludes that betting against Netflix is risky.

A 1990-2015 study found that window blinds cause frequent injuries and deaths in young children, primarily through cord entanglement. While most injuries were minor, entanglement caused nearly 80% of hospitalizations and over 94% of deaths, often occurring at home when children were briefly unsupervised. Researchers and safety advocates argue that voluntary standards and parental supervision are insufficient, advocating instead for mandatory standards requiring inaccessible or unexposed cords. While a mandatory federal rule remains in early stages, the Window Covering Manufacturers Association proposed a voluntary standard requiring stock products to be cordless or have inaccessible cords by late 2018. Advocates emphasize that completely removing accessible cords is the only effective way to protect children.

26-year-old Ryan Kerr was remanded in custody after admitting to several attacks, including punching a woman and leaving a man unconscious. Kerr has prior assault convictions and showed no remorse. His defense requested psychiatric reports for rehabilitation, and Judge Ticehurst will sentence him on October 13.

Peterborough City Council pledged £4 million for homeless families and brought 179 empty homes back into use last year. The council published Phase Two budget proposals as government grants have been cut by 80% over eight years due to outdated population figures. Residents are urged to join the "Stand Up For Peterborough" campaign against future funding shortfalls. Additionally, Public Space Protection Orders introduced six months ago have reduced littering and unauthorised cycling, and a new mental health service, CHUMS, launched to support children and young people.

Chef Shannon Bard and her husband Tom permanently closed their Portland restaurant, Zapoteca, to spend more time with their five children. They continue to own their other restaurants, Toroso and Salud, plus a catering company. Bard is a cookbook author known for television appearances.

This COVID-19 study evaluated convalescent plasma plus best supportive care versus supportive care alone. Conducted under ethical guidelines with IEC approval and informed consent, the study hypothesized that early, high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma would reduce the need for mechanical ventilation. The primary objective assessed clinical efficacy and safety, while the secondary objective compared convalescent plasma to standard of care regarding clinical severity, oxygenation, ventilation, and hospitalization.

The NAAIM Exposure Index, compiled by the National Association of Active Investment Managers, measures members' average exposure to US Equity markets through a weekly survey. Displayed as a two-week moving average, it estimates investor sentiment, where high readings indicate bullishness and low readings indicate bearishness. Although used as a contrarian indicator, the index is not predictive of future market movements. Backtests revealed poor performance, concluding it is not a worthwhile contrarian trading strategy compared to alternatives like the VIX.

Driven by increased demand, Lubrizol Corp. is investing US$80 million to expand its thermoplastics polyurethane (TPU) production capacity across North America, Europe, and Asia. The Ohio-based company operates in 17 countries, employs 8,300 people, and reported US$6.5 billion in 2016 revenues.

Jeff Horn defends his WBO welterweight title against Gary Corcoran in Brisbane. Horn aims to validate his disputed victory over Manny Pacquiao, with promoter Bob Arum noting a win could lead to major 2018 fights against Terence Crawford or Pacquiao. Corcoran, the underdog fighting outside Britain for the first time, expects an aggressive bout. The buildup included accusations from Corcoran's camp about Horn head-butting and claims of biting, but both fighters made weight and are prepared.

President Trump announced a deal with Pfizer to lower drug prices for Medicaid and patients, with new medicines launched at parity with other countries. In exchange, Pfizer avoids certain import tariffs by continuing to invest in U.S. manufacturing. Policy experts are skeptical about the deal's impact on affordability, noting Medicaid enrollees already pay little and drugmakers are legally required to offer Medicaid the lowest U.S. prices. Separately, Sanofi is being investigated by the European Commission for potential anticompetitive activity.

Manchester City plays Burnley at the Etihad Stadium on Jan. 2 at 10:00 AM ET, streaming on NBC. City manager Pep Guardiola needs a win to keep pace with Chelsea and welcomes back striker Sergio Aguero. Burnley, led by Sean Dyche, seeks points to avoid relegation but struggles away. City aims for an early goal against the physical Burnley side, whose main threats are Andre Gray and Sam Vokes.

This preprint study investigated neural noise in Tourette syndrome (TS) by measuring trial-by-trial EEG variability in response to median nerve stimulation in 19 adults with TS and 19 healthy controls. Results indicated that early and mid-latency somatosensory evoked potential (SEP) components were largely similar between groups, though the P100 component was significantly increased in TS and correlated with tic severity. The TS group exhibited greater trial-by-trial variability at rest and flatter 1/f noise slopes at high-beta and gamma frequencies, indicating increased neural noise. However, variability decreased comparably in both groups following stimulation. The findings suggest that sensorimotor neural recruitment is less stable at rest in individuals with TS but normalizes in response to sensory input.

Facebook published a detailed, 8,000-word rule book of its community standards to increase transparency and address criticism regarding content moderation. For the first time, users can appeal the removal of individual pieces of content and receive specific reasons for takedowns. The rules, enforced by 7,500 moderators and automated software, cover topics like drug use, bullying, and violence, and are updated biweekly based on expert feedback. The standards do not cover government requests regarding local laws, false information, or personal data use.

On June 20, 2017, Apple Inc. issued and sold $1,000,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 3.000% Notes due 2027. The issuance was pursuant to a June 13, 2017 underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, and Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith Incorporated. The senior unsecured notes pay semi-annual interest on June 20 and December 20, starting December 20, 2017, and mature on June 20, 2027. Apple's Form 8-K filing includes the Underwriting Agreement, Officer's Certificate, Form of Global Note, legal opinion, and consent as exhibits.

A federal jury cleared retired Little Rock police lieutenant David Hudson of excessive force accusations for punching Jon "Chris" Erwin seven times outside a restaurant in 2011. The jury ruled the force was reasonable. Hudson testified he punched Erwin to gain compliance after Erwin became agitated, touched the officer, and refused arrest orders while being removed for crashing a private party. Witnesses testified Erwin appeared intoxicated, though Erwin denied resisting and stated his goal was to expose bad policing. The city and restaurant had settled with Erwin before the trial, meaning Hudson would have paid any damages personally. Misdemeanor charges against Erwin were previously dropped.

Finland is increasingly irritated by German troops but remains dependent on Germany for military supplies and food. German influence suppresses Finnish press freedom. War weariness is growing, evidenced by trade union petitions regarding food maldistribution and a widening Socialist-Conservative schism. Common citizens question holding distant Soviet Karelia. Separately, a US official warned Finnish representative Toivola that Finnish press attacks on the US and censorship of US communications risk alienating American and British support. Toivola acknowledged the danger, noting the Finnish press cannot criticize Germany due to food dependence, and agreed that attacks on the US were likely German-inspired and should be curbed.

The passage is an email forwarding a Texas Monthly article titled "How Enron Blew It." The article details Enron's transformation from a traditional pipeline company into a massive trading colossus under Jeff Skilling, who fostered a culture of aggressive, highly rewarded risk-takers. Enron expanded into electricity, broadband, and other commodities using aggressive accounting practices. 

By 2001, the company faced multiple crises: public blame for California's energy crisis, a troubled power plant in India, and the failure of its telecommunications ventures. As Wall Street analysts questioned its accounting, Enron's stock dropped significantly. After only six months as CEO, Skilling abruptly resigned, citing personal sacrifices and a desire for family time. Ken Lay returned as CEO, promising a return to core businesses and a softer corporate culture. Meanwhile, Skilling planned to pursue new technology ventures in Houston, noting his net worth remained tied to Enron stock.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2018. Net sales increased 43% to $51.0 billion, and net income rose to $1.6 billion, compared to $724 million in Q1 2017. Operating income grew to $1.9 billion from $1.0 billion. 

By segment, North America sales increased 46% to $30.7 billion, International sales grew 34% to $14.9 billion, and AWS sales increased 49% to $5.4 billion. Operating income increased in North America and AWS, while the International segment's operating loss widened.

Cash used in operating activities was $1.8 billion for the quarter. Total cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities were $25.0 billion as of March 31, 2018. The company adopted new revenue recognition guidance on January 1, 2018, increasing retained earnings by approximately $650 million. On April 12, 2018, Amazon acquired Ring Inc. for approximately $900 million, net of cash acquired. The company also recorded a provisional tax benefit of approximately $789 million related to the 2017 Tax Act.

Frequent penalty calls have disrupted the series' flow, making it difficult for either team to establish its style of play or assess momentum. The team must improve its quickness, particularly in moving the puck through the neutral zone and from the defense. This work surveys ontologies and ontology design patterns (ODPs) for process modeling in Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) to address interoperability and reuse challenges. The authors define three core requirements—process structure, data and resources, and project goals and participant roles—and manually extract ODPs from ontologies including PMDcore, GPO, WILD, P-PLAN, and Metadata4Ing. A baseline automated method using semantic similarity and the ROBOT framework is proposed to extract these patterns. Evaluation results indicate P-PLAN achieved the highest scores for Process and Resource ODPs, while PMDcore supported all three ODP categories. Limitations include biases from annotation quality and independent ontology processing. Future work will expand to additional MSE subdomains, integrate ontology mappings, and develop a pattern-publishing platform.

FSU linebacker Ethan Pritchard was released from the hospital nearly six weeks after being shot in the back of the head in a case of mistaken identity. He is alert, responsive, and has been transferred to a rehabilitation facility in Jacksonville. Four people were arrested in connection with the shooting. Pritchard's father expressed gratitude for the support from FSU coach Mike Norvell, medical staff, and law enforcement as his son begins a long recovery.

Old Forge High School students held a Math-a-thon, raising $3,864 for St. Jude’s Research Hospital. Rosemarie Corigliano was installed as president of the Wayne Memorial Hospital Auxiliary for a two-year term, with two upcoming fundraisers planned. In July 2021, Public Health Wales investigated a Salmonella outbreak linked to an Eid al-Adha barbecue in Cardiff, UK. A cohort study of attendees identified a traditional raw liver dish, ‘marrara’, as the likely infection vehicle. Whole genome sequencing confirmed identical Salmonella Typhimurium strains in human and food samples from local butchers. The investigation highlighted the importance of culturally sensitive food safety messaging and considering traditional dishes in future outbreak investigations.

GoDaddy is dropping neo-Nazi website The Daily Stormer as a domain host after its publisher mocked Heather Heyer, a victim of the Charlottesville attack. GoDaddy stated the article could incite violence, violating its terms. The site claimed it was hacked, though contributor Andrew Auernheimer called it a prank and noted they have backup domains. Publisher Andrew Anglin is trying to regain site control. The site is known for Nazi themes and orchestrating harassment campaigns. It has faced previous bans from PayPal and an advertiser. A Montana woman sued Anglin over a trolling campaign, prompting supporters to crowdfund over $152,000 for his legal defense.

An appeals court ruled the federal government cannot stop interstate trade of giant exotic snakes within the continental U.S. The U.S. Association of Reptile Keepers sued to overturn a ban on transporting these snakes across state lines, which was implemented to protect native wildlife from invasive predators. The court found the Lacey Act only restricts trade between the continental U.S. and territories, not within the 49 contiguous states. The ruling does not lift import bans or affect state laws. The government is reviewing the decision.

The passage warns that loosening family ties and declining birth rates threaten national survival. It urges Congress to pass legislation encouraging American shipping, or at least establish fast mail lines to South America, to prevent American businesses from being disadvantaged. Finally, it highlights defects in current currency laws that cause fluctuating interest rates and harm commerce during crop seasons. The Coppock Curve Strategy, created by E.S.C. Coppock in 1965, is a long-term momentum indicator used to identify significant stock market swings. The strategy triggers a long entry when the curve crosses above zero and an exit when it crosses below. Backtesting on a monthly S&P 500 chart since 1960 resulted in 12 trades, all profitable. The strategy reduces drawdowns, decreases market exposure, and achieves a higher risk-adjusted return than a buy-and-hold approach.

This pushes the efficient frontier northwest, attracting capital away from brown buildings, which suffer from negative externalities like penalties and higher risk premiums.

On the debt side, climate risk increases mortgage default risk as property values decline below loan amounts. This creates a dilemma for government-backed entities like Fannie Mae between accurately pricing climate risk and maintaining social equity. Conversely, green mortgages offer better terms for energy-efficient homes. Banks favor these because green buildings have higher values, improving loan-to-value ratios, and lower energy bills free up household income, reducing default risk by up to one-third. This logic also supports lending more upfront for green renovations based on expected property appreciation. Finally, private equity firms incorporate ESG into their investment memos and due diligence, aligning social value with higher business returns.

This work introduces a theoretical and empirical framework for information design that integrates classic Bayesian persuasion with behavioral framing effects, utilizing Large Language Models (LLMs). While traditional models focus on quantitative signal correlations, the authors address how natural language and non-textual cues influence decision-making. They propose a formal model where a sender optimizes a framing strategy and a recommendation scheme to influence a receiver's belief. The framework defines three optimization variants: recommendation-only, framing-only, and joint framing and recommendation. Theoretical results indicate that framing-only optimization is NP-hard and highly sensitive to errors in the belief oracle. In contrast, jointly optimizing framing and recommendation yields a continuous utility function that is robust to errors and admits a quasi-polynomial-time approximation scheme (QPTAS). Empirically, the authors implement a practical hill-climbing approach for joint optimization, using LLMs to generate framings and map them to beliefs. Case studies and human evaluations demonstrate the method's efficacy. Overall, the work establishes a systematic, algorithmically driven approach to persuasive communication, highlighting the tractability of joint optimization over framing-only approaches.

The passage details various container and distributed system design patterns. The adapter pattern modifies application container interfaces to ensure consistency in monitoring, logging, and health checks, promoting modularity and reuse. The text then transitions to multi-node patterns, starting with microservices, which decouple application functions into separate services communicating via APIs to improve reliability, agility, and scaling. 

Replicated load-balanced services use multiple identical replicas behind a load balancer to provide redundancy and scale for stateless applications. This pattern can be enhanced with readiness probes, session tracking, caching layers, rate limiting, and SSL termination. Sharded services partition data across multiple replicas, where each shard handles a specific subset of requests, enabling stateful services to scale beyond a single machine's capacity. Sharding relies on consistent hashing functions to distribute load evenly and minimize disruption during scaling.

The scatter/gather pattern achieves parallelism by distributing a request to all leaf nodes simultaneously, which process the data and return partial results to a root node for aggregation. This pattern is useful for parallel processing but faces challenges like overhead and the straggler problem, requiring replication for reliability. Finally, the passage covers Functions as a Service (FaaS) and event-driven processing. FaaS simplifies deployment and scales automatically but introduces challenges in debugging, background processing, and memory retention. Patterns for FaaS include the decorator pattern for transforming requests or responses and event-based pipelines for handling asynchronous tasks like two-factor authentication.

This study investigates high-energy (1 MeV) electron beam irradiation as a controlled method for defect engineering in monolayer MoS2. By varying irradiation time, researchers analyzed the resulting modifications using Raman, photoluminescence (PL), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM), and first-principles calculations. 

Irradiation induced sulfur vacancies and subsequent oxygen incorporation, leading to the emergence of Mo5+ and Mo6+ oxidation states. KPFM revealed an increased work function, indicating p-type doping. PL spectroscopy showed quenching of the A exciton and enhancement of defect-bound emissions, which exhibited strong electron-phonon coupling. Circular polarization-resolved PL measurements demonstrated that increasing defect density reduced valley polarization from 62% to 38% due to defect-mediated intervalley scattering. First-principles calculations corroborated these findings, showing that oxygen interactions at sulfur vacancy sites create acceptor-like states near the valence band. The research establishes high-energy electron beams as an effective approach for tuning the optical and electronic properties of MoS2.

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC with an integrated AFE and precision reference. It operates in ACQ (acquisition) and CONV (conversion) states, transitioning via the CONVST/CS signal, and supports low-power NAP and Power-Down modes. The device uses a multiSPI interface supporting legacy SPI and source-synchronous protocols for data transfer, with options for single or dual SDO-x. Data transfer frames are initiated by pulling CONVST/CS low, requiring 32 SCLKs for optimal read/write operations. Nine configuration registers control device ID, reset/power, SDI/SDO protocols, data output flags, input ranges, and alarm thresholds. Application examples include industrial analog input modules for PLCs, utilizing programmable input alarms with hysteresis for temperature sensing. Power supply decoupling and specific PCB layout guidelines are provided to optimize performance and reduce noise.

Characterized using a swept-ring-down method at 780 nm, the microcavities demonstrate a maximum finesse of 0.89 × 10^6 and a quality factor of 2.3 × 10^9. The performance is limited by transmission, scattering, and absorption losses. The fabrication method also enables the creation of compact, manually assembled cavity systems as small as 2 mm³, which are suitable for fiber integration and compact laser applications. These microcavities are ideal candidates for quantum networking, high-precision sensing, and classical optical applications due to their small mode volumes, moderate radii of curvature, and robust performance.

The passage discloses techniques for enhancing trick-play modes (fast-forward and rewind) in streamed video. To overcome issues like buffering pauses and low-quality thumbnails in existing systems, a streaming client maintains a normal buffer window for continuous playback and a trick-play window. The trick-play window stores only a subset of selected video frames, such as key frames, from portions outside the normal buffer, omitting intervening frames. 

Using metadata and indexes, the client requests specific individual frames from a streaming server or proxy server without downloading entire video segments. A proxy server may generate necessary metadata, indexes, or proxy streams if the origin server lacks these features. The video player uses these sparsely buffered frames to emulate faster-than-real-time playback by adjusting display timing and frame selection. Furthermore, the system adaptively selects streams of varying bitrates based on performance metrics to optimize the trick-play experience, ensuring smooth playback with low latency and high quality.

At 51.3 GPa, zircon transformed to textured reidite with some relict zircon near fractures. Spectroscopic analysis revealed that the 51.3 GPa sample exhibited blue cathodoluminescence, increased REE3+ line intensity, and bright yellow speckles confined to planar defects, indicating REE3+ segregation. This trace element segregation occurred rapidly without prolonged annealing, likely due to the reconstructive mechanism of the phase transition causing local charge imbalances that expel trivalent trace elements into interstitial positions, promoting rapid diffusion along planar defects. The patent application details improvements for ladar (laser radar/lidar) computer vision systems, particularly for autonomous vehicles, to overcome the high cost, size, and power limitations of conventional systems. The inventors disclose three primary techniques to optimize scanning ladar transmitters. First, an optical field splitter/inverter (e.g., a W-shaped reflector or triangular prism) is positioned downstream from scanning mirrors to split and invert the scan pattern. This shifts the fast portion of the scan to the edges and the slow portion to the center, increasing gaze time on central regions of interest, and can be configured for overlapping coverage. Second, an induced periodic phase drift is applied to Lissajous scan patterns by driving scanning mirrors slightly off resonance. Optimized using a total least squares approach, this drift reduces scan gaps and blindspots in targeted regions without reducing revisit times. Third, a compact beam scanner assembly employs an ellipsoidal conjugate reflector (ECR) reimaging mirror positioned between two scannable mirrors. This reimages the beam spot onto the second mirror, allowing both mirrors to be smaller and equally sized, thereby reducing the form factor and increasing scan speed and field of view. A coplanar angle constraint ensures the reflected ray fan remains planar, eliminating field distortions.

The NVIDIA Ampere GA10x architecture delivers significant performance enhancements over the prior Turing generation. The passage describes methods, systems, and devices for small data transmission (SDT) using Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) in New Radio (NR) networks. It addresses the inefficiency of LTE's Radio Resource Control (RRC) connection establishment for small data by enabling User Equipment (UE) to transmit small data via a configured grant Physical Uplink Shared Channel (PUSCH) while remaining in an RRC-IDLE or RRC-INACTIVE state. A network apparatus broadcasts configuration information, including NOMA parameters, demodulation reference signal (DM-RS) ports, and multiple access (MA) signatures, to define the configured grant PUSCH. 

To mitigate sequence collisions in NOMA transmissions, the system exploits the randomness of user-specific reference bits and data bits. A UE generates reference bits based on a UE-specific identity and an MA identity, jointly encodes them with information bits using a systematic low-density parity check (LDPC) or Polar encoder, and uses the encoded reference bits to generate a preamble or DM-RS. This approach reduces signaling overhead, latency, and power consumption while enhancing spectral efficiency and decoding performance. The passage also details various NOMA schemes (codebook-based, sequence-based, interleaver-based), resource allocation configurations, and a general 5G communications system architecture.

In Pelitsie v. National Surety Corporation of New York, the court determined whether the insured failed to comply with a burglary insurance policy's record-keeping clause. The policy required records enabling the insurer to accurately determine the loss amount. The plaintiff kept a check-cashing fund in a safe, recording only the combined total of cash and checks on a scratch pad. After a burglary, the plaintiff could not provide specific details about the stolen checks. The court held that for stolen checks, the insured must maintain records listing each check's amount, drawer, and payee or check number to allow claims against the drawers. Because the plaintiff failed to keep adequate records of the stolen checks, he breached the policy condition. The judgment was reversed, and the cause was remanded with directions to dismiss the complaint.

This study evaluates the application of steady-state variance reduction techniques (VRTs) to time-dependent Monte Carlo neutron transport simulations, focusing on their interactions with population control techniques (PCTs). VRTs like implicit capture (IC), weight windows, CADIS, FW-CADIS, and Cooper-Larsen (CL) modify particle weights to improve efficiency. PCTs like uniform combing (UC) and weight-based combing (WC) regulate particle counts over time. 

Tested on pulsed slab, AZURV1, and 1D SCRAM problems using Shift and MC/DC codes, results showed that combining CL weight windows with UC significantly improved efficiency. In contrast, combining weight windows with WC caused memory exhaustion due to excessive splitting, and pairing IC with UC underperformed. The authors conclude that selecting compatible VRT and PCT combinations is crucial for time-dependent simulations, and adapting steady-state VRTs for time-dependence offers promising efficiency gains.

Despite low US language enrollment threatening programs, language education remains vital because "language connects" people. Instructors create plausible, authentic scenarios—such as moving abroad, finding an apartment, or job hunting—where students use the target language for real-world purposes. Guidelines include designing authentic assessments, providing student autonomy, and offering just-in-time instruction. This approach has yielded positive outcomes, including deeper cultural understanding, increased feelings of connection, and higher continuation rates in language studies. Applicable across all levels (K–16) and languages, fostering imagined communities emphasizes the essential "why" of language learning, ultimately ensuring the success of language education.

This study investigates whether Large Language Models (LLMs) default to egoism or altruism in social simulations using a Schelling-variant migration model with over 200 agents. Introducing a shared message board to simulate social influence, the researchers employed mixed-methods evaluation to assess emergent behaviors. The experiments reveal a fundamental bifurcation in LLM social tendencies. "Adaptive Egoists" (e.g., o1-mini, o3-mini, Qwen2.5-7B) default to self-interest but demonstrate increased altruism when exposed to social norms via the message board. In contrast, "Altruistic Optimizers" (e.g., Gemini-2.5-pro, Deepseek Series) inherently prioritize collective welfare, even at personal cost, regardless of social interaction mechanisms. The authors conclude that selecting an LLM for social simulation represents a theoretical choice regarding the underlying model of a social actor, suggesting that evaluation should shift from task performance to the embodied social theories of egoism and altruism.

This retrospective study using the MIMIC-IV database investigated the association between resting heart rate (RHR) and all-cause mortality (ACM) in 1,918 intensive care unit (ICU) patients with intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). Patients were divided into four RHR quartiles. Results indicated that patients in the higher RHR quartiles had significantly higher ACM rates at 30 days, 90 days, and 1 year. Multivariate Cox regression and restricted cubic splines analysis revealed a nonlinear relationship, identifying 90.3 bpm as a critical threshold. An RHR below 90.3 bpm served as an independent protective factor against ACM, whereas an RHR exceeding 90.3 bpm was independently associated with an increased mortality risk. Subgroup analyses showed an interaction between RHR and age, with patients over 60 exhibiting higher hazard ratios. The study concludes that RHR can be used to stratify mortality risk and guide clinical management for ICH patients in the ICU.

Siqi Zheng lectures on quantitatively measuring the benefits of green buildings and cities using the hedonic pricing model. This model decomposes a complex commodity, like a house, into individual attributes (e.g., rooms, subway access, parks, green certification) plus an unobservable residual. By running regressions on real estate transaction data, researchers can estimate the willingness to pay (WTP) for specific features, such as a 6% price premium for LEED certification. Zheng contrasts revealed preference (observing market transactions) with stated preference (surveys). A major challenge in this analysis is causal inference, as researchers face endogeneity issues like omitted variables, reverse causality, and selection bias, leading to "apples-to-oranges" comparisons. To achieve "apples-to-apples" comparisons, researchers seek a counterfactual—an identical but unobservable scenario. Techniques to address this include Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs), geographic matching, instrumental variables, and difference-in-differences. Zheng applies these concepts to real-world examples, including the Winthrop Center's design choices, Bryant Park's private-public restoration increasing nearby property values, High Line Park's environmental gentrification, and a Chinese subway project using land value capture to fund transit-oriented development.

The Turtle Trading Strategy is a trend-following approach developed by Richard Dennis and William Eckhardt in the 1980s. This study explores dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) using natural dyes extracted from mangosteen peel (MP) and grass jelly leaves (GJL). Furthermore, GJL-rich samples exhibited better stability over ten operational cycles. The study concludes that optimizing natural dye mixtures enhances DSSC performance, offering a low-cost and eco-friendly approach to solar energy conversion.

The lecture reviews the LSZ theorem, which relates scattering amplitudes to time-ordered correlation functions via the on-shell limit. Scattering amplitudes are obtained by truncating external propagators from connected Feynman diagrams. Initial and final states are distinguished by taking negative and positive momentum roots, respectively. Corrections to external propagators are absorbed into a constant Z, which is independent of momentum and identical for a given particle type.

The lecture then transitions to fermions, detailing the history of the Klein-Gordon equation and Dirac's pursuit of a first-order, Lorentz-covariant wave equation. Dirac introduced constant Hermitian matrices (alpha and beta) instead of scalars, leading to the Dirac equation for a four-component spinor. By defining gamma matrices, the equation is written compactly, with the matrices satisfying the Clifford algebra. For massless particles, the equation reduces to two components. Different representations of the gamma matrices are related by similarity transformations and are physically equivalent. The lecture concludes by setting up the proof of the Dirac equation's Lorentz covariance for the next session.

Phuket Governor Norraphat Plodthong ordered lifeguards back on patrol at Phuket’s beaches by April 1, 2018. The directive was issued at a March 21 meeting attended by local officials. Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt’s Schmidt Sciences is funding a $45 million, five-year project to deploy uncrewed surface vessels (USVs) in the Southern Ocean to study its role as a major carbon sink. Data collection in the region has been limited by extreme conditions and reliance on commercial shipping routes. The remotely piloted USVs will use machine learning to gather continuous, sophisticated CO2 data outside standard routes, including during winter, and will make it public. This public-private partnership with NOAA occurs as federal science funding faces severe proposed cuts, making outside funding increasingly critical for climate research.

The passage documents various AGESA procedures for processor and memory initialization. It details the enabling and disabling of the pre-memory stack (cache-as-RAM) before and after main memory availability. It describes `AmdCreateStruct` for creating and initializing parameter block structures. Additional procedures retrieve DIMM data eye bitmaps, obtain APIC and base PCI addresses for processor cores and dies, determine available execution cache size pre-memory, identify the current executing processor core, and map memory addresses to specific DIMMs (FRUs) and their internal locations. Scientists investigating the ignition of swamp gas that creates will-o’-the-wisps found that microbubbles of air and methane in water can produce tiny electrical zaps, or "microlightning." Lab experiments showed that differently charged bubbles of varying sizes create sparks when jostled together. While some scientists doubt this fully explains the phenomenon due to differences between the underwater lab setup and airborne swamp flames, the findings advance triboelectricity research. Scientists suggest these microbubble sparks could be harnessed for environmentally friendly chemical reactions and breaking down pollutants.

The Solawave 4-in-1 Renewal Wand is on sale for just over $100. It targets specific facial areas with vibration and warmth in three-minute sessions, and WIRED staffers noted positive skin-tightening results around the eyes. Solawave's Red Light Therapy Face Mask is also on sale for $227.

Devices in a daisy-chain topology share CONVST/CS and SCLK inputs. The host programs identical registers (SDO_CTL_REG bits 7-0 to 00h). Devices sample inputs on the rising CONVST/CS edge and shift data MSB-first on SCLK edges. The host receives data sequentially from device N to 1. Optimal frames require 32 × N SCLK capture edges; shorter frames cause errors, while longer frames require host alignment.

The President addresses Congress on conserving national resources, noting the public domain's reduction due to past lax distribution and fraud. The administration continues prosecuting land frauds and withdrawing coal, oil, phosphate, and water-power sites. The President urges Congress to validate past executive withdrawals and grant the Secretary of the Interior clear authority to temporarily withdraw lands pending new legislation.

He recommends classifying public lands by their principal value, separating surface agricultural rights from subsurface mineral rights, and leasing minerals on a royalty basis to prevent monopolies. For water-power sites, he suggests limited-term leases to avoid private monopolies. Soil conservation is highlighted as the most critical resource, requiring both federal and state action.

Regarding arid lands, reclamation projects are underfunded, leaving settlers in distress. The President recommends issuing $30,000,000 in bonds to complete these projects. For timber lands, he suggests repealing existing laws and selling timber publicly before opening the land for agriculture or mining. National forests are adequately managed, but he recommends federal funding for reforestation at the sources of navigable streams, leaving private forest regulation to the states.

He urges Congress to enact these recommendations promptly without waiting for an ongoing investigation into the Interior and Forest Service.

The document standardizes the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP, which protect guest register state from the hypervisor. VMEXITs are categorized as Automatic Exits (AE) or Non-Automatic Exits (NAE), with the specification detailing required NAE events and minimum guest state exposure. NVIDIA RTX IO uses Microsoft’s DirectStorage API for GPU-based lossless decompression, improving I/O performance and reducing CPU load. The Consumer Confidence Index (CCI), published by The Conference Board, and the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index measure consumer optimism regarding the economy. Backtests from 1993 show that investing in the S&P 500 when US consumer confidence is above its 12-month moving average yields an 8.4% CAGR with lower drawdowns than a buy-and-hold strategy. Conversely, investing when confidence is below the average yields a 1.58% CAGR. Consumer confidence impacts economic behavior: optimism stimulates spending, production, and hiring, while pessimism reduces economic activity. Natalie Grabow, 80, set the world record as the oldest woman to finish the Kona Ironman World Championship, completing the race in 16 hours, 45 minutes, and 26 seconds. She began competing in triathlons at age 60, a year after teaching herself to swim at 59. Grabow started running in her 40s and progressed to triathlons in her 50s. Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations calculate thermal properties using the Green-Kubo (GK) and Non-Equilibrium MD (NEMD) methods, both requiring heat flux (HF). HF is also needed for Interfacial Thermal Conductance (ITC) and Spectral Decomposition of the Heat Current (SDHC). The MD code LAMMPS originally used an HF formula limited to pair potentials, causing incorrect thermal conductivity for many-body interactions. Although exact formulas by Torii et al. exist and specific corrections were made for certain systems, a general implementation for many-body potentials, control surfaces, and SDHC is lacking. This work implements Torii et al.'s formulas in LAMMPS to calculate HF for control volumes, control surfaces, and SDHC for arbitrary many-body potentials. The passage also introduces the Hardy and Torii formulas for instantaneous heat flux.

COPD, a leading US cause of death caused almost exclusively by smoking, causes coughing and shortness of breath. Diagnosed via breathing tests, it is incurable but treatable to stop lung decline. Quitting smoking is the only way to reduce risk.

This qualitative study evaluates distance education in Turkish sports higher education during the COVID-19 pandemic, based on interviews with 14 sports sciences lecturers. Findings revealed four main themes. Positive aspects included independence from time and space, resource accessibility, technological integration, and economic benefits. Negative aspects involved social, psychological, technological, and educational issues, notably motivation loss, communication barriers, inequality of opportunity, and the inability to conduct applied sports lessons effectively. Challenges centered on infrastructure, connection problems, and assessment difficulties. Regarding management, participants felt the crisis was poorly handled, citing delayed decision-making, lack of responsibility from authorities, and inadequate platform support. The study concludes that while distance education is a viable alternative, it requires field-specific adaptations for applied courses and strict data security measures.

This study uses first-principles calculations to investigate the tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) effect in a Mn3Sn(01-10)/MgO(110)/Mn3Sn magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ). Mn3Sn is a noncollinear antiferromagnet that breaks time-reversal symmetry, allowing it to generate a finite TMR effect despite lacking net spin polarization. By using a practically thick MgO barrier, the calculations yield a TMR ratio exceeding 1000%. The TMR effect is primarily driven by the momentum-dependent spin splitting of the x-component in bulk Mn3Sn, which remains finite across momentum states, combined with the electron filtering properties of the MgO barrier, which exhibits its lowest decay rate near zero in-plane momentum. These results demonstrate that Mn3Sn is a promising electrode for antiferromagnetic spintronic devices.

A Journal of Neuroscience study reveals that barn owls process visual information similarly to humans and primates. Despite having simpler brains, barn owls can group moving elements to distinguish objects from backgrounds. Researchers tested this by having owls spot a target dot moving differently among other dots. The owls succeeded, and their ocular tectum activated based on movement, indicating this brain area handles the visual processing task.

Jeff Bezos has proposed building data centres in space to address Earth's growing digital demands and ease constraints on land, energy, and cooling. Orbital facilities could utilize solar energy and bypass terrestrial limitations caused by rising cloud and AI computing needs. However, significant engineering challenges remain, including radiation shielding, vacuum cooling, power storage, and low-latency communication, alongside high launch and maintenance costs. Despite these hurdles, aerospace and technology firms are exploring orbital infrastructure, driven by falling launch costs and hardware advances. If realized, this could profoundly shift the digital landscape as data demand continues to rise.

This patent application describes a geographically-based graphical user interface (map GUI) for a social networking application that facilitates real-time location sharing. The system predicts a user's presumed destination by correlating their current trajectory, derived from location sensor data, with historical location information, including habitual places and recurring trajectory patterns. The presumed destination and an estimated time of arrival are then shared with the user's friends via the map GUI using avatars and destination icons.

The location sharing system comprises client devices hosting location sharing applications and a server system featuring API, application, and database servers. The database stores entity graphs, message data, and location information. The processing environment includes modules for location tracking, historical location analysis, destination prediction, and map GUI generation. 

The system extracts trajectory patterns by clustering historical trajectories based on similarity and averaging them. If communication with a user's device is lost, the system can extrapolate the user's current location based on the identified trajectory pattern. The map GUI allows users to view friends' locations, initiate chats, and receive notifications when a friend reaches their destination. The document also details the software architecture, machine hardware components, and provides definitions for technical terms used in the disclosure.

The MSPM0G microcontrollers feature an ARM Cortex-M0+ CPU with five operating modes (RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, SHUTDOWN) to optimize power consumption across two power domains. The system includes a Power Management Unit, a Clock Module with multiple oscillators, and a DMA controller. Memory consists of up to 512KB of flash and 128KB of SRAM, both with ECC options. 

The device integrates numerous peripherals, including GPIO, dual 12-bit ADCs, DACs, comparators, and various timers (TIMGx, TIMAx, RTC, watchdogs). Communication interfaces include UART, I2C, SPI, and CAN-FD. Security is provided via an AES accelerator, TRNG, secure keystore, and CRC module. An event manager facilitates digital event transfers between peripherals, the DMA, and the CPU.

Additional features include a Serial Wire Debug interface, a Boot Strap Loader for memory programming, and factory constants for device identification. The document also details application layout recommendations, device nomenclature, development tools, revision history, and mechanical packaging information.

The passage introduces EchoingECG, a probabilistic student-teacher framework that estimates echocardiogram (ECHO) variables from electrocardiograms (ECGs). It addresses ECG signal complexity and data scarcity by integrating PCME++ and ECHO-CLIP. To manage signal complexity, the framework uses probabilistic contrastive learning, allowing many-to-many mappings that capture inherent uncertainties in ECG signals. To mitigate the need for large-scale annotated datasets, it employs ECHO-CLIP as a teacher model to distill echo-based cardiac information into ECG representations. The framework's contributions include a probabilistic multimodal ECG model, a knowledge distillation approach reducing dataset dependency, and experimental evidence of uncertainty-aware evaluation.

Chris King, who lost both hands in an industrial accident and was the first UK patient to have both transplanted, attended his first live rugby match at Headingley Stadium. He drew the winning half-time ticket and enjoyed the Rhinos' 42-22 victory over the Widnes Vikings.

This study presents a bibliometric analysis of academic publications on "Digital Accessibility in Education" from 2013 to 2024, using data from the Web of Science, Scopus, and ERIC databases. Digital accessibility aims to create inclusive IT products and services for all members of society, including individuals with disabilities. The analysis reveals a significant increase in publications, particularly after 2020, largely driven by the COVID-19 pandemic and digital transformation. 

Scopus hosts the highest number of publications, with journal articles being the primary document type. English is the dominant language, and higher education is the most frequently researched educational level. The USA, UK, and Spain contribute the most publications. Citation relationships show an uneven distribution, with the USA and UK acting as major research hubs. While a few authors, documents, and countries are highly cited and well-connected, many remain isolated. The study concludes that digital accessibility in education is a growing field, but it requires enhanced international collaboration, robust legal frameworks, and a focus on improving computer literacy for students with disabilities.

Optical Genome Mapping (OGM) is emerging as a comprehensive alternative to current standard of care (SOC) cytogenetic tests for hematologic malignancies, which are often subjective and require multiple testing modalities. This study evaluated a streamlined OGM data analysis and reporting workflow using VIA software on 10 retrospective myeloid malignancy samples through blinded technologist and director reviews. OGM detected all SOC variants and identified additional novel variants in five of six positive cases. The VIA workflow reduced technologist review times by approximately 50% compared to previous software, averaging 25 to 47 minutes depending on case complexity. The study concludes that OGM with VIA offers an efficient, objective method to standardize cytogenomic variant analysis and reporting, potentially addressing laboratory labor shortages.

Headteacher Mark Ryan of St. Patrick’s Catholic Primary School received community support after a newspaper inaccurately reported he took a two-week term-time holiday and threatened a parent with a fine. This paper examines the normative assumption that educational disparities should be corrected, using luck egalitarianism from contemporary political philosophy. Luck egalitarianism posits that inequalities caused by "brute luck" (factors beyond individual control, such as social background) are unjust and should be corrected, while those resulting from "option luck" (individual choices) are the individual's responsibility. However, applying this theory to education faces critiques highlighted by Elizabeth Anderson: the harshness objection, where individuals face severe consequences for their choices, and the humiliation objection, where compensation policies stigmatize disadvantaged individuals.

To address the harshness objection, the paper explores "fresh start," which allows individuals to reset after poor choices, and "sufficiency," which guarantees a baseline threshold of resources regardless of responsibility. To address the humiliation objection, the paper introduces the value of "respect," emphasizing the need to avoid practices that cause shame or stigma. The paper concludes that empirical research on educational disparities should not only focus on fairness but also incorporate the values of fresh start, sufficiency, and respect to better understand and address educational inequalities.

The Los Angeles Dodgers defeated the Arizona Diamondbacks 9-5 in their NL Division Series opener on October 6, 2017. Facebook's new algorithm limits reach, making social influencers—credible users with large followings—valuable for businesses. Plaintiff Thomas E. Duvoisin, as Liquidating Trustee for Southern Industrial Banking Corporation (SIBC), sued defendants to recover alleged fraudulent conveyances under 11 U.S.C.A. § 548(a). Defendants moved to dismiss, asserting plaintiff lacked standing and that recovered assets would not result in equal creditor distribution. SIBC's confirmed Modified Plan of Reorganization created a Liquidation Trust and distributed stock or stock purchase rights in the successor-in-interest to impaired unsecured creditors. The court denied the motion, finding that recovering the transfers would increase the successor-in-interest's assets, thereby benefiting creditors' stock values. The court also held that 11 U.S.C.A. § 1123(b) grants the plaintiff standing to enforce these claims, distinguishing defendants' cited cases as inapplicable.

In Hardin v. White et al., the court ruled on two issues. First, an injunction bond does not need to be double the judgment amount if the injunction only restrains the sale of specific property under execution, rather than the judgment's collection. Second, a creditor who sells real estate under an execution for part of a judgment exhausts their remedy under that decree for that property and cannot subsequently sell the debtor's right of redemption for the debt's remainder. The creditor attempted to use a separate decree from a chattel mortgage foreclosure to sell the right of redemption for the balance of a real estate foreclosure decree. Because both decrees involved the same underlying debt, which can only be collected once, the court treated them as identical. The lower court's judgment was affirmed on both the original hearing and rehearing.

The IMF advised China to prioritize financial stability over growth goals to curb high credit growth and debt. It recommended creating a financial stability sub-committee, increasing regulatory staff, and granting the banking watchdog more autonomy. The IMF warned that rapid financial product development poses systemic risks and stressed that banks need more capital buffers. Stress tests on 33 banks revealed a potential capital shortfall equal to 2.5% of GDP under a severely adverse scenario. Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a genetic disorder causing abnormal, sickle-shaped hemoglobin cells that block blood flow and reduce healthy red blood cell counts. It affects people globally, particularly those of sub-Saharan African descent. Symptoms include severe pain crises, acute chest syndrome, anemia, and organ damage, with smoking increasing complication risks. Diagnosed via blood tests, SCD requires lifelong management through medical treatments like vaccinations, pain relief, blood transfusions, and potentially stem cell transplants, alongside lifestyle choices such as quitting smoking, eating well, and exercising to improve quality of life.

Coach Quenneville provides updates and insights on his team's playoff series. Thousands of Budget $aver and Sugar Free ice pops were recalled across 15 states due to potential Listeria contamination, which can cause severe infections, miscarriages, and short-term symptoms.

Research from the University of Exeter shows that the Fal oyster fishery in Cornwall is sustained by its traditional, inefficient sail-driven and hand-hauled dredging methods. Motorizing the fleet could increase fishing nine-fold, threatening stocks. The native European flat oyster is already threatened by pollution, overfishing, and non-native species. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at record highs, aided by AMD gains. Heikin Ashi, meaning "average bar," is a Japanese charting technique that smooths price movements to highlight trends and reduce noise. Unlike traditional candlesticks that show real prices, Heikin Ashi uses mathematical averages, making it a lagging technical indicator. Its calculations involve average open, high, low, and close values, with haOpen acting as an exponential moving average. Backtesting reveals that Heikin Ashi can be used in profitable trend-following strategies, particularly on longer timeframes, such as a simple crossover strategy on the S&P 500 or combined with the ADX indicator. The technique can also be customized by adjusting its period parameter to filter price noise.
The speaker discusses a tough overtime loss, noting their third-period success and missed opportunities. They view the painful experience as a learning opportunity that brings the group closer.

Enron Corp.'s shares fell over 20% on October 22, 2001, after the company confirmed the SEC requested information regarding transactions with limited partnerships run by CFO Andrew Fastow. On October 22, 2001, Enron Corp. shares fell over 20% after the company announced the SEC requested information regarding related-party transactions involving limited partnerships run by CFO Andrew Fastow. Enron reported a $35 million charge related to these partnerships and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity to repurchase 55 million shares to unwind its involvement. FHA loans require lenders to consider the credit and debt of both spouses, even if only one is on the mortgage. This joint liability applies to legally married couples during purchases and refinances, potentially lowering borrowing power if the non-borrowing spouse has significant debt. Alternatives include switching to a conventional loan, purchasing a home before marriage, or using a quit claim deed for separate property transactions.

Trinidad and Tobago won the men's 4x400 meters relay at the World Athletics Championships, denying the United States a seventh consecutive world title. Lalonde Gordon overtook Fred Kerley on the final straight to secure Trinidad's first world title in this event and their only gold of the championships, with a year-fastest time of 2:58.12. A 16-year-old Iowa girl with severe depression requested her matted hair be shaved off before school portraits, feeling it was too painful to untangle. Student hairdresser Kayley Olson refused, instead spending 13 hours over two days untangling and restyling it into a shoulder-length cut.
