In *Hunter v. Bales*, the Supreme Court affirmed a specific performance decree for the plaintiff. Moore orally agreed to sell land to Thompson, then to Hunter. Moore executed a title bond to Thompson but later deeded the land to Hunter, who knew of the bond. Thompson tendered the purchase money and demanded a deed, which was refused. The Court held Thompson had prior equity over Hunter. It ruled that in equity, a valid land sale contract makes the vendee the owner and the vendor a trustee with a lien. The Court also held that in a specific performance suit, the plaintiff need only offer to bring the purchase money into court once liquidated, and a vendee who tenders the purchase money and interest is not chargeable with further interest unless the vendor proves the vendee used the money.

In *Asa B. Meech v. City of Buffalo*, property owners challenged a second assessment for sewer construction costs. Buffalo's common council had initially assessed $1,058.63 and contracted with Randolph to build the sewer. During construction, Randolph struck an unforeseen quicksand, making completion impossible at the contract price. He threatened to abandon the work. The council agreed to pay an additional $588.13 and assessed property owners for the deficiency. The court held that the supplementary assessment was authorized by the city charter, which permits a further assessment when the original proves insufficient to defray actual improvement expenses. The court also found the city could voluntarily increase the contract price under equitable circumstances, as its charter contained no prohibition against doing so. Judgment was affirmed against the plaintiffs.

This qualitative case study examined how peer mentoring and storytelling in a 14-week movement education course developed 21st-century skills among Physical Education Teacher Education (PETE) students in Türkiye. The course utilized social media for pre-lesson communication and task sharing, with peer mentors creating narrative content combining fundamental movement skills with familiar stories. 

Results revealed three themes. First, peer learners excluded non-contributing members but supported those making an effort, while peer mentors divided tasks to ensure completion despite conflicts. Second, peer mentors enhanced their accountability and teaching responsibility by creating content, while peer learners practiced teaching and collaboration. Third, storytelling connected course content to daily life, making learning more memorable and engaging than traditional methods. 

The study concludes that peer mentoring provides realistic field experiences, fosters professional skills, and bridges students and staff, while storytelling ensures permanent learning. It recommends integrating these methods throughout undergraduate PETE programs and conducting long-term studies.

This passage presents a systematic review and computational taxonomy of the social science of large language models (LLMs). Viewing LLMs as purpose-driven social artifacts, the authors analyze 270 studies using a PRISMA-compliant pipeline. In Study 1, unsupervised machine learning (Sentence-BERT embeddings, K-means clustering, and LDA topic modeling) reveals a stable three-way partition: "LLM as Social Minds" (individual model behavior and cognition), "LLM Societies" (multi-agent interactions and emergent coordination), and "LLM–Human Interactions" (trust, reliance, and productivity at the human-LLM interface). In Study 2, this machine-derived taxonomy is compared against an expert-coded classification, demonstrating strong alignment (Macro-F1 = 0.954, NMI = 0.811, ARI = 0.867). The authors argue these three clusters should be treated as levels of analysis rather than mutually exclusive camps, clarifying evidentiary standards across domains. The taxonomy functions as a measurement model to avoid category mistakes and guide future research toward anti-shortcut stress tests and institutional design. The authors conclude that understanding AI's sociality requires shifting focus from whether LLMs resemble persons to engineering and auditing the institutions through which their predictions affect people.

The document describes AMD's Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine, which extends SEV and SNP to facilitate page migration between memory tiers. TMPM offloads page migration, pauses DMA traffic during migration, and migrates pages protected by Secure Nested Paging (SNP). Key commands include PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO for concurrent DMA targets and PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST for SNP guest pages. TMPM supports moving up to 128 pages per command via a Page Migration List, with performance maximized using 128-page commands and pacing interrupts. Certain IOMMU data structures and buffers do not support migration. TMPM firmware can be reloaded when no operations are in flight, requiring specific procedures depending on the EPYC family. A restriction is that all system physical addresses must be 4k aligned.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2016. Net sales increased 29% to $32.7 billion in Q3 2016 and $92.2 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2016. Operating income grew to $575 million in Q3 2016 from $406 million in Q3 2015, and to $2.9 billion for the nine months. Net income was $252 million in Q3 2016 and $1.6 billion for the nine months. The company operates in three segments—North America, International, and AWS—with AWS sales increasing 55% in Q3 2016. Total cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities were $18.3 billion as of September 30, 2016.

The San Francisco 49ers ruled out quarterback Brock Purdy, Ricky Pearsall, and Jauan Jennings for Thursday's game against the Rams due to injuries. Mac Jones will start at quarterback, with Robinson and Bourne likely starting at receiver against a Rams defense Jones called the best in the NFL.

King Salman and Turkish President Erdogan held talks in Riyadh, reviewing bilateral relations, cooperation, and regional and international developments. Several high-ranking Saudi officials attended the meeting, which was preceded by an official reception for Erdogan.

A year-long knowledge exchange project between the Institute of Education and Diversity Role Models trained Citizenship student teachers in England to foster trans-inclusive classrooms. Amidst rising media hostility and draft UK government guidance proposing restrictions on teaching gender identity and social transition, student teachers expressed a lack of confidence in discussing transgender identities compared to sexual orientation. 

To address this, educators utilized "actualizing" to make LGBTQ+ rights concrete, though this largely focused on sexual orientation. Storytelling and personal narratives were employed to build empathy and challenge prejudice. Additionally, teachers used domestic legislation like the Equality Act 2010 to frame LGBTQ+ youth as rights holders, a method supported by international frameworks such as the UNCRC and Yogyakarta Principles+10. 

Participants noted that effective trans inclusion requires whole-school approaches beyond discrete Citizenship lessons, including clear behavior policies, visibility, and "upstander" training to prevent bullying. The project concluded that while proposed government guidance poses risks, combining human rights education with personal stories effectively promotes trans equality, highlighting the need for continued teacher training and civil society partnerships.

The President urges Congress to substantially reduce tariff duties on Cuban imports into the United States. He cites reasons of morality, national interest, and Cuba's constitutional commitment to closer relations with the US. This request aligns with prior policies by President McKinley and responds to an urgent plea from Cuban President Palma for legislative relief to avoid financial ruin. The President argues that this unique reciprocity will not harm American industries or the protective tariff system, noting that past fears regarding Hawaii proved baseless. He emphasizes that the US, having helped Cuba achieve independence, must provide economic support to ensure the young republic's prosperity and stability.

The passage references tables tracking medical problems after BNT162b2 booster doses (5, 10, or 30 µg) and additional boosters (Doses 4 or 5). It defines serious medical problems and notes that in Phase 1, two participants experienced serious issues (inflamed appendix and nerves) after Dose 2.

Malaysia's central bank will allow all resident entities to short-sell government securities starting May 2 to boost liquidity. Non-bank entities gain expanded hedging and foreign exchange limits. The bank is also considering short-selling shariah-compliant bonds, adding new currency hedging options, and implementing a new financial market code of conduct to encourage onshore ringgit trade and stabilize the currency.
To prevent avian flu, Taiwan authorities advise cooking eggs to 70°C, washing hands after handling shells, cooking poultry thoroughly, wearing masks, and seeing a doctor for fevers.

In Charles Jones v. Orin S. Bacon, the plaintiff sought to enforce an alleged indemnity agreement with the defendant's testator, McKechnie, who had purportedly promised to protect the plaintiff from losses on notes he endorsed for his son-in-law, Kingsbury. After a jury verdict for the plaintiff, the defendant appealed, arguing the trial court improperly admitted evidence. The appellate court agreed, finding that testimony regarding McKechnie and Kingsbury's hop speculation—including McKechnie's refusal of a profitable offer that would have paid Kingsbury's debts—was inadmissible. The court ruled this evidence was foreign to the issues, calculated to excite jury sympathy for the plaintiff and Kingsbury, and highly prejudicial to the defendant. Accordingly, the judgment was reversed and a new trial granted.

Magda Enriquez is a divorced mother of six and a Council of State member representing the Nicaraguan Women’s Association AMNLAE. Educated in the US, she returned to Nicaragua and founded a school for mentally retarded children. Discovering malnutrition as a primary cause, she worked in slums, motivated by Roman Catholic liberation theology. She secretly joined the Sandinistas in 1976. Following a violent 1978 land sit-in where ten children died from poison and delayed medical care, she sought military training. Her children are also active in the revolution, including a 14-year-old son in the militia. Enriquez relies on community and party solidarity to help raise her children while she works. She has traveled internationally to prepare for upcoming elections, noting that Nicaraguans are experiencing democracy for the first time. She acknowledges that women's problems persist but believes the revolution provides opportunities to solve them, challenging American government narratives about her country.

Harry Kane led England to the World Cup quarter-finals, beating Colombia 4-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw. Kane scored the opener and a shootout penalty, becoming the tournament's top scorer with six goals. England will face Sweden next. Following the match, Radamel Falcao accused the American referee of bias toward England, and Diego Maradona called the result a "monumental theft."

Between 24-48 weeks, 33.8%-40.8% of subjects across groups reported AEs, alongside 24 total deaths and two fatal bleeding events. No pregnancies or concerning lab signals occurred. The AEGEAN study showed high, sustained apixaban adherence up to 48 weeks, but an educational program provided no additional benefits.

Kinlochleven first responders received three defibrillators and life support training via local fundraising and charity Lucky 2B Here. They will be placed at the Co-op and GP's surgery. The group seeks donations, having raised £2,900 of £3,500.

Retirees and FIRE (Financial Independent Retire Early) individuals risk going broke due to sequence of returns risk, high withdrawal rates, and poor diversification. An example of a couple retiring in 2000 with a 5% annual withdrawal rate shows they depleted their funds by 2017 after experiencing early market downturns. Monte Carlo simulations of historical S&P 500 returns reveal a significant chance of lower-than-expected returns due to compounding effects. While the 4% rule is a common benchmark, the passage suggests FIREs require more conservative rates, such as 3% or even 2% as recommended by Edward Thorp, to survive severe early market declines. Additionally, diversification and moderate spending are advised to mitigate sequence risk.

Hinsdale South High School seniors were named Illinois State Scholars. The program recognizes the top 10 percent of graduating seniors based on ACT and SAT scores, unweighted GPA, and class size at the end of junior year.
An Appleton couple featured in People Magazine shares their story to encourage CPR training after Luke Benrud saved his wife Andrea using CPR when she collapsed from a rare heart defect.

Body camera footage shows Grand Rapids Officer Kevin Penn pressing his AR-15 rifle muzzle to a suspect's head during an August 19 arrest. The suspect, who was drunk and uncooperative, was tased by another officer before Penn used the rifle to control him. Kent County Prosecutor Chris Becker declined to charge Penn, stating the action is untrained and uncondoned but not criminal under these facts. Penn resigned after other officers reported his behavior. The suspect was charged with resisting arrest and later released.

Facing threats to economic growth and sluggish inflation, the European Central Bank (ECB) is expected to temper expectations for a quick exit from its stimulus programme. Governors will likely maintain low interest rates and a September expiry for the 30-billion-euro monthly bond-buying scheme. Downside risks include a stronger euro, US trade tariff threats, and delayed eurozone reforms. With inflation below the 2.0 per cent target and economic indicators showing some loss of momentum, ECB President Mario Draghi may emphasize these risks to push back expectations of an interest rate rise, ensuring a gradual policy normalization.

Manheim Township police charged four men in separate incidents. Jonathan Miles faces drug and child endangerment charges for growing marijuana while caring for his daughter. Glen VanDerSchaaf was charged with indecent assault. Tyran Ellis faces corruption of minors charges for receiving a child's nude photo. Gilberto Isaac-Suarez was charged with burglary and assault following a domestic dispute.

This study examined how sex and trauma type affect the correlation between self-reported (PCL-5) and clinician-administered (CAPS-5) PTSD assessments in 100 adults. CAPS-5 scores were similar across sexes and trauma types. However, females exhibited a stronger correlation between PCL-5 and CAPS-5 scores than males. Males showed significant deviation from the ideal regression line and a higher rate of misclassified PTSD cases based on PCL-5 alone. Additionally, civilian trauma yielded a stronger correlation between the two measures than military trauma for both sexes. The findings suggest clinicians should consider sex and trauma type when interpreting self-reported PTSD measures, as relying solely on PCL-5 may lead to misclassification, particularly in males.

Companies participate in exhibitions to enhance brand image and interact with customers, requiring experienced event hosts. Traditional recruitment agencies are expensive with limited databases. Professionate, an online event staffing agency, provides a global platform connecting companies and candidates. Companies can browse candidate profiles, images, and reviews, while candidates can post profiles and apply for temporary jobs directly. Recruitment agencies can also use the platform to find more profiles.

UNICEF warns that Yemen's two-year war may deprive a generation of children of education, risking early marriage and military recruitment. Over 73% of teachers have been unpaid since October due to the conflict and central bank relocation, threatening the school year for 4.5 million children.

A Channel 4 documentary titled "The Super Orgasm" explores women experiencing up to 100 orgasms in one session. Through three experiments measuring arousal, brain waves, and brain blood flow, researchers found these women were easily aroused and showed distinct neurological patterns during multiple orgasms. However, experts criticize the documentary as unscientific due to its small sample size and lack of controls. They argue the term "super orgasm" is misleading, viewing it simply as multiple orgasms, which vary greatly among women. Experts warn against the documentary's implication that all women should achieve this, noting the participants are outliers and most women are satisfied with fewer orgasms.

The lecture defines continuity and proves a theorem equating continuity at a point to function limits and sequence convergence. It proves the sine function is continuous using an epsilon-delta argument, and the cosine function is continuous using sequence convergence. It also demonstrates that a function equal to 1 on rationals and 0 on irrationals is discontinuous everywhere. Furthermore, it proves that sums, products, quotients, and compositions of continuous functions are continuous, using these properties to show that polynomials and certain rational functions are continuous. The lecture concludes by previewing the min/max theorems and the Intermediate Value Theorem.

Cover 3 is a common football zone defense with three deep defenders and four underneath players, balancing coverage against both pass and run attacks. Deep defenders divide the field into thirds to prevent vertical routes, while underneath defenders cover Hook, Curl, and Flat zones to force short passes. This scheme adds a third deep defender compared to Cover 2 and brings an extra safety near the line to stop the run. Its weaknesses include vulnerability in the flats, susceptibility to "four verticals" and seam routes, and perimeter run defense gaps. Variations include flipping safety roles, fire zone blitzes, Cover 3 Buzz, and pattern-reading concepts like Rip/Liz, which combine zone and man coverage rules.

Biotech news updates cover the FDA approval of a second generic mifepristone and Amgen's Repatha trial, which showed reduced heart risks. Other topics include a new NIH office to reduce animal testing, delayed Medicare drug price negotiations, MoonLake's autoimmune drug failure, and Trump's tariff threats on prescription drugs.

In response to a House resolution, the President transmits documents and instructions regarding the 1848 Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo. The United States commissioners were instructed to secure Mexico's ratification of the Senate's amendments without modifying them. Mexico ratified the amended treaty based on a letter from the US Secretary of State before formally meeting the commissioners. A "protocol" of subsequent conversations was created but initially withheld from Congress as it was not deemed material to the binding treaty. The President argues the protocol did not alter the treaty, addressing three points: the substituted Article 9 still protected the rights of ceded territory inhabitants; the removed Article 10 nullified expired land grants while preserving valid titles; and the suppressed paragraph in Article 12 still allowed Mexico to transfer the $12 million payment. The President concluded the protocol merely contained explanations consistent with the ratified treaty.

John Jacob Beechwood faced an involuntary bankruptcy petition and claimed immunity as a "farmer" under the Bankruptcy Act. Beechwood argued that his retroactive resignation from his full-time corporate legal employment on September 16, 1940, established his farming status by September 20, 1940, the date he committed an act of bankruptcy by conveying his farm to his wife. The court rejected this defense. It found that on the dates of the acts of bankruptcy, Beechwood's principal income derived from his corporate employment and private legal work, not from farming. The court concluded he was a lawyer and businessman residing on a farm, not a farmer under the Act, and ordered him adjudicated as a bankrupt.

The New York Times reported that former Trump campaign chairman Paul Manafort was picked up on calls by officials. Manafort denied knowingly speaking to Russian intelligence or involvement with the Russian government. The report follows the resignation of National Security Adviser Michael Flynn over calls with the Russian ambassador regarding U.S. sanctions. Rep. Elijah Cummings expressed alarm over the report, while Press Secretary Sean Spicer maintained that nothing has changed regarding Trump's denial of campaign contacts with Russians.

The passage is a memorandum from S. E. Mezes outlining the Inquiry's tasks to assist an upcoming peace conference. It lists practical tasks, such as establishing boundaries and governments, estimating state strength, arranging economies, safeguarding minorities, and rewriting international law. It then categorizes these tasks as either required or potentially necessary across various regions, including Russia, Poland, Austria-Hungary, the Balkans, and Turkey.

The inaugural address emphasizes the enduring strength of the Constitution and the founding principle that all people are created equal. The President states that freedom must be secured by the people through collective action to address modern challenges. He highlights the need for a strong middle class, equal pay, voting rights, equal treatment for gay Americans, immigration reform, and child safety. The address also calls for addressing climate change through sustainable energy and asserts that lasting peace does not require perpetual war, emphasizing alliances and peaceful conflict resolution. The President concludes by urging citizens to actively shape the nation's future and uphold the values of life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.

Amazon is planning a new wave of layoffs, preparing to cut up to 15% of its human resources staff (the PXT division) and likely affecting other consumer business areas. The exact total number and timing are unknown. CEO Andy Jassy is reducing employee costs while investing heavily in AI, previously warning that AI adoption will decrease the corporate workforce. These cuts differ from Amazon's typical attrition process. Concurrently, the company is hiring 250,000 seasonal warehouse staff for the holidays.

A study in the Journal of Hematology & Thromboembolic Diseases by University of Brasilia scientists found that Bt toxins (Cry-toxins) in GM crops can cause blood abnormalities, including anemia and leukemia-like patterns, in mammals. The research demonstrated that these toxins do not require an alkaline insect digestive tract to be toxic, are active in distilled water, and their adverse effects increase with long-term exposure. The authors concluded that further studies are needed and it is premature to consider these toxins safe for mammals. The passage also references a French study linking GM corn and Roundup to cancer in rats, criticizes biotech corporations for funding biased research, and notes the author's advocacy for banning GMOs and protesting Monsanto.

December manufacturer incentives offer savings on fuel-efficient vehicles. The 2017 Kia Optima Hybrid provides up to $5,000 off or 0% APR financing. Plug-in hybrid leases include the Kia Optima at $249/month, Hyundai Sonata at $289/month, and Chevrolet Volt at $273/month. For electric cars, the 2017 Kia Soul EV has an $18,100 discount or a $159/month lease, while the Chevrolet Bolt EV leases for $303/month. The 2018 Chevrolet Equinox diesel has $4,000 off nationwide. The Toyota Yaris iA offers $2,000 off in Southern California.

The Global Meat Starter Culture Market report by Index Markets Research forecasts market trends from 2018 to 2025. It details revenues by segment, end-user, and region, profiling key manufacturers like Chr. Hansen and Danisco. The report segments by product type (Maturation and Surface Starters) and application (Meat, Poultry, Seafood, Others). Geographically, it covers the US, China, Europe, Japan, Southeast Asia, India, and the Rest of World. Additionally, it provides SWOT, investment analyses, and strategic guidance for market players using primary and secondary research.

Founded in 1888 in Cheltenham, H H Martyn & Co became a major employer known for diverse craftsmanship. The firm produced ironwork, statues, and architectural features for prestigious global projects like the Marble Arch gates, Buckingham Palace, the Cenotaph, and Selfridges. Martyn's also fitted out over 100 ocean liners, including the Titanic. During WWI, it began manufacturing military aircraft, spawning the Gloster Aircraft Company. Additionally, the firm contributed to Sir Henry Segrave's land speed record car and manufactured motor vehicles. Bought by Maples in the mid-1930s, Martyn's closed in 1971 due to post-war recession and the decline of British shipbuilding.

On September 9, 2020, Amazon.com, Inc.'s Board of Directors elected General (Ret.) Keith B. Alexander as a director and appointed him to the Audit Committee. Gen. Alexander is Co-CEO, President, and Chairman of IronNet Cybersecurity, Inc., and previously served as Commander of U.S. Cyber Command and Director of the NSA. He was granted a restricted stock unit award for 288 shares, vesting in three annual installments starting November 15, 2021, and entered into a standard director indemnification agreement.

In 1826, Captain Jones negotiated the first Hawaiian treaty with a foreign power, the US, which was unratified but considered morally binding. In 1829, Captain Finch delivered a letter from the US President urging peace and respect for Hawaiian laws. Between 1831 and 1839, US naval vessels intervened in Hawaiian affairs, including protecting Catholic converts from persecution by the native government. In 1839, French commander Laplace forced a treaty on Hawaii for Catholic protection by threatening hostilities. Following British consul Charlton's complaints, a forced treaty was negotiated in 1836. In 1843, Lord George Paulet seized the islands and forced a cession from King Kamehameha III. US Commodore Kearney protested the cession, and Rear-Admiral Thomas later disavowed Paulet's actions and restored the Hawaiian flag.

The passage proposes a Bayesian framework for community detection in network data using recursive bipartitioning. This method addresses the inconsistency of pre-determining the number of communities by recursively dividing the network into two sub-networks until a stopping rule is met. The framework uses the Bayes factor as a stopping rule to evaluate the presence of community structure. It is applied to three network models: stochastic block models, edge exchangeable models, and latent space models. The authors establish the consistency of this method under the stochastic block model using Erdős-Rényi modularity and detail Gibbs sampling algorithms for inference.

Progress Software Corporation held its Q3 2025 earnings call on September 29, 2025. Michael Micciche opened the call, introducing CEO Yogesh Gupta and CFO Anthony Folger. He issued a safe harbor statement regarding forward-looking risks and noted that financial figures would be non-GAAP unless otherwise indicated. The passage also includes unrelated financial article headlines and stock chart data.

A study published in Nature reveals that WASP-121b, a hot Jupiter exoplanet 880 light-years away, has a stratosphere where temperature increases with altitude. Using NASA's Hubble Space Telescope, researchers detected glowing water molecule signatures indicating this atmospheric layer, which reaches 2,500 degrees Celsius. This is the strongest evidence of an exoplanet stratosphere to date. The discovery allows scientists to compare exoplanet atmospheres with our solar system and serves as a technical milestone toward eventually studying Earth-like exoplanets for signs of life using future observatories.

Winthrop University will receive $1.1 million from a $20 million National Science Foundation grant shared among 10 South Carolina institutions for complex materials research. The funding supports 36 summer student research experiences, faculty research, and $330,000 for capital equipment. Led by Maria Gelabert, researchers will study electronic, optical, and biomaterials for applications including lasers, water treatment, and regenerative medicine. The initiative, MADE in SC, is managed by the state's EPSCoR office. Winthrop will also host two-week summer teacher workshops for high school outreach.

The NHS Patient Charter outlines patients' legal rights, NHS pledges, and patient responsibilities. It guarantees access to free, equal, and timely care, alongside rights to safe, high-quality treatment, NICE-recommended medicines, informed consent, privacy, and choice. Patients also have the right to complain and receive compensation if harmed. In return, patients must look after their health, treat staff with respect, and follow treatment plans. The Charter serves as a partnership, balancing patient empowerment with shared responsibility during times of NHS strain.

Coach Sutter addresses the team's fatigue after a lengthy series against Chicago, hoping for a recharge. He notes recent lineup changes and the inexperience of players in their first Stanley Cup Final. Sutter praises Kyle's energetic performance and Mike Richards' winning mindset and role acceptance. He mentions Jonathan's focus and identifies areas for a young player's improvement, such as ice time management and nutrition. Additionally, Sutter compares the atmospheres of Manhattan Beach and Madison Square Garden, discusses defensive changes involving Willie Mitchell, Greener, and Drew, and details first-period line adjustments made because several players, including Jeff, Trevor, Stolly, and Kopy, lacked their game.

The Average True Range (ATR) is a volatility indicator developed by J. Welles Wilder Jr., typically used for stop-loss orders and position sizing. Calculated as a 14-day moving average, it was applied to SPY data using Python's `pandas_ta` library. A backtested strategy holding the asset during high volatility and selling during low volatility performed better when adjusted for risk but had similar drawdowns to buy-and-hold. The author concludes ATR alone yields unpromising results but may perform better combined with other indicators.

A University of Bristol study reveals that chloroplasts split from their cyanobacterial ancestors over 2.1 billion years ago in low salinity environments. The symbiotic relationship with a eukaryotic host took another 200 million years to form. The research indicates complex organisms like algae first evolved in freshwater before colonizing marine environments around 800-750 million years ago, which has significant implications for understanding the carbon cycle.

The neo-Nazi website Daily Stormer, founded by Andrew Anglin, was dropped by its domain registrar GoDaddy after publishing an article mocking Heather Heyer, a victim of the Charlottesville car attack, citing potential incitement of violence. The site briefly moved to Google Domains, which also terminated the registration for violating terms of service. The site's web host remains obscured by Cloudflare, a company previously criticized for forwarding complainants' information to Anglin. Additionally, the Daily Stormer faced a brief hacking claim by Anonymous, though Anglin stated he regained control. Anglin is currently facing a lawsuit from the Southern Poverty Law Center for a harassment campaign against Tanya Gersh. Anglin has not participated in the lawsuit, his whereabouts are unknown, and a successful suit could result in his assets being seized and the site shutting down.

This retrospective cohort study at Mulago National Referral Hospital in Uganda evaluated the immediate outcomes and direct costs of managing 267 children admitted with clinical measles in 2018. The median patient age was 1.0 year, and the median hospital stay was 4.0 days. Mortality was 11.3%, with severe pneumonia being the most common complication. The average direct healthcare cost per patient was $33.13 USD, while non-healthcare overhead costs averaged $81.37 USD, totaling $114.50 USD per case. Higher costs were associated with male gender, comorbidities, prolonged hospital stays, and mortality. The study concludes that the high costs and mortality rates emphasize the need to promote measles immunization.

On August 17, NASA will broadcast a six-hour spacewalk starting at 10:00 am EDT. Russian cosmonauts Fyodor Yurchikhin and Sergey Ryazanskiy will exit the ISS at 10:45 am to deploy five nanosatellites, including one testing a 3D-printed casing and another commemorating Russian space anniversaries. They will also collect residue samples and install new handrails and struts. This is Expedition 52's only spacewalk and one of the longest this year, following Peggy Whitson's record-breaking 7-hour, 4-minute spacewalk in March.

Ten people died and fifteen were injured in a deliberate van attack in Toronto. One victim, Anne-Marie D'Amico, was identified. Suspect Alex Minassian, 25, was arrested and faces court. Police are investigating the motive and seeking witnesses to identify remaining victims.

The present disclosure provides a recommendation model training method and apparatus to improve model performance in big data applications. The method selects positive samples from a sample set and adds them to a training set. It calculates sampling probabilities for negative samples using a preset algorithm based on one or more of three rules: negative correlation with the score difference between positive and negative samples, negative correlation with the vector distance between their eigenvectors, and positive correlation with the variation of a ranking indicator after exchanging their rankings. Negative samples are selected based on these probabilities, added to the training set, and used to train the recommendation model. The trained model generates estimated scores for subsequent samples, enabling iterative training and faster convergence. The apparatus includes first and second sampling units and a training unit to perform these operations.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere architecture and TSMC 7nm process, introduces significant advancements for AI and HPC workloads. It features 108 Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs) and 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, supporting data types including TF32, BF16, FP64, INT8, and Binary. Fine-grained structured sparsity using a 2:4 pattern doubles compute throughput by skipping zero-value computations. 

The A100 improves memory architecture with 40 GB of HBM2 DRAM providing 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, and a 40 MB L2 cache enhanced by compute data compression and L2 residency controls. Each SM includes 192 KB of combined L1 data cache and shared memory. New asynchronous copy and hardware-accelerated barrier instructions optimize data movement directly from global to shared memory, bypassing the register file to improve efficiency. 

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology partitions a single A100 into up to seven isolated GPU instances, providing dedicated compute, L2 cache, and memory resources for multi-tenant environments. The GPU utilizes third-generation NVLink (600 GB/sec total bandwidth) and PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV for high-speed interconnects and virtualization. 

Additional hardware features include five NVDEC units, an NVJPG decode engine, and an Optical Flow Accelerator. CUDA 11 supports these advancements with Task Graph acceleration, asynchronous barriers, and cooperative groups. The A100 powers the DGX A100 system, delivering 5 PFLOPS of performance and scaling efficiently for large-scale AI and HPC clusters.

The passage details the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol, outlining communication mechanisms between guests and hypervisors. It describes MSR protocol functions for CPUID requests, AP reset holds, GHCB GPA registration, page state changes, VMPL requests, and guest termination. The document provides examples of GHCB negotiation and VMGEXIT processing for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests. It defines Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) events, including standard processing, IOIO, MSR, MMIO, page state changes, SNP guest requests, AP creation, #HV doorbell page management, #HV timers, IPIs, and Secure AVIC. Additionally, it addresses SMP booting under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP, detailing AP reset hold mechanisms and AP creation features. Finally, it specifies the configuration and behavior of the #HV doorbell page for Restricted Injection, detailing how hosts and guests manage interrupt presentation, acknowledgement, and end-of-interrupt (EOI) cycles.

On February 8, 2022, NVIDIA, SoftBank, and SVF Holdco mutually terminated the September 13, 2020 Share Purchase Agreement to acquire Arm Limited due to significant regulatory challenges. Sellers retain the $1.25 billion prepayment, and NVIDIA retains its 20-year Arm license. NVIDIA will record a $1.36 billion charge in Q1 fiscal year 2023, inclusive of the prepayment.

The "High/Low" zone offense combines an outside three-player passing attack with an inside high/low rotation. It can be initiated from almost any alignment and creates matchup problems for zone defenses, leading to open outside shots when the defense collapses. Its basic continuity involves entry passes to the wing, feeding the post rolling to the basket or flashing to the middle, and initiating ball reversals to the weakside. Post roll and high post flash options provide scoring, passing, or kick-out opportunities. The offense can be initiated using various entries, including Dribble Clear, 1-4 Slice, Mid Screen, and Horns. Furthermore, quick-hitting set plays such as Pin Down, Weakside Double, and Vegas can be used to prevent rushed shots late in the clock or following timeouts.

Charlie Tillett, a former CFO and entrepreneur, presents a guide on creating financial plans for startups. He emphasizes that financials act as a scoreboard, help identify key business drivers, and manage cash flow. Tillett explains the venture capital perspective, noting that VCs seek 3x to 5x returns over a 5-7 year horizon and require significant ownership, which dilutes founders through subsequent funding rounds and employee option pools. He advises building financial models from the bottom up rather than using automated software, using an income statement approach to evaluate business models. Tillett provides industry benchmarks for gross margins, R&D, and G&A expenses, highlighting that staffing typically consumes 50-66% of costs. He also covers equity distribution, recommending vesting schedules for all team members to incentivize future work, and discusses the importance of hiring an experienced CFO when raising venture capital.

This paper presents a Proof-of-Concept (PoC) for analyzing Instant Messaging App (IMA) data in criminal investigations using Knowledge Graphs (KGs), speech-to-text, and NLP. Developed within an Italian national project, the solution addresses the time-consuming nature of analyzing seized mobile phone data. The pipeline extracts chat dumps into a Neo4j property graph, uses Whisper to transcribe audio messages, and employs a Named Entity Recognition and Linking (NEEL) pipeline to extract and link entities. Two interfaces were developed: Neo4j's native UI for graph visualization and DAVE for faceted search and document exploration. Tested on two real investigations (fraud and corruption), the system successfully processed chats and linked entities. Investigators provided positive feedback, particularly on graph visualizations and audio transcriptions, though limitations in NER accuracy and query complexity remain, prompting future work in fine-tuning, interface development, and multimedia enrichment.

AQTWM, Inc. (Aqua Terra) filed a preliminary prospectus for an initial public offering of common shares in Canada, excluding Quebec. Co-led by TD Securities, Canaccord Genuity, and RBC Capital Markets, the offering's details are undetermined and its completion is not assured. The securities are not offered in the U.S. Aqua Terra is an oilfield water management and logistics company serving Canadian and U.S. onshore oil and gas producers across multiple hydrocarbon regions.

Top drugmakers are meeting with Donald Trump Jr. and administration officials at a summit hosted by BlinkRx, a company positioned to benefit from a shift to direct-to-consumer drug sales. Separately, Pfizer’s agreement with the Trump administration to lower drug prices has prompted other companies to scramble for their own deals, though the actual impact on lowering prices remains unknown. The passage also lists various industry headlines, including setbacks for Sarepta and Medicare price negotiations.

The lecture discusses coding for bandwidth-limited, additive white Gaussian noise channels, focusing on multi-level codes in Euclidean space. The probability of error is estimated using a union-bound that separates coding gain from the lattice and shaping gain from the region, normalized by SNR.

Shaping uses an n-sphere as the optimum region, yielding a maximum theoretical gain of 1.53 dB. Practical techniques like shell mapping, used in the V.34 modem, achieve about 1 dB of this gain.

Lattices provide coding gain, with densest known lattices identified in various dimensions (e.g., D4, E8, Barnes-Wall, and the Leech lattice). Although nominal coding gain increases with dimension, the rising number of nearest neighbors limits the effective coding gain to approximately 4 dB.

Trellis codes, introduced by Ungerboeck, expand the constellation rather than the bandwidth. Using set partitioning and convolutional codes, a simple 4-state code achieves 3 dB gain, while higher-state codes can reach 5-6 dB. Four-dimensional trellis codes, such as the Wei code, reduce constellation expansion and are used in V.34 and ADSL standards.

To approach the Shannon limit, multi-level coding and Bit-Interleaved Coded Modulation (BICM) are presented. The lecture concludes that coding for traditional channels is a mature field close to the Shannon limit, with future research focusing on multi-user networks and data compression.

The lecture presents thesis research on manufacturing microfluidic devices using polymers via hot embossing. Polymers are chosen for being cheap, transparent, and mechanically tough. The hot embossing process involves heating a thermoplastic above its glass transition temperature, pressing a microfabricated stamp into it, cooling it, and removing the stamp. Key process parameters include temperature, load, and hold times. The research aims to develop efficient modeling tools to predict embossing outcomes and address pattern-dependent non-uniformity. A linear elastic model successfully predicted topography for short hold times, while a linear dashpot was added to account for plastic flow during longer holds. De-molding challenges, such as differential thermal contraction causing ridges or splaying, can be mitigated by carefully controlling the de-molding temperature. The lecture concludes with a Q&A on course logistics and project optimization strategies.

UNC Chapel Hill reinstated professor Dwayne Dixon after a threat assessment found no policy violations or threats. Dixon, placed on leave following allegations, is a gun rights advocate who has counterprotested alt-right rallies. A Turning Point USA spokesperson called for his firing over these affiliations.

The gold/silver ratio measures the price relationship between the two metals, calculated by dividing the gold price by the silver price. Historically fixed by governments, it now floats. Traders use it primarily for mean-reversion strategies, buying silver and shorting gold when the ratio is high, and vice versa when low, using futures, options, or ETFs. However, the authors' backtests, including a pair trade strategy, showed flat or poor performance. They concluded they could not find a robust, profitable trading strategy using the ratio for either equities or the metals themselves.

Hetzner, South Africa's largest specialist hosting company, now peers directly at NAP Africa in Isando via a 10Gbps circuit. Along with existing NAP Africa Cape Town and JINX connections, Hetzner routes over 65% of its local traffic through these exchange points. Hetzner advocates for settlement-free peering to reduce costs, lower latency, and increase resilience. The company contributes over 4Gbps of traffic and peers with major operators like Telkom, MTN, and Google. Hetzner operates a carrier-neutral data centre in Samrand and invites other network operators to establish peering.

The author opposes a 35-storey development proposal in North Delta, arguing it violates the North Delta Area Plan and Cougar Creek ISMP. The project fails to provide adequate tree preservation, public amenities, and rainwater infiltration due to its underground parking, increasing flood and drought risks. The author states highrises encourage land speculation rather than providing actual housing. The proposal should only be considered if the developer reduces the underground footprint to allow at least 15% permeable open space for trees and infiltration. The author recommends mandating a 15% permeable land set-aside for all multi-family developments to ensure long-term environmental sustainability.

The Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) Specification outlines attestation, resiliency, and update procedures for AMD firmware. Update packages must verify existing firmware versions to prevent out-of-sync states and avoid forced resets. Patches are non-persistent across reboots and can be applied during or after OS boot. Issuing SFS commands requires specific memory alignment and a customer-provided deployment agent to package signatures and communicate with ASP firmware via TEE mailbox interfaces. The ASP verifies customer and AMD signatures, executes the patch, updates patch levels, and returns status. SFS packages must match specific firmware versions and are designed to run in parallel with system traffic to minimize performance impact. While most updates require no system restart, SEV/SEV-ES virtual machines must restart for SEV firmware updates, whereas SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue operating.

Apple Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2018, reports a 17% year-over-year increase in net sales to $53.3 billion and net income of $11.5 billion. For the nine months ended June 30, 2018, net sales grew 15% to $202.7 billion, with net income of $45.4 billion. Growth was primarily driven by higher iPhone and Services net sales, while Mac and iPad net sales declined. During the quarter, Apple repurchased $20.0 billion of common stock and paid $3.7 billion in dividends. The company's total assets stood at $349.2 billion. The U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act lowered Apple's statutory federal income tax rate to 21% and imposed a deemed repatriation tax, resulting in a reduced provisional tax estimate.

This paper introduces EqDiff-CT, a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) for synthesizing CT images from CBCT scans in head and neck imaging. While CBCT offers daily image guidance, it suffers from artifacts and inconsistent Hounsfield Unit values, whereas planning CTs cannot reflect daily anatomical changes. Existing synthetic CT generation methods, including deformable image registration, GANs, and CNNs, face limitations such as instability, hallucinated structures, and lack of interpretability. To address these issues, the proposed framework utilizes a group-equivariant, attention-enhanced, time-conditioned U-Net denoiser trained with a non-adversarial objective combining mean square error and structural similarity index. Evaluated on the SynthRAD2025 Head & Neck dataset, the model outperforms baseline diffusion and CycleGAN models across multiple metrics while preserving critical anatomical structures. The paper also outlines the mathematical formulation of the conditional DDPM, detailing the forward diffusion and reverse sampling processes.

CDC reports U.S. illnesses from mosquito, tick, and flea bites tripled since 2004. Venice, CA, is vulnerable due to still waters. West Nile Virus (WNV), spread by mosquitoes feeding on infected birds, is endemic in Los Angeles County. While 80% of infected humans show no symptoms, 20% experience mild symptoms, and less than 1% develop severe neurological issues. Local agencies manage standing water to prevent breeding. Residents are advised to use insect repellent and eliminate standing water in yards.

The speaker expects Dallas to improve after a first-game loss and stresses focusing on current preparation rather than past series. Anticipating a more aggressive Dallas, the team must limit the time and space of key players like Modano, Hull, and Nieuwendyk by having forwards and defense work in unison. Winning the next game to lead 2-0 is crucial to pressure Dallas. The speaker notes a player's improved defensive play and reports the team is mostly healthy, with only one minor casualty. He explains that playoff rivalries are built through competition and that playing in June indicates a deep playoff run. The speaker criticizes the team's poor puck decisions and lack of penetration, noting Brian tried to do too much, leading to turnovers. Although the team played poorly, they remained close. He mentions a missed offside call before a Dallas goal but dismisses it as the reason for the loss. With the series tied 1-1, the speaker rejects panic, noting the team plays well with adversity and must stick to their game plan in Dallas.
To celebrate the Aug. 21 solar eclipse, the Weston Public Library will distribute free viewers, host a projector craft, and stream NASA's coverage. Weston will see 70% coverage.

Researchers developed a model to interpret potential sources of influenza A H5 RNA in wastewater, prompted by H5N1 outbreaks in birds and cattle. They retrospectively tested biobanked wastewater solids from a California publicly owned treatment works (September 2023–May 2024) for total IAV and H1, H3, and H5 subtypes. The study aims to identify the timing of the first H5 detection and estimate theoretical contributions from humans, cow milk, poultry feces, and wildfowl feces using a mass balance model.

The SteelSeries Arctis GameBuds are currently discounted to $128 on Amazon. These highly rated earbuds are compatible with Xbox, PlayStation, Switch, PC, and smartphones. They feature a 2.4GHz USB-C dongle, Bluetooth, 40-hour total battery life with the case, active noise-canceling, and game-specific equalizer settings via a mobile app. Their comfortable fit, sound isolation, and physical buttons make them suitable for gaming and everyday use.

James Harden scored an NBA-record 60 points in a triple-double, leading the short-handed Houston Rockets to a 114-107 victory over the Orlando Magic. Harden, who also had 10 rebounds and 11 assists, broke Calvin Murphy's 1978 Houston single-game scoring record of 57 points. Playing a season-high 46 minutes due to injuries to Chris Paul, Trevor Ariza, and Eric Gordon, Harden scored 18 fourth-quarter points, including a four-point play to reach 60. Hezonja and Speights led the Magic with 17 points each. Aaron Gordon missed the game for Orlando with a hip injury.

Researchers synthesized two metal inorganic-organic complex (MIOC) crystals, MIOC-4 and MIOC-7, by introducing chloride into zeolitic imidazolate frameworks (ZIFs). This replaced coordination bonds with hydrogen bonds, lowering the melting barrier to enable the formation of bulk MIOC glasses. MIOC-7, featuring benzimidazole ligands, exhibited higher thermal stability and glass transition temperatures due to steric hindrance and π-π interactions. Mixed-ligand synthesis produced binary mixed-crystals with tunable melting and glass transition temperatures. Structural analysis showed that melting initiates with the slippage and breaking of hydrogen bonds, while short-range coordination bonds remain intact in the glass. The ligand-tuning strategy was successfully expanded to other metals (Co, Cu) and anions (SCN-). Furthermore, MIOC-7 glass demonstrated enhanced, excitation-dependent photoluminescence compared to its crystalline form, indicating potential for anti-counterfeiting applications.

This application describes a networked exercise system, such as a treadmill, that provides streaming and on-demand exercise classes with social, competitive, and gamification features. The treadmill includes a deck with a continuous track and slats, motors for adjusting incline and speed, and an upper assembly with posts, arms, and crossbars. It features separate rotary or linear controls for different functions, which provide tactile, audible, and visual feedback. Sensors measure various machine and user performance metrics. The system incorporates a display and user interface that allows users to browse live and archived classes, view performance data, and interact with instructors and other users.

Successful early offense and press break execution requires coaching players, not systems, using the "Whole-Part-Whole" method. Coaching objectives focus on developing confidence, quick ball advancement, and transitioning into early offense. The teaching method involves demonstrating roles, walking through options, using progressive breakdown drills, and practicing at game speed against tough defense. Game strategies emphasize tenacious defense, breaking on every possession, and scouting opponents. Additionally, applying immediate defensive pressure can disrupt an opponent's early offense and create steals.

Socket 940 specifications detail its mechanical, material, marking, and electrical requirements. The LCP (UL 94 V-0) base and cover maintain a flatness under 0.25 mm and cover thickness ≤1.17 mm. A stainless steel actuation lever requires <3.6 kgf to actuate, with insertion/extraction forces ≤2 kgf when open and ≥0.013 kgf per pin when closed. Pin displacement is <1.0 mm, and the socket withstands 50 actuation cycles. Contacts are high-strength copper alloy plated with 1.27-µm nickel and 0.76-µm gold. SMT solder balls are 0.76 mm tin/lead with 0.20 mm co-planarity. Required markings include the socket ID, orientation symbols, UL symbol, and lot traceability. Electrical specs include a 1.5 A current rating per contact, circuit resistance ≤25 mΩ, self-inductance <4 nH, capacitance <1 pF, and differential impedance of 100 Ω ±10%. The socket requires a dielectric withstanding voltage ≥650 Vac and insulation resistance ≥1000 MΩ.

The speaker highlights a player's mental resilience and calm demeanor after facing adversity. They compare Bergeron and Ryan O'Reilly, noting their strong face-off skills and two-way play. The speaker also observes similarities between the two teams, such as strong defense, physical forechecking, and mobile defensemen. The Trump administration's plan to hire hundreds of federal prosecutors is off to a slow start, with new hires down by more than half compared to previous years. Despite this, the Justice Department maintains high hiring standards, recruiting from top-tier law schools and prominent firms. The NVIDIA GA10x Ampere architecture introduces significant performance and feature improvements over the prior Turing generation. It enhances Async Compute to process RT Core, graphics, and compute workloads concurrently. Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection rates and add an Interpolate Triangle Position unit to accelerate ray-traced motion blur. Third-generation Tensor Cores introduce TF32 and BF16 data types and Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity, doubling matrix throughput and enhancing DLSS for 8K gaming. 

The architecture debuts GDDR6X memory utilizing PAM4 signaling to achieve up to 936 GB/sec bandwidth, alongside Error Detection and Replay (EDR) for memory overclocking. NVIDIA RTX IO, paired with Microsoft's DirectStorage API, enables GPU-based lossless decompression to bypass CPU storage bottlenecks. The display engine supports HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a for high-resolution, high-refresh-rate outputs. Additionally, the architecture includes a 5th-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode and a 7th-generation NVENC. Specific GPUs include the GeForce RTX 3090 and 3070 for consumer gaming, and the NVIDIA A40 and RTX A6000 for data center and professional workloads, featuring up to 48GB of memory, PCIe Gen4, NVLink scalability, and virtualization support.

The ADX (Average Directional Movement Index), developed by Welles Wilder in 1978, measures trend strength on a 0 to 100 scale. Backtesting shows that stand-alone ADX strategies, such as DI+/DI- crossovers and breakouts, produce moderate returns on the S&P 500 but are insufficient on their own. However, ADX performs significantly better when used as a filter alongside other indicators. Combining ADX with an unrevealed mean-revertive indicator reduces market exposure, increases the profit factor, and yields stronger returns on the S&P 500 and Nasdaq. Ultimately, while ADX is a lagging indicator, it is versatile and adds the most value when supplementing other trading strategies.

The speaker discusses a hockey game, highlighting an overtime play where they passed to a teammate for the deciding goal. They express excitement to return to their supportive hockey town. The speaker notes that penalties hurt their momentum and stresses the need to stay out of the box against the opponent's elite power play. They emphasize quick changes, intensity, and attention to detail. Finally, they express confidence in their roster's depth to step up despite losing key players.

A study by Stanford, Harvard, and the Census Bureau found that in 99% of U.S. neighborhoods, black boys earn less in adulthood than white boys from similar backgrounds. Black and Native American children have the lowest upward economic mobility, while whites and Asians have the highest. The racial income gap persists even among the top 1% of earners and is primarily driven by disparities between black and white men. Neighborhoods impact outcomes, but the gap is larger in affluent areas. Parity occurs in areas with low white racial bias and a high presence of black fathers. Researchers suggest historical experiences may contribute to these disparities.

Praising Berliners' historical courage against tyranny, the speaker urges a "new civil courage" to build a united, democratic, and prosperous Europe. In 2016, the author's dividend growth retirement portfolio gained 15%, outperforming the S&P 500's 11.66% return every month. The portfolio grew from 27 to 35 companies through eight new purchases and one sale. Top performers included Chevron, JPMorgan, and AT&T, while Gilead Sciences and CVS Health were the biggest losers. This paper introduces the grouped satisficing path, extending the "win-stay, lose-shift" principle to player groups in multi-agent reinforcement learning. The study analyzes the topological properties of this path and establishes sufficient conditions for its existence. The main theorem proves that if a pure strategy game has a convex and compact strategy set, a continuous and partially analytic payoff function, and every sub-game has an equilibrium, a finite-length grouped satisficing path exists from any initial joint strategy to an equilibrium. These findings are applied to continuous games, N-player games, and finite-state Markov games, guaranteeing the existence of satisficing paths to mixed equilibria in these scenarios.

Virtual education provides benefits such as schedule flexibility, individualized instruction, credit recovery, and accommodations for special needs, while presenting challenges like internet access issues, student isolation, and maintaining engagement. A study of Indiana school superintendents and virtual program administrators used surveys and interviews to examine these factors, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic. 

The pandemic was the primary factor driving the implementation and maintenance of virtual programs. Both groups identified maintaining enrollment during the pandemic, credit recovery, and learner flexibility as the top benefits. The most frequently cited challenges were student engagement, ensuring curriculum and instruction quality, and staffing. 

Interviews highlighted the pandemic's impact on school corporations, teachers, and students. Corporations faced financial concerns over enrollment loss and accelerated technology plans. Teachers experienced stress and a lack of professional development, though they improved their technology skills. Students struggled with social-emotional issues, attendance, and engagement, requiring significant parental support. The study concludes that while the pandemic spurred the rapid growth of virtual education in Indiana, the benefits and challenges observed align with historical trends in virtual learning.

E-mini futures are electronically traded, smaller-sized futures contracts created by the CME in 1997, enabling retail investors to trade indexes, commodities, and currencies with leverage. They require a margin, such as the $10,000 minimum for the S&P 500, though more capital is recommended to cover potential losses. A backtested strategy on the S&P 500 e-mini showed a 79% win ratio and remained profitable during the 2022 bear market. The passage advises against scalping due to high competition and costs, emphasizing that success requires a disciplined, backtested trading plan. It also addresses FAQs regarding trading costs, expiration settlements, day trading rules, and inherent risks like volatility and leverage.

The lecture covers theoretical models of protein folding and interlocked 3D chains. In the HP (Hydrophobic-Hydrophilic) model of protein folding, proteins are represented as chains of H and P nodes folded on a lattice. The goal is to maximize adjacent H-H bonds, as hydrophobic nodes cluster inside. Finding the optimal fold is NP-hard, but a 1/3 approximation algorithm exists for the 2D square lattice using node parity. Unique optimal foldings also exist for certain chain lengths. Protein design, or creating a sequence to fold into a target shape, is proposed as an open problem.

The second topic, interlocked 3D chains, relates to Lubiw's problem: determining the minimum cuts needed to unlock a chain, currently bounded between n/4 and n/2. The lecture details conditions for chain separability and interlocking. While 2-chains (hairpins) and combinations with 3- or 4-chains generally separate, a 3-chain and 4-chain can interlock, as can an 11-chain and a 2-chain. Separability is proven using scaling techniques, whereas interlocking relies on topological arguments. These interlocked chains serve as rigid infrastructure in PSPACE-completeness proofs for chain reconfiguration, though the complexity of unfolding from a straight configuration remains open.

For Amazon Big Deal Days on October 7 and 8, WIRED editors independently selected and personally tested various deals under $100 for Prime members. The list includes electronics, smart home devices, kitchen appliances, pet accessories, and personal care items.

This passage examines the digital transformation of education in Thailand, aligned with the "Digital Thailand 4.0" strategy and accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic. Using bibliometric analysis, the research identifies essential competencies for educators to become digital transformation leaders. The study outlines five key components: Digital Literacy (foundational technology skills), Digital Readiness (organizational and individual preparedness), Digital Culture (embracing technology, hybrid learning, and data security), Digital Mindset (adopting design thinking and innovation), and Digital Leadership (rethinking and reinventing practices to guide change). The transition to Education 4.0 shifts traditional teaching toward online, project-based, and innovation-driven learning. The passage concludes that while this digital transformation is irreversible, technology cannot replace good teachers; rather, educators must adapt to effectively guide students and institutions into the digital era.

Songyang Academy, with over 1,500 years of history, evolved from a Buddhist temple into one of China's four major academies. It experienced fluctuations through various dynasties, flourishing during the Song Dynasty before declining due to wars and political changes. The academy's educational philosophy aligns with modern general education by emphasizing moral education, all-round development, the unity of knowledge and action, autonomous learning, and mutual questioning. It features a flat management structure involving students. The study concludes that integrating Songyang Academy's traditional concepts with modern education can provide valuable methods for cultivating well-rounded talents.

The passage details Texas Instruments' support resources, trademarks, and ESD handling precautions. It provides a revision history from November 2024 to April 2025, highlighting updates to device features, electrical characteristics, and functional descriptions, including timers, UART, SPI, and ADCs. Additionally, it includes mechanical, packaging, and orderable information, along with soldering guidelines, part marking details, and legal disclaimers.

Kobe University researchers discovered that orchids rely on wood-decaying fungi to germinate, obtaining carbon from rotting logs. Seedlings of four studied orchid species grew exclusively near deadwood, forming specific fungal partnerships that mirror those of adult orchids with coral-shaped rhizomes. This finding reveals a hidden carbon pathway in forest ecosystems, explains the evolution of fully fungus-dependent orchids, and indicates that wild orchid conservation requires protecting deadwood and its fungi.

This study examined the attitudes of 30 elementary teachers toward inclusive education in Liloan District, Cebu Province, Philippines, using a descriptive correlational design and a Modified STATIC survey. The theoretical framework incorporated the Theory of Planned Behavior, Bronfenbrenner's Ecological Systems Theory, and Bandura's Social Learning Theory. 

Results indicated that while most teachers had limited experience and introductory training in inclusive education, they held positive attitudes regarding the advantages, professional issues, and philosophical aspects of inclusion. However, they expressed neutral views on logistical concerns, citing inadequate resources and support. Statistical tests found no significant relationship between the teachers' demographic profiles and their attitudes toward inclusion. 

The study concluded that while foundational philosophical support for inclusion exists, targeted professional development, improved logistical resources, smaller class sizes, and multi-level support systems are necessary to translate these positive attitudes into sustainable, long-term inclusive practices and prevent teacher burnout.

Students returned to Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School under heavy security and emotional support following the February 14 shooting that killed 17 people. Students expressed nervousness but also pride in their peers' gun control activism. Concurrently, Dick's Sporting Goods announced it would stop selling assault-style rifles and restrict gun sales to individuals 21 and older. In Florida's legislature, committees advanced a school-safety bill raising the minimum age for long gun purchases to 21 and allowing trained, deputized teachers to carry concealed weapons. The arming provision is opposed by the school superintendent and some students, while some victims' parents urged its passage. An NRA lobbyist opposed the gun restrictions, and Governor Rick Scott pushed for a bill before the legislative session ends on March 9.

The speaker feels honored by a recent recognition, despite missing a rookie trophy nomination. He delayed joining the Flyers for a year to prepare in Europe. Motivated by veteran players, he overcame a slow start in his first five games as his confidence and performance improved.

The MSPM0 MCU data sheet details the device's peripherals and architecture. It features up to 128KB SRAM divided into two banks with ECC/parity options and write-execute mutual exclusion. Analog peripherals include 12-bit ADCs, a DAC, comparators, a temperature sensor, and a shared VREF module. Communication interfaces comprise UART, I2C, SPI, and CAN-FD. The device incorporates general-purpose and advanced timers, watchdogs (IWDT, WWDT), an RTC, and a math accelerator. Security is supported via AES-128/256, TRNG, a Keystore, and CRC modules. The document also outlines application layout requirements, such as decoupling capacitors and pull-up resistors, alongside device nomenclature, development tools, revision history, and mechanical packaging information.

The author notes their daughter has the skills for a literature professor career but advises against it due to a severe shortage of full-time academic jobs and struggles in related fields like journalism and publishing. Instead, the author encourages her interest in librarianship and asks readers for advice on guiding talented liberal arts students.

A recent paper analyzed the hypothetical impact of a 40 percent budget cut to the National Institutes of Health (NIH) by examining past grants and FDA drug approvals. Researchers found that over half of the drugs approved in the 21st century are linked to research that would have been at risk under a smaller budget. Of 557 approved drugs studied, 14 directly cited at-risk NIH grants, while 59 percent indirectly cited NIH-funded research. The study concluded that drugs linked to at-risk research are just as significant as unlinked ones, frequently receiving FDA priority reviews and possessing higher market values. The authors noted these findings represent a conservative estimate, as they did not account for indirect research pathways.

The court affirmed the dismissal of Brian O’Loughlin’s defamation lawsuit against the Patrolmen’s Benevolent Association and its president, Phil Caruso. O’Loughlin sued after Caruso wrote in a PBA publication that O’Loughlin and others who requested refunds of a $20 memorial contribution had "no feelings" and were "a disgrace." The court ruled these statements were vague, indefinite expressions of pure opinion that cannot be objectively proven true or false, and therefore are not actionable defamation.

Global population growth drives cereal production and pesticide use, particularly herbicides. While crop rotation improves soil and yields, crop protection chemicals negatively impact the environment, human health, and soil productivity. The market includes insecticides, herbicides, and fungicides, with herbicides dominating due to low cost and R&D. Geographically, North America leads, followed by Asia Pacific and Europe, with Asia Pacific expected to grow rapidly. The market features global, regional, and local vendors competing on price, quality, and innovation.

The global vertical farming market, growing stacked crops without soil in controlled environments, is projected to reach USD 6 billion by 2022 at a 21% CAGR. Growth drivers include population increases and technology adoption, while high urban investments and energy consumption hinder it. North America holds the largest share, and Asia-Pacific is the fastest-growing region. The market is segmented by component, type, crop, and region.

Kayleigh Gray and her employer, Sign Build, donated 25 pairs of acrylic turtle doves to Royal Preston Hospital's Neo Natal Unit after it cared for her premature daughter. The doves are given to parents, with one staying with the baby and one taken home.

Tesla, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2022. Only 18% of American workers feel confident about a secure retirement. To ensure sufficient savings, individuals should take three steps. First, determine projected retirement income based on current savings rates, as saving 10% is no longer sufficient due to higher healthcare costs, low interest rates, and longer lifespans. Use online calculators to estimate total savings and combine this with Social Security benefits to see if it replaces 100% of current income. Second, monitor and minimize investment fees, as high fees drastically reduce total returns over time. Third, confirm correct asset allocation by balancing risk and return based on age, such as subtracting your age from 110 to find the percentage to invest in stocks. Following these steps can help ensure a substantial retirement nest egg.

An analysis by Notre Dame Law professor Derek Muller found that BigLaw and larger plaintiffs-side firms are shifting further left. In 2023-2024, 92.45% of their campaign contributions went to Democrats, up from a 6-1 ratio in 2017-2020. Contributions totaled about $52 million for Democrats and $4 million for Republicans. Cleary Gottlieb Steen & Hamilton had the highest percentage of Democratic contributions at 99.7%, while Nelson Mullins Riley & Scarborough had the lowest at 66.4%.

E-mini Russell 2000 Index futures are cash-settled financial derivatives trading on the CME Globex platform, representing $50 times the index value. They allow traders to speculate or hedge on U.S. small-cap stocks. Contracts follow quarterly cycles and terminate on the third Friday of the contract month. A trading strategy for these futures requires market timing and risk management; a backtested example is the Russell 2000 rebalance strategy, which buys after June 23rd and sells in early July. The passage introduces iMOOE, a physics-guided invariant learning framework for zero-shot out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization in partial differential equation (PDE) dynamics forecasting. Existing methods lack zero-shot OOD capabilities because they do not explicitly model the fundamental invariance principles across varying PDE dynamics. The authors propose a two-level PDE invariance principle: operator invariance, where elementary spatial operators remain invariant across domains, and compositionality invariance, where the aggregation method of these operators, physical parameters, and forcing terms is fixed.

To capture this invariance, iMOOE utilizes a mixture of operator experts (MOOE) architecture with parallel specialized neural operator experts and a fusion network. It is trained using a frequency-enriched invariant learning objective that includes maximal prediction, risk equality, and frequency enrichment losses to estimate PDE invariance from limited training domains. 

Experiments on five simulated PDE systems and real-world sea surface temperature data show that iMOOE achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot OOD forecasting performance, significantly reducing normalized mean squared error and Fourier root mean squared error. The framework is also compatible with diverse neural operators, consistently enhancing their OOD generalization.

This lecture discusses interacting quantum gases, focusing on Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) and their superfluid properties. The Bogoliubov approximation simplifies the interacting Hamiltonian by replacing the condensate operator with a macroscopic number, yielding a solvable model of non-interacting quasiparticles. This reveals a linear dispersion relation for low-energy phonon excitations and a quadratic one for high momenta. Interactions cause quantum depletion, where atoms occupy finite momentum states; this depletion is small in dilute cold gases but large in liquid helium.

Quasiparticle spectroscopy is performed using a stimulated Raman process with two laser beams to measure the dynamic structure factor and dispersion relation. For trapped, inhomogeneous condensates, the Gross-Pitaevskii equation describes the macroscopic wave function, incorporating a mean-field interaction term that flattens the density. In the Thomas-Fermi approximation, kinetic energy is neglected, showing the density follows the inverted trapping potential. The healing length defines the boundary scale where kinetic and interaction energies balance.

Adding angular momentum to a quantum fluid creates vortices—singularities with zero density and a 2π phase wrap. Multiply charged vortices are unstable and decay into singly charged ones, which repel each other and form hexagonal lattices.

To study strongly correlated systems, atoms are placed in optical lattices, which reduce kinetic energy. In the tight-binding limit, the system is described by the Bose-Hubbard model with tunneling (J) and on-site interaction (U) parameters. A mean-field decoupling approximation transforms the many-body problem into an effective single-site Hamiltonian. By applying perturbation theory in the superfluid order parameter, the transition between the superfluid state (J >> U) and the Mott insulator state (U >> J) is determined. The resulting phase diagram features Mott insulator lobes. These phenomena are observed experimentally through Bragg spectroscopy, time-of-flight interference patterns, and quantum gas microscopes.

This paper investigates using Large Language Models (LLMs) to detect and fix API misuses in data science libraries, which present unique challenges due to dynamic typing and complex data structures. The llama model achieved the highest detection F1-score (61.18%) and fix rate (51.28%). Few-shot prompting yielded mixed results across different models. DSCHECKER outperformed the existing LLMAPIDET tool, detecting approximately 35% more misuses. The authors also developed DSCHECKERagent, an agentic version that autonomously retrieves API documentation and variable information. While its performance was lower than DSCHECKER (48.65% F1-score, 39.47% fix rate), it demonstrates potential for real-world applications where prior misuse information is unavailable. The study concludes that LLMs, when provided with appropriate contextual information, are effective for detecting and fixing data-centric API misuses.

The lecture introduces additive energy, defined as the number of quadruples satisfying an additive relation in an Abelian group. While small doubling implies large additive energy, the converse is generally false. The Balog-Szemerédi-Gowers (BSG) theorem states that a set with large additive energy must contain a large subset with small doubling. A two-set version of this theorem is also presented and shown to imply the one-set version using the Ruzsa triangle inequality.

The proof of the BSG theorem is reduced to a graphical version involving restricted sumsets in dense bipartite graphs. This graphical version is proved using a "path of length 2 lemma," established via dependent random choice, and a "path of length 3 lemma." These lemmas demonstrate that large subsets of vertices exist where every pair is connected by many paths of length 3. This allows bounding the complete sumset of the subsets, proving the graphical BSG theorem and subsequently the additive BSG theorem. The core principle is transitioning from typical or partial additive structure to complete structure on large subsets.
