To protect against foreign dangers, the speaker advocates for fortifying coasts, maintaining adequate Army and Navy forces, and organizing the militia. Domestically, the speaker recommends internal improvements like roads and canals to strengthen the Union, and government support for domestic manufacturers to reduce reliance on foreign supplies. The speaker also emphasizes cultivating friendly relations with Indian tribes, managing public finances with economy and fidelity, and paying off the national debt.

Concluding, the speaker celebrates the unprecedented success and harmony of the nation, attributing it to republican principles. The speaker pledges to preserve peace, promote harmony, and follow the examples of previous administrations, relying on divine protection and the support of other government departments.

This qualitative study explores the perspectives of infectious disease diagnostics (IDD) stakeholders on the utility and barriers of implementing metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) for routine clinical use. While mNGS offers a culture-independent method for rapid pathogen detection, overcoming limitations of traditional methods, its clinical adoption remains slow. Through interviews with ten UK-based participants, five themes were identified: diagnostic choice, infrastructure, open data sharing, COVID-19, and communication. Major barriers to mNGS implementation include high costs, slow turnaround times, inadequate physical and digital infrastructure, lack of bioinformatics training, and challenges with accreditation and standardization. Conversely, the COVID-19 pandemic served as a proof of concept, demonstrating the public health benefits of genomic sequencing and building manufacturing capacity. Participants emphasized the need for equitable funding, decentralized local laboratories, improved intra- and interhospital communication, and collaboration between clinical, academic, and commercial sectors. The study concludes that addressing these drivers is essential to transition clinical microbiology into the next-generation sequencing era.

Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson, and Omar Yaghi won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). These highly porous structures store large quantities of gases, water, and chemicals, enabling applications like water collection, greenhouse gas capture, and PFAS extraction. Robson created a hole-filled crystalline structure in the late 1980s. Kitagawa later developed gas-absorbing MOFs, and Yaghi synthesized an exceptionally porous material in 1999. The scientists share an 11 million Swedish kronor prize.

Fourteen NHS staff recreated a 1927 photograph of a matron and nurses, originally found in a Sandwell Hospital broom cupboard, to mark the health service's 70th anniversary. The recovered and recreated images will be displayed at a hospital tea party tomorrow.

Professor Andrew Lo uses a classroom auction to demonstrate how a lack of information affects valuation, then transitions to discussing the federal government's recent takeover of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. He explains that these government-sponsored entities were taken over to prevent systemic market panic, with the government backing their debt by printing money, which raises potential inflation and taxpayer concerns. 

Lo then begins a lecture on present value relations, defining an asset simply as a sequence of current and future cashflows. He introduces the value operator, noting that market prices serve as one example. To value an asset, cashflows occurring at different times must be converted into a single base currency, or numeraire, using market-derived exchange rates or discount factors. He introduces the interest rate, or opportunity cost of capital, to simplify these conversions. By applying these discount factors, one can calculate the net present value of any asset under conditions of perfect certainty and no market frictions. Future lectures will expand on this framework to include annuities, perpetuities, and uncertainty.

This VentureWire newsletter from November 7, 2000, reports on private company business news. In Puerto Cortés, Honduras, Sergio Romero visits the Avontuur, a 97-year-old wind-powered schooner. Unlike the port's modern cargo ships, it uses a small crew to transport small cargo from Europe.

Title IX staff ensure compliance with evolving federal regulations regarding sex discrimination and sexual misconduct in higher education. Most Title IX staff are located in Human Resources (29%) or Student Affairs (28%). The three main positions analyzed are Heads, Deputy Heads, and Investigators. Between 2019-20 and 2023-24, the percentage of institutions with dedicated full-time Title IX positions increased from 33% to 43%, though 56% still lack a dedicated position. Doctoral institutions are most likely to have these roles (64%). Over five years, the total Title IX workforce grew by 38%, with investigators and deputy heads seeing the largest increases. Women hold 77% of Title IX positions, with Black women comprising 13%. Median salaries for Title IX positions exceed the overall higher education professional median, and women and people of color in these roles are paid equitably or more than equitably compared to White men. The report recommends institutions reassess Title IX officer responsibilities, increase staffing, and prepare for shifting regulatory compliance requirements.

Berkshire Hathaway sold its General Electric shares, profiting over $1 billion from a $3 billion crisis-era investment. This coincided with GE's leadership change and stock slump. This study explores kindergarten teachers' views on the importance, teaching, and integration of visual arts in early childhood education within the Municipality of Piraeus. The passage describes a display device designed to protect defect-detecting circuits from static electricity and optimize defect detection accuracy. The device includes a substrate with a display area, a pad area, and a circuit area containing a crack sensing circuit. Crack sensing lines extend around the display area, connecting input pads to test data lines and switching elements. This patent application describes a system and method for indicating wireless channel status in 5G New Radio systems operating at high frequencies. To overcome high pathloss, beamforming is used, but beam failures can occur, requiring recovery procedures. The embodiments provide methods for a User Equipment (UE) to decode frames after a beam failure recovery procedure by assuming a quasi-co-located (QCL) relationship exists between a channel (such as a PDCCH or PDSCH) and a newly identified beam. The UE uses the corresponding spatial domain receive filter to decode frames until an updated QCL configuration is received. Alternatively, the UE may assume no QCL configuration exists until Transmission Configuration Indication (TCI) states are updated, relying solely on the channel's demodulation reference signal (DMRS) for decoding. These techniques reduce signaling overhead and improve communication system performance following beam failure recovery. The application also details the corresponding communication system architecture, including access nodes and UEs, and computing systems for implementing the methods.

To help children become better conversationalists and cultivate curiosity, adults can use five strategies: ask specific, open-ended questions instead of rote ones; engage with children's questions rather than dismissing them; model asking questions out loud; admit when you do not know an answer and demonstrate how to find it using resources; and model active listening by giving full attention, asking follow-up questions, and repeating back what was heard. Encouraging this curiosity gives children confidence to explore complex problems.

This cross-sectional study investigated the relationship between physical activity and self-esteem among 10th and 11th-grade students at Capa Science High School in Istanbul. Males exhibited higher self-esteem and physical activity levels than females. Regular exercise, greater height, and higher self-reported school success were also associated with higher self-esteem. No significant differences in self-esteem were found across BMI groups. The authors note that the specific demographic of the study population may limit generalizability, and recommend further research to explore causal mechanisms.

Experts note diagnosis is difficult due to common symptoms and requires blood tests and a biopsy while consuming gluten. The findings align with other countries and are deemed essential for healthcare planning. However, the study does not differentiate between latent and actual celiac disease, and further provincial studies are needed for national representation.

The disclosed system and method optimize basal insulin dosages for diabetes treatment using automated insulin delivery (AID) records. A processor calculates the total insulin delivered (basal and bolus) over a predetermined period and determines the proportion of basal insulin. If this proportion exceeds a threshold (e.g., 70%), the system calculates a modified average basal dosage to align with the threshold and instructs a wearable pump to deliver the adjusted dosage. The system can exclude insulin delivered near boluses, apply clustering algorithms to generate time-dependent basal profiles, and adjust basal limits based on the user's hypoglycemic events. The drug delivery system includes a wearable pump, a continuous glucose monitor, and a personal diabetes management device that communicate wirelessly to execute an artificial pancreas application.

Tail risk, or "fat tails," describes the increased probability of rare, extreme market events compared to a normal distribution. Investors hedge against left tail risk to avoid severe losses, survive market downturns, and prevent behavioral mistakes like panic selling. The passage presents six tail risk hedging strategies: buying put options, diversifying into foreign assets, holding cash, utilizing Cambria’s Tail Risk ETF (TAIL), adopting Ray Dalio’s All Weather Portfolio, and employing trend-following strategies. While these methods can protect portfolios during market meltdowns, they typically require sacrificing overall returns during rising markets, making them psychologically difficult for investors to maintain over time.

The lecture explores the operator-field mapping in AdS/CFT, detailing how the scaling dimension of a boundary operator relates to the mass of the corresponding bulk gravity field. In the semiclassical limit, small perturbations around pure AdS are treated as free fields. For a massive scalar field, solving the equation of motion near the boundary yields two asymptotic solutions with exponents delta and d-delta. The scaling dimension of the dual operator is given by delta = d/2 + sqrt(d^2/4 + m^2 R^2). 

Normalizable modes correspond to states in the Hilbert space, while non-normalizable modes act as sources that deform the boundary theory's action. The mass-dimension relation indicates that massless fields map to marginal operators, negative mass squared (above the BF bound) to relevant operators, and positive mass squared to irrelevant operators. This mapping extends to gauge fields, which dualize to conserved currents of dimension d-1, and metric perturbations, which dualize to the stress tensor of dimension d. Finally, the lecture explains that boundary correlation functions can be computed using a generating functional, which corresponds to the on-shell classical gravity action evaluated with specific boundary conditions in the semiclassical limit.

The passage presents a new exact algorithm for computing Nash equilibria in multiplayer imperfect-information games, a problem known to be PPAD-hard. The authors formulate the problem as a nonlinear complementarity problem (NCP) using a generalized sequence-form representation, modeled as a quadratically-constrained feasibility program solved via nonconvex quadratic optimization.

Experiments on strategic-form games showed the NCP approach had faster runtimes than a prior mixed-integer bilinear program (MIP). In three-player Kuhn poker with dominated actions removed, the NCP approach computed an exact Nash equilibrium in 2.47 seconds (maximum deviation gain of 1.4 × 10^-17). In contrast, Gambit's logit quantal response equilibrium (QRE) tracing, the only competing method that succeeded, took over 40 seconds and yielded a deviation gain of 1.667 × 10^-5.

The NCP approach is highly accurate for small games but has limited scalability, failing to solve the full Kuhn poker game within 24 hours. The logit QRE method solved the full game in minutes, making it more suitable for larger instances where approximation is acceptable. The authors conclude their NCP approach is best for exact computation in small games, while larger games may require approximation methods like logit QRE or iterative self-play algorithms.

In John Q. A. Simmonds v. Nicholas T. P. Simmonds (1904), the appellee sued to recover 117.5 acres of land in Bell County. The appellee's title relied on a land certificate issued to Willard Chamberlain, a patent, and an 1850 transfer from Chamberlain's agent to Joseph P. Sneed, who later deeded the land to the appellee. The appellant, lacking a paper title, challenged the transfer's genuineness, the agent's authority, and the certificate's identification. The court affirmed the judgment for the appellee, holding that the transfer, being over thirty years old, from proper custody, and found genuine by the jury, was admissible as an ancient instrument with a conclusive presumption of the agent's authority. The transfer sufficiently identified the land certificate. The court also upheld the exclusion of a Land Office affidavit claiming ownership by a third party, as it could not disparage the appellee's title, and the exclusion of the appellant's character evidence, as a mere conflict in evidence does not put a witness's character in issue.

The lecture discusses the Asymptotic Equipartition Property (AEP), Markov sources, and the Lempel-Ziv universal compression algorithm. The AEP states that for a discrete memoryless source, the sample average of the log pmf approaches the entropy, H(X), as the sequence length n increases. Typical sequences, which collectively approach a total probability of 1, number approximately 2 to the power of n times H(X), demonstrating that entropy determines the bits required for source coding.

Because discrete memoryless sources are impractical, the lecture introduces Markov sources to model sources with memory. In an ergodic Markov chain, states transition based on single-step probabilities and reach a steady-state distribution. Coding for Markov sources relies on conditional entropy, H(X given S), which is achieved by encoding blocks of n letters.

The lecture also covers the Lempel-Ziv (LZ77) universal data compression algorithm. This algorithm requires no prior probability model and adapts to statistical structures automatically. It uses a sliding window of size W to find the longest match of unencoded symbols within the window. It encodes the match length using a unary-binary code and the match position using log W bits. Asymptotically, the Lempel-Ziv algorithm achieves an optimal H(X given S) bits per symbol.

Iron Sulfate heptahydrate, or copperas, is a water-soluble salt produced during titanium dioxide manufacturing or by crystallizing hot Sulfate solution. It contains 18-20% iron and free acid, which can cause it to become dusty and attack storage containers. As a WHO essential medicine, it treats iron deficiency. It is also used agriculturally to treat iron chlorosis and supply iron, and industrially for water purification, reducing Cr6+ in cement, and historically in textiles, leather, and ink.

This paper investigates whether k-replica joint measurements are necessary for efficiently estimating nonlinear functions of quantum states, specifically tr(ρ^k O). The authors prove that k-replica protocols require exponentially many samples to estimate tr(ρ^(k+1) O), while (k+1)-replica protocols achieve this with constant sample complexity. This establishes a fine-grained hierarchy of quantum replica advantage for any integer k ≥ 2. The proof relies on a general indistinguishability principle, showing that ensembles constructed from large Haar-random states via tensor products and mixtures are hard to distinguish from their average. This principle is also applied to derive lower bounds for spectrum testing and rank testing. Furthermore, the authors provide upper bounds, demonstrating that ⌈(k+1)/2⌉-replica measurements suffice to match the √d dependence in the lower bound.

The article details Enron's rise from a traditional pipeline company to a dominant energy trading colossus and its subsequent decline. Jeff Skilling, who joined as a consultant and later became CEO, transformed the company by creating the "Gas Bank," shifting Enron from a broker to a risk-assuming banker. Skilling fostered an aggressive, highly competitive corporate culture that recruited top-tier talent, offered uncapped merit-based bonuses, and utilized a harsh performance review system known as "rank and yank."

Enron expanded into trading electricity, broadband, and other commodities, employing aggressive accounting practices like mark-to-market accounting to maximize short-term profits. The company's culture became increasingly cutthroat, paranoid, and focused on immediate gains over teamwork or long-term customer relationships. Skilling also pushed out asset-heavy divisions and executives, such as Rebecca Mark, to align with Wall Street's demand for quick returns.

In 2001, Enron's fortunes reversed. The company faced severe criticism for its role in the California energy crisis, its telecommunications ventures failed, and Wall Street analysts began questioning its accounting practices, causing the stock price to plummet. Amidst these challenges, Skilling abruptly resigned after just six months as CEO, citing personal sacrifices. Ken Lay returned as CEO, promising a return to core businesses and a softer corporate culture, while Skilling expressed intentions to remain involved in Houston's commodity trading.

A penalty-kick shoot-out, governed by IFAB Laws 10 and 14, decides tied soccer games requiring a winner. Teams alternate five kicks from 12 yards. If tied, sudden-death pairs continue until one team scores and the other misses. Only players on the field at the end of play are eligible; teams with more players must "reduce to equate." Coaches should prepare by reviewing rules, identifying and ranking shooters, practicing the process, and analyzing opponents. Goalkeepers may be replaced if injured during the shoot-out. The team scoring the most goals wins, though these goals do not count toward individual statistics.

Nassim Nicholas Taleb is a statistician, mathematician, philosopher, trader, and investor focused on randomness, uncertainty, and probability. He is known for his *Incerto* book series, which includes *Fooled by Randomness* (2001), *The Black Swan* (2007), *Antifragile* (2012), and *Skin in the Game* (2018). These works explore the misunderstanding of chance, the impact of rare and unpredictable events, systems that benefit from volatility, and the importance of having personal stakes in decision-making. 

Taleb argues that the world is driven by unpredictable tail events, making forecasting futile. He distinguishes between Mediocristan (contained risks) and Extremistan (multiplicative risks) and warns against confusing luck with skill in financial markets. 

As a trader, Taleb made significant money using options strategies, particularly during the 1987 crash. He co-founded Empirica Capital and later became an advisor to Universa Investments, a hedge fund founded by Mark Spitznagel. Universa utilizes tail-risk hedging and the barbell strategy, aiming for small losses over time with massive gains during market crashes.

The barbell strategy involves structuring a portfolio with two extremes: low-risk assets on one side and high-risk assets on the other, avoiding the middle ground. This approach provides stability while capturing outsized gains during extreme market events. The passage also includes numerous quotes from Taleb’s books, emphasizing themes of uncertainty, risk management, decentralization, and the limits of human knowledge.

This paper studies the ML-separability and ML-definability of modal µ-calculus (µML) formulae by propositional modal logic (ML) formulae across various model classes: all models, words, binary trees, and d-ary trees (d ≥ 3). It establishes the computational complexity of these problems, finding that ML-definability is ExpTime-complete (PSpace-complete for words), while ML-separability ranges from PSpace-complete for words to 2-ExpTime-complete for d-ary trees with d ≥ 3. The authors provide effective constructions for separators and definitions when they exist, noting that separator sizes reflect the complexity landscape. Additionally, the paper demonstrates that ML lacks the Craig interpolation property over trees of outdegree bounded by d ≥ 3, formulating interpolant existence as a special case of separability, which is shown to be coNExpTime-complete. Finally, the results are applied to graded modalities, revealing distinct complexity behaviors for definability and separability depending on whether the separating language includes graded modalities.

The DAWN-Plasma study was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 trial evaluating convalescent plasma plus standard of care (SOC) versus SOC alone in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. Approved by Independent Ethics Committees, the study followed the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP guidelines. Between May 2020 and January 2021, 489 patients were randomized in a 2:1 ratio to convalescent plasma (n=326) or control (n=163). The intervention group received 800-1000 mL of convalescent plasma in 4 doses with high neutralizing antibody titers. The primary endpoint was the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Results showed no significant difference between groups for the primary endpoint (83.7% vs 84.1%) or any secondary endpoints. Safety profiles, including adverse events, serious adverse events, and fatal events, were similar between both groups. Higher baseline neutralizing antibody titers (NT50) were correlated with better outcomes, but the intervention did not significantly increase NT50 levels by Day 6. The study concluded that early high-titer convalescent plasma did not change the natural course of COVID-19 in hospitalized patients.

During the COVID-19 pandemic, researchers Arthur Santiago and Cristiano Mattos developed a dialogic educational activity for a non-formal education course in a Brazilian physics teacher education program. The activity, analyzed through the Cultural-Historical Activity Theory (CHAT) and Paulo Freire’s critical pedagogy, utilized the Discord platform to facilitate remote emergency education. The objective was to enhance students' conscious awareness of social contradictions by having them investigate the debate over reopening schools during the pandemic. 

The activity was structured in seven stages, beginning with thematic preparation by the teacher and culminating in students researching, discussing, and collaboratively producing an infographic on the risks and benefits of school reopenings. Discord's features, such as persistent text and voice channels, allowed students to self-organize, share information, and communicate asynchronously and synchronously without constant teacher management. 

The study found that combining students' prior familiarity with Discord and the Freirean-inspired thematic approach fostered student agency, autonomy, and productive dialogic interactions. Students connected their personal challenges with broader socio-political issues, overcoming the typical limitations of emergency remote teaching. The platform enabled a new division of labor where students independently organized meetings and tasks, demonstrating that dialogic activities can successfully mediate between individual experiences and collective socio-political problems in a remote learning environment.

The passage describes electronic gaming systems and methods featuring a stop-based bonus game. A bonus game construct—such as a wheel, reel, dice, or grid—displays multiple stop positions associated with either high-value first awards (e.g., jackpots) or lower-value second awards (e.g., credits). When a player selects a stop position associated with a second award, they receive that award, and the position is subsequently re-associated with a first award for future plays. This mechanism progressively increases the player's chances of winning a first award. These upgraded associations can persist across different player sessions. If a first award is won, the stop positions may reset to their default state. The gaming system includes standard electronic gaming machine components, such as processors, memory, displays, credit mechanisms, and random number generators, and can be networked with casino servers.

This study examines using generative AI in undergraduate physics education by comparing three laboratory approaches for teaching electric potential: traditional physical equipment, a pre-built digital simulation, and an AI-engaged simulation where students prompt, validate, and refine AI-generated models. Results showed that students in both simulation groups significantly outperformed the physical equipment group on immediate conceptual questions, with no significant differences between the two simulation groups. There were no significant differences in midterm or final exam scores across any groups. Furthermore, students in both simulation groups reported more positive attitudes toward the activity than those using physical equipment. The study concludes that using generative AI to design and validate simulations supports conceptual learning as effectively as pre-built simulations and better than physical equipment, while offering opportunities to develop modeling skills without compromising traditional learning objectives.

Electroweak unification combines weak and electromagnetic interactions despite differing strengths and coupling structures. The coupling difference is mitigated by projecting left-handed spinor components, simplifying the weak current to a vector current. Particles are grouped into doublets using Pauli matrices to define charged and neutral currents. A hypercharge current, derived using the Gell-Mann-Nishijima equation concept, incorporates right-handed particles. Finally, an isospin triplet and a hypercharge singlet are mixed using the weak mixing angle. This mixing produces the W+, W-, photon, and Z boson, achieving a consistent unified picture.

Community Board 7 of Manhattan brought a proceeding to compel the New York City Department of City Planning to disclose documents related to the "Trump City" proposal under the Freedom of Information Law (FOIL) after its request was denied. The Department argued the board lacked the capacity to sue. Lower courts ruled in favor of the board. The Court of Appeals reversed, distinguishing "capacity" from "standing." The Court held that statutory entities require explicit or necessarily implied authority to sue, absent clear legislative intent to the contrary. The New York City Charter does not expressly authorize community boards to sue. Furthermore, such authority is not a necessary implication of their purely advisory role under the Uniform Land Use Review Procedure. The Charter's specific list of documents boards are entitled to receive, the lack of subpoena power, and legislative history indicate an intent to deny community boards the power to compel document disclosure through lawsuits. Consequently, the board lacked the capacity to maintain the proceeding, and the petition was dismissed.

Europe faces challenges with an ageing population, and current action programs often lack factual foundations or remain at the pilot stage. This paper proposes using digital wellness services over omnivore mobile platforms for the "young elderly" (aged 60-75) to keep them healthy, active, and independent, thereby reducing future health and social care costs. The authors suggest a three-step approach: proactive prevention, mobile-based intervention, and the development of commercial ecosystems to sustain the services. 

Wellness is conceptualized across four dimensions: intellectual, physical, social, and emotional. The BeWell research program in Finland employs the Wellmo omnivore platform and Tieto cloud services to design and test these services with young elderly user groups. A survey of 101 young elderly respondents indicated that they are confident users of mobile apps and consider wellness issues important. These findings support the viability of digital wellness services as an intervention to build wellness routines. The study addresses four research questions, concluding that the young elderly are a relevant user group, find wellness important, can form wellness routines through appropriately designed services, and require a digital business environment to sustain these routines.

This study examined the spatiotemporal evolution of SARS-CoV-2 Alpha and Delta variants in Vietnam in 2021. Researchers analyzed 1,303 genome sequences, predominantly of the Delta AY.57 lineage. While rigorous public health measures successfully contained the Alpha variant, the highly transmissible Delta AY.57 lineage spread rapidly in an immunologically naive population, causing a large nationwide outbreak starting in May. Phylogeographic analysis indicated that strict travel restrictions limited viral dispersal, leading to distinct geographic clusters. The evolution of the AY.57 lineage was driven by weak purifying selection. The findings emphasize the critical role of genomic surveillance in informing pandemic responses.

Chinese textile firms are increasingly using North Korean factories and workers to exploit cheaper labor. Garments assembled in North Korea from Chinese materials are often labeled "Made in China" and exported globally. This practice persists as UN sanctions ban coal but not textiles, with textiles being North Korea's second-largest export in 2016. North Korean workers are highly productive and earn significantly lower wages than Chinese workers. Additionally, Chinese factories employ North Korean workers domestically, though new UN sanctions cap their numbers. These workers in China earn about $300 monthly, keeping a third while the rest goes to the North Korean state, which requires specific living and ideological conditions for them.

This systematic review evaluated the effects of marijuana (MJ) and cannabinoids on the microbiome across various health conditions. Following PRISMA guidelines, researchers analyzed 9 human studies (1 case-control, 6 cohorts, 2 clinical trials) involving 2,526 participants. The review found that MJ use and endocannabinoid supplements alter the gut and oral microbiota in patients with HIV, inflammation, obesity, cognitive deficits, and pain. For instance, MJ use in HIV patients correlated with changes in specific bacteria, while OEA supplements in obese participants increased *A. muciniphila* and decreased energy intake. Adverse events included coughing, wheezing, and drowsiness. Due to limited data, a meta-analysis was not conducted, but the findings indicate that MJ and the GI microbiota individually contribute to pain and other manifestations, warranting further research.

This study develops a mathematical model to evaluate a screening-isolation strategy for controlling infectious diseases in a semi-isolated community without vaccines or medications. Simulations demonstrate that the strategy effectively controls disease spread for basic reproduction numbers (R0) of 3.0 and 6.0, but fails at 8.0 without additional measures like social distancing. Disease control is highly sensitive to the time lag between infection and isolation. Higher screening frequency (every 3 days versus weekly) and efficiency (0.9 versus 0.7) significantly reduce infection sizes. Additionally, strict border control is necessary, as infection rates increase proportionally with external influx. The study concludes that regular, periodic community-wide screening, particularly using highly sensitive PCR-based tests, can successfully control epidemics in semi-isolated communities if the screening time lag is minimal.

The authors identify an intervalley superconducting phase in the half-filled second moiré bands of approximately 2°-twisted bilayer MoTe2. Using exact diagonalization on a continuum model, they find that superconductivity emerges as an intermediate phase between a ferromagnetic Chern insulator and a non-Abelian fractional spin Hall insulator when the short-range component of intervalley interactions is screened. The superconducting state exhibits time-reversal symmetry, extended nodal s-wave pairing, and is continuously connected to the fractional spin Hall insulator across the phase boundary. The authors demonstrate that non-uniform quantum geometry is crucial for stabilizing this phase and provide a field theory for the continuous transition.

A letter signed by fired prosecutor Michael Ben’Ary states his termination during a terrorism prosecution resulted from a false social media post by a pro-Trump commentator. Over-the-counter (OTC) trading is a decentralized process where two parties trade financial instruments directly without a centralized exchange, often via dealer networks. OTC markets trade stocks, bonds, derivatives, and commodities, frequently involving small companies, penny stocks, and foreign American Depository Receipts (ADRs). While OTC offers flexible, customized contracts and capital access for companies unable to meet formal exchange requirements, it is less transparent and less regulated. This leads to higher counterparty risks, liquidity issues, and susceptibility to fraud like pump-and-dump schemes. The text notes that OTC stocks generally yield negative returns and are not recommended for long-term investing or day trading. Additionally, large cryptocurrency transactions can be conducted via OTC desks.

Moina Shaiq founded the "Meet a Muslim" program in Fremont, California, to answer questions and dispel stereotypes about Islam. The program has since expanded to various venues and states. The disclosure proposes a method for transmitting and receiving a sounding reference signal (SRS) in a wireless communication system by configuring a guard period for SRS transmission. The guard period is set considering other uplink transmissions, such as PUCCH or PUSCH. When the guard period overlaps with a specific uplink channel, the priority between the guard period and the uplink channel is configured identically to the priority between the SRS and the uplink channel. The guard period may be configured for antenna switching, with its symbol count determined by subcarrier spacing. The disclosure also details methods for handling collisions between the guard period and other uplink channels or SRS resource sets, including applying priority rules, dropping symbols, or shifting transmission slots to prevent performance deterioration.

Cover 0 is a man-to-man defensive scheme with zero high safeties, designed to maximize blitz pressure while covering all eligible receivers. Its strengths include simple assignments, easy adjustments to offensive motion, and effectiveness against the run, Run-Pass Options (RPOs), and both short and long passing routes due to heavy pressure. However, it is a high-risk coverage with no safety help, making it vulnerable to big plays, draw plays, quarterback scrambles, and pick plays. It leaves the middle of the field open. In a standard Cover 0, defensive backs and one linebacker play man coverage while two linebackers blitz. Variations include Cover 0 "Rat," which rushes five players and leaves one to cover crossing routes or a scrambling quarterback, and dropping a hybrid defensive lineman into coverage to cover a running back.

This study explores holistic education in Indian higher education by integrating the philosophies of Indian sages-thinkers with modern policies like India’s NEP 2020 and UN SDG 4.7. Using a systematic literature review, the study identifies Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) as a bridge between traditional academic goals and broader human development. It evaluates global SEL frameworks and introduces the LIBRE/EMC2 framework, which promotes "whole brain learning" through four core dimensions: empathy, mindfulness, compassion, and critical inquiry. The review validates these four dimensions within the Indian context, demonstrating their alignment with both ancient Indian educational ideals and contemporary neurocognitive research. The findings support the LIBRE/EMC2 model as a foundation for curriculum design, assessment, and policy implementation, while noting limitations regarding database coverage and recommending future development of culturally sensitive evaluation tools.

A University of Maryland study found that sustained energy drink consumption significantly increases young adults' risk of cocaine use, non-medical prescription stimulant use, and alcohol use disorder by age 25. President Woodrow Wilson proclaims a state of war between the United States and the Imperial German Government following a Congressional declaration. Invoking the Revised Statutes, Wilson establishes regulations for "alien enemies," defined as un-naturalized German males aged fourteen and older within the US. Compliant alien enemies may pursue peaceful lives, but non-compliant individuals face restraint, security requirements, or removal.

Twelve specific regulations are mandated for public safety. Alien enemies are prohibited from possessing firearms, weapons, explosives, aircraft, wireless apparatus, and signaling or cipher devices; such property is subject to seizure. They cannot approach military or government facilities, publish attacks against the US government, or aid enemies. Additionally, they may be barred from prohibited areas, forced to relocate, required to register, and must obtain permits to enter or depart the US. Violators are subject to summary arrest and confinement. These regulations apply to all areas under US jurisdiction.

In *People v. John Ortiz*, the defendant appealed his simple assault conviction after being charged with assault with a deadly weapon. Ortiz followed his wife, found her with Albert Donaso drinking wine in his kitchen, and cut Donaso with a pocket-knife during a struggle. Ortiz claimed self-defense, testifying that Donaso rushed him with a knife. 

The appellate court rejected the appellant's objections. The court found no error in sustaining an objection about who accompanied Ortiz's wife, as the husband had already testified to it. The court noted no objection was made to a question about why a witness fled. The court ruled it was proper cross-examination for the district attorney to request Ortiz to demonstrate drawing and opening his pocket-knife to test his self-defense claim. Finally, the court held that striking testimony about whether Ortiz wrote threatening letters was not reversible error, as it was a collateral issue to the central question of self-defense. The judgment was affirmed.

NVIDIA's Blackwell architecture introduces neural shaders, integrating AI into the rendering pipeline to enhance performance and visual quality. Key AI technologies include Ray Reconstruction (RR), DLSS, DLAA, RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression (NTC), Neural Radiance Cache (NRC), RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. These features use AI to generate higher-quality pixels, compress textures efficiently, approximate complex lighting and materials, and render realistic skin and faces in real-time. The Blackwell GPU family consists of the flagship GB202 (GeForce RTX 5090), high-end GB203 (RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti), and performance GB205 (RTX 5070). The document details the specifications for these chips, including transistor counts, Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs), CUDA cores, RT cores, Tensor cores, and memory interfaces. In *Archibeque v. Miera*, the court held that under the organic act, only the supreme court possesses appellate jurisdiction; district courts cannot exercise strictly appellate powers. Appeals from justice of the peace to district court are tried de novo, with the transcript serving only to confirm the case originated in justice's court and the appeal was properly taken. The district court committed no error in overruling a motion to dismiss for transcript defects or in allowing the plaintiff to file his account. The jury's verdict for defendant Miera was upheld, as discrepancies in witness testimony regarding whether Miera's cattle or the plaintiff's own stock damaged his wheat were properly for the jury to weigh, and the verdict was not clearly against the weight of evidence. Judgment affirmed.

This study used machine learning to predict depressive symptom severity (DSS) based on sleep quality, anxiety, and brain structure across three independent cohorts. Results showed that sleep quality robustly predicted DSS across all datasets, and adding anxiety scores significantly improved this prediction. Brain structural and functional measurements did not predict DSS or mediate its link with sleep. Anxiety mediated the relationship between sleep and DSS. Longitudinal data indicated that baseline sleep and anxiety predicted future DSS, except in participants who received neurofeedback therapy. The findings suggest sleep and anxiety are critical behavioral predictors of depressive symptoms.

The Base Cross offense is a basketball strategy that creates size mismatches by using a smaller player to set a baseline screen for a larger post player. The primary action involves the point guard passing to the wing, making a give-and-go cut, and screening for the post. The offense utilizes multiple entries, including pass, dribble, UCLA, and Hawk. Its success depends on precise execution, defensive recognition, and specific counters against tactics like trailing, switching, or fronting the post. If the initial post-up is unavailable, the offense flows into ball reversal options utilizing weakside down screens, mid screens, and back cuts. Coaches should implement the offense using breakdown drills, emphasize individual skill development, scout opponents to anticipate defensive reads, and prepare to defend against it.

The NHS Patient Charter (NHS Constitution) outlines patients' legal rights, NHS pledges, and patient responsibilities to ensure fair, free, and needs-based healthcare. The Charter serves as a partnership framework, empowering patients, guiding staff, and emphasizing shared responsibility, particularly as the NHS faces operational pressures.

In 1977, Conrad Lapp signed a promissory note in Colorado for his company Joslyn Fruit's debt to Pacific Gamble Robinson Co. His wife did not sign. After default, the Lapps moved to Washington, and Pacific Gamble sued in Washington, seeking to reach the Lapps' community property. The trial court and Court of Appeals refused to hold the marital community liable. The Washington Supreme Court reversed, applying Colorado law under the "most significant relationship" test, since the entire transaction occurred in Colorado and both parties were Colorado domiciliaries at the time. Under Colorado law, Mr. Lapp's property and earnings—including those characterized as community property in Washington—are subject to the debt, while Mrs. Lapp's separate property is not. Justice Horowitz dissented, arguing Washington law should determine the source of funds for collection and that community property should be protected from Mr. Lapp's separate debt.

The professor introduces a financing sources panel for an MIT course, featuring Axel Bichara, Julianne Zimmerman, and Amir Nashat. The paper introduces Flow Matching for Corrected Posterior Estimation (FMCPE) to address model misspecification in Simulation-Based Inference (SBI). SBI approximates posterior distributions from simulated data but suffers from biased or overconfident estimates when simulators inaccurately reflect real-world processes. FMCPE leverages the flow matching paradigm to refine posterior estimators trained on abundant simulated data using a small set of scarce, high-fidelity calibration data. The method jointly trains two flow matching steps: one to couple real observations with simulated counterparts, and another to transport the simulation-based posterior toward the true posterior. Experiments on synthetic and real-world tasks demonstrate that FMCPE consistently outperforms standard SBI baselines (NPE and MFNPE), producing more accurate and better-calibrated posteriors even with limited calibration data. The approach is computationally efficient, amortized, and applicable as a post-processing step to any SBI model.
I am unable to summarize this passage.

The SD Memory Card Physical Layer Specification Version 6.00 defines SD card types (SDSC up to 2GB, SDHC up to 32GB, SDXC up to 2TB), form factors (Standard, miniSD, microSD), and read/write properties (RW and ROM). Cards operate within specific voltage ranges (2.7-3.6V, with UHS-II adding 1.70-1.95V) and support various bus speed modes, including Default, High, UHS-I (SDR/DDR), and UHS-II/UHS-III. Speed Classes (0-10) and Application Performance Classes dictate minimum performance.

Communication is host-controlled via command, response, and data tokens protected by CRC. Cards operate in either card identification mode or data transfer mode. Initialization involves voltage verification (CMD8), operational condition setting (ACMD41), and address assignment (CMD2, CMD3). UHS-I initialization includes a voltage switch sequence (CMD11) and optional tuning (CMD19), while UHS-II uses a distinct PHY and device initialization sequence.

Data transfer supports single and multiple block read (CMD17/18) and write (CMD24/25) operations, with erase functions including standard Erase, Discard, and Full User Area Logical Erase (FULE). Write protection is achieved via mechanical switches, internal protection, or password protection (CMD42). The specification also details Card Ownership Protection (COP) and Force Erase Password (FEP) features to manage card locking, unlocking, and data erasure.

A study of 173 women found adding half a litre of water to breakfast promoted weight loss. Other research shows this amount burns 23 extra calories, or 2kg of fat annually. Additionally, while low-carb, high-protein diets aid weight loss by increasing satiety, a new study suggests overeating meats is not optimal.

The passage contains three diplomatic documents from early 1917. In the first, Arthur James Balfour argues that the Central Powers used calculated brutality in Belgium and elsewhere to intimidate both enemies and neutrals, and that a durable peace requires three conditions: removing causes of international unrest, discrediting the Central Powers' aggressive methods among their own populations, and establishing international sanctions against aggressors. DS-STAR is a novel data science agent that generates solution code through an iterative process of planning and verification. It addresses the limitations of existing agents, which primarily focus on structured data and lack robust verification, by automatically analyzing heterogeneous data files to generate textual summaries of their structure and content. DS-STAR then utilizes a core loop involving a planner, a coder, and an LLM-based verifier. If the verifier deems a plan insufficient, a router agent decides whether to append a new step or correct an existing one. The framework also includes debugging and retrieval modules for handling execution errors and large numbers of files. Evaluated on the DABStep, KramaBench, and DA-Code benchmarks, DS-STAR significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of its analyzer and router agents, and analysis shows that increased refinement iterations improve accuracy, particularly for complex tasks.

The Yankees will host the Red Sox for a best-of-three AL Wild Card series starting Sept. 30, 2025. New York enters as the No. 4 seed despite having the AL's second-best record, while Boston is the No. 5 seed after trading Rafael Devers. This marks the sixth postseason matchup between the rivals, with Boston leading 3-2. Games will be broadcast on ESPN and available through various streaming and audio platforms.
Apple will replace swelling batteries for free in 13-inch MacBook Pros without Touch Bar built between October 2016 and October 2017. Check eligibility via Apple Support page using serial numbers.

The "Sell the Rip" strategy involves selling an asset—either closing a long position or opening a short—when its price rises to an overvalued level, anticipating a market correction. Based on mean reversion, it is primarily used by short-term traders and is not recommended for long-term investing or stocks with strong fundamentals. Traders use oscillating and momentum indicators, such as RSI and Bollinger Bands, to identify overbought conditions. A backtest on the S&P 500 using RSI showed that modifying exit criteria to sell sooner improved the equity curve and reduced drawdowns, despite a lower average gain per trade. The strategy has been profitable on the S&P 500 over the past three decades but is less effective in trend-following commodity markets.

AI in education promises personalized learning, which requires greater student autonomy. However, the traditional education system has resisted fundamental change for over 200 years because the prescribed curriculum acts as the system's anchor, dictating teaching, assessment, and student outcomes while leaving no room for student control. Using Panarchy theory, the authors explain that education systems possess high resilience and adaptability but lack transformability, absorbing innovations without altering core structures. To achieve transformation, the authors propose a balanced curriculum that splits time between state-controlled content and student-directed learning. Rather than implementing whole-school reforms, which the system typically rejects, transformation should begin within small, autonomous subsystems inside existing schools. These subsystems allow students to personalize their learning with teacher facilitation and AI integration. Successful examples, such as the ICEE program in China and various school-within-a-school models in Australia, demonstrate how these small innovations can survive, grow, and eventually influence the broader education system.

Due to the Scripps National Spelling Bee doubling in size, associate pronouncer Rev. Brian Sietsema took over some duties from Jacques Bailly to help Bailly pace his voice. The Martingale trading strategy involves doubling the trade size after each loss to recover previous losses and secure a profit equal to the initial bet once the market reverses. Originally developed for 50% probability gambling by Paul Pierre Levy, it is a risk-seeking method that differs from anti-Martingale, double-down, and averaging down strategies. While it theoretically offers a near 100% win rate with infinite capital, it carries severe risks, particularly in the stock market where assets can fall to zero. A backtest on SPY yielded undesirable results. The authors do not recommend the strategy, advising instead to spread equity across uncorrelated strategies.

A New York Times survey of 65 federal judges found widespread dissatisfaction with the U.S. Supreme Court’s emergency docket decisions regarding President Trump. Most respondents disagreed that the Court made appropriate use of the docket or provided sufficient guidance to lower courts, and a majority felt it harmed the judiciary's public perception. This article examines the integration of dance education and social studies to foster holistic student development, contrasting this with the narrow focus of standardized tests like PISA and NAEP, which exclude the arts. The Miami Dolphins earned their first win of the season against the New York Jets, but lost Tyreek Hill to a feared dislocated left knee injury. The lecture concludes the discussion on conjugate gradients (CG) and related Krylov subspace methods. The Arnoldi algorithm creates an orthogonal basis for the Krylov subspace, which can approximate low eigenvalues of large symmetric matrices via Ritz values. For symmetric positive definite matrices, CG solves linear systems by producing orthogonal residuals and A-orthogonal (conjugate) search directions. This process is equivalent to minimizing a quadratic energy function, offering faster convergence than steepest descent. Each CG cycle requires one matrix multiplication and two inner products. For non-symmetric or indefinite matrices, CG fails, and the more expensive MINRES method, which minimizes the residual norm using the Arnoldi basis, is used instead. The choice between iterative Krylov methods and direct elimination ultimately requires experimental comparison.

Police and Crimestoppers warn the public about counterfeit banknotes during the festive season. Over 237,000 fake notes were removed in the first half of 2017. This cross-sectional study investigated antimicrobial resistance (AMR) patterns among 346 clinical isolates at a tertiary care hospital in Chennai from November 2023 to May 2024. AMR is a critical global health threat, exacerbated in India by over-the-counter antibiotic access, weak regulations, and low awareness. Of the 346 samples analyzed, 76.3% showed positive growth, with Gram-negative bacteria dominating at 75.4%. E. coli (28.8%) and Klebsiella spp. (26.9%) were the most frequently isolated organisms, primarily from urine and sputum samples. The study revealed high resistance rates to third-generation cephalosporins and Polymyxin B, while Amikacin and Gentamycin demonstrated higher sensitivity. The findings underscore the urgent need for antimicrobial stewardship, including multidisciplinary teams, regular surveillance, and stricter control over antibiotic sales, despite study limitations such as a short duration and small sample size.

Stone tools dating back 385,000 years found in India suggest humans might have migrated from Africa much earlier than previously thought. A study published in Nature dated the tools to 385,000-172,000 years ago. No human remains were found, and researchers seek further funding to study the artifacts' origins.

The passage describes an industrial data services platform utilizing Basic Information Data Types (BIDTs) to generate contextualized data presentations. BIDTs are structured data types—State, Rate, Odometer, and Event—defined on industrial devices alongside user-configurable metadata. A gateway device discovers these BIDTs and organizes the data using user-defined asset models, which establish hierarchical relationships among plant facilities, production lines, and industrial assets. An application server system, which can be on-premise or cloud-based, aggregates asset models from multiple gateway devices into a unified plant model. Based on this model, the application server generates graphical data presentations for client devices. Multiple asset models can be created to suit different user roles or destination platforms. Furthermore, a gateway device registry manages secure communication channels between gateway devices and cloud platforms.

Current clinical treatment for thoracic aortic aneurysms (TAAs) relies primarily on maximum aortic size, though similar-sized aneurysms can have different underlying causes and mechanical vulnerabilities. Researchers generated synthetic TAA data via finite element simulations combining compromised elastic fiber integrity and dysfunctional mechanosensing. They trained four neural network architectures (CNN-DeepONet, FNN-DeepONet, UNet, and Laplace Neural Operator) to predict these initiating insults using either dilatation alone or both dilatation and distensibility maps. Predictions using both dilatation and distensibility were significantly more accurate than using dilatation alone. The UNet architecture achieved the highest overall prediction accuracy. These findings suggest that measuring full-field aortic shape and mechanics with neural networks could improve personalized TAA diagnosis and treatment beyond the current size-based standard.

Joe Hadzima presents a lecture on legal issues for startups, focusing on issue spotting across the business lifecycle. He discusses founder equity splits, vesting schedules, and employee equity compensation. Finally, he outlines securities laws, advising against explicit stock offers in business plans, and explains venture capital financing instruments like convertible notes, liquidation preferences, and anti-dilution protections.

The SanDisk Sansa Fuze is a portable digital audio/video player featuring a 1.9” color screen, FM tuner, built-in microphone, and microSDHC expansion slot. The manual also provides troubleshooting tips, warranty information, and the software End User License Agreement.

This paper examines the impact of digitalization on sustainable development (economy, society, and environment) and the influence of national cultural characteristics on digitalization levels. Using the Digital Economy and Society Index (DESI) for 28 EU countries, the authors analyze correlations between DESI, various sustainability indices, and Hofstede’s cultural dimensions. 

Results indicate that digitalization strongly and positively correlates with economic and social development metrics, including competitiveness, innovation, and GDP. However, digitalization has a negative relationship with environmental wellbeing. Regarding cultural dimensions, power distance and uncertainty avoidance negatively correlate with digitalization, while individualism and indulgence show positive correlations. Long-term orientation shows no relationship. 

The study confirms that digitalization drives economic and social progress but negatively impacts the environment. Furthermore, cultural traits significantly affect a society's digitalization level, suggesting that macromarketing tools tailored to cultural characteristics can aid in implementing technological changes. The authors note limitations, including the restricted scope of EU countries and the underdeveloped state of current sustainability measurement methodologies.

The passage compares the Trump administration and RFK Jr.’s autism policies to a 1963 U.S. delegation’s visit to the Soviet Union, where political ideology dictated that intellectual disability could only have organic causes. The appellate court affirmed the trial court's judgment, finding no error in instructing the jury about an interrogatory inconsistency and substantial evidence supporting the verdict.

The Houston Astros defeated the Chicago White Sox 7-1 on April 22, 2018, completing a three-game sweep and extending their winning streak to six games. Over 50 people escaped a UPS fire at Lucknow's Scope Hospital without injuries. ICU patients were moved to other hospitals, and a probe was ordered.

Defending champions India will play Bangladesh in the Champions Trophy semi-final at Edgbaston on June 15. Both teams feature balanced bowling and batting lineups. The match will be broadcast live on Star Sports Network at 3 PM IST and streamed on Hotstar.

The 2018 Baku Declaration by the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) and the Communiqué from the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) address critical issues for the Global South, including India. LeBron James is a 41-year-old billionaire NBA player in the final year of his Lakers contract. As the highest-earning player in league history, his wealth stems from his NBA salary and lucrative endorsements, including a lifetime Nike deal. James makes strategic investments in brands like Blaze Pizza, Liverpool FC, and SpringHill. He spends his fortune on luxury vehicles, multiple mansions, and extensive physical maintenance, though he remains frugal with personal technology expenses. Jean Melchior sued Hilite International, Inc. for infringing patents related to cam phasers that use torque reversals to transfer hydraulic fluid without a pump. A jury found Hilite infringed and the claims valid, and the district court denied Hilite's motion for judgment as a matter of law. The Federal Circuit reversed, holding the asserted patent claims invalid. The court determined that a prior German patent, Danckert, anticipated claim 22 of the '017 patent because Melchior's only distinguishing argument—a "direct transfer in a closed line"—was not a claim limitation. The court also held the remaining claims of the '506 and '254 patents invalid as obvious over Danckert in view of Shirai. This qualitative study examines Norwegian Physical Education Teacher Education (PETE) students' perceptions of a flipped learning (FL) framework. Twenty-two students participated in the intervention, which required watching 10-20 minute instructional videos before class to dedicate in-class time to active, student-centered learning in dance and motor learning units. Data from semi-structured interviews generated five themes: expectations, simple input, deep learning, a supportive learning environment, and challenges. Students reported that FL increased peer accountability for preparation, offered a more accessible alternative to reading, and fostered deeper understanding through video rewatching and class discussions. The videos also reduced uncertainty for practical activities. Reported challenges included the inability to ask questions during preparation, technical issues, and time consumption. Overall, students perceived FL positively, noting improved motivation and learning, and recognized it as a useful tool for their future teaching careers.

St. Jude researchers identified kinases Mst1 and Mst2 as hidden drivers that regulate dendritic cell function and T cell production to fight cancer and infections. Using the NetBID algorithm, they discovered that Mst1/2 and the Hippo signaling pathway control CD8α+ dendritic cells, which are more metabolically active than CD8α- cells. Mst1/2 integrates metabolism and cytokine signaling through the unconventional NF-κB pathway to trigger interleukin-12 production, priming CD8 T cells. These findings suggest new treatment strategies for cancer and immune disorders.

A Roman pottery fragment found on Chapel St Leonards’ beach is the third Roman artefact discovered there recently, suggesting a lost Roman settlement lies under the sand. The Alabama Supreme Court answered a certified question from the Eleventh Circuit in the negative, holding that an insurance policy provision limiting "insured" to employees acting "within the scope of duties" does not conflict with a separate provision covering "violations of constitutional/civil rights" so as to create an ambiguity construed against the insurer.

Shrader and Livingston sued Attalla police officers for sexual abuse under 42 U.S.C. § 1983. EMCC's linebacker policy covered civil rights violations but limited insureds to employees acting within their scope of duties. Plaintiffs argued this created ambiguity or illusory coverage because civil rights violations typically occur outside scope of employment.

The court found the Titan cases inapplicable, as Titan II relied solely on law-of-the-case from Titan I, and the Titan policy contained different conflicting provisions. The court held that "under color of law" under § 1983 and "scope of employment" overlap significantly—civil rights violations can occur within scope of duties. Therefore, no conflict exists between the provisions, and the policy is neither ambiguous nor illusory.

This study examines the impact of outdoor temperature drops on COVID-19 severity during the Omicron wave in Tomsk, Russia, from January to March 2022. The authors propose the "compromised airway epithelium" hypothesis, suggesting that the airway epithelium of infected individuals is vulnerable to temperature drops, leading to worsened symptoms. Using a case-crossover design, they analyzed daily hospitalizations as a proxy for disease severity alongside daily temperature fluctuations. The analysis identified 14 instances where a temperature drop exceeding 3 degrees Celsius was associated with a surge in hospitalizations with a 1-2 day time lag. Temperature acted as the primary trigger in 8 of these instances and an additional factor in 6. Three hospitalization surges were unlinked to temperature changes. The authors conclude that short-term drops in outdoor temperature worsen COVID-19 symptoms in infected individuals. They suggest that this predictable 1-2 day lag can help healthcare systems prepare for sudden increases in hospitalizations. Future research directions include examining air humidity, the "supersaturation in the airways" effect, and air pollution using a similar mechanistic approach.

Chiral phonons carry angular momentum and energy in both metallic and insulating materials, overcoming the limitations of chiral-induced spin selectivity. The thermal on/off ratio is 1.07 at room temperature and increases to 1.2 at 50 K due to reduced phonon-phonon scattering. These findings offer a blueprint for nanoscale thermal switches and diodes controlled by external magnetic fields.

The lecture transitions from tree-level to loop diagrams in QED, introducing quantum fluctuations. Loop diagrams require integrating over free internal momenta, leading to divergences caused by extrapolating QED to arbitrarily high energy scales. In the late 1940s, Feynman, Schwinger, and Tomonaga developed renormalization to remove these divergences, a process later simplified by Freeman Dyson. Renormalization also shows that physical mass, charge, and fields differ from the bare parameters in the Lagrangian due to interactions. Loop diagrams correct propagators and vertices. Vertex corrections generate an anomalous magnetic moment. While the Dirac equation predicts a g-factor of 2 in the nonrelativistic limit, Schwinger calculated the first loop correction, matching experimental results. Subsequent higher-order calculations, involving increasingly numerous diagrams, continue to agree with highly precise experimental measurements.

The lecture covers two analytical methods for optimal control: Pontryagin's minimum principle and dynamic programming. It begins with a recap of reshaping the phase space for a linear system using manual linear feedback and minimum time optimal control with bounded inputs. The minimum time solution, a bang-bang controller, is derived using Pontryagin's minimum principle, which converts constrained optimization into an unconstrained one using Lagrange multipliers.

The lecture then introduces dynamic programming, which leverages additive cost functions to recursively compute the cost-to-go. Taking the continuous limit yields the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation. The HJB sufficiency theorem guarantees that a policy satisfying this equation is optimal, provided the value function's partial derivatives are smooth.

This framework is applied to the Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) problem, which minimizes an infinite horizon quadratic cost. By assuming a quadratic form for the cost-to-go function, the HJB equation leads to the Riccati equation. Solving the Riccati equation backward in time yields the optimal feedback gains. 

Finally, the lecture contrasts the two methods: Pontryagin's principle is a necessary condition that applies locally along a trajectory and handles non-smooth value functions (like those in bang-bang control), whereas the HJB theorem is a sufficient condition requiring smoothness. These analytical techniques form the foundation for future algorithmic approaches to nonlinear optimal control.

This study investigates the effects of femtosecond pulsed-laser irradiation on the microstructural and superconducting properties of niobium (Nb) thin films. Laser irradiation generates laser-induced periodic surface structures (LIPSS) with a periodicity of approximately 260 nm. The formation of LIPSS induces microstructural changes, including reduced film thickness, a decreased lattice parameter due to compressive stress, and increased grain size. These modifications slightly depress the intrinsic superconducting properties, lowering the critical temperature (Tc) by about 0.3 K and the upper critical field (Hc2) by roughly 50 mT in an isotropic manner. 

Conversely, the extrinsic flux-pinning landscape becomes highly anisotropic. Transport, magnetic, and magneto-optical measurements, supported by time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau (TDGL) simulations, reveal that the critical current density (Jc) is enhanced along the direction of the LIPSS. Optimally treated samples exhibit higher Jc at low magnetic fields and temperatures compared to pristine films. The undulated surface topography acts as an effective pinning site for vortices, multiplying the critical current density along the channels by a factor of approximately two. The findings demonstrate that laser processing enables controlled modification of superconducting properties, making it a promising technique for fabricating superconducting circuit elements.

The Education Department restarted loan forgiveness for income-based repayment borrowers with 25 years of on-time payments. Government furloughs may delay processing, risking taxation before a tax exemption expires Dec. 31. About two million are enrolled.

President Nixon announces an increased rate of American troop withdrawals from Vietnam, bringing 100,000 more troops home by December 1, 1971. He reviews progress since taking office, noting significant reductions in troop levels and casualties. He attributes this success to "Vietnamization" and military operations in Cambodia and Laos, which he claims disrupted enemy supply lines and demonstrated South Vietnamese combat capability. Nixon rejects setting a fixed withdrawal date, arguing it would endanger remaining forces and prisoners of war by removing incentives for enemy negotiation. He calls on Hanoi to negotiate and release prisoners of war. Defending American soldiers, he emphasizes ending the war in a way that ensures South Vietnam's survival and honors the sacrifices made, aiming for a lasting peace.

Researchers discovered a new genus and species of clingfish, the "duckbilled clingfish" (Nettorhamphos radula), in a 1977 museum specimen from Southern Australia. Named for its broad, flat snout, the fish possesses 1,800 to 2,300 backward-pointing conical teeth, ten times more than other known clingfish. Because only two specimens exist, researchers used CT scanning to noninvasively study its skeleton. The discovery, detailed in the journal Copeia, adds to a well-studied region's clingfish diversity. Clingfish are of scientific interest for their suction abilities, which could inspire surgical and tracking devices.

Lattice Semiconductor (LSCC) designs low-power, programmable chips. Its revenue is rebounding due to data center strength, offsetting weak automotive and industrial markets. Inventories are normalizing, financials are solid with no debt, and Q3 guidance implies growth. Despite raising the target price to $70, the author maintains a HOLD rating due to expensive valuation and a thin margin of safety.

Tesla Motors, Inc.'s 2015 Annual Report on Form 10-K outlines its business of designing, developing, manufacturing, and selling fully electric vehicles and energy storage products. The company produces the Model S sedan and Model X SUV, with over 107,000 Model S vehicles delivered worldwide by the end of 2015. Tesla plans to unveil the lower-priced Model 3 in 2016 and begin deliveries in 2017. The company also markets Tesla Energy products, including the Powerwall and Powerpack, which began production at the Gigafactory in Nevada in late 2015.

Tesla sells vehicles directly through its own global network of stores, service centers, and Supercharger stations rather than franchised dealerships. Manufacturing occurs primarily in Fremont and Lathrop, California; Tilburg, Netherlands; and the Gigafactory. The company's core technology includes proprietary battery packs, power electronics, dual motor powertrains, and autopilot systems.

The filing details numerous risk factors, including potential delays in the production ramps for Model X and Model 3, challenges in bringing the Gigafactory online, and reliance on single-source suppliers, notably Panasonic for battery cells. Additional risks involve lithium-ion battery safety, managing international expansion, fluctuating currency exchange rates, competition from established automakers, dependence on government incentives, and reliance on key personnel such as CEO Elon Musk and CTO JB Straubel.

During finals season, Lehigh students face stress and overcrowded libraries, prompting them to seek alternative study spaces. Students use academic buildings, cafes, and the bookstore for quieter environments. Some arrive early to secure library seats, though seat-saving causes frustration. To accommodate students, Lehigh extends building hours, keeping Fairchild-Martindale Library open 24 hours daily. The document is a Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) outlining analyses for ECGs, immunogenicity, and protocol changes, along with programming and presentation specifications. ECG assessments will be tabulated, and QTc intervals will be summarized categorically. Immunogenicity will be analyzed descriptively for anti-drug antibodies (ADA), calculating incidence from treatment-induced and treatment-boosted cases. Protocol changes include rewording the primary efficacy analysis and altering secondary variable terminology. 

Appendix A details presentation specifications, including formatting rules, handling missing dates, and calculation formulas for durations and body metrics. Appendix B specifies SAS programming quality control requirements, covering program structure, log review, output validation, and dataset verification. Appendix C provides a list and mock shells for planned tables, figures, and listings, covering demographics, adverse events, ECGs, laboratory results, pharmacokinetics, and plasma glucose recovery.

Scientists increasingly recognize ultraprocessed foods as addictive substances that alter the brain's reward system similarly to alcohol and nicotine. Comprising over half of American diets, these engineered combinations of fats, sugars, and salts trigger cravings, loss of control, and withdrawal. Experts argue these "foodlike products" are designed to be irresistible, undermining individual willpower. Consequently, researchers and policymakers are pushing for regulations like warning labels, taxes, and school bans, while some companies are beginning to offer less processed alternatives in response to public demand.

The Trump administration released the 2018 Nuclear Posture Review to modernize the US nuclear arsenal with smaller bombs and enhanced deterrence. President Trump stated the strategy modernizes the nuclear triad, deters attacks, and maintains arms control commitments. Defence Secretary Jim Mattis noted Russia and China are pursuing new nuclear capabilities, challenging US superiority, with Russia relying on nuclear escalation. The report also identifies North Korea and Iran as threats. To deter regional aggression, the US plans to develop low-yield options, including modifying submarine-launched ballistic missile warheads and pursuing a sea-launched cruise missile. The US pledged not to use nuclear weapons against non-nuclear NPT-compliant states. Officials emphasized flexibility against aggressive regimes and non-state actors while reaffirming extended deterrence commitments to allies.

The federal government agreed to give provinces and territories 75 percent of marijuana tax revenues for two years, retaining 25 percent up to $100 million annually. Provinces will share funds with municipalities to offset legalization costs. Ministers will review the framework in December 2018. First-year revenues are estimated at $400 million, with provinces permitted to add their own markups. Ministers also discussed equalization payments, the Canada Pension Plan, the global economy, and a strategy to share corporate ownership information to combat tax evasion, money laundering, and terrorist financing.

ANU and the Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris studied alumino-silicate glass, commonly used in phone screens. Researchers found that adding elements like sodium, potassium, calcium, and magnesium creates organized clusters at a nanometre scale, influencing glass flexibility and fracture resistance. This could lead to more shatter-proof screens. ANU plans to collaborate with manufacturers. Meanwhile, smartphone durability remains an issue, and Samsung and LG continue researching foldable displays.

The speaker pledges to continue the predecessor's reforms targeting abuses of power by capital combinations in interstate commerce, necessitating further legislative and executive action, including antitrust amendments and agency reorganization.
