Despite conceding a freak goal and scoring own goals recently, Deery noted the team remains in the top six with 13 games left and expressed confidence their fortunes will improve.

Top-ranked Virginia defeated North Carolina 71-63 to win the ACC Tournament championship at Brooklyn's Barclays Center. Prior to the final, North Carolina defeated Duke, whose star Marvin Bagley III showcased his NBA draft potential. Clemson also secured an NCAA Tournament berth for the first time in seven years, while Brett Yormark hopes to bring the tournament back to Barclays Center.

The Maui News confirmed that mayoral candidate Mike Victorino struck two male teens with his vehicle on April 13. Police and Victorino's wife stated he was neither speeding nor intoxicated. The teens sustained non-life-threatening injuries, and Victorino remained at the scene. Police and a victim's mother dispute whether the teens were in a crosswalk.

Congressional investigations into Enron's collapse intensified on February 6, 2002. Former CEO Jeffrey Skilling was expected to testify before Rep. Billy Tauzin's committee, while former Chairman Kenneth Lay was subpoenaed after canceling his voluntary appearance. William Powers, who led Enron's internal investigation, testified that top executives, including Lay, knew partnerships were hiding losses and enriching themselves, though he declined to characterize the actions as fraud. Former CFO Andrew Fastow, who earned $30 million from the partnerships, was also scheduled to testify.

Labor Secretary Elaine Chao addressed hearings on strengthening retirement account protections. Arthur Andersen CEO Joseph Berardino faced congressional criticism over the firm's auditing role and document shredding. In other developments, Enron's interim financing package shrank significantly, its broadband unit owed back taxes, and the Houston Astros sought to terminate the Enron Field naming rights agreement, which Enron planned to challenge. The scandal also generated extensive media commentary on corporate accounting and whistleblower impacts.

Linebackers require toughness, athleticism, and high intelligence to serve as the "quarterback of the defense." Positioned behind the defensive line, they relay calls, align the defense, and defend against both runs and passes. The position includes variations like Sam, Mike, Will, and Jack. Ideal linebackers possess skills such as agility, tackling, and strength, with a lean-muscular build. Historically, Ray Lewis, Chuck Bednarik, and Lawrence Taylor are highlighted as some of the best to play the position. While the NFL's shift to spread offenses has slightly decreased the value of inside linebackers, versatile players who can rush, cover, and stop the run remain highly sought after for their ability to disrupt offenses and create defensive flexibility.

The Bank of Canada and markets are competing over the loonie's value, with the bank preferring a low dollar to aid exporters while markets push it higher on economic strength. The loonie recently reached nearly 75.50 U.S. cents, up 2 percent from the prior week. Its volatility reflects mixed signals from oil prices and the Canada-U.S. interest rate gap. Strong economic data, including 3.7 percent annualized Q1 growth, has led markets to expect an interest rate hike. Bank of Canada officials recently signaled tightening may come sooner than thought, with CIBC now predicting a rate increase in Q4 rather than 2018.

This study investigated whether role-taking and literacy interventions could reduce the influence of demographic and appearance-based cues on trust and risk-taking in social engineering scenarios. Using a 4x2 mixed factorial design, 139 Arab participants evaluated 16 personas offering a mobile hotspot before and after being assigned to Persuader, Persuadee, Literacy, or Control groups. Results from repeated measures ANOVAs and Bayes Factors supported the null hypothesis, showing no significant changes in trust or risk-taking behaviors across any persona factors or roles post-intervention, though issue involvement decreased. Qualitative feedback indicated participants found the intervention engaging and reflective. The authors conclude that short-term interventions may raise awareness but are insufficient to alter deeply ingrained cognitive biases, suggesting future research explore long-term, immersive strategies.

The Great Southern Storm named an initial 45-player colts squad for the Great Southern Colts Carnival in Kulin. Glynn Verbruggen takes over as head coach from Phil Gilbert. The squad, featuring State 16 and State Country colts players, will train twice before the final team is selected. North Albany has the most representatives with 12 players.

The CSU Board of Governors reviewed feedback from the first two on-campus stadium games. Student government is rebranding the tailgating lot and adding pre-game programming to increase student awareness, as many previously only parked there. Attendance was 37,583 for the first game and 27,038 for the second. Initial stadium congestion improved by the second game. Transportation planning was successful, with high transit ridership, manageable post-game traffic, and 50 vehicles towed from campus lots and surrounding neighborhoods each weekend.

Allen Iverson discussed his memoir "Misunderstood" with Stephen A. Smith, identifying his 2013 divorce from Tawanna Turner as his life's lowest point, which coincided with his NBA retirement. Iverson and Turner have since reconciled. This period prompted a self-reevaluation, leading Iverson to address his alcohol use and pursue sobriety. He also noted his influence on younger NBA players, helping them feel comfortable expressing themselves.

Judge Nasir Khan Yousafzai sentenced four convicts in separate murder cases. Shehzado received death and a Rs. 200,000 fine. Ajab Khan, Fateh Khan, and Dilbar Khan received 25-year imprisonments with fines. Advocate Samad Khan Mandokhail represented victims' families.

Texas is replacing the STAAR standardized test with a new law requiring three exams throughout the school year and banning practice tests. While the law aims to reduce student stress and instructional time lost to testing, critics—including parents, teachers, and administrators—worry it will instead increase testing pressure. The TEA must study reducing the weight of these tests on school accountability ratings, but the report is not due until 2029-30 and is not mandatory, meaning high-stakes pressure will likely remain when the system launches in 2027-28. Experts note the overhaul largely codifies existing district practices. Critics advocate for less restrictive testing-day protocols to reduce student anxiety and greater teacher input. Some educators and parents favor using norm-based exams like MAP, which they describe as less stressful and time-consuming than criteria-based tests.

Germany aims to organize Middle Europe to serve its foreign policy, potentially mastering the continent. The United States seeks to disestablish this imperialistic control without thwarting economic unification. Middle Europe's current control relies on an alliance among ruling powers in Berlin, Vienna, Budapest, Sofia, and Constantinople, bound by the subjugation of specific nationalities and war debts. To counter this, the US possesses two main assets. First, the economic weapon: controlling Germany's access to raw materials and markets, threatening it with revolution and financial ruin if excluded. Second, assets in Austria-Hungary: leveraging nationalist discontent among Czechs and South Slavs while offering the preservation of the empire through disarmament and a league of nations. By balancing these threats and safety, the US can compel Austria-Hungary to seek independence from Berlin.

This paper constructs strong pseudorandom unitaries (PRUs) in the quantum Haar random oracle model (QHROM). The proposed construction makes two queries to the Haar random oracle and requires O(log^(1+ε)(n)) bits of randomness to achieve security against polynomial-query adversaries. The security proof utilizes the path-recording framework, introducing an approximate isometry to merge independent databases and conducting a query-by-query analysis. The document also reviews related work on quantum pseudorandomness and idealized quantum cryptographic models.

LAPIS is an extensible compiler framework built on MLIR that bridges the gap between C++ computational science and engineering (CSE) codes and Python-based machine learning (ML) codes. It compiles native Python ML functions into performance-portable Kokkos-based C++ source code, bypassing traditional boilerplate. LAPIS introduces a custom Kokkos dialect, lowering passes, a memory reference model, and a Kokkos C++ emitter. It maps high-level MLIR operations to Kokkos constructs, including parallel loops, synchronization operations, and linear algebra kernels like GEMM and GEMV. The framework supports frontends such as torch-mlir and MPACT, lowering linalg-on-tensors to platform-agnostic mid-level dialects. LAPIS employs heuristics for parallelism estimation and loop mapping to optimize performance across CPU and GPU architectures, automatically inserting synchronization where necessary. Demonstrated on AMD MI300A, NVIDIA H100, and Intel Granite Rapids CPUs, LAPIS matches the performance of hand-optimized implementations for sparse and dense linear algebra and successfully couples CSE with AI/ML use cases, overcoming the extensibility and portability limitations of existing compilers like TACO and Triton.

Chipotle released a new queso dip, but customers are complaining on Twitter about its high price and taste. A company spokesman defended the cost, citing real ingredients and positive test market feedback, and stated there are no plans to lower the price.

The May 23, 2001, State Bar of Michigan e-Journal contains case summaries across multiple legal practice areas, including Bankruptcy, Civil Rights, Constitutional Law, Criminal Law, Employment & Labor Law, Family Law, Insurance, Litigation, Municipal, Negligence & Intentional Tort, and Real Property. The issue also features classified advertisements, Fields of Practice attorney listings, bar events, archived e-Journals, and contact information for editorial and advertising inquiries.

CEMEX, a Mexico-based cement company, became a global building materials leader through strategic acquisitions and its "CEMEX Way" post-merger integration (PMI) process. From 1982 to 2007, CEMEX expanded in four stages: Laying the Groundwork, Stepping Out, Growing Up, and Stepping Up. The CEMEX Way standardized business processes, technology, and organizational structure globally while simultaneously learning and adopting best practices from acquired firms. This approach enabled CEMEX to reduce PMI duration from 25 months to under five months, achieve significant cost savings, and successfully integrate major international targets like Spain's Valenciana and Sanson, the U.S.'s Southdown, the UK's RMC, and Australia's Rinker, overcoming the cement industry's traditionally localized nature.

Peggy Mahoney forwarded an Energy Central Deregulation Public Forum email to Enron colleagues. The forum posed a new question regarding policy changes to encourage natural gas exploration on federal lands and the continental shelf due to expected high demand and prices. The email also published responses to a previous question about whether power generators manipulated the San Diego market for higher profits and if price caps should be imposed. Respondents were divided. Some attributed price spikes to supply and demand imbalances, weather, and flawed deregulation, arguing that price caps would deter investment and cause shortages. Others alleged market manipulation and power withholding, suggesting price caps or cost-of-service regulations are necessary to protect ratepayers.

The 1956 Hungarian revolt was a nationwide uprising against Communist rule, unlike earlier localized riots in East Berlin and Poznan. Following Soviet occupation in 1944, Hungarian Communists consolidated power by 1949 under Mátyás Rákosi, whose policies caused widespread discontent. After Rákosi's dismissal and inspired by de-Stalinization and Polish unrest, a student rally in Budapest on October 23 escalated into violence when state police shot into the crowd. Revolutionary councils demanded nationalism, neutrality, and Soviet withdrawal. Soviet tanks initially worsened the situation, leading to Imre Nagy's appointment as prime minister and János Kádár replacing Erno Gero. Although the Soviets temporarily withdrew and promised sovereignty, this was a camouflage. Distracted by the Suez Crisis, the world watched as Soviet forces invaded on November 3-4. Despite fierce Hungarian resistance, the Soviet army crushed the revolt by November 30, resulting in approximately 25,000 Hungarian and 7,000 Soviet casualties.

Paul Clement is set to become Swansea's manager, replacing Bob Bradley. Bayern Munich permitted Clement to speak with the 19th-ranked Premier League club. He is expected to sign until 2019 and receive a £30 million transfer budget to avoid relegation. Clement previously managed Derby County and assisted Carlo Ancelotti at Bayern Munich, Paris Saint-Germain, and Real Madrid.

A federal judge dismissed Drake's defamation lawsuit against Kendrick Lamar and Universal Music Group over Lamar's song "Not Like Us." The judge ruled the lyrics calling Drake a "certified pedophile" were nonactionable opinion made during a heated rap battle. Drake plans to appeal.

Springfield Officer Conrad Lariviere faces disciplinary action for writing "Hahahaha love this" on Facebook regarding a car fatally striking a counter-protester at a Virginia white supremacist rally. Lariviere apologized, denied racism, and said people shouldn't block roads. Police Commissioner John Barbieri initiated an internal investigation, while Mayor Domenic Sarno denounced the comments.

The DAWN-PLASMA study is a phase 2, randomized, open-label, multicenter trial evaluating convalescent plasma (CP) plus standard of care (SOC) versus SOC alone in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. The primary endpoint is the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Eligible adults have confirmed SARS-CoV-2 and specific illness severity, excluding those already on mechanical ventilation or with recent anti-CD20 therapy. Participants were randomized 2:1 to receive SOC plus CP or SOC alone. The CP intervention consisted of 800-1000 mL (four 200-250 mL doses) with a minimum neutralizing antibody titer of 1/160, administered early. The study adhered to ICH-GCP guidelines, requiring IEC approval and informed consent. Six initial participants were substituted due to withdrawal or screen failure, with no loss to follow-up post-intervention.

The passage details video output data signals representing the 8 MSBs of G/Y/YC, B/CB/C, and R/CR video data, which vary by mode (RGB, YUV444, Y/C, BT.656). It also defines pin states, internal pull configurations, and operating I/O supply voltage.

Williams & Connolly confirmed hackers accessed a small number of attorney emails via a zero-day attack. The firm stated there is no evidence of further IT system access or confidential client data extraction. The hackers are believed to be a nation-state actor. A previous warning indicated hackers tied to the Chinese government are targeting law firms for U.S. national security and international trade information.

Coppin State University, a Maryland HBCU, significantly increased out-of-state enrollment through its "Expand Eagle Nation" program, which offers in-state tuition to students from states without HBCUs. Over two years, qualifying out-of-state enrollment grew from 81 to 416, contributing to a 26% overall enrollment increase this year. This growth occurs as colleges nationwide seek out-of-state students ahead of a projected demographic cliff and amid rising HBCU popularity following the affirmative action ban. Coppin supported this influx with targeted advertising, transfer partnerships, academic preparation, and new housing, though officials noted challenges in convincing students the tuition offer was genuine.

The Democratic Party now controls all branches of government, reflecting the nation's desire to reinterpret its plans and point of view. While America possesses great material wealth and moral force, these have come with inexcusable waste, squandered natural resources, and ignored human costs of industrial achievement. Government has been used for private interests rather than the people. The nation's task is restoration: to correct evil without impairing good, and to purify and humanize common life. Specific reforms needed include the tariff, banking system, industrial system, agricultural efficiency, and natural resource conservation. Government must safeguard citizens' health and rights as matters of justice, not pity. This work must proceed not as partisans but with knowledge and care, restoring rather than destroying. The day calls for dedication to humanity, not party triumph.

The TPS7H500x-SP series are radiation-hardness-assured current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting topologies such as buck, forward, and push-pull with switching frequencies up to 2 MHz. The devices feature programmable undervoltage lockout, soft start, dead time, leading edge blank time, and duty cycle limits. They support internal, external, and primary-secondary synchronization modes. Protection mechanisms include cycle-by-cycle current limiting, hiccup mode, external fault protection, and thermal shutdown at 175°C. The document details the internal voltage reference, error amplifier, and peak current mode control. It provides design equations for a synchronous push-pull converter using GaN FETs, covering component selection for output voltage, transformer, FETs, and frequency compensation. Additionally, it outlines power supply requirements, PCB layout guidelines to minimize noise and EMI, and mechanical packaging information.

Indianapolis Public Schools is hosting public meetings to discuss a taskforce recommendation to close three high schools by the 2018-2019 year due to declining enrollment since the 1970s. All seven district high schools are currently under capacity. The first meeting is Tuesday, followed by others in April and May. The administration will identify schools for closure in June, with a board vote in September.

The paper proposes LG-CD, a visual-linguistic multimodal model for remote sensing change detection. It addresses the limitations of unimodal approaches by integrating natural language with visual data. The method uses a SAM2 encoder with lightweight adapters to extract and fuse multi-scale visual features from bi-temporal images. A Text Fusion Attention Module (TFAM) uses CLIP to encode text prompts into word-level and global embeddings, employing multi-head cross-attention to align textual semantics with visual features. Finally, a visual-semantic fusion decoder integrates this information to generate change detection masks, improving accuracy, robustness, and generalization.

The White House stated it was not defending Roseanne Barr's racist tweet but demanded ABC apologize for airing derogatory comments about the administration. President Trump and Press Secretary Sarah Sanders cited past media statements to highlight a perceived double standard regarding negative comments about the President. Sanders insisted Trump was focused on other matters and was simply calling out media bias.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan noted that the final minicamp practice was balanced, with both offense and defense performing well despite areas needing improvement. He explained that his father observes practices and reviews film to provide advice, though he is not officially on staff. Shanahan relies on his father's perspective to catch details he misses due to his demanding schedule. Before training camp, Shanahan plans to vacation in Mexico with his family to rest. He also emphasized that play-action is crucial to his offense, as it pressures defenses, protects the quarterback and offensive line, and generates explosive plays.

Will Ma's lecture covers post-flop poker strategy. He explains that players typically check to the preflop aggressor, who holds a stronger range. When betting, a general rule is to bet around half the pot on the flop and increase the percentage on the turn and river. The "Fundamental Theorem of Poker" states that players should bet strong hands for value, bluff weak hands to fold better hands, and check middle hands. When facing bets, players should fold most weak hands to avoid reverse implied odds, but can call with good draws or pairs due to implied odds. Raising usually requires two-pair or better in deep-stacked situations. The lecture also discusses leading flops when your range is stronger, bluffing with hands that have outs, and knowing when to abandon a bluff when the board no longer supports your represented range.

This email compiles July 2001 news articles on California's energy crisis. Topics include lawmakers debating competing bills to rescue Southern California Edison from bankruptcy; PG&E suing the state over Gov. Gray Davis's seizure of long-term power contracts; a consumer advocate criticizing a rescue plan for SDG&E; the state selling surplus power at a loss due to low demand; consumer prices rising slightly; Contra Costa County funding energy conservation upgrades; and Duke Energy reporting a 27% profit increase.

Prof. Cyril Dim explains that cervical cancer is a malignancy of the cervix caused by sexually transmitted human papillomavirus (HPV), specifically types 16 and 18. It progresses from asymptomatic, treatable pre-cancerous lesions—detectable via Pap smears—to early-stage cancer, which is curable, and late-stage cancer, which is incurable and fatal. Symptoms include post-coital bleeding, foul-smelling discharge, weight loss, and pelvic pain. Diagnosis requires a tissue biopsy, while treatments include surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy depending on the stage. 

Nigeria faces a high cervical cancer burden and mortality rate due to a lack of structured screening programs. Men act as HPV reservoirs but face no harm from partners with cervical cancer. Women with early-stage cancer can still get pregnant. Preventive measures include HPV vaccines and regular screening. In religious environments, the disease is sometimes misattributed to witchcraft.

A federal judge dismissed Spencer Elden's 2021 lawsuit claiming the 1991 Nirvana album cover featuring him as a naked 4-month-old was child pornography. Judge Fernando Olguin ruled the image is analogous to a family photo of a nude bathing child and does not meet child pornography criteria.

The team believes they are better than their recent two-game performance indicates. The opponent outpositioned and outdefended them, capitalizing on mistakes, turnovers, and poor puck possession. Face-offs are a major issue; centers must at least tie, and wingers need to provide better support against the opponent's physical play. While the team's goaltender played well, they failed to adequately test the opposing goalie. Key players like Alfy, Jason, and Mike Comrie need to improve and return to previous form. The speaker praised Rob Niedermayer as a strong, effective playoff role player. Chris Neil was given the day off for the birth of his child. Moving forward, the team plans to adjust their attack strategy, avoid risky stretch passes, be more patient with the puck, and utilize the fourth line more for energy. The speaker anticipates an emotional home crowd to support the team.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly present in higher education, aiming to develop 21st-century skills through learning, self-correction, and reasoning. AI transforms teaching, research, management, and external relations by offering personalized learning, automated grading, and streamlined administration. While AI provides advantages like high accuracy, speed, and adaptive platforms, it also presents challenges. These include equity of access, data privacy, teacher training, financial costs, and AI's inability to think creatively or process emotions. Successfully integrating AI requires a participatory process, developing AI literacy among stakeholders, and reshaping the teacher's role while maintaining academic freedom.
Precisely estimating m-qubit polynomial functionals is a cornerstone of quantum information and physics.

The speaker expresses surprise and gratitude at being put back in the lineup by coach Pat after a two-week absence. Nervous but determined to contribute, they helped the team win. The speaker reflects on winning their third cup in nine years and building a foundation for next year despite a difficult season with roster changes. They credit Pat's no-nonsense approach and relentless focus for preventing complacency, noting that while Pat is a tough coach, his methods are effective and well worth it.

An analysis by Derek Muller found BigLaw and larger plaintiffs-side firms are shifting left. In 2023-2024, 92.45% of their campaign contributions went to Democrats, up from a 6-1 ratio in 2017-2020 to 12-1. Democrats received about $52 million versus $4 million for Republicans. Cleary Gottlieb Steen & Hamilton had the highest Democratic contribution rate (99.7%), while Nelson Mullins Riley & Scarborough had the lowest (66.4%).

The lecture covers discrete symmetries—parity (P), time reversal (T), and charge conjugation (C)—in quantum mechanics and quantum field theory. While P and C correspond to unitary transformations, T requires an anti-unitary (anti-linear) operator to maintain the Schrödinger equation under time reversal. For complex scalar fields, these symmetries can include phases restricted to plus or minus one, with C exchanging particles and antiparticles. For Dirac fields, P, T, and C require matrices acting on spinor space to keep the Dirac equation invariant. The lecture also introduces path integrals for fermions, which use Grassmann variables—anti-commuting numbers where the square of any variable is zero. The integration of Grassmann variables is defined to be linear and yield the same result as differentiation.

U.S. stock index futures rose, driven by a strong earnings season start and rebounding oil prices. However, geopolitical tensions and the French election limited risky bets. S&P 500 profits are estimated up 10.8%. Qualcomm and Visa shares rose, while eBay fell. Upcoming data includes jobless claims, and oil recovered on potential OPEC supply cut extensions.

The passage describes systems, devices, and methods for spatially and temporally synchronizing a rotating LIDAR sensor with one or more cameras. The cameras are arranged in a ring around the LIDAR's axis of rotation and operate in a rolling shutter mode, with rows of sensing elements aligned parallel to the LIDAR's axis. A controller synchronizes the timing and viewing directions of the camera's image pixel capture with the LIDAR's light pulse emissions and detections. This process aligns image capture times and fields-of-view with LIDAR data collection, improving the combination of sensor data. The system includes components such as a power supply, controller, actuators, rotating and stationary platforms, and a housing. The method involves rotating the LIDAR to scan the environment, capturing a sequence of image pixels using the synchronized cameras, and associating the LIDAR data with the image pixels based on timing and field-of-view overlap. This combined data is used to generate representations of the environment, such as colored 3D point clouds or images with depth information.

Quantbot Technologies LP increased its Zoe’s Kitchen (ZOES) shares by 114.5% in Q2. Several other institutional investors also adjusted their ZOES holdings in Q1. In August, Director A. Alexander Taylor II purchased 3,100 shares. Analysts have a consensus "Hold" rating and a $17.55 target price on the stock. Zoe’s Kitchen reported quarterly earnings of $0.06 EPS on $74.30 million in revenue, a 12.1% year-over-year increase. The company operates fast-casual restaurants serving Mediterranean-inspired dishes.

The appellate court affirmed Bradford Washington's two judgments convicting him of murder and other crimes. The court found his claims regarding a detective's testimony, jury instructions on consciousness of guilt, and the prosecutor's summation theory to be unpreserved and without merit. The second judgment was affirmed based on the first.

Darren Osborne was sentenced to life in prison with a minimum of 43 years for driving a van into worshippers outside a London mosque last June, killing Makram Ali and injuring nine others. Found guilty of murder and attempted murder, Osborne was reportedly "brainwashed" into Islamophobia after watching a BBC drama. Ali's family expressed satisfaction with the verdict, while police noted the community united rather than divided following the attack.

Facebook's iOS and Android apps are adding a "Trending News" section. Accessed via the "Explore" tab, it ranks aggregated stories by publication volume and displays headlines, videos, photos, and related posts.

In the second quarter, hedge funds trimmed healthcare stakes as the sector rallied following dimmed Republican efforts to repeal the Affordable Care Act. Jana Partners and Third Point sold significant healthcare shares. Overall, hedge funds gained 1 percent. Meanwhile, funds sold off various energy stakes as the sector fell 7 percent due to declining oil prices, with Third Point, Jana, and Omega Advisors exiting multiple positions.

The Bankruptcy Court denied Fincke's motion to reconsider its prior ruling that he violated Massachusetts securities law § 410(a)(2) by falsely stating in Access's October 2002 Business Plan that patent counsel had advised the company's product did not infringe any known patents. On damages, the court found the Investors' testimony of reliance on the Business Plan not credible and held that only Zimmel's stock purchases in October and November 2002 ($1.5 million total) were made "by means of" the misstatement. The court entered judgment for Zimmel of $1,500,000 plus 6% interest from May 25, 2007, and for Access of $281,534.62 plus 12% interest from July 6, 2004, for Fincke's fiduciary duty breaches.

The passage describes an electronic cigarette featuring a coil-less atomizer that uses woven fiber tubes, such as carbon fiber, to replace traditional heating wires and wicks. The woven fiber tube acts as both the heating element and the liquid wick. It features a central heating section with higher electrical resistance and end sections that contact a liquid supply. Liquid is transported to the heating section via capillary action through the tube's hollow interior and porous walls. The tube can be shaped into U, C, or L forms and made from various conductive and composite materials. The manufacturing process involves installing the tubes on a board, masking the heating section, and sputtering conductive material onto the unmasked end sections to create the desired resistance differential. During operation, an airflow sensor detects a user's puff, triggering the control electronics to heat the section and vaporize the liquid, while additional liquid is continuously drawn via capillary action.

The BIRDS workshop aims to bridge the gap between digital library professionals, who often lack computational resources, and computer science researchers, who are rarely aware of real-world library challenges. The full-day, interactive workshop seeks to foster collaboration, identify common challenges, and promote innovative research systems for digital libraries. Its format includes a keynote, scientific speed-dating, a panel discussion, and breakout group discussions. Targeting approximately 25 practitioners and researchers, the workshop is organized by Christin Katharina Kreutz and Hermann Kroll.

The Ohio Supreme Court upheld the constitutionality of R.C. 3105.03's one-year durational residency requirement for divorce. The court found that, unlike welfare or voting rights, divorce is not a basic need, so the requirement does not penalize the constitutional right to interstate travel. The court held that Ohio has a compelling interest in overseeing marriage and divorce laws for its residents, and that the one-year requirement is the least restrictive means of ensuring the state's divorce laws are not applied to nonresidents, since domicile intent is difficult to verify otherwise.

Released shortly after the 1987 Black Monday crash, Oliver Stone's film "Wall Street" remains the preeminent movie on finance. Its success stems from its rags-to-riches narrative, fairy tale elements, and immersive depiction of 1980s excess. The story follows lowly broker Bud Fox, who achieves wealth through the charismatic Gordon Gekko. Michael Douglas's Oscar-winning performance as Gekko, an embodiment of corporate greed, is a major highlight. Unlike other financial villains, Gekko targets corporations rather than everyday individuals. Decades later, the film endures as a time capsule of the era, driven by its memorable quotes, 1980s culture, and cautionary tale.

On August 17, 2022, Apple Inc.'s Compensation Committee approved the Executive Cash Incentive Plan, enabling eligible executives to receive cash awards based on Committee-established performance goals. Concurrently, Apple's Board adopted amended and restated bylaws. Key bylaw amendments include allowing special Board meetings on under 48 hours' notice, enhancing disclosure and procedural requirements for shareholder nominations and proposals, clarifying Board authority over shareholder meeting locations and conduct, revising procedures for shareholder-requested special meetings, mandating non-white proxy cards for shareholder solicitations, and adding emergency operational provisions. The report was signed on August 19, 2022.

A developer modified Google's HDR+ camera app for Snapdragon Android phones. Amazon is refunding unsafe solar-eclipse glasses. HBO refuses to pay hackers leaking shows and emails. Waymo patented car body technology that softens during pedestrian collisions to reduce injuries.

Amazon.com, Inc.'s 2016 Form 10-K outlines its operations across three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). In 2016, the company reported $135.99 billion in net sales, $4.19 billion in operating income, and $2.37 billion in net income, employing approximately 341,400 people. The filing details extensive risk factors, including intense competition, international expansion challenges, fulfillment network optimization, seasonality, data security, and evolving tax regulations. Management focuses on long-term free cash flow growth, driven by increasing operating income and efficiently managing working capital. AWS sales grew 55% to $12.22 billion, generating $3.11 billion in operating income. Total operating cash flow for 2016 was $16.44 billion.

Retired Justice Anthony Kennedy’s memoir discusses his judicial philosophy and notable Supreme Court cases. Kennedy emphasizes judicial humility and integrity, rejecting strict originalism and pragmatism in favor of interpreting the Constitution through a broadened perspective over time. He reflects on his controversial opinions, including *Citizens United*, where he believed voters hold the true power over campaign money; *Obergefell*, which he based on marriage's history and the welfare of children; and *Bush v. Gore*, where he focused solely on legal issues. He details his reconciliation with Justice Antonin Scalia following Scalia's harsh dissent in the same-sex marriage case, which occurred shortly before Scalia's death. Kennedy expresses dislike for the term "swing justice," stating the cases swung, not him. On abortion, he separates personal moral views from legal duties, noting he considered resigning but stayed to protect constitutional rights. The memoir also covers his views on presidential deference to the Court, his opposition to cameras in the courtroom to prevent grandstanding, a chilling meeting with Vladimir Putin regarding capital punishment, and a personal anecdote about his house being ransacked after declining to lower Lynette Fromme’s bail.

The Simons Observatory's Large Aperture Telescope (LAT) uses SMuRF electronics to read out thousands of TES detectors. Because the LAT receiver cabin is exposed to diurnal temperature swings, its room-temperature RF transmission lines are susceptible to systematic phase drifts that could mimic detector signals. To assess this, researchers analyzed off-resonance tones and found that the phase drifts correlate with ambient temperature but remain at the picosecond level over a day-night cycle. Analytical conversions show this phase drift contributes minimally to on-sky detector noise, remaining within the readout noise budget and not affecting the telescope's mapping speed.

Evelyn Montiel's family ran an ice cream business in East Oakland. As a high school student, she worked long hours to keep it afloat. She became the first in her family to attend college but dropped out due to depression. The organization Students Rising Above (SRA) helped her transfer to USC, where she thrived. After graduating during the recession, she struggled to find a job and returned to the family business. SRA later connected her with an investment firm interview, launching her finance career. She now works as a broker at a Silicon Valley startup and credits SRA for her success.

Tesla, Inc. filed its Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022. The company designs, manufactures, sells, and leases electric vehicles and energy generation and storage systems, operating through two reportable segments: Automotive and Energy Generation and Storage. Automotive products include the Model 3, Y, S, X, and Tesla Semi, alongside the development of Full Self-Driving technology. Energy products include Powerwall, Megapack, and solar energy systems like Solar Roof.

Tesla sells products directly to customers globally and operates manufacturing facilities in the US, China, and Germany. The company relies on a global supply chain for thousands of parts and is developing its own battery cells to meet growing demand. Its business is impacted by various governmental programs, incentives like the Inflation Reduction Act, and regulations concerning vehicle safety, self-driving, and dealer operations.

The company faces significant competition in both the automotive and energy markets. Tesla emphasizes ESG initiatives, human capital development, and intellectual property protection. Key risk factors include macroeconomic conditions like the COVID-19 pandemic, supply chain disruptions, production ramp delays, supplier issues, battery cell availability, product defects, product liability, financing risks, reliance on key personnel like CEO Elon Musk, and cybersecurity threats.

Top stories feature Chiaro Networks raising $100 million, Bertelsmann and iSyndicate forming a European joint venture, Novalux securing $109 million, online retailer Miadora shutting down, Sun Microsystems launching a $50 million Asian investment program, and Mayfield Fund naming a marketing partner. NVIDIA Corporation's FY2017 10-K Annual Report covers the fiscal year ended January 29, 2017. The company operates through two reportable segments, GPU and Tegra Processor, targeting four primary markets: Gaming, Professional Visualization, Datacenter, and Automotive. NVIDIA focuses on visual and accelerated computing, leveraging its GPU technology for artificial intelligence and deep learning. 

NVIDIA employs a fabless manufacturing strategy, relying on third-party suppliers like TSMC and Samsung for wafer fabrication, and independent subcontractors for assembly, testing, and packaging. The aggregate market value of voting stock held by non-affiliates was approximately $28.98 billion as of July 29, 2016. During FY2017, NVIDIA paid $261 million in cash dividends and repurchased shares under its buyback program, with an additional $2.00 billion authorized by the Board through December 2020. Risk factors detailed in the filing include intense competition, reliance on third-party manufacturers, potential product defects, cybersecurity threats, international operations risks, and fluctuating operating results. On November 27, 2001, Enron Corp. struggled to find willing sellers for near-term gas and power, causing its trading volume to drop significantly, though the company claimed only a slight reduction. Dynegy Inc. confirmed it was renegotiating its acquisition of Enron, potentially cutting the original $9 billion buyout price by over 40% to around $5 billion by lowering the stock exchange ratio. Enron simultaneously sought $500 million to $1 billion in additional funding and debt extensions, but was turned down by investors including Prince Alwaleed, Blackstone, and Carlyle. Moody’s kept Enron’s credit rating unchanged at the lowest investment grade. Enron announced the closure of its equity trading unit and faced multiple employee and shareholder lawsuits. Analysts noted the deterioration of Enron's core trading business, while some hedge funds considered trading its volatile stock and bonds.

Modeling electron-photon interactions in optical cavities requires dedicated computational tools for non-local coupling terms. The sinc basis set is a promising solution due to its orthonormality and systematic improvability. Although direct implementation has a high O(N^4) cost, sparse or low-rank approximations can mitigate this scaling, making sinc functions suitable for extended interactions.

The DAWN-Plasma trial was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 study evaluating convalescent plasma plus standard of care (SOC) versus SOC alone in 489 hospitalized COVID-19 patients. Participants received four units of high-titer convalescent plasma early in their hospitalization. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients alive and free of mechanical ventilation at Day 15. The study found no significant difference between the treatment and control groups for the primary endpoint (83.7% vs. 84.1%), any secondary endpoints, or safety outcomes, including adverse and serious adverse events. The trial concluded that early administration of high antibody titre convalescent plasma did not change the natural course of COVID-19 in hospitalized patients.

This study used 2009-2020 NHANES data from 32,498 US adults to identify empirical dietary patterns and their associations with cardiovascular disease (CVD), socioeconomic vulnerability (SDOH score), and SNAP participation. Researchers identified four dietary patterns: "American" (least healthy), "Prudent", "Legume", and "Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy" (healthiest). The American pattern was most common overall and more prevalent among adults with CVD, higher SDOH scores, and SNAP participation. Higher SDOH scores and SNAP participation were also associated with lower adherence to the Prudent and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy patterns, but higher adherence to the Legume pattern. Some associations varied by race and ethnicity, such as the lack of a link between higher SDOH scores and the American pattern among Hispanic individuals. The authors conclude that dietary patterns vary by cardiovascular health and socioeconomic vulnerability, suggesting that clinical and public health interventions should consider these naturally occurring patterns to improve nutrition and health equity.

This is the June 4, 2001, State Bar of Michigan e-Journal. The publication provides case summaries across multiple practice areas, including Business Law, Civil Rights, Contracts, Criminal Law, Employment & Labor Law, Family Law, Litigation, and Negligence & Intentional Tort, featuring three U.S. Court of Appeals Sixth Circuit opinions. It also contains classified advertisements, fields of practice attorney listings, news and moves, bar events, and editorial content. The e-Journal is provided to members at no additional charge due to advertiser support.

A player's stable personality, skill, and size allow him to perform under pressure and score key playoff goals without overreacting. After making defensive adjustments, they played an inspired game, dictating play five-on-five. A study shows biased online images train AI to perceive women as younger and less experienced, evidencing workforce discrimination against older women.

The Wham play is a complementary football run concept similar to a Trap, but uses a Tight End or Fullback to pull and kick out a Defensive Lineman. Its strengths include creating favorable running angles quickly and unexpectedly, serving as an effective change-up. However, it is complex and time-consuming to install, requiring precise front identification, strict blocking rules, and a physically powerful blocker. Teams often use specific formations to ensure predictable defensive fronts. The passage details specific blocking assignments against 3-4 Odd and 4-3 Even fronts. Variations include the Gun H-Back Wham RPO, which targets the Nose Tackle and adds a pass option, and the Shotgun Influence Wham, which uses a pulling Guard to influence a defender before the Fullback traps him.

The filing also lists the company's registered securities, including common stock and notes due in 2021, 2028, and 2033. The report was signed by Assistant Secretary Keith R. Dolliver.

This study evaluated horizontal Hepatitis C (HCV) transmission among household members of HCV-positive patients in Huye, Rwanda. Using a cross-sectional design, 148 participants from 30 families were tested via HCV Ab rapid test and ELISA. The study found a 10.8% HCV prevalence. Significant correlations were identified with HBV, HIV, and unprotected sex, while blood transfusion and awareness levels were not significant. The study concluded that unprotected sex was the primary transmission factor and recommended early screening, education for household members, improved follow-up by the Ministry of Health, and further countrywide phylogenetic research.

President Donald Trump has nominated Travis Hill, a senior Treasury Department adviser, to chair the FDIC. Pending Senate confirmation, Hill is expected to implement a pragmatic, deregulatory approach aligning with Trump’s economic strategy. He will oversee deposit insurance and bank assessments, though his nomination may face scrutiny over potential regulatory leniency.

Nunavut MLA George Hickes is warning against the intimidation of civil servants who wish to speak with their elected representatives. The Chamber of Mines of Namibia will host the Mining Expo & Conference on April 25-26 in Windhoek. The Construction Defining Functionality (CDF) framework analyzes computational problems by distinguishing between internal generative rules (intensionality) and observable behaviors (extensionality). It models problems using a tripartite architecture consisting of syntactic, semantic, and logical spaces connected by structural mappings. CDF classifies problems based on structural coherence. ComCDF problems, such as 2-SAT, possess local, compositional structures that support stable, polynomial-time reasoning. Conversely, ExpCDF problems, such as 3-SAT, contain non-local syntactic structures that induce exponential semantic explosion and computational intractability. The framework establishes that this intractability is an intrinsic structural property of the problem's generative syntax rather than an artifact of inefficient algorithms.

Patents grant temporary monopolies on 3D printing technologies, after which they become widely accessible. Scott Crump's 1992 FDM patent led to both inexpensive desktop printers and costly industrial machines used for demanding applications. Other methods include stereolithography and powder bed fusion, the latter driving metal additive manufacturing (AM). Manufacturers view AM as a next-generation tool for a $12.8 trillion market. AM utilizes diverse materials, scales from small to massive parts, and achieves competitive throughput for short-run production. Applications include NASA propulsion systems and GE engine components, which reduce weight and part counts. As industrial patents expire, entrepreneurs package these processes for the public. The Wohlers Report serves as a comprehensive annual industry resource.

European shares rose, with the STOXX 600 and German DAX reaching multi-month highs, largely unfazed by the formal start of Brexit negotiations. At the UN Climate Summit, President Xi Jinping reaffirmed China's clean energy commitments, positioning the country as a global leader amid stalled climate action by the US, EU, and India. China pledged to cut greenhouse gas emissions by 7-10% by 2035, reach 3,600 GW of installed wind and solar capacity, and make electric vehicles mainstream. Having invested $625 billion last year, China's domestic market and research have driven down global green technology prices and reshaped the global economy. China also committed to expanding its carbon trading market and increasing forest extent.

A randomized controlled trial in Cambodia evaluated the efficacy of 3.5 mg/kg versus 7.0 mg/kg primaquine over 14 days to prevent *Plasmodium vivax* recurrences. Patients received artesunate and were relocated for 90 days to prevent reinfection. G6PD-normal patients were randomized to 3.5 mg/kg, 7.0 mg/kg, or no primaquine; G6PD-deficient patients received no primaquine. Among 156 allocated patients, the 90-day recurrence rate was 81.4% without primaquine, 24.4% with the 3.5 mg/kg dose, and 4.7% with the 7.0 mg/kg dose. The high dose significantly reduced recurrence risk compared to the low dose, and both primaquine regimens were well tolerated. The study concludes that the 7.0 mg/kg regimen is more effective and should be endorsed in Cambodia and likely other Southeast Asian countries.
Paulo Dybala expects to play against Barcelona and renewed his Juventus contract until 2022 by choice. Fans are relieved by his return following his crucial first-leg performance.

English local authorities will receive millions in refunds after the Ministry of Justice overcharged for council tax summons fees since 2013-14 due to an administrative error. Councils overpaid about £9m annually. The MoJ is urgently reducing fees and will soon outline a reimbursement scheme. In 2016-17, total arrears costs reached £292m, thousands faced court, and at least 62 people were imprisoned for council tax offences.

enGene hired Hussein Sweiti as chief medical officer. He previously worked at Johnson & Johnson as global medical head, oncology clinical development.

The Council of Regional Accrediting Commissions (CRAC) encourages colleges to use artificial intelligence to improve the inconsistent, time-consuming process of transferring college credits, which often leads to credit loss and students abandoning degrees. Cryotherapy, invented in the 1970s for arthritis, involves brief exposure to extreme cold. Enthusiasts claim it provides various health benefits, but it lacks FDA approval and scientific backing, with the FDA warning of potential injuries. Facilities like Polar Brrr Cryo in Michigan offer supervised three-minute sessions, where the cold is said to stimulate the vascular system and promote healing. Bollinger Bands, created by John Bollinger, measure market volatility using a simple moving average (SMA) and two standard deviation bands. The bands widen during high volatility and contract during low volatility. Traders use various strategies, including the Squeeze, Breakouts, %B, Walks, and Reversals, to identify overbought or oversold conditions, trend strength, and entry or exit points. Settings like the SMA period and standard deviations can be adjusted for different timeframes and asset classes. While Bollinger Bands can be profitable in mean-revertive markets like stocks or as a breakout indicator in gold, they have limitations, such as delayed signals and false positives. The passage recommends using them alongside other technical indicators and risk management techniques.

The holiday effect is a stock market anomaly where returns increase around specific holidays. Backtesting the S&P 500 around seven US holidays reveals that Independence Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas offer the most tradeable effects. The article also identifies a post-holiday effect, noting that holding stocks for the second day after a holiday yields strong returns. While the holiday effect is real, it is small and best used as a supplementary trading strategy.

Scottish councils can raise basic council tax rates by up to 3% following the end of a government freeze. Amazon is developing an AI chip for Alexa, which had a popular Super Bowl ad and strong Echo Dot holiday sales. Amazon and Google lost money discounting speakers, while Apple's speaker is delayed. CES featured Sony's Aibo robot dog. Amazon also announced Alexa will power Big Mouth Billy Bass, and a rogue Alexa played loud music in Germany.

The document is an AMD legal agreement and technical specification for the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB). The agreement outlines licensing terms, warranty disclaimers, liability limitations, export controls, and California governing law. The specification standardizes the GHCB to enable guest operating systems to interoperate with hypervisors supporting SEV-ES and SEV-SNP, which protect and encrypt guest register state during world switches. 

The GHCB is a 4KB decrypted page mirroring the SEV-ES VMCB save state area. The specification details the GHCB MSR protocol for negotiation and CPUID requests, Guest Physical Address (GPA) registration, and the GHCB layout. VMEXITs are classified as Automatic Exits (AE) or Non-Automatic Exits (NAE). For NAEs, the guest uses a #VC exception handler to communicate with the hypervisor via the VMGEXIT instruction. 

The document defines the required state and handling for various NAE events, including IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, MMIO access, Page State Change, SNP Guest Requests, SNP Extended Guest Requests, SNP AP Creation, #HV Doorbell, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, Secure AVIC, and Termination Requests. It also covers SMP booting challenges, NMI handling, debug register support, and SNP Restricted Injection using hypervisor doorbells. Version 2 and its revisions introduce hypervisor feature advertisement, SEV-SNP support, SEV-TIO, and Secure AVIC enhancements.

A report by Lucas Chancel and Thomas Piketty states that India's income inequality surged since the 1980s, with the top 1% capturing 22% of national income, the highest since 1922. This aligns with pro-business policies starting in the mid-1980s. Conversely, the 1950s-1970s saw reduced inequality and faster growth for the bottom 50% and middle 40% due to market regulations. Russia is increasingly targeting Ukrainian drone pilots, viewing them as top threats due to their combat effectiveness. The passage introduces "Doublethink," a Bayesian model averaging method that establishes a correspondence between Bayesian posterior odds and frequentist p-values to simultaneously control false discovery and familywise error rates. The authors applied this method to identify direct, non-genetic risk factors for COVID-19 hospitalization in UK Biobank using 1,912 variables. The analysis identified significant individual variables, such as unspecified dementia and acute lower respiratory infections, and tested groups of correlated variables to recover signals diluted by collinearity, such as age, sex, and obesity. Comparing these findings to 127 published studies, the authors confirmed many established risk factors but found no direct effects for diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and hypertension, suggesting their effects may be mediated. The method is limited by its focus on direct rather than total effects, high computational demands, and reliance on large sample assumptions. Doublethink provides a systematic approach to evaluating direct risk factors in biobank-scale data while bridging Bayesian and classical statistical frameworks.

The passage traces the evolution and value of software development patterns, from algorithms and object-oriented design to open-source collaboration. Patterns offer shared learning, a common vocabulary, and reusable components.

The text details single-node container patterns, where tightly coupled containers share a machine:
- Sidecar: Augments an application container with additional functionality like HTTPS, configuration synchronization, or monitoring, without altering the original application.
- Ambassador: Brokers interactions between the application and external services, enabling sharding, service brokering, and request splitting.
- Adapter: Standardizes application interfaces for monitoring, logging, and health checks, ensuring consistency across heterogeneous systems.

The passage also covers multi-node distributed patterns, which rely on network communication:
- Microservices: Breaks applications into small, decoupled services with formal APIs, enhancing agility and independent scaling, though increasing debugging complexity.
- Replicated Load-Balanced Services: Uses identical, stateless replicas behind a load balancer for redundancy and scaling. This pattern can be enhanced with caching layers and SSL termination, and adapted for session tracking.
- Sharded Services: Divides stateful services into shards, where each handles a subset of requests, allowing the system to manage larger data sets. Sharded caches improve memory utilization, and shards can be replicated for added resilience.

Teams must prepare for defensive, even, and offensive jump ball situations. Defensive jump balls, where opponents have the advantage, require specific alignments (Box, Diamond, "Y") and rotations to prevent easy shots by anticipating the jumper's tipped direction. Even jump balls involve boxing out and coordinated clockwise or counter-clockwise rotations. Offensive jump balls utilize a height advantage to execute set plays like the Double Tap, Post Split, Jumper Fly, and Spread, while ensuring defensive balance is maintained.

Following Trump's vague response to the Charlottesville rally, Merck CEO Ken Frazier resigned from the American Manufacturing Council to protest intolerance. The passage examines two stocks with a 7.1% forecast dividend yield. Taylor Wimpey announced a policy targeting £1.3bn in shareholder returns from 2016 to 2018. With 2016 free cash flow of £511.6m and plans for a £450m dividend in 2017, the author views its 7.1% yield as affordable and sustainable. Conversely, Connect Group's 7.1% forecast yield is supported by strong cash generation, but the firm has £141.7m in net debt and a negative net tangible asset value of minus £151.8m. The author notes a trading slowdown could force Connect to cancel its dividend, concluding that the risks outweigh the rewards.
A 2017 Regina Police Service survey of 462 people found high satisfaction with service quality and integrity. However, nearly 25% felt ethnic insensitivity, prompting ongoing reconciliation training.

Defending baseline out of bounds plays in basketball requires specific strategies because the defense has a 5-on-4 numerical advantage. Standard half-court or zone defenses are often ineffective since baseline plays involve direct cuts to the basket and screen actions. The passage outlines four effective defensive methods:
1. Jam: A no-switching, aggressive defense that disrupts plays, protects the middle, and smothers the inbounder.
2. Jump Switch: Aggressively switching screens and denying passing lanes to create turnovers, especially useful under five seconds.
3. Trap: Double-teaming the receiver of the inbounds pass to force turnovers.
4. Combination Defense: Using Box & One, Diamond & One, or Triangle & Two alignments to surprise the offense and deny key players the ball. All strategies emphasize protecting the basket initially before applying aggressive pressure.

This study examines the molecular signature of neuropathic pain using Morton’s neuroma tissue compared to control nerves. Researchers analyzed 22 Morton’s neuroma and 11 control nerve samples using RNA sequencing and immunofluorescence. Results identified 3,349 differentially expressed genes, with upregulated genes linked to immune and inflammatory responses, and downregulated genes related to nervous system development. Deconvolution analysis revealed increased macrophages and Memory B cells, while specific M(GC) MARCO+ macrophage subset genes correlated with paroxysmal pain. Histological validation confirmed demyelination and increased intraneural T-cells and M(GC) MARCO+ macrophages. The findings implicate ongoing neuroinflammation in chronic human neuropathic pain.

The authors propose extending the iterative proportional fitting (IPF) algorithm for Schrödinger bridge (SB) problems to handle marginal distributions given as unnormalised densities rather than data samples. Using off-policy reinforcement learning, this data-to-energy and energy-to-energy IPF is the first general method for such bridges. The paper presents three contributions: the proposed IPF learns low-transport-cost stochastic bridges on par with data-to-data IPF; existing data-to-data IPF can be improved by learning the diffusion coefficient alongside the drift; and the algorithm enables scalable, data-free image-to-image translation by translating prior distributions to posteriors in latent spaces. The passage also provides background on the SB problem and IPF formulation.

The passage covers multiple news stories from May 2001 regarding Enron and the energy sector. Enron CEO Kenneth Lay privately pitched a deregulation plan to California leaders, who remained noncommittal, while Californians actively conserved energy. Enron's Dabhol Power project in India faced escalating disputes with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board over unpaid bills and contract validity, leading to rejected payments and termination notices. In Washington, Senator Dianne Feinstein sought hearings into potential undue influence by Enron on the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), following reports that Lay offered support to FERC's chairman in exchange for policy alignment. The Senate confirmed two new FERC commissioners. Additionally, Saudi Arabia prepared to sign gas development agreements with foreign oil companies, and an impending shift in Senate control raised the possibility of electricity price cap legislation for California.

The coach reviews a one-goal game, citing an early penalty and missed scoring chances. He stresses that team speed, not physical play, is their main advantage and was crucial in prior playoff victories against Detroit, Vancouver, and San Jose. He discusses using home ice for favorable line matches against specific opponents. He notes that previous playoff losses provided learning experiences. Overnight trading involves buying at the market close and selling at the next day's open or close to exploit the overnight edge, as average gains from open to close have been zero over the past 30 years. Traders use various strategies, including seasonal effects, mean-reversion, and weekday effects. To maximize returns and minimize drawdowns, it is essential to construct a portfolio of uncorrelated strategies across different asset classes, time frames, and strategy types. While backtests are approximations, overnight trading's short holding period allows traders to capitalize on brief market movements and improve risk-adjusted returns.

The lecture details the construction of Succinct Non-Interactive Arguments (SNARGs) using Batch Arguments (BARGs) and somewhere extractable hash functions. A BARG allows a prover to succinctly demonstrate that multiple instances belong to an NP language, utilizing semi-adaptive soundness. Somewhere extractable hashes enable hashing values with local openings and statistical binding on a specific index, which can be extended to multiple indices. To construct a SNARG, the generator creates a hash key and a BARG CRS. The prover computes all wires of a verification circuit, hashes them, and generates a BARG proving that every gate is satisfied via valid openings and that the output wire is 1. This study theoretically demonstrates that coupling a quantum critical system to an optical cavity amplifies its physical responses. Focusing on a ferromagnetic transverse field Ising model (TFIM) coupled to cavity photons, the authors show that when the cavity mode directly couples to the quantum critical degree of freedom (the order parameter), superradiant phase transitions (SRPTs) can be achieved at arbitrarily weak light-matter coupling strengths. This direct coupling enhances intrinsic squeezing and light-matter quantum entanglement beyond the levels found in the standard Dicke model. Conversely, when the cavity couples to a non-critical mode, ferromagnetism and superradiance compete, resulting in a complex phase diagram featuring a tricritical point. These predictions, supported by large-S analysis and density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) calculations, suggest that quantum criticality can be harnessed in cavity-matter platforms to enhance entanglement and metrological performance, with potential experimental realization in materials such as CoNb2O6, LiHoF4, and CrI3.

The Reconfigurable Power Station (RPS) is an autonomous system designed to extend the operational range of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) by automatically exchanging depleted Swap Cartridges (SCs) for energized ones. Once a UAV lands, the RPS secures it and uses a swapping mechanism to remove the depleted SC, store it in a Modular Power Bay (MPB) for recharging, and install a compatible energized SC into the UAV's Universal Integrated Swap system (UIS). The system is managed by a central processor, accommodates multiple UAV types and sizes, and can be applied to other unmanned vehicles.

Experimental progress in orbitronics utilizes methods like torque measurements, magnetoresistance, and direct imaging to study orbital angular momentum (OAM). Experiments show materials like CuOx generate strong OAM, which converts to spin and transports over longer distances than spin currents. Two-dimensional materials also exhibit distinct orbital Hall effects. 

Theoretically, orbital Hall and Rashba-Edelstein effects generate OAM without spin-orbit coupling. However, OAM torque magnitude and relaxation length remain unresolved, with conflicting evidence on long-range transport versus strong crystal field dissipation. 

For MRAM applications, orbital torque enables using light, low-resistivity metals. Challenges include increasing torque efficiency, ensuring compatibility with high tunneling magnetoresistance systems, and reducing layer thicknesses. Box 1 explains OAM generation from orbital texture, while Box 2 outlines MRAM requirements like high endurance, low write current, and scalability. Overall, orbitronics promises robust, tunable devices using abundant, non-hazardous materials.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture introduces significant advancements in memory, compute, and partitioning for HPC and AI workloads. The Tug Ocean Prince, push-towing the oil-laden Barge New London, struck a charted rock in the Hudson River, causing an oil spill. Trapped-ion quantum computers face slow gate operation times due to ions' charge-to-mass ratios, whereas free electrons offer faster operation but cannot be laser-cooled. This paper proposes a two-frequency planar Paul trap to simultaneously confine laser-cooled Ca+ ions and electrons in the same space, coupling their quantum systems. In this setup, an electron experiences a combined Coulomb and harmonic potential, resulting in three state categories: low excited atomic states, transitional Rydberg-like states, and trap-induced harmonic oscillator-like states above the ionization threshold. These trap-induced states, tunable via trap parameters, could enable faster quantum gates, high-resolution photon counting, and RF-to-optical signal conversion. The authors detail a planar ring trap design optimized to maximize the confining pseudopotential's steepness while maintaining a symmetric field for both particles.

This disclosure describes ultrasonic fingerprint sensor systems integrated under displays, such as OLED displays. The apparatus includes a display, an underlying ultrasonic sensor system configured to transmit and receive ultrasonic waves through the display, and a multi-functional film positioned in the acoustic path. This film may consist of a light-blocking layer, an electrical shielding layer, an adhesive layer, and a mechanical stress isolation layer. These components reduce optical and electrical interference, dissipate heat, minimize mechanical stress on the display, and allow for sensor separation and rework. The ultrasonic sensor system features a piezoelectric transceiver layer and sensor pixel circuits on a substrate, configurable in "receiver up" or "receiver down" orientations. Additionally, the system may utilize high or low acoustic impedance layers, foam backing, stiffeners, or air cavities to enhance acoustic reflection, provide mechanical support, and protect the sensor. This integration enables fingerprint authentication through the active display area without compromising display or sensor performance.

Local operators for heavy-to-light and heavy-to-heavy transitions are renormalized. Heavy-to-light currents yield a constant anomalous dimension independent of spin structure, while heavy-to-heavy currents produce a non-trivial anomalous dimension depending on w = v·v', reflecting kinematic dependence. Matching between full QCD and HQET is simplified by using dimensional regularization for both UV and IR divergences, making HQET loop graphs scaleless and allowing Wilson coefficients to be extracted from the full theory calculation alone. Power corrections at order 1/M_Q are constructed by integrating out the B_v field, yielding a kinetic energy term (breaking flavor symmetry) and a magnetic moment term (breaking both flavor and spin symmetry). Reparameterization invariance (RPI), arising from the arbitrariness in splitting heavy quark momentum into M_Q v + k, partially restores boost symmetry broken by introducing v. RPI connects leading and sub-leading operators, constraining the kinetic energy Wilson coefficient C_k = 1 to all orders in perturbation theory, while the magnetic moment coefficient C_f receives a non-trivial anomalous dimension.

The focus shifts from block codes to convolutional codes, which combine linear and finite-state dynamical structures to approach channel capacity with lower-complexity decoding, such as the Viterbi algorithm. 

Convolutional codes are defined using Laurent sequences—semi-infinite sequences over the binary field with a definite starting time. These sequences form a field with well-defined addition, multiplication, and inverses. The D-transform is introduced as a generating function notation for these sequences. Rational Laurent sequences, which are ratios of polynomials, are shown to be eventually periodic, analogous to rational numbers.

A convolutional code consists of all output sequences generated by passing Laurent sequences through an encoder. For an encoder to be finite-state and realizable, its impulse response must be rational and causal. Encoders are equivalent if they generate the same code, meaning their generator vectors differ by a rational, causal multiple. A canonical encoder is polynomial with minimal degree and no feedback.

The lecture concludes by analyzing the free distance (minimum distance) of a rate 1/2 convolutional code. Using the code's linear and finite-state properties, including state transition diagrams, the free distance is determined to be 5. The next lecture will cover trellis diagrams, catastrophicity, and the Viterbi algorithm.

The parents of two daughters (ages 17 and 15) had a July 2003 custody agreement granting the father sole custody and the mother visitation "subject to the children's wishes." The father subsequently moved to Florida with the daughters without informing the mother and obstructed her communication and visitation efforts. Family Court found the father committed multiple intentional violations of the custody order but denied the mother's custody petition, granting her unfettered phone, email, and correspondence access instead. On appeal, the court upheld that remaining with the father was in the younger daughter's best interests but found that visitation should not have been left to the child's wishes, noting the father's willful interference raised questions about his fitness and the mother had turned her life around. The matter was remitted to Family Court for immediate consideration of court-ordered visitation between the younger daughter and mother, with an updated in camera hearing if necessary. The suspension of the mother's child support payments was also affirmed.

Growth was driven by higher sales across all product and service categories and geographic segments. The company held $195.6 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, and had $107.0 billion in term debt. Denise Ricco and her family are participating in SPARK, a large study seeking genetic markers for autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Organized locally by Rush University, the study aims to test 50,000 individuals with ASD and their families using at-home cheek swabs or in-person professional testing. Participants receive a $50 gift card. The research seeks to better understand the genetic causes of autism, including inherited and new traits, and potentially improve treatment efficacy. The Passing Game offense relies on basic rules, off-ball screens, and continuous movement rather than set patterns, ensuring all five players are involved. Strengths include continuous motion, creativity, effectiveness against any defense, and tempo control. Weaknesses include potential breakdowns from selfish players, poor rebounding, and impatience. Success requires fundamental skills in passing, shooting, screening, rebounding, and reading defenses. Key rules involve maintaining 12-15 foot spacing, setting solid screens, using a triple-threat position, and limiting dribbling. The offense features 3-person (Hi/Lo), 4-person (Four Out), and 5-person (Motion) variations. Against zone defenses, it utilizes sharp passing, skip passes, and weak-side attacks. While coaches may initially feel a loss of control, the offense provides steady performance, exposes weak defenders, and induces opponent fatigue.

In Avendano v. Stavrakos, the plaintiff appealed the denial of his motion to set aside a jury verdict for the defendant and the judgment dismissing his complaint. The court dismissed the appeal from the order and affirmed the judgment, concluding the jury's finding of no negligence was a fair interpretation of the evidence.

This systematic literature review examines digital leadership in education, focusing on its definition, effects, and influencing factors. Using PRISMA guidelines, researchers analyzed 39 empirical articles from Scopus, Web of Science, and EBSCO databases. 

Regarding the definition, only 11 articles defined digital leadership, often using terms like technology leadership, e-leadership, or digital leadership. Most definitions lacked key leadership elements (interaction, ability, followers, goals) or the educational context. The study suggests a Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) driven model for a more dynamic definition.

The effects of digital leadership were discussed in 28 articles, impacting students (academic achievement), teachers (technology integration, professional development, job satisfaction), and schools (management efficiency, digital culture, transformation). 

Influencing factors were analyzed in 10 articles, categorized into internal factors (individual characteristics, professional experience, digital literacy) and external factors (infrastructure, school culture, policies, training, COVID-19). 

The study concludes that future research should explore the dynamic nature of digital leadership, its role in lifelong learning and data security, follower involvement, and multicultural contexts.

The NCAA implemented the targeting rule in 2008 to protect players and prevent brain injuries. Targeting is defined as taking aim at an opponent for forcible contact beyond a legal tackle, block, or playing the ball, including helmet-to-helmet hits and hits on defenseless players. The penalty is 15 yards and an automatic ejection; if it occurs in the second half, the player is also suspended for the first half of the next game. Unlike the NFL's "unnecessary roughness" rule, NCAA targeting results in automatic disqualification, though replay officials can overturn the ejection. Repeat offenders face additional one-game suspensions.

This study investigates the coarsening dynamics of phase-separating DNA droplets in active, self-stirring fluids compared to passive fluids. Experiments and simulations reveal that while active coarsening is faster and loses self-similarity over time, the mean radius growth exponent remains identical to passive fluids, challenging classical coarsening theory. However, the total number exponent differs between the two. Active droplets exhibit size-independent effective diffusivity, violating the Stokes-Einstein-Sutherland relation. The research identifies the collision kernel exponent as a unifying control parameter. Positive kernel exponents, which favor collisions between large droplets, explain the loss of self-similarity and the non-linear relationship between the coarsening exponents observed in active and anomalously diffusing systems. This framework helps decouple active and passive mechanical contributions to condensate coarsening in biological systems.
