A 34-year-old Mission man was released on a promise to appear in court after collisions at a Maple Ridge strip mall injured a woman and her son.
Despite not scoring initially, the speaker stayed positive by focusing on playing well overall. They eventually scored but emphasized that winning is the most important thing.

Ray Jones, Jr. was convicted of the first-degree murder of his infant son and sentenced to life imprisonment. He appealed based on two assignments of error. First, Jones argued the trial judge erred in admitting his inculpatory statements made at a hospital and police station, claiming they were involuntary and obtained in violation of Miranda. The Supreme Court of Louisiana held the hospital statements were voluntary, unsolicited, and not the product of police interrogation, so Miranda warnings were unnecessary. For the police station statement, the court ruled the officer's remarks did not amount to interrogation, and any error in its admission was harmless beyond a reasonable doubt due to overwhelming evidence. Second, Jones contested the restriction of his cross-examination of a witness. The court found the trial judge acted within his discretion to exclude irrelevant questioning. The conviction and sentence were affirmed.

Generative AI disrupts higher education by challenging traditional assessments like essays and MCQs, which are vulnerable to AI-generated content and academic integrity issues. As AI detection tools prove unreliable, the passage advocates for integrating AI into assessment design rather than avoiding it. This includes using AI as an auxiliary tool for drafting, critiquing, and generating ideas to foster AI literacy, critical thinking, and authentic, real-world skills. A case study of a UK postgraduate immunology module illustrates this approach: students used ChatGPT to draft essay outlines, peer-reviewed them, and completed the final essay independently. Student feedback highlighted AI's utility in planning but noted limitations in accuracy and depth. The passage concludes that higher education institutions must provide AI literacy training for educators and students, rethink assessment policies, and focus on higher-order cognitive tasks to maintain integrity and prepare students for an AI-driven society.

NBA Commissioner Adam Silver stated the 2026 All-Star Game will remain at the Clippers' Intuit Dome in Los Angeles despite an ongoing investigation into the team for allegedly circumventing salary cap rules. The investigation follows a report regarding a $28 million endorsement deal between Kawhi Leonard and a company that received investment from Clippers owner Steve Ballmer. Potential penalties include fines, voided contracts, and forfeited draft picks.

Starting April 1, a new Scottish law will criminalize disclosing or threatening to share intimate private photos or videos, carrying a maximum five-year prison sentence. Justice Secretary Michael Matheson stated the law addresses technological changes and is part of broader efforts to eliminate domestic abuse, harassment, and sexual violence.

The description details a system for controlling mobile agricultural machines using active ground terrain mapping. A pose detection sensor identifies the machine's geographic position and orientation. Based on these signals, a virtual point cloud is defined and attached to the machine, estimating the ground surface beneath and around it. Elevation values are generated for each point in the point cloud. A weighting function assigns confidence values to these elevation estimates based on their distance from the pose detector. As the machine moves over a fixed map structure of the field, the elevation values and weights are aggregated into discrete map cells. Control signals are then generated to adjust controllable subsystems, such as header or boom height, using the aggregated elevation data. The system can be implemented across various computing environments, including cloud architectures and mobile devices.

This qualitative study explores the perceptions of education and industry leaders in Mauritius regarding micro-credentials, which certify specific skills to bridge the gap between higher education and workforce needs. Through semi-structured interviews with 10 educational leaders and 4 industry leaders, the research examined the definition, integration, and perceived value of micro-credentials. 

Findings reveal varied definitions among participants, ranging from short courses to mini-qualifications, alongside a mixed understanding of digital badges. Respondents preferred a hybrid model for integrating micro-credentials into existing academic credit systems to maintain flexibility. While viewed as a disruptive innovation and the future of education, leaders recommended a prudent, phased implementation. 

A major challenge identified is the lack of a unified national framework and the need to adapt the Mauritian National Qualifications Framework (NQF) to recognize these credentials. The study concludes that while micro-credentials are not fully understood, there is broad consensus on their importance. It recommends integrating them into a unified framework to ensure academic recognition, reliable assessment, and employer acceptance.

Matthew Shashy was sentenced to four years probation for firing a shotgun outside Maxwell Air Force Base in January 2017. Convicted of intimidating Air Force personnel, Shashy committed the act after prior anti-government graffiti incidents. A civilian tracked his license plate, leading police to his barricaded home, where he surrendered and additional firearms and literature were found.

Brookfield Infrastructure Partners (BIP) has delivered strong historical returns and AFFO growth since 2012. The company targets 6-9% annual distribution growth, which the author views as potentially aggressive. BIP's current 4% yield is lower than historical levels due to stock price increases. This overvaluation benefits current unitholders by allowing BIP to issue new units to fund higher-yielding investments, though this strategy depends on unit prices. The author concludes BIP remains attractive with a safe, growing dividend and an expected 10% total return.

A NIAID-funded Phase 2 trial found that combining a 16-week course of omalizumab with oral immunotherapy (OIT) greatly improves OIT efficacy for children with multiple food allergies. After 36 weeks, 83 percent of children receiving omalizumab and OIT safely consumed two grams of at least two allergens, compared to 33 percent receiving a placebo. Omalizumab recipients also experienced fewer adverse events. Larger studies are needed to confirm these findings.

Equifax began in 1874 tracking consumer credit for businesses, treating people as the product. Modern credit bureaus collect extensive financial data without consent, and lawmakers struggle to regulate them.

An archaeological search at Dublin City Hall for an Easter Rising rifle dropped by rebel Willie Halpin found no weapon. Consultant archaeologist Franc Myles, funded by Dublin City Council and supported by the Halpin family and Lord Mayor Nial Ring, excavated a narrow gap between buildings. The rifle was likely removed in the years following the Rising. However, the dig uncovered other artifacts, including roof fragments with a bullet hole, 1930s milk bottles, pottery, and a 1980s crisp bag.

The Vanguard Mid-Cap Growth ETF (VOT) has an implied analyst target price of $145.80, offering 9.77% upside. Underlying holdings Sensata Technologies, Global Payments, and Markel show 10.26% to 11.37% upside. The passage questions whether these targets are justified or overly optimistic, noting they require further investor research.

Tanzania launched the Tanzania Business Clinic (TBC) to improve its business climate following the Cabinet's adoption of a regulatory reform blueprint. The TBC will use experts and public officials to solve sector-specific challenges. Set for implementation in the 2018/19 financial year, the blueprint amends various laws to attract private investment. This follows Tanzania's poor ranking in the World Bank's Doing Business 2018 Report. Officials hope the reforms will change regulators' mindsets, stimulate local production, and create jobs.

John Knight left $5.25 million to LHSC’s ovarian cancer research team in tribute to his wife, Mary, who died of the disease in 2008. Announced on Valentine’s Day, the funds will hire researchers, buy equipment, and foster global collaborations to study how the cancer metastasizes, as it lacks early screening tools. Victoria Hospital’s A-block lobby was named the Mary and John Knight atrium.

Julia Banks won the federal seat of Chisholm for the Liberal Party in 2016, ending Labor's nearly 20-year hold. Doubts regarding her dual Greek-Australian citizenship could trigger a constitutional crisis and byelection. Local voters expressed mixed reactions; some swing voters and Liberal supporters intend to vote conservative again, while Labor voters hope the issue damages the Turnbull government. Political analysts and Labor strategists suggest a byelection in the marginal seat would be tight, with Labor potentially regaining it. Banks originally won in 2016 by a 2.84% swing after Labor's Anna Burke retired.

Former Facebook executives Palihapitiya, Parker, and Garcia-Martinez express regret over the platform's negative societal impact. Palihapitiya cites destructive feedback loops, Parker notes altered relationships, and Garcia-Martinez claims the company lies about data influence. Palihapitiya is using his earnings to fund structural changes.

The passage outlines various on-field non-verbal communications used in soccer, primarily hand signals, to coordinate during matches. These signals direct set pieces, passes, runs, defensive positioning, throw-ins, and substitutions. Examples include pointing to direct player movement, tapping the chest for throw-ins, and circling hands to request a substitution. The text also details other cues like head nods, mentions a historical example involving Pelé, and advises coaches to develop these signals to overcome loud crowd noise.
OpenAI's GPT-5 launch faced criticism for livestream glitches, inaccurate numbers, and unmet expectations. CEO Sam Altman says the model was misunderstood and his AGI attitude changed.

On May 24, 1870, President Ulysses S. Grant warned citizens against joining illegal military expeditions against the Dominion of Canada from US territory. He ordered US officers to prevent these activities and arrest participants, warning they would forfeit government protection.

The passage details the Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 for SD memory cards, covering UHS-I, UHS-II, and UHS-III bus speed modes and selection sequences. UHS-I requires 1.8V signaling via ACMD41 and CMD11, supports 4-bit mode, and uses CMD19 for tuning. UHS-II and UHS-III offer speeds up to 624MB/s, utilizing a multi-step initialization (PHY, Device, Enumeration, Configuration, SD-TRAN). The host controls communication via broadcast or addressed commands in either card identification or data transfer modes. Initialization involves CMD0, CMD8, and ACMD41 to verify voltage and capacity, followed by CMD2 and CMD3 for identification. Data operations include block read/write commands with CRC, erase operations (ERASE, DISCARD, FULE), and write protection (mechanical, internal, password-based). Card Ownership Protection (COP) and Force Erase Password (FEP) manage locking via CMD42. CMD6 switches functions like access mode and power limit, while CMD55 enables application-specific commands.
11-year-old Damian Sunderland faces months of surgery after a relative's dog attack. He recently received skin grafts from his arms and legs to reconstruct his face and lips.

The NVIDIA RTX Blackwell architecture introduces the AI Management Processor (AMP), a RISC-V based GPU context scheduler that offloads tasks from the CPU to reduce latency and improve multitasking. Blackwell adds hardware encode and decode for 4:2:2 chroma video, a ninth-generation NVENC with an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode, a sixth-generation NVDEC, and DisplayPort 2.1b support. Max-Q power efficiency improvements feature advanced power and clock gating, separate voltage rails, accelerated frequency switching, and faster deep sleep entry. DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, capable of generating up to three frames per rendered frame, and transitions to transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA to enhance image quality. The architecture also debuts neural shaders using the Cooperative Vectors API, enabling features like RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. Blackwell powers the GB202, GB203, and GB205 GPUs, including the GeForce RTX 5090, 5080, 5070 Ti, and 5070.

VentureWire's May 22, 2001 newsletter covers venture capital and technology industry news. Top stories include Kodiak Venture Partners closing a $290 million fund, Mercury acquiring Freshwater Software for $147 million, Celetron raising $48 million, and TVM's first close on a life science fund. The newsletter details numerous new funding rounds for companies including CGtime, Lawson Software, NetContinuum, Danger, NuVasive, and SeeCommerce. Adverse news includes staff cuts at AgWeb and Ironmax, and Rx.com ceasing prescription fulfillment. Mergers and acquisitions include Blink.com buying BookmarksPlus, Everstream acquiring The MusicBooth, Primus acquiring AnswerLogic, and MindArrow buying Control Commerce. Additional sections report on new product launches, executive appointments, board additions, a tech funding program formed by the University of Pittsburgh and Redleaf Group, and personnel updates at 3i, Charles River Ventures, and Growth Capital.

This Phase 2/3 study evaluated the safety and immunogenicity of the SII-NVX-CoV2373 vaccine in 920 Indian children and adolescents aged 2 to 17. Participants were randomized 3:1 to receive the vaccine or a placebo. The vaccine demonstrated non-inferior immune responses compared to adults, achieving over 98% seroconversion for anti-S IgG and neutralizing antibodies after the second dose. It also elicited immune responses against the Delta, Omicron BA.1, and Omicron BA.5 variants. SII-NVX-CoV2373 was safe and well-tolerated, with no adverse events of special interest or causally related serious adverse events reported; most adverse events were mild and resolved without sequelae. These results support the vaccine's use in pediatric COVID-19 vaccination.

Mud Bay, a Pacific Northwest pet store chain, introduced an Employee Stock Ownership Plan in 2015 to improve jobs and customer experience. Despite strong sales, net profit margins fell from 2.18% in 2014 to 1.99% in 2017 due to increased wages, benefits, training, and reduced prices. To address profitability, COO Tracy Yamane proposed closing stores an hour earlier, a move supported by co-CEO Marisa Wulff but opposed by co-CEO Lars Wulff due to concerns about customer inconvenience and lost revenue.

Founded in 1988, Mud Bay focused on natural dog and cat products, consultative selling, and customer education. In 2014, facing 48% staff turnover, the executive team developed a "Good Jobs Vision" with five strategies: investing in staff, offering less at everyday low prices, standardizing processes, improving efficiency through cross-training, and partnering with animal welfare organizations.

Between 2014 and 2017, Mud Bay raised average hourly wages to $15.06, increased medical insurance eligibility to 82%, and reduced SKUs and prices. While staff turnover dropped to 31% and total sales grew by 70%, the company struggled to fully implement process standardization and continuous improvement. The decline in profitability prevented the finalization of the 2018 budget, prompting the leadership team to analyze the potential impact of reducing store hours before making a final decision.

This qualitative study investigated the experiences of 17 students and 4 lecturers regarding Physical Education (PE) teacher training in distance mode at North-West University, South Africa. Data were collected through open-ended questionnaires and semi-structured interviews. The analysis revealed five themes. First, lecturers were perceived as available and responsive, though students missed physical contact. Second, lecturers' passion motivated students, increasing their competence and confidence. Third, obstacles included students' lack of foundational knowledge, technological illiteracy, limited internet access, and assignment administration delays. Fourth, videos positively aided practical training, but delayed feedback hindered immediate correction. Finally, the course content positively influenced students' perceptions of PE's value. Recommendations to improve distance PE training include adding face-to-face contact, providing technological training, enhancing video use, increasing learning management system interactions, and improving university administration systems.

Poor document management costs businesses time, money, and customers through lost files, storage expenses, wasted supplies, and security risks. Improving these processes boosts workflow, productivity, and business growth. Businesses can enhance document management by tracking print costs and using Xerox ConnectKey technology to scan to and print from cloud services. Xerox apps like CapturePoint and Mobile Link streamline workflows and mobility. Additionally, setting printing restrictions such as PINs and color limits saves money and improves security, while automated low-toner alerts maintain supplies.

Passports certify US citizenship and are issued only to citizens who establish citizenship, US domicile, and intent to return. Expatriated individuals—those who permanently abandon US allegiance and domicile for a foreign country—cannot receive passports. Even without expatriation, those permanently domiciled abroad are ineligible, as foreign settlement presumes intent to stay unless proven otherwise. Passport decisions depend on individual circumstances. Adverse factors include severed US ties, foreign homes, and no US domicile plans. Favorable factors include maintained US ties, health or financial barriers to returning, or representing US enterprises abroad. Special rules apply to US citizens in countries with US extraterritorial jurisdiction, like Turkey, where members of American communities can inherit US citizenship and passport protections regardless of paternal US residency, provided their pursuits are legitimate.

A city court reserved its order on Shashi Tharoor’s anticipatory bail plea regarding his wife Sunanda Pushkar’s death. Delhi Police opposed the plea, citing flight risk and potential witness tampering. Tharoor’s defense argued he cooperated during the concluded probe and was not arrested before the chargesheet. Tharoor, charged with abetment of suicide and cruelty, is the sole accused in the case.

Matt Barbet's "Home Roads" podcast, launching June 8 on iTunes and Acast, features the ITV presenter riding bikes with professional cyclists and other figures. The show explores their lives, careers, and personal stories. Initial episodes feature Alex Dowsett, Sarah Storey, Nicolas Roche, and David Millar, while future guests include Ben Saunders, Simon Warren, Simon Mottram, and Philippa York.

The 200-day moving average (200 DMA) is a widely used trend-following indicator that calculates an asset's average closing price over 200 trading days. A price above the 200 DMA indicates an uptrend, while a price below signals a downtrend. The strategy's primary advantage is capital preservation during bear markets and recessions, a "play defense" approach favored by investors like Paul Tudor Jones. Backtests show it achieves lower drawdowns compared to buy-and-hold strategies. However, during prolonged bull markets without major recessions, the strategy often underperforms due to frequent whipsaws and false signals, resulting in a low historical win rate of 28%. Variations, such as Jeremy Siegel’s 1% threshold strategy, can improve risk-adjusted returns. The 200 DMA is also utilized as a trend filter or in moving average crossover systems. The simple moving average (SMA) is typically preferred over the exponential moving average (EMA) for its simplicity.

The NVIDIA A100 GPU architecture introduces significant improvements in memory bandwidth and caching, including a 40 MB L2 cache, an HBM2 memory subsystem, and L2 cache residency controls to optimize data fetch efficiency. It also features Compute Data Compression to save bandwidth. A key addition is Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology, which partitions a single A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory resources, ensuring quality of service and fault isolation for multi-tenant environments. The architecture debuts third-generation NVLink, offering 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, and PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV support. Additional hardware features include an NVJPG decode engine, an Optical Flow Accelerator, improved atomic operations, and five NVDEC units. CUDA 11 advances bring hardware-accelerated Task Graphs, asynchronous copy operations, asynchronous barriers, and enhanced cooperative groups. The A100 powers the DGX A100 system, delivering 5 PFLOPS of performance with a fully optimized software stack via the NGC Private Registry. Finally, the A100 supports fine-grained structured sparsity (2:4 sparsity) to increase compute throughput and reduce memory bandwidth usage with virtually no loss in accuracy.

The lecture discusses hinged dissections, noting the lack of general animation software and suggesting it as a potential project. Greg Frederickson's books on various dissections are highlighted. The universality of hinged dissections for 2D polyforms, such as polyominoes, is proven using induction and dual graphs, with slender adornments enabling continuous motion. Physical applications of these concepts include mesoscale liquid actuation, DNA origami, and chain-folding robots that remain connected during reconfiguration. The Montucla dissection technique is explained for converting between rectangles of different sizes. The lecture also details how to achieve a pseudopolynomial bound on the number of pieces in hinged dissections by limiting recursion depth and using specific gadgets like kite fans and pseudocuts. Finally, 3D dissections are explored, requiring matching volumes and Dehn invariants as necessary and sufficient conditions. While determining if Dehn invariants match is decidable, finding efficient algorithms for 3D dissections remains an open problem.

Researchers found that New Caledonian crows and kea parrots learn object properties through incidental play, improving their success in solving subsequent tool-based tasks. Additionally, activists warn that tourist wildlife selfies posted on Instagram are fueling the cruel treatment of animals in the Amazon.

The passage details the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol, focusing on Guest Non-Automatic Exits (NAE). When an NAE event occurs, hardware throws a #VC exception, prompting the guest to update the GHCB and invoke VMGEXIT. The document specifies required NAE events, state exchanges via the VALID_BITMAP, and error handling protocols. 

It outlines various NAE events, including IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, MMIO access, Page State Change, SNP Guest Requests, AP Creation, #HV Doorbell Page, #HV Timer, and Termination Requests. It explains SMP booting challenges under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP, introducing AP Reset Hold and AP Creation features to manage vCPU states securely. 

Additionally, the passage describes the #HV doorbell page used with the Restricted Injection feature. It defines the PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields for managing interrupt delivery and End-Of-Interrupt (EOI) optimizations. The document specifies host and guest behaviors for acknowledging interrupts, handling non-maskable events, and securely mapping doorbell pages without compromising guest state integrity.

The coach discusses a recent win where the team played with five defensemen, praising the forwards, Max, Jannik, and Raffi for their speed and physical play. He notes the differing goaltending styles between the teams and expresses a need for clarification regarding the opposing goalie initiating contact. He compares the physical Boston series to previous ones against Nashville and Chicago. Manny is day-to-day and not skating. The coach reflects on his career path from a limited player to coaching in the Stanley Cup Final, emphasizing his excitement and focus. He expects a hard-fought series due to both teams' big-game experience. He maintains a one-game-at-a-time philosophy, declines to discuss lineups, and praises a young player's upside. He believes the team's time off was used well to stay sharp and refuses to comment on unverified rumors, focusing only on his team and the Bruins.

The Saskatchewan Roughriders are considering using return specialist Christion Jones as a defensive back. Jones, who practised as an emergency DB this week, has prior experience at the position from college. He is a versatile player, also listed as a backup receiver and tailback, and currently ranks third in the CFL for punt and kickoff return averages. Head coach Chris Jones is cautious about increasing Jones's workload to protect his return performance but will use him if necessary.

Joan Jordan, an Irish software engineer diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS) in 2010, faced years of job rejections before resuming work at Eupati. She authored the book "huManS Multiple Sclerosis," featuring tips from MS patients, and seeks a sponsor for more copies. For World MS Day, she is speaking at Trinity College as MS Ireland and Novartis launch a report titled "Making Ireland the Best Place to do Multiple Sclerosis Research." The report recommends an MS Research Community, improved data sharing, patient involvement, and funding models.

The passage describes systems and methods for address obfuscation in memory devices to protect against malicious attacks, such as row hammer. To prevent bad actors from reverse-engineering wear-leveling movement patterns, a configurable mapping function maps logical addresses to physical addresses in an unpredictable manner. This mapping function uses selectable per-bit logic operations—such as inversion, XOR, XNOR, or pass-through—and can vary across memory devices, dice, arrays, or over time based on triggers, random numbers, or unique identifiers. The memory device includes selection and mapping components that route logical address bits through subcomponents to determine the corresponding physical addresses. This variability ensures that reverse-engineered patterns are not applicable to other memory entities or at later times. A security key may allow manufacturers to bypass the obfuscation for testing and debugging purposes.

This document is the user manual for the SanDisk Sansa Fuze MP3 player. It outlines safety instructions, including hearing safety and device cleaning, and provides disposal guidelines. The manual details the player's hardware features, such as its 1.9-inch color screen, FM tuner, built-in microphone, and microSDHC slot. It provides step-by-step instructions for charging the battery, navigating menus, and connecting to a computer. Users are guided on transferring music, photos, and videos via drag-and-drop, Windows Media Player, or Sansa Media Converter. The guide explains how to play music, audiobooks, and videos, view photo slideshows, listen to FM radio, and record voice. Additionally, it covers deleting content, adjusting system settings like display and power saver, troubleshooting common issues, and outlines SanDisk's warranty and software license agreement.
12,000-year-old camel engravings at Jebel Misma indicate early human presence in a once-verdant Nefud landscape.

The passage argues that modern K-12 education wrongly prioritizes vague skills, such as critical thinking and metacognition, over the acquisition of actual knowledge. The author asserts that skills cannot be applied without foundational background knowledge, using examples like cricket terminology and string theory to demonstrate that simply looking up complex information is insufficient without prior study. The text criticizes the devaluation of knowledge as mere "memorization" and points to grade inflation and reduced testing requirements as evidence of this educational retreat. Conversely, it highlights that schools using knowledge-rich curricula have seen academic gains. While some states are adopting High-Quality Instructional Materials (HQIM), the author warns that many approved curricula still lack sequential knowledge building and that AI could further dilute educational quality. Ultimately, the author argues that neglecting knowledge acquisition widens educational disparities for poorer students and deprives children of essential intellectual development.

This study analyzed 2021 Nigeria Malaria Indicator Survey data to assess insecticide-treated net (ITN) usage among children under 5 and pregnant women. Despite ITNs being a cost-effective malaria intervention, utilization remains below Nigeria's 80% target. The study found that 56% of households owned at least one ITN, with ownership significantly higher in rural areas, the North West and North East zones, and lower wealth quintiles. Only 41.4% of children under 5 and approximately 50% of pregnant women slept under an ITN. For both groups, ITN usage was significantly higher among younger individuals, rural residents, those in northern regions, and lower wealth quintiles. Pregnant women with less education also showed higher usage. The authors conclude that addressing regional and socioeconomic disparities is essential to improve ITN coverage.

NVIDIA's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended May 1, 2022, reports revenue of $8.29 billion, up 46% year-over-year. Net income was $1.62 billion, down 15% from the prior year, primarily due to a $1.35 billion acquisition termination charge related to the canceled Arm Share Purchase Agreement. The company operates through two segments: Graphics and Compute & Networking. As of May 1, 2022, NVIDIA held $20.34 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities. During the quarter, the company returned $2.10 billion to shareholders through share repurchases and dividends, and its Board of Directors increased the share repurchase program to $15 billion through December 2023. NVIDIA noted that supply chain constraints, COVID-19 lockdowns in China, and the war in Ukraine are impacting its operations and demand forecasting.

HMD Global has not released the Nokia 8 kernel source code 136 days after promising to do so. This delay violates the GPLv2 license, drawing criticism from developers and costing the company goodwill, despite the device's bootloader remaining locked.

Mario Batali is taking a leave of absence from his businesses and was removed from ABC's "The Chew" after Eater reported sexual misconduct accusations by four women. Batali apologized, taking full responsibility for his past behavior.

Researchers reclassified 560-million-year-old fossils found in Newfoundland as one of Earth’s earliest animals. Previously considered decomposed organic matter, the spongelike creature was named after punk rocker John Lydon for its spiky appearance. Paleontologist Christopher McKean and colleagues identified pores indicating it was a filter feeder, suggesting it may be an ancestor of modern sponges.

A University of Queensland study found that Black, Western Green, and Jameson's mamba venoms launch a dual neurological attack. The venom initially causes flaccid paralysis, which current antivenoms treat. However, this treatment unmasks a second toxicity that causes painful spastic paralysis. This explains why some patients initially improve before experiencing severe muscle spasms. The study also noted venom function varies geographically. Researchers state these findings highlight the need for new, specialized antivenoms to improve snakebite treatment.

This systematic review examines the application of artificial intelligence (AI) in assessment, grading, and feedback within higher education, guided by the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework. Analyzing 20 studies published between 2010 and 2023, the review finds that AI enhances efficiency, scalability, and consistency in grading, particularly for objective assessments. AI also provides timely, personalized feedback that supports adaptive learning and reduces educator workloads. However, challenges persist regarding AI's ability to evaluate subjective constructs like critical thinking, alongside concerns about algorithmic bias, data privacy, and ethical implementation. The review highlights varying adoption rates globally, noting that African nations and Zambia face unique resource constraints but recognize AI's potential to standardize assessments. Ultimately, the review concludes that while AI offers transformative benefits for educational practices, it should complement rather than replace human judgment, requiring transparent policies and interdisciplinary collaboration to ensure equitable and effective learning environments.
The speaker views crowd cheers as support before going to Detroit to gain ground. They react to players' tendencies once the puck hits them rather than pre-sorting them.

The speaker enjoyed the physical intensity and detailed a play where they caught a deflected puck and passed to a teammate. Their focus is helping the team win by scoring or defending. They contributed to two goals and are focused on the next home game. The speaker appreciated their family attending the Stanley Cup Finals and praised teammate Cory as an underrated player who excels at moving the puck and making plays.

The passage details Birmingham City FC's top ten away matches over a decade, highlighting memorable moments for fans and the club. Key matches include a 1-0 win at Bristol City in 2017 to avoid Championship relegation, a 2-1 Europa League victory at Club Brugge in 2011 featuring a 100th-minute winner, and a 2-2 draw at Bolton in 2014 where a late equalizer secured safety. Other notable games were a 2-1 win at Reading in 2009 to clinch Premier League promotion, a 3-2 victory at Tottenham in 2007, and wins against Fulham (5-2), Crystal Palace (4-0), Derby (3-0), Wolves (2-1), and Shamrock Rovers (4-0). These matches featured late goals, promotion clinchers, and passionate away support.
Ray Lewis, Brian Urlacher, Randy Moss, Terrell Owens, Brian Dawkins, Bobby Beathard, Jerry Kramer, and Robert Brazile were voted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

Best Buy's Techtober sale offers the Acer Swift 16 AI laptop for $800. It features 16 GB RAM, 1 TB storage, a 16-inch OLED screen, and an Intel Core Ultra 7 256V CPU. The sale runs through October 12, alongside Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days. A thinner alternative, the Lenovo Yoga Slim 7i Aura Edition, is available for $900.

On April 20, 2010, the Deepwater Horizon rig exploded in the Gulf of Mexico, killing 11 workers and spilling nearly five million barrels of oil. BP, which leased the rig from Transocean for the Macondo well project, faced scrutiny over its organizational culture and operational decisions. BP historically utilized an "asset federation" model that decentralized decision-making, which reduced incentives to share risk management practices. Prior to the disaster, BP had experienced other safety breaches, including a 2005 refinery explosion and a 2006 pipeline spill.

Investigations into the Deepwater Horizon disaster highlighted several key decisions made while closing the Macondo well that prioritized cost and time over safety. These included using a long string casing with fewer gas barriers instead of a safer, more expensive liner-tieback option; using only six centralizers instead of the 21 recommended by Halliburton's model, which warned of a severe gas flow problem; conducting a partial, 30-minute mud circulation instead of the recommended 6-12 hours; and canceling a cement bond log test to assess the cement job's integrity.

The disaster caused extensive environmental damage to Gulf Coast wetlands and wildlife, along with severe economic impacts on the fishing and tourism industries. BP faced massive financial losses, a drop in stock value, and established a $20 billion compensation fund. The U.S. government implemented a temporary moratorium on deep water drilling, leading to further regional job losses. Investigations concluded that BP's operational decisions repeatedly favored expediency and cost-reduction over caution.

In his inaugural address, the President addresses the nation's severe economic crisis, asserting that the only thing to fear is fear itself. He acknowledges the material difficulties facing the country, including high unemployment, shrunken values, and frozen trade, attributing these issues to the failures and selfishness of financial and business leaders. He calls for a shift away from valuing mere monetary profit toward social values and the joy of work.

The President declares the primary task is putting people to work through government projects and national planning. He proposes measures to raise agricultural values, prevent foreclosures, reduce government costs, unify relief, and supervise transportation and utilities. He also demands strict supervision of banking and investments to prevent speculation, alongside a sound currency.

Prioritizing domestic recovery over international trade, he advocates for a "good neighbor" policy in world affairs. He calls for national unity, discipline, and sacrifice, comparing the effort to a trained army. While hoping for legislative cooperation, he warns that if Congress fails to act during the national emergency, he will seek broad Executive powers comparable to those used in wartime. He concludes by expressing faith in democracy and asking for divine guidance.

This lecture explores limited attention in economics. Psychological experiments like change blindness and dichotic listening show attention is limited and affected by distractions, including physical environment, worries, and poverty. Inattention persists even in high-stakes situations, evidenced by stock market reactions to old news (EntreMed) and ticker confusion (Zoom).

To measure inattention, the lecture reviews Chetty et al.'s study on sales taxes. Because sales taxes are added at the register, they are less salient than posted prices. Making the after-tax price explicit on tags reduced demand, revealing consumers react to sales taxes only a quarter as much as regular price changes. Conversely, salient excise taxes are used to deliberately alter behavior for "sin goods" with externalities.

The lecture also examines why inattention causes large welfare losses via "learning by noticing." If individuals lack the correct theory about what variables matter, they never encode relevant information, preventing learning. A study on Indonesian seaweed farmers showed they ignored pod size because they didn't consider it relevant. Trial participation alone did not change behavior, but explicitly summarizing data and providing recommendations did, demonstrating that systematic learning failures occur when people do not initially attend to the right dimensions.

The MACD and RSI strategy combines two momentum indicators to analyze market trends and movements. Traders can combine these indicators in various ways, such as using MACD to identify the overall trend and RSI to find price swings or mean-reversion trades. 

While some analysts argue that combining two momentum indicators is redundant, others find it beneficial for confirming signals. The accuracy of MACD versus RSI depends on the specific parameters and markets tested, making backtesting essential. The passage highlights a specific backtested strategy that incorporates both indicators alongside a mean reversion filter, which performed well on certain assets like SMH and XLP. Ultimately, the focus should be on creating and backtesting profitable strategies rather than determining which indicator is inherently better.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture introduces significant advancements for AI and HPC workloads. It supports TF32, FP16, and BF16 for deep learning training, and IEEE-compliant FP64 for HPC applications. A major feature is Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity, utilizing a 2:4 pattern to double compute throughput by skipping zero-value computations. The memory architecture combines L1 data cache and shared memory (192 KB/SM), features 40 GB of HBM2 DRAM with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, and includes a 40 MB L2 cache with residency controls. The A100 enables simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution and introduces Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology, partitioning a single GPU into up to seven isolated instances with dedicated resources. Interconnect improvements include third-generation NVLink (600 GB/sec total bandwidth) and PCIe Gen 4. Additional hardware includes NVJPG decode, an Optical Flow Accelerator, and five NVDEC units. CUDA 11 advances provide asynchronous copy operations, asynchronous barriers, and Task Graphs to reduce launch overhead. The DGX A100 system leverages eight A100 GPUs to deliver 5 PFLOPS of performance. The architecture also details sparse neural network pruning, demonstrating that fine-grained structured sparsity maintains accuracy while improving efficiency.

Danny Langston appealed a summary judgment favoring Personal Service Insurance Company and George Johnson, Jr. Langston was injured in a Florida auto accident while riding in a vehicle owned by Johnson, Jr. and operated by Fred Johnson. The passage outlines SEV-ES guest-hypervisor communication, covering non-maskable interrupts (NMIs), debug register virtualization, and #HV doorbell page interrupt delivery. For NMIs, the hypervisor intercepts #DB and relies on the guest's "NMI Complete" message. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported. 

Under SNP RestrictInjection, the host signals the guest using a #HV doorbell page containing PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields. The host emulates APIC behavior, presenting interrupts by writing vector numbers to PendingEvent and setting NoEoiRequired to optimize end-of-interrupt (EOI) cycles. Non-maskable events are indicated via specific PendingEvent bits.

The guest acknowledges interrupts by atomically exchanging PendingEvent with zero. For EOIs, the guest atomically clears NoEoiRequired; if unsuccessful, it issues an explicit APIC register write via VMGEXIT. Guests must execute HLT with interrupts disabled, with the host re-entering the guest if interrupts are pending. The doorbell page is configured via VMGEXIT and must be accessed with C=0. Both host and guest must account for non-cooperative behavior, which may cause denial of service but not state corruption.

The passage details the Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 for SD memory cards, covering data transfer, erase operations, write protection, and command structures. Block write transfers use CRC checks to prevent erroneous data writing, with multiple block writes offering faster performance. Erase operations include standard Erase, Discard, and FULE (Full User Area Logical Erase), with Discard and FULE specific to SDHC and SDXC cards. Write protection is achieved via a mechanical switch, internal protection, or password-based card locking. Card Ownership Protection (COP) introduces a Force Erase Password (FEP) to secure the card against unauthorized access or erasure. The Switch Function command (CMD6) manages access modes, command systems, driver strength, and power limits. SDSC cards use byte addressing with variable block lengths, while SDHC and SDXC cards use block addressing with a fixed 512-byte block length. The host can control the bus clock for power saving or flow control, provided 8 clock cycles are given after transactions. All commands and data blocks are protected by CRC7 and CRC16, respectively. Commands are divided into classes (CCC) defining supported functionalities, and application-specific commands (ACMD) must be preceded by CMD55. Read, write, and erase operations have defined timeout conditions.

The lecture discusses linear algebra, beginning with permutation matrices used to reorder equations and minimize numerical errors or fill-in. A Plinko board model is used to illustrate diffusion via sparse matrices. The main focus is eigenvalues and eigenvectors, defined by the equation Aw = λw. Eigenvalues are determined by solving the characteristic polynomial det(A - λI) = 0, and eigenvectors are found in the null space of A - λI. The instructor explains the difference between algebraic and geometric multiplicity. When a matrix has a complete set of eigenvectors, it can be diagonalized through eigendecomposition (A = WΛW⁻¹). This decomposition is useful for solving linear systems of equations and decoupling linear ordinary differential equations. For matrices without a complete set of eigenvectors, alternative transformations like the Jordan normal form or singular value decomposition are mentioned.

The Exponential Moving Average (EMA) is a lag indicator that places greater weight on recent price data than the Simple Moving Average (SMA), making it more responsive to market changes. This study conducts a systematic literature review of Information Systems journals (2000–2017) to explore the inter-relationship between digital transformation, digital business strategy, and organizational capabilities. Using Wolifswinkel’s guidelines, 28 articles were analyzed to identify 12 dimensions of digital transformation, 6 of digital business strategy, and 10 of organizational capabilities. The findings reveal that research primarily focuses on the US, Europe, and sectors like automotive, banking, and healthcare. The study proposes a conceptual framework illustrating that digital transformation is digital business strategy in action, driven by organizational capabilities. Shared dimensions across the concepts include collaborative ecosystems, use of technology, and digital leadership. The resulting framework guides CEOs, CIOs, and IS researchers in deploying the appropriate organizational capabilities to achieve effective digital transformation and improved business performance.

This paper addresses the multi-period resource allocation problem under stochastic demands, aiming to maximize total revenue subject to a resource constraint. The authors first analyze a static, open-loop formulation where all allocations are determined initially. This convex optimization problem is solved using a bisection method on the dual variable, but it fails to adapt to sequentially revealed demands or temporal correlations. To overcome this, the authors propose a sequential, adaptive policy based on a shrinking horizon optimization framework. This closed-loop approach re-solves the optimization problem at each time step, updating the joint distribution of future demands by conditioning on observed history. The primary contribution is the formulation and empirical evaluation of this policy. Simulations using synthetic jointly log-normal demands demonstrate that while the sequential solution matches the static solution for independent demands, it outperforms both the static solution and a roll-forward baseline for non-independent demands. The adaptive method achieves higher revenue by exploiting temporal correlations, with performance approaching an oracle upper bound. The algorithm is applicable under any demand model, provided the conditional quantile functions are known.

Research indicates a strong correlation between a company's technological maturity and its business performance. While technology is crucial, the cultural elements of digital transformation are often the most difficult to implement. Digital "leaders" outperform "laggards" by adopting four key cultural themes:

1. Growth Mindset: Leaders encourage sensible risk-taking, experimentation, and long-term employee development, viewing failures as learning opportunities.
2. Data Transparency: Leaders promote open data access and shared context for decision-making, whereas laggards hoard data and rely on individual business judgment.
3. Measurement: Leaders use data-driven metrics to set realistic goals and track progress, granting teams autonomy. Laggards set ungrounded goals and focus on process adherence.
4. Organizational Alignment: Leaders use transparent, data-driven objectives to align teams vertically and horizontally. Laggards struggle to connect priorities with overall strategy.

Organizations typically fit one of four patterns: data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, or data reliant. Successful digital transformation requires aligning core beliefs, company values, and daily practices around a strong data culture.

This article examines the impact of anti-Critical Race Theory (CRT) bans on Native content instruction in teacher education programs at predominantly white institutions in Idaho, Utah, and Arizona. Using Tribal Critical Race Theory (TribalCrit) and ethnographic methods, the authors analyze how these bans perpetuate "colonial unknowing" and the invisibilization of Native peoples. The passage details recent anti-CRT legislation in the three states and highlights the predominantly white teacher workforce's lack of preparation in Native histories. Through personal stories and observations, the authors identify three main impacts: the continued silencing of Native perspectives, the perpetuation of Native invisibility in public education, and the refusal of some pre-service teachers to engage with culturally sustaining pedagogies. The authors conclude that critical democratic education must recognize Native nationhood and sovereignty to support all students.

This study analyzes self-reported mask-wearing behavior across the U.S. from September 2020 to May 2021 using the COVID-19 Trends and Impact Survey (CTIS). To address small sample sizes and survey biases, researchers employed Bayesian binomial regression models, raking, and bias correction using ground-truth vaccination data. The findings reveal significant spatial heterogeneity in mask-wearing, with higher proportions in urban counties compared to rural ones. Temporally, masking peaked in January 2021 and sharply declined by May 2021, coinciding with increased vaccinations, lower infection rates, and changing CDC guidance. Additionally, community-reported masking estimates closely matched the bias-corrected self-reported data. The authors conclude that the high spatial variability in masking behavior necessitates localized public health messaging and targeted data collection rather than a uniform national approach.

In this lecture, Russ Tedrake discusses the control challenges of walking robots, emphasizing that control, rather than actuator or power limitations, is the fundamental hurdle. Walking robots require dealing with limit cycles and impacts, also known as hybrid dynamics. Limit cycle stability is introduced using the Van der Pol oscillator, which exhibits stable periodic motion due to state-dependent nonlinear damping. Because standard Lyapunov functions do not apply to limit cycles, Poincaré sections and maps are used to convert continuous-time limit cycle stability into discrete-time fixed-point stability.

Historically, the study of legged locomotion was advanced by Muybridge's photography, McMahon's ballistic walker model, and Tad McGeer's passive dynamic walking machines. The lecture then introduces the rimless wheel model to explain the essential dynamics of walking. This model demonstrates a stable rolling limit cycle created by the balance between potential energy gained moving down a slope and energy lost during inelastic ground collisions. The rimless wheel's dynamics can be fully understood analytically via its Poincaré map. More complex models, such as the compass gait and kneed walkers, also exhibit stable limit cycles but are more fragile. Future lectures will cover applying optimization methods to these hybrid dynamic systems.

This study evaluates the Disk Potentiation Test (DPT) for detecting KPC and MBL carbapenemases in 147 imipenem-resistant gram-negative isolates from a Dhaka hospital. This study investigates the role, importance, and hindering factors of curriculum literacy in education using thematic content analysis of 29 peer-reviewed articles from the Scopus database. Curriculum literacy involves understanding, evaluating, and analyzing educational programs to improve teaching and adapt to digital transformations. While it promotes innovative practices and educational equity, teachers globally, especially in Türkiye, lack sufficient curriculum literacy due to inadequate training and bureaucratic obstacles. 

Findings show a significant increase in related studies, peaking at 89 between 2020 and 2025. Research is predominantly in social sciences and concentrated in Australia, the USA, and Turkey. Thematic trends evolved from social studies education (2010-2015) to cultural contexts (2015-2020), and recently to digitalization, artificial intelligence, and learning disabilities (2020-2025). The study identifies a positive but weak relationship between teachers' digital literacy and curriculum literacy. It concludes that curriculum literacy is critical for effective pedagogy and recommends interdisciplinary approaches, alongside targeted training for teacher candidates on digital platforms and innovative teaching methods, to improve educational quality and equity.

This paper examines the digitalization of Vietnamese higher education (HE), driven by government policy and accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic. The HE system, overseen by the Ministry of Education and Training (MOET), includes 237 universities. Before the pandemic, digitalization was slow and varied due to limited infrastructure, funding, digital skills, and fragmented oversight, though most institutions utilized learning management systems (LMS).

Government initiatives, including the National Digital Transformation Program and the 2022-2025 IT Project, set targets for digitalizing management, teaching, and learning. The pandemic prompted MOET to allow up to 30% of Bachelor and 20% of Master/Ph.D. programs to be taught online, accelerating the adoption of LMS, blended learning, and paperless administration. National database systems and digital data warehouses, such as the Vietnamese Knowledge System, were also established to share resources.

To further support digitalization, the paper recommends that MOET provide clear guidance, increase funding, and train institutional leaders. Higher education institutions (HEIs) are advised to support lecturers through training in intellectual property, pedagogy, digital skills, personalized learning, and mentorship. Additionally, HEIs should enhance student support by providing digital skills training and implementing paperless administrative procedures.

A bear trap is a bullish trading pattern where a sudden price drop tricks traders into shorting, only for the price to reverse upward. Market manipulators often create these traps to trigger retail stop-loss orders, which act as buy orders, allowing manipulators to buy at a discount. Retail traders fall victim due to FOMO and impulsive decisions. To spot bear traps, traders can look for price breaking support after an uptrend, divergences with indicators like MACD or RSI, and fundamental signals. To avoid them, traders should consider fundamentals, avoid crowd-following, control FOMO, and backtest their strategies. A mean reversion strategy buying on breakdowns demonstrated historical success with this pattern.

The lecture reviews sequence convergence and the squeeze theorem, applying them to prove special limits using the binomial theorem. This study presents an enhanced DiffCSP framework using guided diffusion to discover novel superconductors. The authors conclude that while generative AI accelerates materials discovery, challenges remain in predicting synthesizability and distinguishing genuine novelty from artifacts of incomplete reference datasets. The lecture explains how to construct the spacetime of a compact spherical body in general relativity. Using Schwarzschild coordinates, the exterior vacuum solution is found by setting the Ricci tensor to zero. Matching this to the Newtonian weak-field limit yields the Schwarzschild metric, the first exact solution to Einstein's field equations, derived by Karl Schwarzschild in 1916. Birkhoff's theorem states that any spherically symmetric vacuum exterior is described by this metric, even if the interior source varies with time. For the interior, the body is modeled as a perfect fluid. A mass function is defined, distinguishing between gravitational mass and baryonic mass due to gravitational binding energy. Combining the Einstein equations with stress-energy conservation produces the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff (TOV) equation, which describes relativistic hydrostatic equilibrium and is used to model stellar interiors.

The lecture covers the Fiat-Shamir paradigm, which eliminates interaction in protocols by replacing the verifier with a hash function. While sound in the random oracle model, its security in the standard model was a long-standing open problem. The focus is on proving the soundness of a parallel-repeated zero-knowledge protocol for Hamiltonicity under Fiat-Shamir in the standard model, based on work by Canetti, Lombardi, and Wichs (2019). 

Applying Fiat-Shamir to this protocol yields a Noninteractive Zero Knowledge proof (NIZK) based on lattices. The proof relies on the fact that for a false statement, there is a unique "bad" verifier challenge (beta) for every prover message (alpha) that allows cheating. The challenge is designing a hash function that avoids this bad beta without knowing it. 

The solution uses a commitment scheme with a trapdoor (the secret key of a public key encryption scheme) to compute the bad beta. To avoid breaking zero-knowledge, the hash function uses fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) to evaluate an encrypted function g. In the actual scheme, g is an all-zero circuit. In the analysis, g is replaced by a function g* that uses the trapdoor and secret key to compute and avoid the bad beta. By semantic security, a cheating prover cannot distinguish the actual scheme from the analysis, proving soundness. This requires the assumption of circular-secure FHE, though later work removed this requirement. The lecture concludes with a break before discussing NIZKs.

This lecture from MIT's Advanced Data Structures course introduces temporal data structures, specifically persistence and retroactivity, within the pointer machine model. Confluent persistence allows combining versions into a DAG; while general constant overhead remains an open problem, logarithmic overhead is possible for disjoint versions. The passage details various single-node and multi-node container patterns for building distributed systems. 

Single-node patterns include:
- Ambassador: Brokers connections between application containers and external services, and performs request splitting for experimentation.
- Adapter: Standardizes heterogeneous application interfaces for monitoring (e.g., Prometheus), logging (e.g., Fluentd), and health checks (e.g., MySQL), promoting modularity and reuse.

Multi-node distributed patterns include:
- Microservices: Decouples application functions into separate services communicating via APIs, enhancing agility and independent scaling, though complicating debugging.
- Replicated Load-Balanced Services: Uses identical stateless replicas behind a load balancer for redundancy and scale. Enhancements include session tracking, caching layers (e.g., Varnish), rate limiting, and SSL termination (e.g., nginx).
- Sharded Services: Partitions data across shards to scale stateful services. Consistent hashing minimizes data remapping during scaling changes. Replicated sharded services and hot sharding improve reliability and handle uneven traffic loads.
- Scatter/Gather: Parallelizes computation by scattering requests to multiple leaf nodes and gathering combined results at a root. Leaf sharding handles datasets too large for a single machine, while replication mitigates the "straggler" problem and ensures availability.
- Functions and Event-Driven Processing (FaaS): Simplifies deployment and auto-scales based on events. Ideal for stateless, short-lived tasks like the decorator pattern (transforming requests/responses), but unsuitable for long-running background processing or holding large data in memory due to cost and architectural constraints.

The ADS868xW device features a multiSPI digital interface supporting standard SPI and source-synchronous protocols with single or dual SDO-x options. It supports single and daisy-chain connection topologies. The device operates in three states: RESET, ACQ, and CONV, controlled by CONVST/CS and RST signals. Data transfer frames begin on the falling edge of CONVST/CS and end on the rising edge, requiring 32 SCLKs for valid write operations. Nine configuration registers control device ID, reset/power control, SDI/SDO protocols, data output formatting, input range, and alarm thresholds. Application examples include industrial analog input modules for PLCs, utilizing programmable input alarms with hysteresis for temperature sensing. Power supply recommendations include decoupling capacitors for AVDD and DVDD, and the device offers NAP and power-down modes to reduce power consumption. PCB layout guidelines recommend separating analog and digital sections and placing decoupling capacitors close to supply pins.

OSCAR is a one-shot multi-label causal autoregressive discovery method that infers causal structures from individual event sequences. It uses two Transformers as density estimators to identify the Markov Boundary of each label through parallelized conditional mutual information testing. Unlike traditional methods that are computationally intractable in high dimensions, OSCAR's time complexity is independent of event and label cardinality. Evaluated on a real-world vehicular dataset with 29,100 event types and 474 labels, OSCAR computed Markov Boundaries in 11.7 minutes with 55.26% precision, while existing algorithms failed to complete within three days. OSCAR provides interpretable causal graphs and quantified causal indicators, making large-scale causal discovery practical for real-world sequential data.

The lecture discusses iterative methods for solving large sparse matrices, where direct elimination is too expensive. These methods use a preconditioner matrix P, which is simpler than the original matrix A but similar enough to speed up convergence. Common preconditioners include Jacobi (diagonal of A), Gauss-Seidel (lower triangular part of A), successive overrelaxation (SOR), and incomplete LU.

The error in each iteration is multiplied by an iteration matrix M (M = I - P^-1 * A). Convergence depends on the eigenvalues of M; all must have a magnitude below 1, and the largest (the spectral radius) determines the speed. 

Using a standard 1D test matrix, Jacobi's method is analyzed. Its spectral radius is very close to 1, requiring order n^2 iterations. While Jacobi quickly eliminates high-frequency errors, low-frequency errors persist. Weighted Jacobi improves high-frequency convergence but does not solve the low-frequency issue. Gauss-Seidel uses updated values immediately, squaring the eigenvalues and effectively doubling the speed of Jacobi, but it still requires order n^2 iterations. Multigrid is introduced as a future solution to accelerate the convergence of low-frequency errors.

The NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture introduces real-time ray tracing using dedicated RT Cores and a hybrid rendering model that combines rasterization and ray tracing. A Reversal Day occurs when a stock or market index changes direction after an extended trend, often accompanied by high volume. Bullish Reversal Days happen when prices move upward after a downtrend, while Bearish Reversal Days occur when prices decline after a rally. Reversals are caused by market sentiment, economic conditions, company-specific news, and technical analysis. They can be identified using trend changes, heavy volume, and technical indicators like RSI and Bollinger Bands. Various markets, including stocks, forex, commodities, and bonds, are prone to reversals. Backtests of reversal day strategies on gold indicated that the bullish strategy had merit, whereas the bearish strategy produced losses. Understanding these signals aids investors in making informed decisions.

Cocoa futures are financial derivatives representing a contract to buy or sell 10 metric tons of cocoa at a pre-agreed future price. They trade on ICE (symbol CC, physically delivered) and CME Globex (symbol CJ, financially settled), with expirations in March, May, July, September, and December. The minimum price fluctuation is $1.00 per metric ton. Prices are driven by supply and demand factors, and the market shows seasonality, typically performing better in summer. Key trading risks include adverse price movements due to leverage and liquidity issues. Investors can also access the market via the iPath Bloomberg Cocoa ETN (NIB) or trade cocoa CFDs, which are broker agreements without expiry or delivery.

Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) are tax-free medical savings accounts tied to high-deductible health plans, currently sparking renewed GOP interest. While HSA users consume less healthcare overall, the impact on actual health is unclear, with emergency room visits increasing for lower-income families. Additionally, a lack of medical price transparency makes savings targets difficult to determine. Ultimately, HSAs are only viable for individuals with extra cash beyond daily expenses.

This study investigated burnout prevalence, associated factors, and coping strategies among prison officers at the Nsawam Medium Security Prison in Ghana. Using a quantitative cross-sectional design, 243 officers completed questionnaires based on the Maslach Burnout Inventory. The overall burnout prevalence was 9%. High emotional exhaustion was reported by 42% of officers, while 68.7% experienced low personal accomplishment. Perceived causes of burnout included irregular shifts, heavy workload, and lack of training. Shift allocation was significantly associated with emotional exhaustion, and junior officers experienced higher depersonalization. Female officers and those with postgraduate degrees had significantly higher odds of burnout. The most common coping strategy was talking to colleagues. The study concludes that addressing irregular shifts, heavy workloads, and providing development opportunities are necessary to reduce burnout among prison officers.

Optical Genome Mapping (OGM) is emerging as a comprehensive alternative to current standard of care (SOC) cytogenetic tests for hematologic malignancies, which are often subjective and require multiple modalities. This study evaluates a streamlined OGM data analysis and reporting workflow using Variant Intelligence Applications (VIATM) software. Ten retrospective myeloid malignancy cases were independently reviewed by technologist-director teams. OGM via VIA detected all variants found by SOC tests and identified additional novel variants in five of six positive cases. Technologist review times averaged 25.2 minutes for negative cases, 28.5 for simple cases, and 47.3 for complex cases, representing a roughly 50% time reduction compared to previous methods. The study concludes that OGM with VIA offers a highly efficient, objective approach to standardize cytogenomic variant interpretation and reporting, potentially addressing laboratory labor shortages.

Based on a 2021 IDC survey of 200 manufacturing decision-makers in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, this white paper examines the use of IT-based simulation, modeling, and data analysis to drive industrial digital transformation. These technologies accelerate product development, reduce costs, and improve quality, though data silos often hinder their potential. As calculation complexity grows, High-Performance Computing (HPC) is becoming essential for enabling advanced simulations, increasing innovation, and unlocking new scenarios like digital twins. Due to the high costs, maintenance demands, and scalability limits of on-premises infrastructure, many enterprises prefer external cloud or HPC as a Service (HPCaaS) models. These offer flexibility, cost optimization, and access to cutting-edge technology. The paper recommends establishing a holistic data strategy, evaluating HPC operating models, prioritizing scalability and security, and leveraging external expertise to implement HPC plans effectively.

The document is a specification update for the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device (Silicon Revision A3), detailing numerous hardware errata, their implications, and resolutions. Key issues involve automatic clock gating failures in PIC, UART, USB, and GLIU domains, typically resolved by disabling the feature. Other errata include data corruption or system hangs during UDMA, ATAC, and PMC operations, which are mitigated by adjusting PRD alignments, using I/O blocking, or trapping incorrectly sized accesses. Additional problems encompass timing violations, unreliable SSMI generation, and failures with LPC, RTC, and ACPI functions. Resolutions range from software workarounds and modified programming sequences to no action required for non-impacting issues. The document concludes with AMD's legal and trademark disclaimers.

This patent describes a hybrid gas turbine electric engine designed to improve efficiency during descent. Traditional gas turbine engines are optimized for takeoff or top of climb, reducing efficiency during lower power phases. The disclosed engine includes a core with compressors and turbines, and an electric motor connected to a shaft. The engine can be undersized for takeoff or climb requirements. During descent, the engine core is either turned off or operated at a minimum temperature to prevent thermal cycling. To maintain aircraft system operations, such as environmental controls, the engine switches to electric power using stored energy or electricity generated by the motor. The fan is allowed to windmill during descent, driving the low-speed spool and the motor to generate electricity. Alternatively, stored energy can power the motor to rotate the fan, producing enough thrust to overcome engine drag. This decouples aircraft system operation from the engine core, reducing overall fuel burn and emissions.

Singapore's rapid economic development and meritocratic ethos shaped its education system. Historically, special education was a separate, welfare-driven system. Following the Prime Minister's 2004 vision for an inclusive society, Singapore implemented Enabling Masterplans, ratified the UNCRPD, and shifted toward integrating students with special educational needs (SEN) into mainstream schools.

Teacher preparation evolved at the National Institute of Education (NIE) to train Special Educational Needs Officers (SENOs) and mainstream teachers. Special education teacher training progressed from a certificate to a diploma (DISE) and advanced degrees. Systemic changes were facilitated by a tripartite relationship between the Ministry of Education (MOE), NIE, and schools, alongside continuous government rule ensuring long-term policy planning.

Despite progress, challenges remain. Special schools are operated by social service agencies rather than MOE, resulting in disparities in teacher pay and status. Additionally, there is a lack of a continuum of educational options, such as special classrooms within mainstream schools for students with moderate to severe needs. Furthermore, special education teacher preparation remains less comprehensive than mainstream programs. Moving forward, Singapore's "Learn for Life" movement aims to foster holistic, inclusive education to meet future societal needs.

The lecture explains that D-branes become dynamical through open string quantization. A D-brane's mass is defined as its ground state energy, calculated via Euclidean path integrals over surfaces with boundaries, and scales as $1/g_s$ at weak coupling. The gravitational interaction between two D-branes can be viewed as either a closed string exchange or a one-loop open string process, demonstrating channel duality. The low-energy effective action for D-branes is the Dirac-Born-Infeld action, which describes their relativistic motion, with massless scalar fields acting as Goldstone bosons from broken translation symmetry. When multiple D-branes coincide, open string excitations become $N \times N$ matrices, resulting in a $U(N)$ gauge symmetry and a Yang-Mills effective action. Separating the branes gives mass to the strings stretching between them, corresponding to the Higgs mechanism and breaking the gauge symmetry.

This background note traces the history and evolution of "unskilled" jobs in the United States from the 19th century to the present. In 1917, the Census Bureau formalized occupational classifications, applying "skill" only to manual labor and categorizing "unskilled" work as requiring no special training. Worker identity, including race and gender, also influenced these classifications. By 1930, 28% of the workforce was in "unskilled" occupations, with African Americans disproportionately represented. In the 21st century, "low-skill" work is typically defined by education requirements or job content, with over half the labor force in jobs requiring a high school degree or less.

The note examines four main "unskilled" occupational groups. Farm labor transitioned from slavery and sharecropping to low-wage immigrant labor, remaining physically demanding and low-paid despite mechanization. Factory labor evolved from artisanal work to assembly lines and automation, accompanied by a decline in manufacturing employment and the persistence of sweatshops and prison labor. Servant and service occupations shifted from domestic servitude to retail, fast food, and care work, characterized by low wages and repetitive tasks. Other labor included dangerous jobs in construction, mining, and modern warehousing, as well as digital micro-tasking and gig work.

Efforts to improve pay and conditions involved government regulations like the Fair Labor Standards Act, labor advocacy through strikes and unions, and employer initiatives such as the "Good Jobs Strategy." However, union decline and industry consolidation worsened conditions for many. The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted these "unskilled" workers as "essential," revealing their critical role in the economy despite facing low wages, inadequate protections, and high health risks. The note concludes that the primary challenge is improving job quality rather than addressing job loss, questioning how to properly value and compensate historically "unskilled" but essential work.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture introduces advancements for HPC and AI workloads. It features third-generation Tensor Cores supporting mixed-precision formats like TF32, which deliver significant speedups in iterative refinement solvers and deep learning tasks. The A100 introduces Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity, utilizing a 2:4 sparse matrix pattern to double compute throughput and reduce memory footprint by skipping zero-value computations without compromising accuracy.

The architecture enhances memory and cache systems, featuring a combined 192 KB L1 data cache and shared memory per SM, a 40 MB L2 cache, and 40 GB of HBM2 DRAM providing 1555 GB/sec bandwidth. It supports SECDED ECC for memory resiliency and introduces Compute Data Compression to improve bandwidth and capacity.

A100 improves data fetch efficiency through asynchronous copy instructions that bypass the register file, asynchronous barriers, and L2 cache residency controls. It supports simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution and includes new hardware accelerators like NVJPG for JPEG decoding, an Optical Flow Accelerator, and five NVDEC units for video decoding.

The Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) feature partitions a single A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances, each with dedicated compute and memory resources, ensuring quality of service and fault isolation for multi-tenant environments. Compute Instances further subdivide these resources for simultaneous context execution.

Interconnect upgrades include third-generation NVLink, providing 600 GB/sec total bandwidth across twelve links, and PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV support. The A100 also enhances error detection, isolation, and containment for large clusters.

CUDA 11 advances include Task Graphs for reduced launch overhead, asynchronous memory copies, and hardware-accelerated barriers. The NVIDIA DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs with NVSwitches to deliver 5 PFLOPS of performance, scalable for large AI clusters. The architecture also details a sparse neural network primer, explaining how fine-grained structured sparsity optimizes compute throughput while maintaining accuracy.

The passage introduces T-Tamer, a framework for managing bi-objective trade-offs, such as accuracy and latency, in cascaded inference. Existing heuristic-driven routing policies lack generalizability and optimality guarantees. T-Tamer models routing and termination as a costly exploration problem over a directed acyclic graph (DAG). The authors prove that "no-recall" strategies, which cannot return to previously inspected models, cannot achieve a constant-factor approximation of optimal utility. In contrast, T-Tamer introduces a "with-recall" dynamic indexing strategy that is provably optimal and computable in polynomial time for common DAG structures, including directed lines, their transitive closures, and directed trees. Experiments on vision and NLP benchmarks demonstrate that this strategy consistently achieves efficient accuracy-latency trade-offs, significantly reducing latency with limited accuracy degradation.

The passage introduces the empirical stochastic inverse problem (eSIP), which involves inferring the probability distribution of unknown physical parameters of a complex system from observed data using computer models. The authors define the eSIP and the general stochastic inverse problem (SIP), aiming to find a parameter distribution that induces the observed data distribution. They adopt a Bayesian approach utilizing the disintegration of measures to establish the existence and uniqueness of a posterior distribution. The main results include an explicit formula for the posterior density, its almost-everywhere continuity, the maximum entropy property of the solution using a uniform prior, and a strongly consistent numerical estimation method based on importance sampling.
