The AMD Security Processor (ASP) verifies AMD signatures on boot firmware and Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) runtime updates. System designers (OEM/ODM) own the firmware root of trust for updates and can optionally co-sign SFS packages using an RSA key pair provided during early boot. SFS updates are non-persistent across reboots and must be applied sequentially. BIOS developers enable SFS and co-signing via specific tokens; the ASP verifies both customer and AMD signatures before executing a patch.

SFS packages can patch registers, replace firmware images, or update drivers. Packages must verify existing firmware versions before applying to prevent out-of-sync dependencies, and partial updates are not applied. For SEV/SNP systems, updates are automatically committed, require HV-FIXED pages if SNP is enabled, and may require SEV/ES virtual machines to stop and restart. SFS provides measurements for attestation, though some attestation schemes prevent updating certain firmware.

Customers apply patches during OS boot or runtime using a customer-provided deployment agent, adhering to specific memory alignment requirements. The ASP process involves protecting the DRAM address, verifying signatures, loading the patch, updating the patch level, and returning status. Commands like GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO and UPDATE_FW retrieve firmware versions and apply updates. SFS packages are named based on CPU family, AGESA release, and a sequential number. Updates run in parallel with system traffic to minimize performance impact.

HF-band RFID, including NFC, increases battery drain in mobile devices by transferring power to passive transponders. The proposed PTF-Determinator method determines the power transfer function (PTF) during the card detection phase by approximating the physical distance between the reader and transponder. A case study simulating and testing the reading of digital business cards showed that the PTF-Determinator reduces transmission energy by up to 80% in simulation and 26% on real hardware. When applied to a state-of-the-art NFC smartphone, this equates to a 13% reduction in battery drain. Additionally, a feature cutting off power beyond a maximum distance reduced transmission energy by up to 75%, resulting in a 39% battery drain reduction on the smartphone.

This lecture explores pleat folding in origami, focusing on hyperbolic paraboloids (hypars) made from concentric squares or circles. While these models appear to self-fold into 3D saddle shapes due to paper's elastic and plastic memory, a theorem proves it is impossible to properly fold a concentric square crease pattern into a 3D form without adding extra creases. By triangulating the pattern, the model becomes foldable, and its existence can be proven using interval arithmetic to bound computational errors. This triangulated model closely approximates, but does not perfectly match, a true hyperbolic paraboloid.

The lecture also covers the mathematical principles of paper folding. Because a folded sheet's Gaussian curvature remains zero, it can only curve in one direction locally, forming a ruled surface. This principle proves that in proper foldings, straight creases remain straight and interior faces remain rigid. 

Additional topics include the creation of "hyperhedra" sculptures by joining hypars, the potential of self-folding structures at nano and macro scales, open problems like the tea bag problem, and the ongoing recreation and study of David Huffman's complex curve crease origami.

The passage details the integration and operation of AGESA software within a UEFI BIOS environment. In the binary image build model, interface call-out functions are routed through a single portal, requiring the host environment to implement a call-out router. The UEFI environment spans four execution stages (SEC, PEI, DXE, RTP) across 16-bit, 32-bit, and 64-bit modes, utilizing specific compilers and libraries. 

AGESA initialization is divided into PEIMs and DXE drivers. PEIMs handle early processor and memory initialization, publishing PPIs to coordinate dependencies and reset requests. The DXE driver performs late initialization and generates data tables (ACPI, DMI) for the operating system. 

The text outlines AGESA entry points executed in sequence: AmdInitReset (minimal processor setup and cache allocation), AmdInitEarly (full processor and HyperTransport initialization), AmdInitPost (memory initialization and transition to post-memory state), AmdInitEnv (artifact data transfer to main memory), AmdInitLate (generation of ACPI/DMI tables), and AmdInitRtb (saving state for suspend mode). Resume paths restore the system state using saved context data.

Host environments must implement required call-out functions, including AgesaAllocateBuffer and AgesaDeallocateBuffer for memory management, and AgesaReset for system resets. Configuration options are customizable via the <plat>Options.c file, covering processor power management, memory interleaving, graphics settings, and FCH controller parameters. Stack procedures manage Cache-As-RAM (CAR) for pre-memory execution. The passage also describes utility functions for creating structures, identifying processor cores, mapping memory addresses, and managing MMIO ranges.

Minorities, women, and veterans completed 54 percent of work hours, surpassing the 38 percent goal, while 18 percent of subcontracts went to small businesses. The project is on schedule for summer 2020 completion. The newly formed Community Benefits Oversight Committee will monitor these goals and the Raiders' philanthropic efforts.

The professor introduces course 6.451, Principles of Digital Communications II, which focuses on modern coding techniques for the additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel. The course is videotaped for OpenCourseWare. Logistics include weekly problem sets (15% of the grade), a midterm (1/3), and a final (1/2). The prerequisite, 6.450, is strictly enforced to ensure students have the necessary mathematical sophistication. There is no required textbook; the professor provides course notes. The TA, Ashish Khisti, will guest lecture for lectures two through four.

The course covers various codes—such as algebraic block, convolutional, and capacity-approaching codes—and their decoding algorithms, aiming to reach channel capacity. The first three chapters serve as a warm-up. Chapter 1 introduces channel models like the deep space and telephone line channels, along with the concept of decibels (dB). Chapter 2 explains converting continuous-time AWGN channels to discrete-time using orthonormal Pulse Amplitude Modulation (PAM), showing that signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and spectral efficiency remain consistent across both domains. Chapter 3 covers the proof of Shannon's channel capacity formula, C = W log2(1 + SNR), which establishes the maximum achievable data rate for a given bandwidth and SNR.

The article compares dollar-cost averaging (DCA) and lump-sum investing strategies. While DCA mitigates behavioral biases by investing capital gradually, studies and backtests show lump-sum investing generally yields higher returns. The article highlights the sequence of returns risk by reshuffling S&P 500 returns from 2000 to 2019. This reshuffle slightly reduced lump-sum returns but devastated DCA returns, dropping its compound annual growth rate from 5.5% to 1.9%. The article concludes that lump-sum investing is the superior strategy because randomness and sequence of returns significantly impact DCA outcomes.

Motley Fool Money details three credit cards requiring a good to excellent credit score (670-850). The Wells Fargo Active Cash Card offers unlimited 2% cash rewards, a $200 bonus after spending $500 in 3 months, 0% intro APR for 12 months, no annual fee, and cell phone protection. The Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Credit Card provides unlimited 1.5% cash back on purchases, 5% on Capital One Travel bookings, a $300 welcome bonus, 0% intro APR for 15 months, and no annual fee. A Citi card offers 2% cash back (1% on purchase, 1% on payment), a $200 bonus after spending $1,500 in 6 months, and 0% intro APR on balance transfers for 18 months. Motley Fool receives compensation from advertising partners but states it does not influence product ratings.

The article reviews nine Vanguard ETFs for portfolio diversification, founded by John Bogle, the "father of passive investing." It details each ETF's tracked index and investment strategy, covering total stock, international stock, real estate, and bond market funds. The authors backtested a combined "Vanguard Ultimate Diversified Portfolio" from 2007 to 2023 using a buy-and-hold strategy with annual rebalancing. This portfolio grew $10,000 to $19,318, yielding lower returns than the S&P 500 partly due to bond allocations. The article concludes by explaining that passive investment strategies are popular for being cost-effective and hands-off.

Weber State University canceled its 27th annual Unity Conference, themed "Navigating the Complexities of Censorship," after officials directed presenters to remove terms like "DEI," "diversity," "equity," and "inclusion" from their slides days before the event. Associate professor Sarah Herrmann and other faculty withdrew, leading to the cancellation. The directive stemmed from Utah's HB 261, which restricts certain DEI concepts in non-academic programming. Because the conference was organized by the Student Access and Success division rather than an academic unit, it was subject to the law. University officials acknowledged communication was unclear and noted they are still navigating the legislation. They are considering restructuring future conferences under Academic Affairs to exempt them from HB 261. The incident highlights ongoing tensions as Utah's legislature pressures public universities, including recent budget cuts and the closure of programs like queer studies.

The President reports national prosperity and the implementation of recent acts. Measures were adopted to maintain peace with Native Americans, protect settlements, and uphold treaty rights, including a new treaty with the Creek Nation. The United States took possession of British-held frontier posts, and boundary and claims commissioners are working under the treaty with Great Britain. Boundary line arrangements with Spain are underway, though Spanish claims adjustments remain unresolved. Agents were appointed to protect American seamen abroad, and negotiations with Algiers successfully liberated captured citizens, with treaties for Tunis and Tripoli in progress.

The President recommends gradually creating a navy to protect commerce and neutral rights. He advises supporting essential manufactures to avoid foreign dependence, establishing agricultural boards to promote improvement, and creating a National University and a Military Academy. He also calls for revising officer compensation to prevent reliance on private wealth.

The President notes that French cruisers are injuring US trade in the West Indies but expresses a desire to maintain harmony while protecting national honor, reserving details for a special message. He reports improving revenues, urges accelerating public debt repayment, and reiterates the need for an efficient militia and secure harbors. Concluding his final address, he congratulates the nation on the government's success and prays for its continued preservation.

This April 23, 2001, email compiles news articles on global energy markets, with a focus on Enron and PG&E.

- **PG&E Bankruptcy:** CEO Robert Glynn's misjudgment of California's electricity market and unprofitable out-of-state expansions, which often competed poorly against Enron, led to the utility's historic bankruptcy.
- **Enron's India Disputes:** Enron's Dabhol Power Company (DPC) sought lender approval to terminate its $3 billion Maharashtra project due to payment defaults by the state electricity board. Separately, developers of the Mangalore project halved its capacity to avoid a similar situation, and India's ONGC disputed Enron's claims of substantial gas reserves at the Tapti fields.
- **Colorado Power Plant:** Tri-State Generation proposed a $1.3 billion coal-fired power plant in Colorado, citing cost advantages over natural gas despite environmental objections.
- **Saudi-U.S. Oil Talks:** Saudi Oil Minister Ali al-Naimi planned to meet U.S. Energy Secretary Spencer Abraham to discuss oil prices following OPEC output cuts.
- **Spanish Market Reforms:** The Spanish government sought to revise electricity market rules to increase competition and reduce the dominance of Endesa and Iberdrola, allowing companies like Enron to participate.
- **Karnataka Power Queries:** A group in Mangalore, India, questioned contradictory official statements on the state's power production, demand, and costs, including comparisons to Enron's rates.

Eilish McCready founded the Fearless theatre school in Glasgow to help children, including shy kids and those with additional needs like autism, develop confidence and social skills without the pressure of performances. The school keeps classes small and focuses on personal development rather than acting ability. Parents, including Lizanne Conway and Lisa Byrne, report significant improvements in their children's confidence, communication, and social interaction. Conway noted the inclusive environment helps her autistic sons navigate daily challenges, while Byrne observed her previously shy daughter now performs confidently. Classes are held at Studio 93 in Glasgow.

Evercore will release its second quarter 2018 financial results on July 25, 2018, followed by a conference call hosted by its executives. The call includes a Q&A session and is accessible via telephone and webcast. Replays will be available by phone for one week and online for 30 days. Evercore is a global independent investment banking advisory firm founded in 1995.

In October 2001, Enron Corp. faced significant financial turmoil as its stock price plummeted following a $618 million third-quarter loss, a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity, and an SEC inquiry into off-balance-sheet partnerships managed by CFO Andrew Fastow. To address potential shortfalls in investment vehicles, Enron may issue up to $1 billion in new stock to help repay $3.3 billion in notes due over the next 20 months. During a conference call, CEO Kenneth Lay attempted to reassure investors of the company's liquidity and defended Fastow, but declined to discuss the partnerships due to the ongoing SEC inquiry and shareholder lawsuits. Analysts criticized Enron's opaque financial reporting. Additionally, Enron sought a $750 million loan from Citigroup, faced a class-action lawsuit, and was listed for a $254 million tax refund under a proposed House stimulus bill. Other unrelated news in the passage includes AES Corp's issues in India, LNG shipping concerns, and British Gas seeking a deal with ONGC.
Winter brings hot fishing. Offshore targets: sailfish, dolphin, wahoo, and kingfish at specific depths using live bait and kite fishing. Inshore: jacks and tarpon at the inlet and beaches.

A study reveals that biased online media trains AI models to perceive women as younger and less experienced than men. Analyzing millions of images, videos, and text, researchers found women are consistently depicted as younger, particularly in prestigious occupations. This skewed data influences human beliefs and causes AI chatbots to generate and rank female resumes lower than male ones. Researchers warn that addressing biases individually overlooks the compounding harm of overlapping inequalities like age and gender.

The SPY and XLU rotating system, based on Michael Gayed’s paper, is a weekly strategy that rotates between the S&P 500 (SPY) and Utilities (XLU) based on past performance. Utilities are targeted for their low beta and interest rate sensitivity, typically outperforming the market when rates fall. While the strategy outperformed the market historically since 1929, it has lagged the market since its 2014 publication. This underperformance may be typical post-publication decay rather than a complete loss of efficacy.

Game is selling an Xbox One S (500GB) bundle for £249.99, including Forza Horizon 3, Tekken 7, Halo 5, and Gears of War 4. Buying these items individually on Amazon UK costs £297.10, yielding a £47.11 savings. The Xbox One S was rated 4/5, praised for its small size, 4K upscaling, and UHD Blu-ray capabilities. The four included games also received high review scores ranging from 4/5 to 5/5.

Researchers are repurposing grape pomace, a wine industry byproduct that causes environmental pollution, into a renewable resource. Pomace is rich in natural antioxidants that neutralize free radicals. Changmou Xu’s team is developing technologies to extract these nutrients, remove pesticides, and use them in food, health products, and cosmetics. Their research indicates pomace-derived compounds can extend the shelf life of fatty foods, reduce acrylamide in potato chips, and combat foodborne pathogens. This approach aims to replace artificial antioxidants like EDTA, meeting consumer demand for natural, "clean label" ingredients while minimizing environmental contamination.

This Phase 1, 2/3, and 3 study evaluated BNT162b1, BNT162b2, and BNT162b2SA COVID-19 vaccines in healthy participants aged 12 and older across 6 countries from April 2020 to February 2023. The study used observer-blinded and open-label methods for initial doses and boosters. BNT162b2 was 95% effective in preventing COVID-19 after two doses, and both BNT162b2 and BNT162b2SA produced immune responses comparable to the original two-dose BNT162b2 regimen. Most medical problems, such as temporary lymphocyte drops, injection site reactions, and systemic events like tiredness and headache, were mild or moderate. Serious medical problems and deaths occurred rarely, and researchers generally did not believe they were caused by the study vaccines.

NASA's Cassini spacecraft completed the first of five close flybys of Saturn, acting as the planet's first atmospheric probe before its mission ends with a fiery descent on September 15. Running low on fuel, the probe will be intentionally crashed into Saturn to prevent contaminating potentially life-harboring moons Titan and Enceladus. During these final passes, Cassini will gather atmospheric, temperature, and aurora data, and attempt to determine the exact length of a Saturnian day. Past Titan flybys prepared the team for these final maneuvers.

The patent application claims priority to multiple prior applications concerning surgical networks and smart energy devices. It details methods for characterizing the state, function, and tissue contact of an ultrasonic device's end effector by measuring and classifying transducer impedance to adjust power levels. The disclosure describes a computer-implemented interactive surgical system featuring a surgical hub, visualization system, robotic system, and intelligent instruments that communicate with a cloud-based system. The surgical hub utilizes a modular enclosure that slidably receives interchangeable modules, including a combo generator (integrating monopolar, bipolar, and ultrasonic components), smoke evacuation, and suction/irrigation modules. This modular design manages power, data, and fluid lines to reduce entanglement and facilitate interactive communication between modules. Furthermore, a surgical data network connects modular devices in the operating theater to cloud computing resources, enabling remote data processing to improve surgical outcomes, reduce costs, and enhance patient satisfaction.

This introductory lecture covers plasma diagnostics, which infer plasma properties indirectly through physical effects. Diagnostics are crucial for validating experiments, simulations, and theories, as demonstrated by historical examples like the Z-pinch, tokamak, and National Ignition Facility. While theorists ideally want the position and velocity of every particle, practical measurements focus on moments like density and velocity, as well as magnetic fields. However, diagnostics face limitations such as sparsity, line integration, instrument filtering, and reliance on poorly understood physics. The course emphasizes fundamental principles over specific implementations. The lecture concludes with an interactive activity where students share their research parameters and the diagnostics they use across various plasma regimes.
The Rams are seeking to interview Jaguars interim coach Doug Marrone for their head coaching vacancy. The Jaguars are also considering making Marrone their permanent head coach.

Amazon.com, Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2015, reports total net sales of $22.7 billion, a 15% year-over-year increase, and a net loss of $57 million. The company revised its reportable segments to North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). North America sales grew 24% to $13.4 billion, International sales decreased 2% to $7.7 billion due to foreign exchange impacts, and AWS sales increased 49% to $1.6 billion. Operating expenses rose across fulfillment, marketing, and technology infrastructure. Trailing twelve-month free cash flow was $3.2 billion. As of March 31, 2015, Amazon held $13.8 billion in cash and marketable securities and $8.3 billion in long-term debt. The filing also outlines ongoing legal proceedings, including patent and wage lawsuits, and tax examinations by the IRS, French Tax Administration, and European Commission concerning transfer pricing and state aid.

In 2017 and 2018, Tesla faced significant financial pressures and cash burn while attempting to ramp up Model 3 production. Founded in 2003 and led by CEO Elon Musk, the company evolved from a niche electric vehicle manufacturer to a mass-market producer, launching the Roadster, Model S, Model X, and Model 3. Tesla also expanded into battery production and solar energy, acquiring SolarCity in 2016. Despite a rising stock price, Tesla struggled with profitability and negative cash flow, funding its operations and expansion through repeated equity and debt offerings that significantly increased its shares outstanding and long-term debt. As Model 3 production delays persisted, analysts questioned whether Tesla would need to raise over $10 billion in capital by 2020, despite Musk's assurances that no further fundraising was needed that year.

Hurricane Harvey damaged up to a dozen Texas Gulf Coast wildlife habitats, harming nesting sites, marshes, and coastlines. State and federal agencies are assessing the impact on threatened and endangered species, including whooping cranes and prairie chickens. Scientists link increasing storm intensity to climate change. Marine impacts include oyster bed losses and potential dolphin injuries from freshwater inflows.

The NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture introduces GDDR6 memory for improved bandwidth and power efficiency, alongside an enhanced display engine supporting 8K resolution and HDR. Turing replaces the SLI bridge with NVLink for higher GPU-to-GPU bandwidth. Its major innovation is real-time ray tracing, enabled by dedicated RT Cores that accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) traversal and ray-triangle intersection. This facilitates Hybrid Rendering, combining rasterization and ray tracing for realistic shadows, reflections, and ambient occlusion. Turing also utilizes Tensor Cores for AI-based NGX features, including Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS), InPainting, and AI Super Rez. Additional rendering technologies include Mesh Shading to reduce CPU bottlenecks, Variable Rate Shading (VRS) for optimized shading rates, Texture Space Shading (TSS) for decoupled shading, and Multi-View Rendering (MVR) for VR. The architecture spans multiple chips (TU102, TU104, TU106) powering products like the GeForce RTX 2080 Ti and Tesla T4. Turing also supports USB Type-C and VirtualLink for simplified VR connectivity and introduces the RTX-OPS metric to measure hybrid rendering performance.

This study introduces a method to analyze public transit mode hierarchies using smart card data from the Seoul metropolitan area, addressing limitations of previous research that assumed spatial homogeneity. The methodology classifies passenger transfers into "ascending" and "descending" phases based on half the total travel distance. It constructs transfer rate matrices to calculate a normalized average hierarchical order for each mode. A case study using 2019 transit data analyzed six modes: walking, community bus, urban bus, intercity bus, light rail, and metro. Results indicate that within Seoul, the hierarchy follows walking, community bus, urban bus, light rail, and metro. For interzonal trips between Seoul and Gyeonggi/Incheon, the intercity bus ranks highest. The findings confirm that a mode's hierarchical order varies regionally based on the relative distribution of transportation infrastructure.

A 16-year-old driver crashed through a "T" intersection into a bayou, resulting in the drowning death of 15-year-old Michael Hill. Hill's father sued the Morehouse Parish Police Jury, alleging inadequate warnings at the intersection. The trial court found the police jury 20% at fault for failing to maintain a double arrow sign and the driver 80% at fault, awarding the plaintiff $31,587.53. On appeal, the court affirmed the factual findings that the police jury knew of the intersection's danger and breached its duty of care. The appellate court amended the fault allocation to 65% for the driver and 35% for the police jury. The general damage award of $150,000 was affirmed as not an abuse of discretion. A concurring opinion noted that survival damages for the victim's pre-death suffering were ignored at trial, though not contested on appeal.

This study assesses the potential of self-archiving (green Open Access) to increase the discoverability of clinical trial results. Using the tools Unpaywall and Shareyourpaper, researchers analyzed a cohort of 1,897 clinical trial publications from German university medical centers published between 2010 and 2020. They found that 54% of these publications were openly accessible, while 46% remained closed-access. Among the closed-access publications, 85% had permissions allowing self-archiving of the accepted or published version in an institutional repository, typically after a 12-month embargo. Despite this potential, only 16% of otherwise closed-access publications with self-archiving permissions were actually made openly accessible in a repository. This indicates a largely unrealized potential for green Open Access to comply with WHO guidelines for clinical trial results. The automated approach developed in this study can support institutional efforts to identify archivable publications, promote self-archiving, and increase the discoverability of research at scale.

Global stock markets rose after Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen indicated potential U.S. interest rate hikes as soon as March, signaling economic confidence. European and Asian markets mostly gained, while Wall Street futures remained tepid. Yellen's hawkish tone surprised markets, boosting bank shares and the dollar. Meanwhile, Chinese inflation ticked higher, raising concerns of potential credit tightening. The dollar strengthened against the yen, the euro weakened, and crude oil prices declined.

In this introductory lecture for MIT course 15.S12, "Blockchain and Money," Senior Lecturer Gary Gensler outlines the course's focus on blockchain technology and its potential impact on finance. Gensler shares his background in finance and public policy, including his time at Goldman Sachs and as CFTC chairman. He reviews the history of the internet, cryptography, and digital currencies, culminating in Satoshi Nakamoto's creation of Bitcoin. 

Gensler explains blockchain fundamentals, such as time-stamped append logs, hash functions, digital signatures, and consensus protocols, emphasizing how the technology addresses the "cost of trust." He contrasts permissioned and permissionless blockchains, noting the financial sector's current preference for permissioned systems. While highlighting blockchain's potential to disrupt finance by lowering economic rents and increasing inclusion, he acknowledges current limitations regarding scalability, privacy, and governance. 

The course will cover technical fundamentals, economics, and financial use cases, requiring class participation, individual write-ups, and a final team project. Gensler aims to foster critical reasoning, separating hype from reality, and exploring both minimalist and maximalist perspectives. Guest Larry Lessig briefly expresses his interest in the course's critical approach to blockchain's potential to reduce the cost of trust globally.

Digital laggards tightly control data in silos, favoring business judgment over data-driven decisions. They struggle to set realistic, data-grounded objectives, relying on qualitative processes that stifle innovation and fail to connect goals with strategy. Conversely, digital leaders use standardized APIs for data flow and embrace measurement to track progress. They use data-driven metrics to provide flexibility, autonomy, and alignment across the organization. Leaders create structured goals connected to company strategy, fostering a culture of innovation and risk-taking. A strong data culture aligns organizations vertically and horizontally. While changing entrenched mindsets is challenging, organizations typically fit into one of four transformation patterns: data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, or data reliant.

On January 28, 2016, Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K announcing its fourth quarter 2015 and year-end December 31, 2015 financial results. The filing incorporates a press release and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures as exhibits, and was signed by Senior Vice President and CFO Brian T. Olsavsky.

Interest in psychedelic drug-facilitated psychotherapy is resurging. Phase II trials showed 54% of MDMA-assisted therapy patients no longer met PTSD criteria, earning an FDA breakthrough designation. A Phase 3 study confirmed its safety and efficacy, demonstrating significant PTSD symptom reduction compared to placebo.

Ireland is highly exposed to exchange rate fluctuations involving the euro, dollar, and sterling. A weak euro attracts US tourists, while weak sterling deters UK visitors and hurts Irish exporters, though it benefits importers. Euro appreciation, influenced by ECB policies and Brexit, may hinder export-driven recovery. Browns coach Kevin Stefanski is noncommittal about rookie Shedeur Sanders becoming the backup quarterback after trading Joe Flacco to the Bengals. Stefanski plans to evaluate the week before deciding the QB2 role, prioritizing the development of young players like Sanders and Dillon Gabriel, who recently started his first game. The team may also sign Bailey Zappe to the active roster as an emergency quarterback. Deshaun Watson remains on the PUP list rehabbing an Achilles injury.

A University of Michigan study reveals that 21% of Gen X women and 10% of men in their 50s and early 60s meet the criteria for ultra-processed food addiction, a rate significantly higher than that of older adults. This generation was the first raised in a food environment dominated by ultra-processed products, with 1980s diet food marketing potentially contributing to women's higher addiction rates. The addiction correlates with being overweight, poor mental and physical health, and social isolation. Researchers warn that current children may face even higher addiction rates in the future.

Qarlinngua, meaning "like pants" in Inuktitut, is a massive sea arch located 80 to 90 kilometres southwest of Arctic Bay, Nunavut. Submitted to CBC North by local hunter Max Kalluk, the formation was initially suspected to be fake but was verified by geologists and tourism officials. Reachable only by boat during a brief summer window, it was formed by wind and water eroding 250- to 600-million-year-old sedimentary rock. Geologists estimate the arch could collapse within decades or millennia, while Nunavut's tourism department plans to promote the remote formation to high-income travelers.
The Bank of England will keep the £5 note and issue the £10 note despite animal fat concerns, rejecting costly alternatives. It will decide on plant-based substitutes for the £20 note by summer 2017.
On September 10, 2019, Bob Iger resigned from the Board of Directors of Apple Inc., according to a Form 8-K filing signed on September 13, 2019.

This study explores the career transitions of lecturers and education personnel in Indonesian higher education institutions using a qualitative grounded theory approach. It examines the adaptation and impact of these transitions, applying Schlossberg’s transition theory (the 4 S factors: situation, self, support, strategies) to non-student campus populations. Using snowball sampling, data were collected from six key informants through in-depth interviews and analyzed via open, axial, and selective coding.

Findings reveal that the 4 S factors are reciprocal, with the situation being the most difficult to control. Career transitions result in changes to behavior, role, learning, and perception. Informants face a dual-role dilemma, often prioritizing organizational responsibilities over individual performance in their primary roles. Unlike Schein’s single career anchor theory, the study found that individuals utilize two career anchors: competence and managerial. The research suggests institutions should consider competence and educational background when managing structural-to-functional position transitions. Limitations include the study's qualitative nature, lack of demographic analysis, and potential researcher bias.

The player returned from injury after a CT scan showed sufficient healing. Medical staff reviewed the scan, determining his current risk level is similar to what it will be in September. He felt comfortable during the game despite some cramping from travel. He won't change his playing style and aims to contribute to the team's success. The team needs to play harder with a chance to win the Stanley Cup on home ice. The decision to get scanned came after learning a teammate was injured, with family and management supportive of the outcome.
Appeal of plaintiff's judgment in Mayor v. Huntington was affirmed with costs.

This bibliometric analysis examines mathematics anxiety research in education using 324 articles from the Scopus database published between 2013 and 2023. Publications have steadily increased, peaking in 2022, with social sciences and psychology as the primary fields of study. Network visualization connects mathematics anxiety to various cognitive and psychological variables. The study identifies *Frontiers in Psychology* as the most active journal, Garcia-Santillan as the most productive author, and the University of Barcelona as the leading institutional affiliate. The United States contributes the most documents and collaborative networks, while Germany is the most cited country. The research concludes that mathematics anxiety remains a prominent, evolving topic in mathematics education literature.

NVIDIA's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 26, 2020, reports revenue of $3.87 billion, a 50% year-over-year increase, and net income of $622 million. On April 27, 2020, NVIDIA completed its $7.13 billion acquisition of Mellanox Technologies, which contributed approximately 14% of total quarterly revenue. The company also reorganized its operating segments into "Graphics" and "Compute & Networking" and issued $5 billion in notes in March 2020.

North Korea displayed new missiles and warned the US of nuclear retaliation during a parade for Kim Il-sung's 105th birthday. Amidst US-North Korea tensions, China warned of potential conflict, and no Chinese representatives attended the Pyongyang event.

This application provides a detection model training method, apparatus, and terminal device to improve medical image detection accuracy while reducing labeling costs and addressing domain migration. The method trains a final detection model using an initial training model comprising an initial detection model and an adaptive model. It utilizes a training sample with labeled source domain data and unlabeled target domain data. The initial detection model identifies target objects in source images, while the adaptive model classifies the domain of all images. A loss function is calculated from these results to adjust model parameters. The adaptive model may include a gradient inversion module that creates an adversarial relationship to extract domain-invariant features. This approach allows unlabeled target domain data to augment the training sample, increasing accuracy without the high cost of professional labeling.

The passage compiles May 2001 news articles concerning Enron's political influence and its Indian power project. FERC Chairman Curtis Hebert reported that Enron CEO Kenneth Lay offered him continued job support in exchange for backing faster electricity deregulation; Lay denied linking the issues. Hebert is expected to be replaced by Pat Wood, a candidate Lay endorsed.

In India, the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB) rescinded its power purchase agreement with Enron's Dabhol Power Co., citing misrepresentation of plant performance and unpaid bills. Dabhol, which had issued a termination notice over $48 million in unpaid bills, disputed MSEB's right to cancel. Bechtel, the project contractor, threatened to withdraw by May 31 due to payment defaults. Indian officials considered whether NTPC should take over the project.

Additional items include California officials criticizing energy suppliers, modest stock market gains, an article on the internet transforming corporations, Australian firms planning to invest in India's energy sector, and El Paso Corp.'s chairman agreeing to testify regarding alleged natural-gas price manipulation in California.

Apple and Google removed several ICE-tracking apps from their app stores, citing guidelines against content targeting groups like ICE officers, following claims by US Attorney General Pam Bondi that such tools endanger officers. Developers of apps like ICEBlock, Eyes Up, and DEICER are appealing the bans and keeping their apps available via Google Play and their own websites. Legal experts argue these apps constitute protected First Amendment speech, while digital rights researchers criticize the centralized control of app stores, noting that Apple and Google offer similar police-tracking features in their own map apps. The Trump administration has additionally threatened to prosecute one developer.

Teams must prepare for defensive, even, and offensive jump ball situations. Defensive jump balls, where opponents have an advantage, require early rotation, watching the jumper's tendencies, and using Box, Diamond, or "Y" alignments to protect the basket and deny passes. Even jump balls require boxing out, anticipating, and coordinated clockwise or counter-clockwise rotations. Offensive jump balls, utilized with a height advantage, involve set plays like Double Tap, Post Split, Jumper Fly, Forward Fly, Spread, Tandem, and Loop. These plays direct the tip to specific players to initiate scoring while maintaining defensive balance.

Alberta Education Minister David Eggen says parents may pay school bus fees despite Bill 1 eliminating them for students living 2.4 kilometres from school. Rocky View Schools parents and trustees prefer paying fees to resolve a $1 million transportation shortfall caused by inflation, a carbon levy, and Bill 1. The board will contact the Ministry of Education, potentially delaying its decision deadline.

On April 15, 2017, Tropical Depression 02W struck the Philippines, weakening to a remnant low pressure area before entering the South China Sea. NASA's Terra satellite captured the elongated remnants on April 17. The Joint Typhoon Warning Center expected wind shear and drier air to prevent re-intensification.

This document provides current mechanical, packaging, and orderable information for TI devices, subject to change. It defines statuses, material types, RoHS values, lead finishes, MSL ratings, and part markings. The Supreme Court considered whether the double jeopardy clause prohibits separate convictions and sentences under 18 U.S.C. §§ 924(c) and 924(j) for the same conduct. While the parties agreed Congress intended cumulative punishments for Section 924(c) and its underlying crime, they debated the specific statutory language proving this intent extends to Section 924(j). Justices questioned whether the consecutive sentencing mandate in Section 924(c)(1)(D)(ii) or the "in addition to" language in Section 924(c) suffices. The government argued Section 924(j) lacks the necessary language to authorize cumulative punishment. Additionally, Justice Gorsuch questioned the precedent requiring a clear congressional indication for cumulative punishments, though this issue was largely unbriefed.

This study develops resting-state functional connectivity (rs-FC) MRI classifiers for Schizophrenia spectrum disorder (SSD) to address existing biomarker challenges in accuracy, generalizability, and specificity. Using discovery (1,015 participants) and validation (683 participants) datasets, researchers applied LASSO and voting algorithms. LASSO classifiers achieved 79.6% accuracy in the discovery dataset and 77.3% in validation, identifying 47 important functional connectivities (FCs). Voting classifiers demonstrated higher sensitivity than LASSO. Additionally, the study explored whether these diagnostic FCs could serve as state or staging markers, noting laterality imbalances in key regions of interest.

The Jabra Elite 65t earbuds are among the first to integrate Alexa using Amazon's mobile accessory kit. While the earbuds deliver excellent sound quality and excel at voice shopping, Alexa's functionality is limited compared to smart speakers. Users cannot make phone calls, send texts, play music from popular streaming services like Spotify, or use navigation. Call quality is decent but struggles in noisy environments, and reminders are unsupported. Additionally, the earbuds have a shorter battery life than competitors and lack a lost-locator feature. Overall, while the audio experience is strong, the Alexa integration currently falls short of a fully hands-free experience.

Following the Las Vegas mass shooting at a country music festival, debates about gun control and safety have emerged. Country musician Charlie Daniels calls the event an anomaly and opposes wider gun-control laws, though he supports regulating "bump stocks." He argues politicians lack gun knowledge and claims strict laws, like those in Chicago, leave people defenseless. Meanwhile, Eric Church honored a shooting victim at the Grand Ole Opry, and Rosanne Cash urged country musicians to oppose the NRA, which has ties to the country music industry. Daniels is scheduled to perform in Cary on Oct. 21.

Shohei Ohtani started Game 1 of the 2025 NLDS for the Dodgers against the Phillies on October 4, marking his first postseason pitching appearance. Ohtani finished the regular season with a 1-1 record and a 2.87 ERA across 14 games. Manager Dave Roberts hoped Ohtani would pitch into the seventh inning. In the first inning, Ohtani retired Trea Turner, Kyle Schwarber, and Bryce Harper, and later struck out in his first at-bat against Phillies starter Cristopher Sanchez. The game was broadcast on TBS, truTV, and HBO Max.

Digital leaders prioritize sensible risks, experimentation, and continuous learning to stay competitive. They rely on data and value knowledge gained from carefully planned experiments. Furthermore, they invest in long-term employee development, focusing on critical thinking skills.

Analyzing solar radiation data from the Mauna Loa Observatory, the author examined atmospheric clarity and the impact of the El Chichon and Pinatubo volcanic eruptions. The data indicates atmospheric clarity at the observatory has remained unchanged since 1980, aside from the periods following these eruptions. During the two years post-eruption, average solar energy reaching the surface decreased by approximately 25 W/m2. The findings support the author's theory that clouds rearrange to oppose changes in forcing; during the volcanic periods, clouds allowed more sunlight through, offsetting the radiation loss by about 7 W/m2. Despite this reduction in solar radiation over two years, temperature records from the observatory and other Hawaiian stations showed no corresponding temperature decrease. The author suggests this lack of temperature change challenges the mainstream climate science assumption that reduced solar energy necessarily causes temperatures to fall, proposing instead that the climate system responds to changes to restore prior conditions.

The speaker praises Winnipeg's passionate fans, strong organization under Mr. Chipman, and smaller, full arena as a great NHL market. To differentiate the Sedin twins, the speaker notes Henrik has a larger face, speaks more, tells jokes, and was captain, while Daniel has a thinner face. When facing goalie Tim Thomas, the speaker emphasizes getting shots through, looking for back-door passes or rebounds, and aiming for corners, while acknowledging Thomas's ability to take away space and make saves.

Energy sector trading provides diversification via ETFs like XLE or individual stocks. The S&P 500 energy sector includes oil and gas businesses and recently outperformed the broader market. Its largest stocks are XOM, CVX, COP, EOG, and SLB. Although commodity trading is difficult due to unpredictable macro factors, the author presents two undisclosed XLE trading strategies with positive historical metrics. Ultimately, diversification is highlighted as more valuable than finding a perfect strategy.

The author compares Canada's big five banks to five small-cap lenders using beta, earnings yield, dividend yield, payout ratio, and dividend history. The big banks have not cut dividends in over a decade, whereas three small-cap lenders previously cut theirs. However, Atrium Mortgage and MCAN Mortgage maintained dividends with yields over 7%. In the author's ranking, MCAN ranked first, followed by Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce and Atrium. Small-cap lenders offer higher yields and lower volatility but have lower liquidity and less diverse business models than the big banks.

The Hawk Offense consists of a wing isolation, high post shuffle cut, and weakside post up. Defenses can counter using two primary strategies. The "Basic NBA Show & Recover" method has weakside defenders temporarily help on dribble penetration and screens ("Show") before returning to their assignments ("Recover") through three phases: wing isolation, high post shuffle cut, and down screen defense. The "All Out SOS Disruption" strategy aggressively traps the ballhandler on the sideline wing to prevent ball reversal. This method uses contact switches, rapid rotations based on the near player concept, and specific trap rotations if the ball is passed out or driven baseline.

AMD is launching the Radeon RX Vega 64 and Vega 56 to compete with Nvidia's GTX 1080 and 1070. While Nvidia retains the single-card performance crown and Vega 64 does not beat the GTX 1080 Ti, AMD offers three-way CrossFire support. The Vega 56 is priced lower than the GTX 1070. AMD's key advantage is FreeSync, which is cheaper and more available than Nvidia's G-Sync. This is bolstered by the new Enhanced Sync driver and efforts to improve minimum frame rates.

Old paper £10 notes cease to be legal tender on 1 March but can be exchanged for new polymer notes. The new Jane Austen £10 notes, circulating since September 2017, last longer, have better security, and include tactile features for the blind. A new £20 note is planned for 2020.

The court affirmed the judgment, ruling that wounding a trespassing animal violates statute and common law. Individuals may expel trespassing stock with necessary force but cannot inflict unnecessary injury or retaliate, as the animal's owner is liable for damages.

The safety is a defensive back position in football, serving as the last line of defense against big plays. There are two main variations: free safety, who roams the middle with more speed and freedom, and strong safety, who is stockier, plays closer to the line, and focuses more on run defense. The position is called "safety" because these players prevent big gains or touchdowns. Other names include "Rover" for strong safety and "Star" for a third safety in special packages. Safeties need coverage skills, tackling ability, speed, and communication skills. Notable safeties include Hall of Famers like Troy Polamalu, Ed Reed, Ken Houston, Ronnie Lott, and Sean Taylor. The position is crucial because a great safety provides confidence to the defense, creates turnovers, and allows cornerbacks to be more aggressive.

Over 30,000 years, the Great Barrier Reef survived five near-extinctions by migrating along the sea floor as sea levels rose and fell. However, researchers warn that this historical resilience may not withstand the current, rapid pace of human-induced climate change, warming sea temperatures, and ocean acidification. The reef is currently experiencing severe coral bleaching and die-offs, threatening the quarter of ocean life that depends on it.

Following the 2024 Arab Summit in Bahrain, educators Jaber Mustafa and Younis Bukhari proposed the "Hope" initiative to address the educational crisis of Arab children, specifically focusing on the Syrian conflict zone. The report highlights the psychological, academic, and developmental impacts of conflict, noting that millions of Syrian children are out of school due to displacement, poverty, and the destruction of educational infrastructure.

Using a triangulation design, the researchers collected qualitative data through interviews with a parent and a child, and quantitative data via surveys. A case study of a Syrian child, Ahmed, illustrated challenges such as limited study time, unsanitary environments, and a lack of resources. Results showed that conflict severely disrupts education, causes psychological trauma like PTSD, and forces families to rely on community learning groups despite scarce materials.

The authors proposed immediate and remedial solutions for emotional and academic support, alongside proactive, sustainable strategies under the "Hope Initiative." The report concludes that prioritizing education through targeted interventions and international collaboration can empower children and foster peace in conflict-affected regions.

Residents of San Andrés Hueyapan, who usually prefer the Popocatépetl volcano's eruptions to earthquakes, are experiencing high stress following a damaging September 19 earthquake and subsequent increased volcanic activity. Authorities warned nearby towns to prepare for potential eruptions. The earthquake caused severe property damage, while the volcano continues to erupt, producing ashfall in surrounding municipalities.

Sean "Diddy" Combs was sentenced to four years and two months in prison and fined $500,000 for transporting sex workers across state lines for drug-fueled sex performances. He was acquitted of more severe sex trafficking and racketeering charges. Prosecutors sought 11 years, while the defense requested no more than 14 months. The Second Circuit affirmed Samuel Israel III's conviction and twenty-year sentence. The court found no abuse of discretion in Judge McMahon's refusal to recuse herself, noting no partiality. The court also rejected arguments that the sentence was unreasonable based on bias, medical needs, cooperation credit, or length, finding it permissible given his criminal history and the money involved.

The disclosure relates to elastomeric compositions comprising dispersed carbon black (CB) particles in a silicone matrix and methods for their preparation. The method involves treating hydrophilic CB particles with a siloxane-containing or silicone-based dispersant that has carbon-black-affinic moieties (e.g., amino, acrylate, or epoxy). This dispersant anchors to the hydrophilic CB surface, rendering the particles hydrophobic and dispersible within a curable, hydrophobic silicone pre-polymer. The treated particles are mixed with the pre-polymer and then addition-cured or condensation-cured to form the elastomer. The passage details various physicochemical properties of the hydrophilic CB particles, including particle size, volatile matter content, oxygen content, pH, zeta potential, and Raman spectroscopy ratios, as well as the structural characteristics of the dispersants, such as amine number and backbone length. These compositions can be applied in industrial fields, including intermediate transfer members for indirect printing, sealants, and applications requiring thermal or electrical conductivity.

In Brooks v. Missouri Pacific Railroad Co., the petitioner, an apprentice machinist drafted into military service, sought a North Little Rock seniority date of November 3, 1955, claiming he would have completed his apprenticeship then but for his service. The District Court granted this, finding his promotion to journeyman would have been automatic. The Court of Appeals reversed, citing Tilton, stating the advancement lacked predictable certainty. The Supreme Court reversed the Court of Appeals, relying on Tilton, and held that the possibility of supply and demand issues should not defeat the veteran's seniority claim. The Court concluded the petitioner is entitled to the November 3, 1955, seniority status at North Little Rock.

The LifeCLEF 2014 plant identification task evaluated content-based image retrieval for plant species identification. The dataset comprised 60,962 pictures of 500 species from 19,504 observations, featuring seven view types (entire plant, fruit, leaf, flower, stem, branch, leaf scan) and contextual metadata. The task required retrieving correct species from multi-image plant observation queries, evaluated using an average classification score per author. Ten research groups participated, employing methods like Fisher Vectors (FV), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and Bag-of-Visual-Words (BoW). IBM AU achieved the best results using a combination of FV, CNN, and segmentation. Results showed FV encoding as the state-of-the-art approach, while CNNs underperformed due to insufficient training data and restrictions on external pre-training. Combining multiple images from the same observation improved identification accuracy, with LeafScan and Flower views yielding the highest scores. The task demonstrated progress in scaling plant recognition technologies for real-world applications.

In soccer, an offensive switch is a tactic where two attacking teammates exchange positions to beat defenders. Switches can be "called" with oral communication or "natural" without it, and may occur with or without the ball. The basic, or lateral/horizontal, switch involves players crossing diagonally toward opposite touchlines. A vertical switch involves exchanging positions front-to-back toward opposite goal lines. The objective is to confuse defenders and free a runner for a pass. Once play allows, players use oral communication to return to their original positions.

Increased model scale and principle-guided prompting improved performance, though reasoning models showed lower precision in TIF tasks. Dr. Edith Mbagwu recommends the SMART goal-setting method to help people maintain New Year's weight loss resolutions. SMART stands for Specific, Measurable, Attainable, Realistic, and Time-based. Specific goals define exact diet and exercise details. Measurable goals track progress through motivating metrics. Attainable and Realistic goals ensure objectives are manageable, suggesting smaller milestones and regular reassessments. Time-based goals require scheduling time for health. This structure helps individuals achieve realistic weight loss targets.

This research investigates the difficulties of distance education in foreign language teaching during the Covid-19 pandemic. Students lacking training on distance education programs, a dedicated study room, or a home internet connection experienced significantly more problems. The study concludes that face-to-face education is more effective and recommends awareness training for both students and teachers, alongside adopting a hybrid education model for foreign language instruction.

The lecture discusses the quantization of the Dirac theory. Standard commutation relations lead to an unbounded Hamiltonian and bosonic behavior, which is resolved by replacing commutators with anticommutators. This ensures a positive definite Hamiltonian and enforces the Pauli exclusion principle, identifying the excitations as fermions. The field is expanded into particle and antiparticle creation operators, which are shown to have spin 1/2 and opposite charges derived from a U(1) symmetry. The lecture also derives the Wightman, retarded, and Feynman correlation functions, relating them to scalar field propagators via a differential operator. Finally, chiral and Majorana fermions are briefly introduced as reduced-component versions of the Dirac spinor.

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC data acquisition device with an integrated analog front-end and reference. Data transfer frames begin on the falling edge of CONVST/CS and end on the rising edge, using SCLK to shift data. Frames are classified as optimal (32 SCLKs), short (<32), or long (>32). The device supports 1-byte or 2-byte (HWORD) read/write commands, with the LSB of the 9-bit address ignored for HWORD operations. Output data words contain conversion results and optional programmable flags, such as device address, range, alarms, and parity. The multiSPI interface supports legacy SPI protocols with single or dual SDO-x, and source-synchronous (SRC) protocols. Configuration registers manage device ID, power control, SDI/SDO protocols, data output, input ranges, and alarms. The device is suited for industrial analog input modules in PLCs, featuring programmable input alarms with hysteresis. Power supply recommendations include decoupling capacitors and programmable low-power modes (NAP and Power-Down).

This study analyzed the interaction between a mitochondrial polygenic score (MGS), lifestyle, and environmental factors on the age at onset (AAO) of Parkinson's disease (PD) using data from 9,745 patients across three cohorts. A higher MGS was associated with an earlier AAO in LRRK2-PD, but not in idiopathic PD (iPD). Gene-environment interactions affecting AAO were observed: in LRRK2-PD, MGS interacted with coffee and caffeinated soda consumption, leading to an earlier AAO in patients with a high MGS. In iPD, MGS interacted with caffeinated soda and pesticide exposure at work, also resulting in an earlier AAO. The findings highlight the importance of considering lifestyle and environmental factors when investigating genetic associations with PD onset and note population-specific effects of the MGS across different ethnicities.

The disclosure presents a system and method for periodic beam failure measurements in wireless communications. A User Equipment (UE) determines a measurement period duration based on the periods of periodic beam failure detection (BFD) reference signals (RSs) that have a quasi-co-located (QCL) relationship with demodulation RSs of PDCCH receptions monitored by the UE. During each measurement period, the UE monitors a subset of these BFD RSs. If the signal quality of all monitored BFD RSs fails to meet a specified threshold, the UE's physical layer reports a beam failure (BF) instance to a higher layer entity. A beam failure is declared if a specified number of consecutive BF instances occur, prompting the UE to identify a candidate beam and send a beam failure recovery request. Additionally, if no BFD RS is transmitted during a measurement period due to overlapping control signals, the measurement period may be ignored or treated as a BF instance when updating the consecutive failure counter, preventing erroneous counter resets and missed beam failures.

The passage introduces MOTO, a multi-objective three-layer optimization framework for mapping local transition-state networks on potential energy surfaces. MOTO comprises a multi-objective explorer for diverse initial guesses, a bilayer minimum-mode kernel using Hessian-vector products to locate index-1 saddles, and a deterministic two-sided descent to certify connectivity. Computational benchmarks demonstrate that HVP-based methods match explicit-Hessian accuracy with significantly lower memory and runtime. Applied to a DFT-parameterized Pd/Fe/Ir(111) spin model, MOTO uncovered meron/antimeron-mediated mechanisms for skyrmion transformations. The framework also proved generalizable by mapping transition-state networks in a Cartesian Ni(111) heptamer system without altering its algorithmic core. Limitations include sensitivity to hyperparameters and near-degenerate curvature.
